> EPR / Efficient Prompt Retriever (Rubin et al., 2022) for LM-feedback demonstration retrieval and its binary positive/negative training; DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020) bi-encoder architecture; BERT-base-uncased encoders (Devlin et al., 2019); LambdaRank (Burges, 2010) for the list-wise ranking loss; FAISS (Johnson et al., 2021) for inference search; GPT-Neo (Black et al., 2021) as scoring/inference LM; KATE/KNN demonstration selection (Liu et al., 2022) and Shi et al. (2022) cross-lingual retrievers as the demonstration-retrieval line.
- **contrasts with**:
> EPR (Rubin et al., 2022) - task-specific, binary LM-feedback labels, manually-limited candidate range; off-the-shelf retrievers BM25 and SBERT (heuristic, no task supervision); Instructor (instruction-tuned embedder); DR-Target (task-specific target-similarity retriever); per-task task-specialized retrievers (Das et al. 2021 KBQA, Hu et al. 2022 dialogue state tracking, Poesia et al. 2022). UDR contrasts by being a single multi-task retriever with list-wise ranking and iterative full-dataset candidate mining.
- **lineage**:
> Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval): a direct generalization of the LM-feedback demonstration-retrieval line (EPR -> UDR), moving from per-task binary-label retrievers to a single multi-task list-wise-ranking retriever; predecessor to later unified/retrieval-based ICL retrievers (e.g., RUIE 2024 for unified information extraction) that cite UDR.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- benchmark_construction_and_size

### 11. GraphIC: A Graph-Based In-Context Example Retrieval Model for Multi-Step Reasoning

2024  ·  arXiv 2410.02203  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02203)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: arXiv 2410.02203 (Oct 2024); published at AAAI 2026 (The Fortieth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, AAAI-26, pp. 30753-30761, AAAI Press, 2026)
- **authors affiliation**:
> Jiale Fu, Jiaming Fan, Xu Yang (corresponding) - Southeast University, PALM Lab / Key Laboratory of New Generation Artificial Intelligence Technology and Its Interdisciplinary Applications (Southeast University), Ministry of Education, China; Yaqing Wang (corresponding) - Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications (BIMSA); Simeng Han - Stanford University (Yale University in arXiv v1). Lead author Jiale Fu is a Master's student at Southeast University.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.02203
- **code url**: https://github.com/jialefu/GraphIC

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Multi-step reasoning: QA / mathematical reasoning, code generation, and logical reasoning (in-context demonstration example retrieval for LLM ICL).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-LLM in-context learning (ICL) setting. Given a fixed candidate pool of training examples with ground-truth chain-of-thought reasoning, the method selects k demonstration examples (in-context examples, ICEs) for each test query to be placed in the prompt. No model parameter updates; the method itself is training-free (no retriever training). Supervision: candidate examples have ground-truth reasoning processes used to build thought graphs; queries have no ground truth so a pseudo reasoning process is generated by the LLM. Standard 8-shot CoT prompting setting.
- **what is retrieved**: Demonstrations (in-context examples / ICEs) for ICL, i.e. (problem, chain-of-thought solution) demonstration pairs, selected via their thought-graph representations.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: a fixed training/candidate example set is the retrievable store; it does not grow during deployment. Thought graphs and reasoning-pattern parameters for all candidates are precomputed offline.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k ranking: GraphIC scores each candidate's reasoning-pattern applicability to the query thought graph and selects the top-k (e.g. 8-shot) examples. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or variable/precision-driven size.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: Retrieve only (Retrieve: yes; Reuse: examples are inserted verbatim as ICL exemplars, not adapted; Revise: no; Retain: no). Not framed as CBR.
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as in-context example retrieval / graph-based reasoning, drawing on cognitive science (Friston) and graph-of-thought / tree-of-thought reasoning work.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: Single demonstration (problem-solution example), represented as a thought graph - a directed, node-attributed graph whose nodes are reasoning steps (math operations / code snippets / intermediate conclusions, embedded via BERT) and edges encode step dependencies.
- **index source**: Static corpus, offline-induced. Thought graphs for all N candidate examples are constructed offline from their ground-truth reasoning, and a reasoning-pattern parameter W_i is precomputed for each during a preparation stage.
- **index structure topology**:
> Per-item dependency GRAPH (thought graph) plus a flat collection of per-candidate reasoning-pattern parameters; retrieval is a flat scan computing a graph-similarity score of each candidate's reasoning pattern against the query thought graph (no clustering/hierarchy over the store).
- **retriever type**: LLM-as-retriever (hybrid): an LLM generates a Formalized Reasoning Representation (FRR) / pseudo reasoning that is rule-parsed into a thought graph; node attributes use a dense BERT embedding model; retrieval is a custom graph-similarity metric (not BM25/standard dense cosine).
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None (training-free / off-the-shelf). No retriever training. The reasoning-pattern parameter W per graph is obtained by a closed-form optimization (rank-1 SVD solution maximizing a bilinear applicability objective under a Frobenius-norm constraint), not learned from similarity labels, LM feedback, or RL.
- **query construction**:
> For a query (which lacks ground-truth reasoning), the LLM generates a pseudo natural-language reasoning process, which is formalized into an FRR and rule-parsed into a query thought graph G^q; correctness of the pseudo reasoning is not required (robust to inaccuracies). Candidate keys are thought graphs built from their ground-truth CoT.
- **query granularity**: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single thought graph is built per query before answering and used for a single retrieval call.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot: retrieval happens once per query before generation; the selected k ICEs are fixed for the whole answer.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieve once per query at prompt-construction time (no confidence/uncertainty/iterative trigger).
- **reranking**: No separate reranking stage; the proposed asymmetric reasoning-pattern applicability metric A(W_i; G^q) is itself the single scoring/ranking function, and top-k are taken directly.
- **retrieved context refinement**: None (no post-retrieval rerank/compression/distillation). Selected examples are inserted directly. (The FRR/thought-graph construction acts as a representation-level filter of shallow semantics, but this happens before similarity computation, not as post-retrieval refinement.)
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation: the top-k retrieved demonstrations are inserted verbatim as in-context exemplars in the chain-of-thought prompt; the LLM then answers the query.
- **planning integration**: One-shot exemplars at plan/answer time: retrieved demonstrations are placed in the prompt before a single CoT generation. No interleaving with planning, no tree/MCTS search, no per-step retrieval.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: a single retrieval feeds the entire CoT generation for the query (retrieval is not interleaved per reasoning step).
- **adaptation mechanism**: Verbatim ICL exemplar (no case adaptation/revision).
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw demonstration (original problem + ground-truth chain-of-thought) injected as text exemplars. The thought-graph / FRR representation is used internally for retrieval scoring, not injected into the prompt.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Single demonstration (raw problem-CoT example). Internally matched via a distilled reasoning-structure representation (thought graph) but the injected unit is a full demonstration.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Representation-level filtering plus robustness to imperfect query reasoning: FRR / thought graphs filter out shallow semantic noise and preserve reasoning structure, reducing distractor selection; the query's pseudo reasoning need not be correct (partially-correct reasoning still aids retrieval), so GraphIC stays accurate even with incorrect generated reasoning. No retriever-aware training or self-reflection relevance evaluator.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: graph (per-item thought graphs over a static candidate store); no episodic/skill/workflow memory that grows.
- **write back**: False - no experiences/cases are written back; the candidate store and its thought graphs are fixed (computed once offline).
- **online growth**: No - the retrievable store does not grow during deployment/test-time; it is frozen after offline induction.
- **write back trigger**: Never (no write-back mechanism).
- **failure experience usage**: Not used as a memory mechanism. Note: success-only candidates (ground-truth correct CoT) form the store; failed solutions are not stored or retrieved. (The query's own possibly-incorrect pseudo reasoning is used only transiently for retrieval, not stored.)
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (append-only is not applicable; the store is static and entries are never mutated).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No - retrieval is not a learned/RL policy. It is a fixed (training-free) top-k selection using a closed-form-computed reasoning-pattern similarity metric; W is solved analytically per graph, not learned as a policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No - single-LLM, private static candidate set; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: GSM8K (math), AQUA / AQuA-RAT (math), MBPP (code generation), ProofWriter (logical reasoning).
- **benchmark family**: QA / math reasoning (GSM8K, AQUA), code (MBPP), and logical reasoning (ProofWriter). Multi-step reasoning benchmarks for ICL demonstration selection.
- **baselines**: 10 baselines: 6 training-free (Random, BM25, BERT dense retriever, Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT, Skill-kNN) and 4 training-based (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, GistScore).
- **key metrics**: Answer accuracy for GSM8K, AQUA, ProofWriter; pass@1 for MBPP; reported as per-dataset and average across the 4 datasets. Also a qualitative score-matrix vs ground-truth 'improve matrix' alignment analysis.
- **headline result**:
> GraphIC (training-free) outperforms all 10 baselines: average accuracy 78.26% with GPT-4o-mini and 70.83% with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (8-shot), beating the best training-free baseline by 2.57%/4.29% and the best training-based baseline by 1.18%/2.50% respectively; largest gains on AQUA (+3.47% GPT-4o-mini, +7.64% Llama-3 over baselines).
- **ablations**:
> Component ablation (Llama-3, 4 datasets): Text (BERT) -> FRR (text-embedding of FRR) -> Graph (graph embedding via cosine, Eq.5) -> +B (backtracking/traceback matrix) -> +S (asymmetric reasoning-pattern similarity) -> +B+S (full GraphIC). FRR filtering lifts GSM8K 74.15->78.31 and ProofWriter 73.75->82.50; graph structure lifts AQUA 50.78->54.72; full reasoning-aware similarity lifts AQUA 54.72->57.48. Backtracking and the asymmetric similarity each add gains, with the best results when all components combined. Also: k-shot analysis (1/2/4/8 shots) showing GraphIC improves steadily with k while baselines (DQ-LoRe, Complex-CoT) degrade; asymmetry analysis showing GraphIC's score matrix aligns best with the ground-truth improve matrix.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Partially: primarily end-to-end task accuracy/pass@1. No standard Recall@k/nDCG retrieval metrics, but it does report a separate retrieval-quality-style analysis (alignment of each method's score matrix with a ground-truth 'improve matrix' built from one-shot solve probabilities), decoupling retrieval-quality alignment from final task accuracy.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome (final answer accuracy / pass@1). Some process-level analysis via the improve-matrix / score-matrix alignment, but no step-wise reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> GraphIC is training-free (no retriever training cost) yet beats training-based methods; it does incur extra retrieval-time cost from invoking an LLM to generate FRR/pseudo reasoning per example/query (acknowledged like Skill-kNN and DQ-LoRe). Rank-1 constraint on W gives a closed-form SVD solution, avoiding expensive d x d matrix optimization (d up to 768 for BERT). No explicit latency/token-cost numbers reported in main text.
- **context budget and selection count**: Fixed-k: default 8-shot; analysis varies k in {1,2,4,8}. No explicit token budget cap; top-k by the reasoning-pattern applicability score, truncated at k.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (not a benchmark paper).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> In-context learning / ICL example selection (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, Skill-kNN, Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT); BERT embeddings (Devlin et al.); graph-/tree-of-thought reasoning (Besta et al. Graph of Thoughts, Yao et al. Tree of Thoughts); cognitive science (Friston hierarchical inference). arXiv v1 additionally framed the model on Bayesian Networks and Personalized PageRank, later reformulated as a reasoning-pattern bilinear/rank-1 metric.
- **contrasts with**:
> Text-embedding similarity retrievers (BERT dense, BM25) that capture shallow semantics; symmetric attributed-graph embedding similarity (cosine of iteratively-aggregated graph embeddings, Eq.5); complexity/diversity heuristics (Complex-CoT, Auto-CoT); training-based retrievers (EPR, CEIL, DQ-LoRe, GistScore). GraphIC contrasts via reasoning-aware thought-graph representation and an asymmetric, sequence-aware similarity metric, while remaining training-free.
- **lineage**: Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval): reasoning-aware / structure-aware in-context example selection for multi-step reasoning, extending text-similarity and skill/complexity-based ICE selection toward graph-based reasoning-structure matching.

### 12. MoD (Mixture of Demonstrations)

2024  ·  NeurIPS 2024  ·  [paper](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/a0da098e0031f58269efdcba40eedf47-Abstract-Conference.html)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37)
- **authors affiliation**: Song Wang (equal), Zihan Chen (equal), Chengshuai Shi, Cong Shen, Jundong Li -- all University of Virginia.
- **paper url**: https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/a0da098e0031f58269efdcba40eedf47-Abstract-Conference.html
- **code url**: https://github.com/SongW-SW/MoD

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: NLP in-context learning: text classification (sentiment, paraphrase, NLI, commonsense reasoning) and generation (open-domain QA, code generation, semantic parsing). Not an agent/planning task; this is ICL demonstration retrieval.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, non-interactive, single-LLM in-context learning. Given a labeled demonstration pool D = {(x_i, y_i)} and a test query x_test, select a set S(x_test) of L demonstrations (default L set to 50, truncated to fit context) to condition a frozen pretrained LLM for few-shot prediction. Supervision is available via the LLM's output log-probability used as a per-demonstration utility signal; retriever models are trained offline and frozen at test time. Single-agent, no environment interaction.
- **what is retrieved**: In-context demonstrations (labeled input-output example pairs) drawn from a training-set demonstration pool.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: a fixed labeled training-set demonstration pool partitioned offline into expert clusters; no growing/episodic memory written at test time.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Set-level completeness rather than independent top-k: experts collaboratively assemble a complete L-sized demonstration SET, with per-expert quotas |S_i| = floor(h(C_i, x_test) * L). Expert-wise training explicitly optimizes each candidate to be the most helpful demonstration GIVEN the other L-1 already-selected demonstrations are optimal, modeling set-level interaction. Emphasized for compositional datasets requiring precise retrieval of multiple all-important, mutually-dissimilar demonstrations.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning; only a Retrieve-analogue exists, no Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False -- the work is framed as demonstration retrieval for ICL via a mixture-of-experts paradigm; it does not cite or position itself as case-based reasoning (no Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner grounding).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: Single demonstration (one labeled input-output example pair). The optimization however targets a SET of L demonstrations assembled across experts.
- **index source**: Static corpus, offline-induced: the training-set demonstration pool is partitioned offline via K-means clustering into C expert groups; per-expert retrievers are trained offline and frozen. No online/test-time growth.
- **index structure topology**:
> Cluster-based / partitioned: the demonstration pool is split by K-means (Sentence-BERT embeddings) into C semantically-coherent clusters, each governed by one expert. Number of clusters C chosen adaptively via within-cluster SSE plus a lambda*C regularization term. Within each expert, retrieval is a flat dense-vector similarity search.
- **retriever type**: Learned dense retriever, one per expert (bi-encoder dual towers: g(x,e) = <M_d(e), M_q(x)>). A mixture of multiple learning-based dense retrievers; expert routing uses cosine similarity between query embedding and cluster centroid.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> LM-feedback / downstream-task-effectiveness: per-expert scorers are trained with contrastive learning where positive/negative labels come from the LLM's few-shot output log-probability P_M(y | demo set, x) used as a utility proxy. Crucially scored in a FEW-SHOT pattern (candidate demo paired with the optimally-selected S_- of the other experts), inspired by coordinate descent, so the signal reflects set-level marginal contribution rather than singleton utility.
- **query construction**: Raw test input x_test is embedded (Sentence-BERT) to (a) route to experts via cosine similarity to cluster centroids h(C_i, x_test) and (b) score candidate demonstrations within each expert via the learned dual-encoder query tower. No query decomposition or expansion.
- **query granularity**: Task-level / per-test-example: a single retrieval is performed for each test query at inference (one-shot, t=0). No step-level or trajectory-level re-querying.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot: the full L-sized demonstration set is retrieved once per test query before LLM inference.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieval always occurs once per test query before prediction; no uncertainty/confidence/reflection-based triggering.
- **reranking**: No explicit separate reranking stage. Selection is via per-expert top-scored demonstrations under quotas; during training a top-K candidate set is scored by the LLM and filtered (top-Ke positives), but this is a training-data construction step, not a test-time reranker.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Distractor filtering during training: the expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) objective and few-shot scoring filter out unhelpful demonstrations so the learned scorers prefer set-compatible demonstrations. At inference, no post-retrieval refinement/compression beyond per-expert top-k selection under quotas.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools; demonstrations are raw labeled example pairs, not tool docstrings).
- **index content separation**: N/A -- no separate lightweight-index-then-content scheme; clusters store full demonstrations.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval setting).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval setting). However, inter-DEMONSTRATION interaction IS modeled via set-level expert-wise training (analogous concept for demos).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation: the retrieved demonstration set S(x_test) is prepended as in-context examples to the frozen LLM, which predicts y_hat = argmax_y P_M(y | S(x_test), x_test). Retrieval is also used as a training signal during the offline scorer-training phase.
- **planning integration**: N/A for planning -- this is one-shot exemplar selection at prediction time (retrieve-then-predict). Not integrated with multi-step planning, tree search, or acting loops.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: retrieval happens once and conditions a single LLM forward prediction; no per-step or per-token interleaving.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not CBR). Retrieved demonstrations are used verbatim as ICL exemplars; no case adaptation/revision.
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw labeled demonstration example pairs (input-output) injected verbatim as few-shot exemplars in the prompt.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw single demonstration (concrete labeled example), assembled into a diverse set; no distilled strategy/guideline/workflow abstraction.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) training: when optimizing the score of a candidate demonstration, the other L-1 demonstrations are held fixed at their optimally-selected values, so unhelpful demonstrations do not corrupt the supervision signal; this directly targets the 'insufficient optimization / noise from unhelpful demonstrations' challenge. Clustering experts also reduces search space and noise.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (static demonstration pool; no episodic/skill/workflow memory written or evolved).
- **write back**: False -- the system does not store new experiences/cases during deployment; the demonstration pool and trained retrievers are fixed after offline training.
- **online growth**: False -- the retrievable store is frozen after offline K-means partitioning and per-expert scorer training; it does not grow at test time.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back; memory is static).
- **failure experience usage**: No persistent storage of failures. During offline training, contrastive learning uses negatives including a hard demonstration (lowest few-shot score) and hard negatives from other batch samples, but these are training-time negatives, not a stored failure memory.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A -- no memory store is mutated; retrievers are trained once offline (append-only training data per epoch into per-expert D_train, but no evolving deployed memory).
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partially: per-expert retrievers are LEARNED dense scorers trained via contrastive learning on LLM-feedback (not RL); expert assignment is fixed K-means + cosine-centroid routing. It is a learned-selection method rather than a fixed similarity-only top-k, but not an RL/value-based policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A / single-model: trained retrievers are shown to TRANSFER across LLMs (trained on GPT-Neo, applied to GPT2-XL, LLaMA-7B, GPT3.5), but this is model transferability, not shared multi-agent memory.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> 12 NLP datasets. Classification: SST-5 (sentiment), MRPC (paraphrase), MNLI & QNLI (NLI), CMSQA/CommonsenseQA & HellaSwag (commonsense reasoning). Generation: WebQs (open-domain QA), GeoQuery & NL2Bash (code generation), Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow (semantic parsing). Compositional splits: GeoQuery (Standard/Template/TMCD/Length) and SMCalFlow-CS (S non-compositional / C cross-domain).
- **benchmark family**: QA (WebQs, CMSQA, HellaSwag) + classification/NLI (SST-5, MRPC, MNLI, QNLI) + code/semantic-parsing generation (GeoQuery, NL2Bash, Break, MTOP, SMCalFlow). Not in the agent/web/embodied/tool/memory families; this is an ICL demonstration-retrieval benchmark suite (following CEIL).
- **baselines**: Learning-free: Random, TopK-BM25, TopK-Contriever (TopK-C), TopK-SimCSE (TopK-S), TopK-BERT. Learning-based: EPR (Rubin et al. 2022), CEIL (Ye et al. 2023, the prior SOTA). Ablations: MoD w/o E (no mixture-of-experts) and MoD w/o C (no expert-wise/coordinate-descent training).
- **key metrics**: Accuracy for classification tasks; Exact Match (EM) for generation tasks except Break which uses LF-EM (semantic-equivalence-aware EM). Reported as per-dataset scores plus a 12-dataset average and absolute gain (Delta) over CEIL.
- **headline result**: MoD reaches 58.63 average across the 12 datasets vs 56.76 for the prior SOTA CEIL, a +1.87 absolute average gain (GPT-Neo 2.7B). Largest single-task gain +6.06 on CMSQA (43.24 vs 37.18). On compositional GeoQuery-Standard, 77.38 vs 73.21 CEIL (+4.17).
- **ablations**:
> Two key components ablated on SST-5, CMSQA, GeoQuery, MTOP: (1) MoD w/o E removes the mixture-of-experts design -> significant drop across all datasets, especially classification (SST-5, CMSQA), showing experts are critical for retrieving diverse/complex demonstrations; (2) MoD w/o C removes expert-wise (coordinate-descent-inspired) training -> moderate drop, showing its role in optimization. Additional studies: reduction of #ICL demonstrations (Fig.2) and cross-LLM transfer robustness (Table 4: retrievers trained on GPT-Neo / LLaMA-7B transferred to GPT2-XL, LLaMA-7B, GPT3.5).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No -- only end-to-end task metrics (accuracy / EM / LF-EM) are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG). Selection quality is judged solely through downstream ICL task performance.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Outcome-only: final ICL prediction accuracy / EM. No intermediate process/faithfulness metrics.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> L (number of in-context demonstrations) set to 50, then truncated when combined length exceeds the LLM's max context per task; average #demos per task ranges ~22-50 (e.g., SMCalFlow 22, NL2Bash 43, SST-5/MNLI/CMSQA/HellaSwag/WebQs/GeoQuery 50). Per-expert counts are budget-allocated by quota |S_i| = floor(h(C_i, x_test) * L). Reduction-of-demonstrations study (Sec 4.4) varies the count.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (not a new benchmark; reuses CEIL/EPR datasets). Compositional splits (GeoQuery Template/TMCD/Length, SMCalFlow-CS S/C) are processed by CEIL [57] to require precise multi-demonstration retrieval.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Mixture of Experts (Jacobs et al. 1991; Shazeer et al. 2017); coordinate descent (Wright); EPR (Rubin et al. 2022, contrastive demonstration scorer with LM feedback) and CEIL (Ye et al. 2023, set-level demonstration selection / DPP, the immediate SOTA predecessor extended here); Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) embeddings; learning-based ICL retrieval line including UDR (Li et al. 2023).
- **contrasts with**:
> Contrasts with singleton scorers EPR/UDR (ignore demonstration interactions) and with CEIL (which narrows candidates via a K-NN retriever before set selection, risking suboptimal sets due to insufficient exploration and exponential search space). Also contrasts with learning-free TopK methods (BM25, Contriever, SimCSE, BERT) that ignore LLM feedback. MoD instead partitions the whole pool into experts (covering dissimilar-but-useful demos) and uses expert-wise training to model set interaction without exhaustive search.
- **lineage**:
> Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval). Sits in the learning-based demonstration-retrieval lineage EPR -> UDR -> CEIL -> MoD, advancing from singleton/DPP set selection to a mixture-of-experts partition with coordinate-descent-inspired set-aware training for large/noisy demonstration pools.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- cost_efficiency_tradeoff

<a id="item-reticl"></a>
### 13. RetICL / Learning to Retrieve Iteratively for In-Context Learning (a.k.a. IterR / iterative retrieval)

2024  ·  EMNLP 2024  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14739)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: EMNLP 2024 (Main Conference, pages 7156-7168); Outstanding Paper. Also arXiv:2406.14739.
- **authors affiliation**:
> Yunmo Chen (Johns Hopkins University; work done while interning at Microsoft), Tongfei Chen, Harsh Jhamtani, Patrick Xia, Richard Shin (Google; while at Microsoft), Jason Eisner, Benjamin Van Durme. Primary affiliation: Microsoft (Microsoft Semantic Machines), with Johns Hopkins University.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.14739

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: In-context learning for few-shot semantic parsing / program synthesis (code-generation-like structured-output tasks). The method is framed as a general ICL exemplar-retrieval framework but instantiated and evaluated on semantic parsing.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline-trained, test-time-deployed exemplar retriever for in-context learning. Given a query and a fixed labeled training set D of (input, output) exemplars, the retriever must compose an ordered set of K=10 ICL exemplars to maximize the inference LLM's probability of producing the correct program. Single-agent (a retriever interacting with a frozen LLM treated as the environment). Supervision: reference target parses are available; the LLM provides token-likelihood feedback used as reward. Training is via RL (PPO) with the LLM as a simulator/environment; no human labels of exemplar quality are used.
- **what is retrieved**: demos / ICL exemplars (input-output pairs, i.e. natural-language query paired with its target semantic-parse / program) drawn from the training set.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: retrieval targets the fixed labeled training set D (a static pool of exemplars). The store does not grow during deployment.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Completeness-oriented portfolio composition rather than fixed independent top-k ranking. The paper frames optimal exemplar-set selection as an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem (Eq. 1) and learns an approximation that models interactions among selected exemplars to build a 'portfolio'; however the final size is still a fixed K (k=10 in main experiments), so it is a fixed-size set whose composition (not just per-item similarity) is optimized.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning; only the Retrieve phase is present in a CBR sense - exemplars are reused verbatim as ICL demonstrations with no Revise/Retain).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False - the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is framed as iterative retrieval / policy optimization (MDP/RL).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: single demonstration (one ICL exemplar = a (query, target-parse) pair) retrieved per step; the full retrieved object is a fixed-length ordered sequence of K=10 such exemplars.
- **index source**: Static corpus: the retrievable store is the fixed training set D, built offline. Exemplar embeddings are precomputed and indexed (FAISS / maximum inner product search). No online/test-time growth.
- **index structure topology**: Flat dense vector index over exemplar encodings (Contriever/EPR embeddings) searched by maximum inner product search (MIPS) via FAISS. No graph or hierarchy.
- **retriever type**: Learned, stateful dense retriever: an off-the-shelf dense encoder (Contriever, optionally EPR-finetuned, frozen) augmented with a learned state-transition/policy module (GRU + query-projection Q + value head). Per-step retrieval is dense MIPS; the policy is RL-trained.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> RL / learned policy trained with LM feedback. Specifically PPO (proximal policy optimization) with Generalized Advantage Estimation; the reward is derived from the inference LLM's completion probability of the reference output (the marginal increase in P_LM(y*|x; exemplars) contributed by each appended exemplar). This is downstream-task-effectiveness / LM-feedback signal rather than contrastive similarity labels.
- **query construction**:
> The query vector at each step is computed by a learned projection Q(s_i) of the current retrieval state s_i (a fixed-length state vector that summarizes previously selected exemplars). Initial state s_0 is a learned parameter; the state is updated by a GRU consuming the encoding of the just-retrieved exemplar. Thus the query is state-conditioned (history-aware) rather than a static encoding of the raw input.
- **query granularity**: step/state-level: a new query vector is constructed at each of the K retrieval steps, conditioned on the evolving retrieval state (the sequence of already-selected exemplars). Task-level input also seeds the process, but selection is iterative/step-conditioned.
- **when to retrieve**: iterative: retrieval is performed in a fixed sequence of K steps (one exemplar appended per step) until K exemplars are assembled; it is not one-shot top-k, nor uncertainty-triggered/active.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: exactly one exemplar is retrieved per step for a predetermined number of steps (K=10 in main experiments). There is no learned/confidence-based trigger deciding whether to retrieve; the iteration count is fixed by the target exemplar budget.
- **reranking**:
> No explicit separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder). Instead, the stateful policy implicitly re-scores candidates at each step via the state-conditioned query; during training a stratified sampling over the top-B buffer constructs the action distribution, but this is for exploration, not a reranking module at inference.
- **retrieved context refinement**: none - retrieved exemplars are inserted into the prompt verbatim via a fixed template; no decomposition, distillation, compression, or distractor filtering is applied to retrieved content.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools/skills retrieved; exemplars are raw (query, parse) pairs encoded by the text embedder).
- **index content separation**: N/A - exemplars are both indexed (by embedding) and used directly as content; no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content separation.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no tools/APIs; static exemplar store).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no inter-tool dependencies modeled).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> prompt augmentation: the ordered sequence of K retrieved exemplars is formatted into an ICL prompt via a predefined template and fed to the inference LLM for generation. During training, the same composition also produces the LM-likelihood reward signal that trains the retrieval policy. Exemplars are used as verbatim demonstrations (no adaptation).
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-generate with iterative exemplar composition inside a learned policy/search loop: the iterative retriever builds the exemplar portfolio step-by-step (an MDP rollout) before the LLM produces the final output. It is not interleaved with the LLM's own reasoning steps; rather the LLM is used as the environment/simulator that scores partial exemplar sets during training. At inference, one full exemplar set is composed, then a single LLM generation produces the program.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-answer: retrieval (the K-step exemplar composition) happens before a single LLM answer generation; retrieval is not woven into per-CoT-step or per-token LLM reasoning. (The iterative steps are over exemplar selection, not over the LLM's reasoning.)
- **adaptation mechanism**: verbatim ICL exemplar - retrieved cases/exemplars are used as-is in the prompt; there is no LLM-prompted or feedback-driven revision of the retrieved exemplars themselves.
- **retrieved item representation**: raw exemplar (a natural-language query plus its raw target semantic parse / program), injected as a verbatim ICL demonstration in the prompt; no distillation into strategy/guideline form.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: single demonstration (raw input-output exemplar). No abstraction into distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retriever-aware/effectiveness-driven training: because the policy is trained with PPO using LM-likelihood reward, it learns to select exemplars that actually raise the probability of the correct output (and to avoid low-contribution exemplars), implicitly guarding against unhelpful retrievals; stratified sampling balances exploration vs exploitation during training. No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none - no episodic/skill/workflow memory is maintained; the only persistent store is the static training set. (The within-rollout 'state' vector is a transient MDP state, not a growing memory.)
- **write back**: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a persistent memory at deployment. (During training, rollout trajectories are placed in a replay buffer for experience replay, but this is a training mechanism, not deployed memory write-back.)
- **online growth**: False - the retrievable store (training set D) is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow at test time.
- **write back trigger**: never (at deployment). The retrievable exemplar store is fixed; nothing is written back during or after inference. (Training uses a transient replay buffer of rollouts only.)
- **failure experience usage**: No persistent storage of failed experiences. During RL training, both high- and low-reward trajectories are sampled and used to estimate advantages (so negative/low-reward rollouts inform the policy update via PPO), but failures are not stored as retrievable corrective cases.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A / none - no deployed memory to mutate (store is static; append-only replay buffer exists only during training and is not a persistent memory).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: True - case/exemplar selection IS a learned RL-optimized policy (MDP formulation; PPO with GAE; state-value head), explicitly contrasted against fixed similarity-based top-k retrieval.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> No cross-agent sharing within a single run. However, the trained retriever generalizes across different inference LLMs (trained with Llama-2-7b but used with Llama-2-13b/70b, CodeLlama-70b-Instruct, and Mistral-7b), i.e. a degree of cross-model transfer of the learned retrieval policy.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: SMCalFlow (Andreas et al., 2020), TreeDST (Cheng et al., 2020), and MTOP (English portion only; Li et al., 2021), following the BenchClamp benchmark (Roy et al., 2023).
- **benchmark family**: Semantic parsing / structured program synthesis (code-generation-like). Not in the standard QA/web/embodied/tool families; closest normalized grouping is 'semantic parsing / code-structured-output' under the ICL demonstration-retrieval setting.
- **baselines**:
> BM25; Contriever (off-the-shelf dense retriever); EPR (Efficient Prompt Retrieval, Rubin et al. 2022, contrastively trained with scoring-LM labels; re-implemented with Contriever base for fair comparison); CEIL (Compositional Exemplars for In-context Learning, Ye et al. 2023, uses Determinantal Point Processes to model input-exemplar interaction). Non-iterative baselines are adapted by taking top-k with original ranks.
- **key metrics**:
> Exact Match at top-k (EM@1, EM@2, EM@3) reflecting beam-search decoding; and SMatch precision/recall/F1 (for the deeply-nested SMCalFlow and TreeDST, to credit correct substructures). All runs use k=10 exemplars, averaged over 3 inference runs; improvements over Contriever/EPR/CEIL are significant (paired t-test, p<0.05).
- **headline result**:
> IterR outperforms all baselines on all three datasets across all metrics. On SMCalFlow with Llama-2-7b: EM@1 = 54.1 (vs CEIL 51.1, EPR 48.5, Contriever 44.0) and SMatch-F = 77.3 (vs CEIL 75.1); on TreeDST EM@1 = 58.2 and SMatch-F = 85.7; on MTOP EM@1 = 63.9 / EM@3 = 71.0. Achieved by adding only ~4M parameters (110M -> 114M) to a frozen off-the-shelf dense retriever.
- **ablations**:
> Table 2 (SMCalFlow, Llama-2-7b): (1) Removing EPR initialization (train from Contriever instead) drops EM@1 from 54.1 to 45.1 and SMatch-F from 77.3 to 68.8 - EPR init gives ~6% gain vs ~1% gain from RL alone, showing EPR domain-specific finetuning + restructured action space drives much of the gain. (2) Replacing GRU state transition with a Transformer decoder drops EM@1 to 50.1 / SMatch-F 75.1 and causes unstable training (warmup led to a trivial near-fixed trajectory). (3) Removing stratified sampling (sampling directly from buffer) drops EM@1 to 52.3 / SMatch-F 75.7, confirming stratified sampling's exploration benefit. Additional analyses: generalization across inference LLMs (Figure 5) and performance vs number of exemplars 1..10 (Figure 6, IterR matches baselines with fewer exemplars).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No - the paper reports only end-to-end downstream ICL task metrics (EM@k, SMatch) of the inference LLM. It does not report standalone intrinsic retrieval metrics (e.g. Recall@k/nDCG) decoupled from task performance.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome-focused (final program EM and SMatch F1). SMatch adds partial-structure credit (substructure correctness), giving a finer-grained outcome signal; the number-of-exemplars analysis offers some process insight, but there is no separate step-wise retrieval-accuracy evaluation.
- **context budget and selection count**: Fixed-k: K=10 exemplars per prompt in the main experiments; selection-count analysis sweeps k in {1,...,10}. The k exemplars are composed sequentially by the policy (not reranked-then-truncated). No explicit token budget cap stated beyond the fixed exemplar count.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey/taxonomy paper).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> EPR (Rubin et al., 2022, used as encoder initialization and baseline); Contriever (Izacard et al., 2022, base dense encoder); CEIL (Ye et al., 2023, DPP-based exemplar selection baseline); PPO (Schulman et al., 2017) and GAE (Schulman et al., 2016) for RL; policy-as-retrieval formulation similar to Lu et al. (2023); reward design inspired by Shin et al. (2021), Shi et al. (2023), and Zhang et al. (2022) (LM-likelihood / contribution-based reward); BenchClamp (Roy et al., 2023) evaluation protocol.
- **contrasts with**:
> Off-the-shelf single-call similarity retrievers (BM25, Contriever) that rank items independently by semantic similarity; contrastively-trained exemplar retrievers (EPR); and set-selection methods modeling interactions non-iteratively (CEIL/DPP). Key contrast: IterR is a stateful, iterative, RL-trained policy that conditions each selection on previously chosen exemplars and on LLM feedback, rather than a static top-k or one-shot set selector.
- **lineage**:
> Group A: ICL demonstration retrieval. Positioned in the lineage of learned exemplar/demonstration retrieval for in-context learning (Contriever -> EPR -> CEIL), advancing it from one-shot similarity/set selection to a stateful iterative retrieval policy trained by RL with LLM feedback (a learned-policy / portfolio-composition view of demonstration retrieval).

### 14. TopK + ConE (Revisiting Demonstration Selection Strategies in In-Context Learning)

2024  ·  ACL 2024  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12087)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: ACL 2024 (Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers, pp. 9090-9101)
- **authors affiliation**:
> Keqin Peng (Beihang University), Liang Ding (The University of Sydney), Yancheng Yuan (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Xuebo Liu (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Min Zhang (Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen), Yuanxin Ouyang (Beihang University), Dacheng Tao (Nanyang Technological University). Corresponding authors: Liang Ding and Yancheng Yuan.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12087
- **code url**: https://github.com/Romainpkq/revisit_demon_selection_in_ICL

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: In-context learning (ICL) demonstration selection for NLP: natural language understanding (text classification, NLI) and natural language generation (machine translation).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-model, single-turn ICL with no additional training of the inference model or retriever. Given a labeled demonstration pool and a test input, the goal is to select k few-shot demonstrations that maximize ICL task performance. The authors first empirically show ICL demonstration choice is both data-dependent and model-dependent (it varies with the retrieval module and, critically, with the inference model), then propose a training-free, model-dependent selection-then-rerank recipe. Supervision: the demonstration pool has gold labels; no preference labels or RL training are used. The inference model itself scores candidates (self-scoring via its own likelihood/cross-entropy).
- **what is retrieved**: Demonstrations (labeled input-output examples / few-shot exemplars) drawn from a training-set demonstration pool.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: a fixed labeled demonstration pool (training set), e.g., SST-2/SST-5/CR/Subj/AGNews/MNLI/QNLI training data, or Flores-200 / WMT22 parallel data for translation. No agent-written growing memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k selection (k-shot, with k = 4 for GPT2-XL and k = 8 for other models). The contribution is a model-dependent reranking objective (minimize conditional entropy of the test input) layered on top of a fixed-size top-k retrieval, not a completeness-recovery or variable-size objective.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a CBR method; at most a single Retrieve phase, no Reuse/Revise/Retain in the CBR sense).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: false. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as ICL demonstration selection.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: Single demonstration (a complete input-output / problem-solution example). Demonstrations are individually scored and combined into a k-shot group.
- **index source**: Static corpus, offline-induced: the retrievable store is the fixed labeled training pool. No online/test-time growth; candidate scores are computed at test time per test sample but the store itself is frozen.
- **index structure topology**: Flat dense vector index for the TopK selection stage (sentence-transformer embeddings, nearest-neighbor search); no graph/hierarchical/cluster topology. The ConE reranking stage scores candidates directly with the inference model rather than via an index.
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid two-stage: (1) selection module = dense retriever (TopK / SBERT cosine nearest neighbors) by default, optionally BM25 or Random; (2) reranking module = LLM-as-scorer using the inference model's own conditional-entropy estimate (ConE). The proposed default is TopK (dense) + ConE.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None / off-the-shelf for the selection stage (pretrained sentence-transformer embeddings; no contrastive fine-tuning of the retriever). The ConE reranker is a training-free, model-dependent score (conditional entropy / cross-entropy estimated by the frozen inference model itself); no learning signal, no RL, no preference labels.
- **query construction**:
> Raw test input used as the query for the TopK selection stage (nearest neighbors in embedding space). For ConE reranking, each candidate demonstration group c is combined with the raw test input x to form a prompt, and the inference model's conditional entropy H_theta(x|c) = H_theta(x,c) - H_theta(c) is computed.
- **query granularity**: Task-level / per-test-sample one-shot retrieval (a single retrieval+rerank pass is done once for each test input before generating its answer); not step-level or trajectory-level.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot: a single retrieval (TopK selection) followed by a single rerank (ConE) is performed once per test sample before inference. No iterative or uncertainty-triggered re-retrieval.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per test sample (not conditioned on confidence, attention, or a learned router). The ConE score itself is an entropy/uncertainty signal but it is used for ranking, not for triggering when to retrieve.
- **reranking**:
> Yes. The core contribution is the ConE reranking stage: TopK retrieves 30 candidates, then candidates are ranked by the inference model's conditional entropy of the test input H_theta(x|c) (lower entropy = better understanding = higher rank). This is a model-dependent, self-scoring reranker (a likelihood/entropy-based reranker rather than a trained cross-encoder).
- **retrieved context refinement**: Rerank only: candidates from TopK are re-ranked by ConE; no decomposition, compression, distractor filtering, or distillation of the demonstration text.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools/skills; demonstrations are raw labeled examples indexed by sentence-transformer embeddings).
- **index content separation**: N/A (no lightweight-index-then-content separation; demonstrations are short examples retrieved and used directly).
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no tool index, no MCP/RapidAPI/function-calling protocol).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation: the selected k demonstrations are concatenated as few-shot exemplars in the inference model's prompt; the model then performs the task (classification label or translation) via standard ICL.
- **planning integration**: One-shot exemplars at inference time. There is no planning/acting/tree-search component; retrieval feeds a single-pass ICL prediction (retrieve-then-rerank-then-prompt). Not applicable to multi-step planning.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: retrieval and reranking happen once per test query, before producing the single final answer. No per-step or per-token interleaving.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved demonstrations are used verbatim as ICL exemplars).
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw demonstration (verbatim labeled input-output example) injected as a few-shot exemplar in the prompt; no distillation, abstraction, or latent encoding of the demonstration.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Single demonstration (raw labeled example); no distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, or skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Model-dependent self-scoring as an implicit relevance/quality evaluator: ConE selects demonstrations that most reduce the inference model's conditional entropy on the test input, favoring demonstrations the model can actually leverage. The authors also show the method reduces sensitivity to demonstration order (smaller variance than Random/TopK). No retriever-aware training or explicit distractor-filtering.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (a static labeled demonstration pool; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory).
- **write back**: false. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the demonstration pool is fixed and read-only.
- **online growth**: false. The retrievable store does not grow at deployment/test time; it is the frozen training pool.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back mechanism exists).
- **failure experience usage**: N/A. No failed/negative experiences are stored or retrieved; demonstrations are gold-labeled training examples (success-only by construction, but there is no experience-collection loop).
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no stored entries are mutated; the pool is static).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: false. Selection is fixed similarity top-k plus a training-free conditional-entropy rerank; no learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, no soft Q-learning, no preference training).
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A / single-model private use; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> NLU: SST-2, SST-5, CR, Subj, AGNews, MNLI, QNLI (7 classification/NLI tasks). NLG (machine translation): 4 language pairs extracted from Flores-200 (1012 examples per language; reported pairs include En<->X and non-English-centric Ru<=>De), plus WMT22 mixed-domain translation (e-commerce, news, social; including Zh=>En). Inference models: GPT2-XL (1.5B), Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and aligned chat models (Vicuna, LLaMA-chat, DeepSeek-chat). Retrieval embedding models for the analysis: all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-MiniLM-L12-v2, all-distilroberta-v1, all-mpnet-base-v2.
- **benchmark family**: QA/NLU text classification and NLI (SST-2/SST-5/CR/Subj/AGNews/MNLI/QNLI) + machine-translation generation (Flores-200, WMT22). Not a planning/web/embodied/tool/code/agent-memory benchmark family.
- **baselines**: Prompting (zero-shot, no demonstrations), Random, BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009), TopK (Liu et al. 2022, dense nearest-neighbor selection), and TopK + MDL (Wu et al. 2023b, select-then-rank by Minimum Description Length). TopK + MDL is the prior state-of-the-art comparison.
- **key metrics**:
> Accuracy for classification/NLI tasks; COMET (reference-based COMET-20 = wmt20-COMET-da and COMET-22 = wmt22-COMET-da) for translation, with comet-compare significance testing (p<0.05). Conditional entropy of the test input is used as an analysis metric to explain why methods work.
- **headline result**:
> On Llama2-7B across 7 NLU tasks, TopK + ConE (Ours) reaches 77.9 average accuracy, vs 76.7 for TopK+MDL (+1.2), 76.1 for TopK (+1.8), 75.0 for BM25 (+2.9), 71.2 for Random (+6.8), and 56.0 for Prompting (+21.9). Largest single-task gains over the previous best are Subj +4.6% and QNLI +1.9%.
- **ablations**:
> 1) ConE is complementary to any selection method: adding ConE to Random/BM25/TopK improves all of them (e.g., +7.5 on SST-2 with Random selection), motivating TopK+ConE as the default. 2) Number of in-context examples N swept 0->16: more demonstrations generally help but GPT2-XL degrades beyond its max length, so N=4 for GPT2-XL and N=8 for others; ConE consistently beats TopK across N. 3) Number of TopK candidates reranked by ConE: more candidates improve performance; default set to 30. 4) Model-scale sweep (GPT2-XL 1.5B to Llama2-13B): consistent gains, with GPT2-XL gaining +2.6% over TopK+MDL and +3.6% over TopK. 5) Order sensitivity: TopK+ConE has higher average and smaller variance than Random/TopK under demonstration-order shuffling. 6) Universality: prior methods (BM25/TopK/MDL) also reduce conditional entropy of test inputs, giving a unified explanation. 7) Works for instruction-tuned/RLHF chat models (Vicuna, LLaMA-chat, DeepSeek-chat) and mixed-domain translation pools.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k/nDCG). Evaluation is end-to-end task performance (accuracy / COMET). Conditional entropy of the test input is reported as an explanatory/analysis quantity rather than a decoupled retrieval-quality metric.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome metrics (final accuracy / COMET). The only process-level quantity analyzed is the conditional entropy of the test input (used to explain mechanism and order-robustness variance), not stepwise reasoning or retrieval-accuracy scoring.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> ConE adds inference-time cost: for each test sample, the inference model must score (forward-pass) 30 TopK candidates to compute conditional entropy, then run final inference. The TopK selection stage narrows the candidate pool to make this feasible (vs enumerating all combinations, which is intractable). The authors note this added inference budget may be unacceptable for extremely large LLMs and flag a more efficient understanding-measure as future work. No explicit latency/throughput numbers are reported.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k injection: k = 4 demonstrations for GPT2-XL (limited by max sequence length), k = 8 for Llama2-7B/13B and chat models. Candidate set = 30 (TopK retrieves 30, ConE reranks and selects the final k). Budget effectively capped by model max length (GPT2-XL degrades when forced to 8-shot).
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (uses existing public benchmarks; Flores-200 contributes 1012 examples per language pair). Not a benchmark-construction paper.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> TopK (Liu et al. 2022, KATE / k-nearest-neighbor dense demonstration retrieval); the select-then-rank framework and MDL reranking of Wu et al. (2023b); OpenICL toolkit (Wu et al. 2023a) for the codebase; Gonen et al. (2023) perplexity/familiarity insight (model performs better on prompts it is more familiar with) motivating the conditional-entropy conjecture; BM25 (Robertson et al. 2009).
- **contrasts with**:
> Purely data-dependent similarity heuristics (BM25, TopK) that ignore the inference model; TopK + MDL (Wu et al. 2023b) which reranks by Minimum Description Length rather than by the model's conditional entropy of the test input; Random and zero-shot Prompting. The key contrast is data-only vs data-and-model-dependent selection.
- **lineage**:
> Group A (ICL demonstration retrieval / selection). Sits in the demonstration-selection lineage from KATE/TopK (similarity-based) -> TopK+MDL (likelihood/MDL reranking) -> TopK+ConE (model-dependent conditional-entropy reranking), and explicitly offers a unified conditional-entropy explanation for prior similarity-based and likelihood-based selection methods.
