Each retrieved chunk is <=200 words and prepended as a 'Background:' field; predictions over k augmented prompts are computed in parallel (not concatenated), so each prompt holds one chunk plus the instruction, sidestepping a single long-context budget. LM-ft data is built with k-tilde=3 retrieved chunks per example (k-tilde+1 for self-contained RC tasks that also have a gold passage). Inference k is fixed and ablated (top-1/3/10), with k=10 strongest at 0-shot.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (uses existing benchmarks; constructs no new dataset). Notable resource scale: fine-tuning over 20 datasets (LM-ft set D_L) and a QA-focused retriever-ft set D_R (adds FreebaseQA, MS MARCO Q-A pairs); retrieval corpus = 399M text chunks (Wikipedia 2021 + 2017-2020 CommonCrawl), max 200 words each.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> REPLUG (Shi et al. 2023b) -- parallel in-context retrieval-augmentation, relevance-weighted output mixture, and the LM-Supervised Retrieval (LSR) objective that RA-DIT generalizes; In-Context RALM (Ram et al. 2023); DRAGON+ dense retriever (Lin et al. 2023) as retriever init; Llama (Touvron et al. 2023a) as the LM backbone; instruction-tuning / label-loss objective (Chung et al. 2022b; Iyer et al. 2022 OPT-IML); 'LMs easily distracted by irrelevant context' (Shi et al. 2023a) motivating distractor-robust LM-ft; FAISS / Atlas index (Izacard et al. 2022) and the Atlas Wikipedia corpus. Conceptually positioned among RALMs: REALM (Guu et al. 2020), RETRO (Borgeaud et al. 2022), Atlas (Izacard et al. 2022b), RAG (Lewis et al. 2020), FiD (Izacard & Grave 2021).
- **contrasts with**:
> REPLUG / In-Context RALM (off-the-shelf fusion of frozen LLM + general retriever) -- RA-DIT argues this is suboptimal because the LLM is not trained to use retrieved content; RA-DIT fine-tunes both. Atlas / REALM / RETRO (expensive end-to-end or continuous RALM pre-training) -- RA-DIT is lightweight fine-tuning that competes without pre-training. SAIL (Luo et al. 2023, most related) -- fine-tunes a 7B LM on retrieval-augmented instructions but concatenates passages in-context and uses non-differentiable BM25; RA-DIT instead uses parallel multi-passage augmentation, a learnable neural retriever, and dual optimization. Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2023) -- adaptive on-demand retrieval with reflection tokens, vs RA-DIT's fixed one-shot retrieval. InstructRetro / RETRO+IT (Wang et al. 2023) -- fine-tunes a cross-attention RETRO LM while freezing memory encoder, vs RA-DIT decoupling and tuning both LM and retriever in the in-context framework.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving). A lineage member of in-context retrieval-augmented LMs that adds lightweight fine-tuning: it extends REPLUG's parallel in-context augmentation and LSR by jointly (but decoupled) tuning the LLM (to use retrieved context and ignore distractors) and the retriever (to LLM preferences). Sits between off-the-shelf RALM fusion (REPLUG, In-Context RALM) and heavyweight pre-trained RALMs (Atlas, RETRO), and alongside concurrent retrieval-aware instruction-tuning / adaptive-RAG work (SAIL, Self-RAG, InstructRetro). Establishes 'dual instruction tuning' as a practical retrofitting recipe.

<a id="item-raft"></a>
### 32. RAFT - Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning (RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG)

2024  ·  COLM 2024  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10131)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: COLM 2024 (Conference on Language Modeling); originally arXiv:2403.10131 (cs.CL), submitted 15 Mar 2024, revised 5 Jun 2024
- **authors affiliation**: Tianjun Zhang, Shishir G. Patil, Naman Jain, Sheng Shen, Matei Zaharia, Ion Stoica, Joseph E. Gonzalez. All from the Department of Computer Science, UC Berkeley.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10131 (OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=rzQGHXNReU)
- **code url**: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla (RAFT code and demo open-sourced under the Gorilla project)
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Domain-specific open-book question answering / knowledge-intensive RAG. Covered domains: biomedical QA (PubMedQA), multi-hop Wikipedia QA (HotpotQA), open-domain QA (Natural Questions, TriviaQA), and code/API-call generation (Gorilla APIBench: HuggingFace, Torch Hub, TensorFlow Hub documentation).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-agent, supervised post-training (fine-tuning) recipe for the 'domain-specific open-book exam' setting where the test-time document collection / domain is known a priori. The model is trained on (question, retrieved documents -> chain-of-thought answer) tuples and at test time is run in a standard RAG setup with top-k retrieved documents. Supervision: question-answer pairs plus GPT-4-1106-generated chain-of-thought answers; golden vs distractor document labels are available during training data construction. Not interactive, no multi-agent, no test-time learning.
- **what is retrieved**: Documents (text passages / API documentation chunks). At training time these are partitioned into 'golden' documents (containing the answer) and 'distractor' documents (irrelevant); at test time they are top-k retriever outputs.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus (the fixed in-domain document collection / knowledge base, e.g. PubMed abstracts, Wikipedia, API docs). No agent-written growing memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k retrieval objective at test time (model evaluated with top-k retrieved documents, typically top-3). RAFT does not optimize the retriever or aim for completeness of a minimal set; instead it trains the reader/generator to be robust to a varying number of top-k documents and to ignore distractors, and it studies generalization across different k at train and test time.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; only a Retrieve-then-read pattern is realized, no Reuse/Revise/Retain of cases).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: false - The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is positioned as a retrieval-augmented fine-tuning recipe.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document (text passage / API documentation entry). 'Golden' documents contain the answer-relevant span; the model is trained to cite verbatim the right sequence from the relevant document.
- **index source**: Static, fixed in-domain corpus known a priori. Retrieval store is not induced online or grown at test time; training data is constructed offline by labeling golden vs distractor documents.
- **index structure topology**: Flat document corpus / flat vector index (standard RAG retrieval over the domain corpus). No graph or hierarchical organization is introduced by RAFT.
- **retriever learning signal**: none (off-the-shelf retriever; RAFT does not train the retriever). The learning signal is applied only to the reader/generator LLM via supervised fine-tuning on golden+distractor contexts with CoT answers.
- **query construction**: Raw input question is used directly as the retrieval query at test time (no query decomposition, expansion, or rewriting in the base RAFT method).
- **query granularity**: Task-level (one query per input question, one-shot at the start of answering).
- **when to retrieve**: one-shot (single retrieval of top-k documents prepended to the prompt before generation; no iterative or active re-retrieval).
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule (always retrieve once per question, both at training-data construction and at test time). No confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger.
- **reranking**: None. No reranking stage is introduced; the model is trained directly to read top-k retrieved documents and ignore distractors.
- **retrieved context refinement**: Distractor handling via training (distractor-aware SFT) rather than post-retrieval filtering. The model learns to ignore distractor documents and to cite-then-reason; there is no separate compression/decompose/rerank stage at inference.
- **index content separation**: N/A - No progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content separation; full documents are placed directly in context.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A - Static document index; no live tool-store synchronization or MCP/RapidAPI integration. For Gorilla APIBench the model generates API calls but RAFT itself does not maintain a live tool index.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A - No modeling of inter-tool/inter-API dependencies.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation as a training signal: retrieved (golden + distractor) documents are concatenated with the question in the fine-tuning input, and the model is trained (standard SFT, supervised next-token) to produce a chain-of-thought answer that cites verbatim spans from the golden document. At inference, top-k retrieved documents are prepended to the prompt (standard RAG).
- **planning integration**: Retrieve-then-read (one-shot exemplar-free): top-k documents retrieved once and placed in context, then the model reasons (chain-of-thought) and answers. No tree search, MCTS, or hierarchical subtask planning.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer (single retrieval feeds a single chain-of-thought reasoning trace that produces one answer). No per-step or per-token re-retrieval.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (no case adaptation; the mechanism is supervised fine-tuning, not CBR-style case revision).
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw document text injected into the prompt context. The generated output is a free-text chain-of-thought ('##Reason: ... ##Answer: ...') that quotes verbatim the relevant span from the golden document as citation.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw document (verbatim passage / API doc). The injected retrieved unit is unabstracted source text; abstraction happens only in the model's generated CoT answer.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Distractor-aware supervised fine-tuning: training each example with one golden document mixed with distractor documents, plus including (1-P)% of examples with NO golden document (only distractors) to force the model to discern and ignore irrelevant content; combined with cite-then-reason CoT supervision. This trains the reader to be robust to irrelevant retrieved text and to a varying number of top-k documents.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). Knowledge is baked into model weights via fine-tuning on the static domain corpus.
- **write back**: false - The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into any external memory at deployment; learning is a one-time offline fine-tuning step.
- **online growth**: false - The retrievable store is the static in-domain corpus; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
- **write back trigger**: never - No write-back; the model is frozen after offline fine-tuning and the document store is fixed.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Distractor (negative/irrelevant) documents are used during training as negative context the model must learn to ignore, including (1-P)% of training examples that contain ONLY distractor documents and no golden document. There is no storage/retrieval of failed trajectories or corrective rules; negatives are static distractor docs, not recorded failures.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A - No stored memory entries to mutate; the only update is the one-time fine-tuning of model weights.
- **retrieval as learned policy**: false - Retrieval is a fixed similarity top-k from an off-the-shelf retriever; it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. RAFT learns the reader/generator, not a retrieval policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A - Single-model, single-agent setting; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: PubMedQA (biomedical QA), HotpotQA (multi-hop Wikipedia QA), Natural Questions (NQ), TriviaQA, and Gorilla APIBench: HuggingFace Hub, Torch Hub, and TensorFlow Hub API-call generation.
- **benchmark family**: QA (PubMedQA), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA), open-domain QA (NQ, TriviaQA), and tool/code (Gorilla APIBench API-call generation over HuggingFace/Torch Hub/TensorFlow Hub documentation).
- **baselines**: LLaMA2-7B (0-shot prompting), LLaMA2-7B-chat + RAG, Domain-Specific Finetuning (DSF, 0-shot), DSF + RAG, and GPT-3.5 + RAG (provided as a stronger-model reference). Base model fine-tuned by RAFT is LLaMA2-7B.
- **key metrics**: Task accuracy / exact-match style scores per dataset (accuracy for PubMedQA/HotpotQA/NQ/TriviaQA; API-call correctness/accuracy for the Gorilla APIBench domains). No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are reported.
- **headline result**:
> RAFT (LLaMA2-7B) achieves 73.30 on PubMed, 35.28 on HotpotQA, 74.00 on HuggingFace, 84.95 on Torch Hub, and 86.86 on TensorFlow, consistently outperforming DSF, DSF+RAG, LLaMA2-7B+RAG, and even GPT-3.5+RAG (71.60/41.5/29.08/60.21/65.59). Gains over the base LLaMA-2 instruction-tuned model are as large as +35.25% on HotpotQA and +76.35% on Torch Hub; vs DSF, +30.87% on HotpotQA and +31.41% on HuggingFace.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Effect of Chain-of-Thought (Table 2): RAFT with CoT vs without CoT yields +9.66% on HotpotQA (25.62 -> 35.28) and +14.93% on HuggingFace (59.07 -> 74.00), showing CoT with citations prevents overfitting and improves accuracy. (2) Fraction P% of training data containing the golden document (Sec 4.4, Fig 5 on NQ/TQA/HotpotQA): training with some examples lacking the golden context helps; optimal P% varies across datasets (around 40%/60%/100%), and overall ~80% golden inclusion is recommended (training setup: 1 golden + 4 distractors). (3) Number of distractor documents at train time and robustness to varying number of test-time documents (Sec 5, Fig 6 on NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA): training with distractors (best at D*+3D for NQ, D*+1D for HotpotQA) beats training with only golden documents and makes the model robust to varying test-time top-k.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No - Only end-to-end task metrics are reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT reported separately because RAFT is retriever-agnostic and focuses on the reader.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome (final answer accuracy / API-call correctness). Reasoning/citation quality is examined qualitatively (Sec 4.3 case study showing RAFT cites correct source vs DSF error) and indirectly via the CoT ablation, but no quantitative process-level metric is reported.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k. Training uses 1 golden + 4 distractor documents (k=5) per example; test-time evaluation typically uses top-3 retrieved documents. The Top-K generalization study (Sec 5) varies the number of train-time distractors and test-time documents but the default is a fixed small k.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A - Not a survey.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Supervised fine-tuning / instruction tuning of LLMs (LLaMA-2); standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020); chain-of-thought reasoning; the Gorilla / APIBench line of work (Patil et al. 2023) for the code/API-call evaluation. Conceptually related to fine-tuning-for-RAG works (RA-DIT - Lin et al. 2023a, Atlas - Izacard et al. 2023, RETRO - Borgeaud et al. 2022).
- **contrasts with**:
> Standard RAG-on-a-general-model (no fine-tuning), domain-specific fine-tuning without context (DSF) and DSF+RAG, and prior fine-tuning-for-RAG methods (RA-DIT, etc.). Key contrast: prior fine-tuning-for-RAG works assume test-time domain/documents can differ from training; RAFT studies the opposite in-domain setting where train and test share the same document collection, and it explicitly trains with distractor documents (open-book-with-distractors) plus cite-then-reason CoT, unlike closed-book SFT or vanilla RAG.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving): a retrieval-augmented fine-tuning / training-recipe method that hardens the reader LLM for static-corpus, in-domain open-book RAG. Sits in the 'finetuning-for-RAG / noise-robust reader' lineage (alongside RA-DIT, Self-RAG) as opposed to experience/memory-based agent retrieval; emphasizes distractor robustness and cite-then-reason CoT over standard top-k RAG prompting.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- benchmark_construction_and_size
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- retriever_type
- tool_document_engineering

<a id="item-rat"></a>
### 33. RAT - Retrieval Augmented Thoughts (Retrieval Augmented Thoughts Elicit Context-Aware Reasoning in Long-Horizon Generation)

2024  ·  arXiv 2403.05313  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05313)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **authors affiliation**:
> Zihao Wang (Peking University), Anji Liu (University of California, Los Angeles / UCLA), Haowei Lin (Peking University), Jiaqi Li (Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence / BIGAI), Xiaojian Ma (Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence / BIGAI), Yitao Liang (Peking University, corresponding author). Affiliated with Team CraftJarvis.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05313
- **code url**:
> https://github.com/CraftJarvis/RAT (official implementation by Team CraftJarvis; Python ~50.3% + Jupyter Notebook ~49.7%; ~248 stars, 27 forks as of mid-2025; includes creative.ipynb and a Gradio demo app; requires OPENAI_API_KEY and GOOGLE_API_KEY for Google Search; last commit Apr 2024; no LICENSE file and no releases observed). HuggingFace demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/jeasinema/RAT.
- **maintained repo url**: N/A (single-paper repo, last pushed Apr 2024; not a continuously-updated leaderboard or paper list).

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Long-horizon generation/reasoning with LLMs across four task families: code generation, mathematical reasoning, creative writing (open-ended text generation), and embodied task planning (Minecraft). Framed as a zero-shot prompting strategy synergizing chain-of-thought (CoT) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-model, inference-time (test-time) prompting setting with frozen black-box / open LLMs (GPT-3.5/gpt-3.5-turbo, GPT-4/gpt-4, and CodeLlama-7b). No fine-tuning of the LM or the retriever; off-the-shelf embedding-based retrieval (OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002) over a static corpus, or live Google search for open-web tasks. Single agent, no multi-agent interaction. All experiments are conducted zero-shot (0-demonstration) with the simplest possible prompts and no benchmark examples used as in-context demonstrations. The core problem: long-horizon generation suffers from hallucination and accumulated errors; the method addresses (1) WHAT relevant information to retrieve for complex multi-step reasoning and (2) HOW to correct reasoning steps with retrieved factual information, by iteratively revising each CoT thought step with RAG after an initial zero-shot CoT is generated.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Documents / passages providing factual knowledge to ground and correct each reasoning (thought) step. Sources vary by task: code snippets/notebooks from the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset (code + math), Minecraft Wiki (minecraft.wiki) and DigMinecraft (www.digminecraft.com) pages (embodied planning), and live Google web search results (creative writing). Not demonstrations, tools, cases, or agent experiences.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> STATIC external corpus / live web (not a growing agent memory). For code and mathematical reasoning, a fixed external vector library built from the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset. For embodied planning, fixed external knowledge from the Minecraft Wiki and DigMinecraft websites. For creative writing, the live open web via Google search. There is no episodic/growing memory the agent writes back to; retrieval reads from external knowledge bases or the Internet.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Top-k document retrieval per step (similarity-style ranking via cosine similarity over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings; for creative writing, top web-search results from Google). The objective is not a formal minimal-complete-set recovery nor a precision-driven variable-size recommendation; however, a stated motivation is that progressive, step-conditioned retrieval ensures more complete coverage of intermediate facts/items (e.g., all intermediary items in a Minecraft plan) than a single task-level query, contrasting classical RAG which over-focuses on the final-target query.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve] only. RAT retrieves documents and uses them to revise a draft thought, but there is no case library, no stored problem-solution cases, and no Retain step. Not a CBR method. (The 'Revise' it performs is revision of the LLM's own draft thoughts with retrieved documents, not revision/adaptation of a retrieved past case.)
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False: RAT does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is positioned as a synergy of chain-of-thought prompting and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Document / passage (a retrieved document or web-page snippet R_i). The iteration/decision unit of generation is the thought step T_i (a CoT step: e.g., a block of pseudo-code with comments, an article outline section, or a sub-goal in an embodied plan), but the retrieved unit itself is a document/passage.
- **index source**:
> Static corpus, offline-induced for code and math (a vector index over the codeparrot/github-jupyter dataset using text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings) and for embodied planning (Minecraft Wiki + DigMinecraft pages); live web index for creative writing (Google search engine). No online/test-time growth of the store driven by the agent. A contamination-avoidance pre-processing step (following Guo et al. 2024) is applied to the code library to remove exact benchmark solutions.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat vector index (semantic embeddings + cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor retrieval over the codeparrot/github-jupyter library) for code/math; a black-box web-search backend (Google) for creative writing; document collections from the Minecraft Wiki / DigMinecraft websites for embodied planning. No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology is used for organizing the store.
- **retriever type**:
> Dense embedding-based retriever (cosine similarity over OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings; the preliminary also mentions Sentence-BERT as a possible embedder) for corpus-backed tasks; the Google search engine (black-box web-search API) for open-web creative writing. The ToQuery(.) operator can be a text encoder or an LLM that translates the prompt + current/past thoughts into a query. Off-the-shelf; not trained.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None (off-the-shelf): neither the embedding model (text-embedding-ada-002) nor the Google search engine is trained or fine-tuned. RAT's novelty is in query construction (using evolving reasoning thoughts as queries) and in WHEN/WHAT to revise, not in learning a retriever. There is no contrastive, LM-feedback, preference, or RL signal applied to the retriever.
- **query construction**:
> Reasoning/draft-conditioned query. After an initial zero-shot CoT T = {T_i} is generated, for each step i the query Q_i = ToQuery(I, T_1, ..., T_i) is formed from the task prompt I plus the current and past thought steps; ToQuery(.) is either a text encoder or an LLM that produces a retrieval query. The query thus evolves as reasoning proceeds (autoregressive query refinement), and previously revised thoughts T*_1..T*_{i-1} condition the revision. The motivation: hallucinations often occur only in details (e.g., a wrong date), which still let the search engine find the relevant topic; the draft answer is a better retrieval cue than the bare task prompt.
- **query granularity**:
> Step-level (per CoT thought step). A distinct query is constructed for each thought step T_i conditioned on the task prompt and all prior thoughts, rather than one task-level query at t=0. This is contrasted in ablations with the 'non-causal' variant (a single query from the initial reasoning to retrieve everything at once) and with CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query).
- **when to retrieve**:
> Iterative (fixed schedule): after generating the initial zero-shot CoT, RAT retrieves once per thought step and revises each step one by one in causal order (T*_1, then T*_2 conditioned on T*_1, ...). Retrieval is not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router-gated; it occurs at every thought step on a fixed per-step schedule.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule (per-thought-step). Retrieval is triggered deterministically for each step of the initial CoT during the revision pass; there is no token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or explicit agent-initiated request signal deciding when to retrieve.
- **reranking**: No dedicated reranking stage. Documents are retrieved by cosine-similarity ranking (or returned by Google search) and the top-ranked k are used directly; no cross-encoder, hierarchy-aware, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker is described.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Query-side / generation-side refinement rather than document distillation. The key processing is (a) using evolving, step-conditioned reasoning thoughts as the retrieval query (iterative query refinement) and (b) using retrieved content to revise/correct the current draft thought step rather than merely summarizing retrieved content (contrasted with classical RAG which 'tends to summarize content retrieved from searches'). No explicit decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, distractor filtering, or compression of retrieved passages is described.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools/skills; retrieved items are raw documents/passages/web results, not engineered tool descriptions).
- **index content separation**: N/A / No: retrieved documents are used directly in the prompt; there is no lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure separation.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no tool index/protocol). Retrieval uses a static embedding index over codeparrot/github-jupyter, fixed Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft pages, and the live Google search API; no MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling tool integration with CRUD auto-sync.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no tools are retrieved; RAT retrieves documents/passages, so no inter-tool dependency modeling, dependency graph, or bipartite KG is applicable).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation for iterative revision. Retrieved documents R_i are prepended to the prompt and the LLM revises the current draft thought step: T* <- p_theta(. | I, T*, R_i), where T* accumulates the already-revised prior steps. The revised CoT is then used to produce the final response progressively (step-by-step). No fine-tuning; pure in-context conditioning. Retrieval is used to correct/ground reasoning steps, not to inject demonstrations or skills.
- **planning integration**:
> Generate-then-retrieve-then-revise, per-step interleaved. The pipeline is: (1) zero-shot CoT generates an initial draft chain of thoughts T_1..T_n; (2) RAT iterates over steps in causal order, retrieving with a query built from the prompt + current/past thoughts and revising each step T_i -> T*_i conditioned on the already-revised prefix; (3) the response is produced progressively following the revised CoT. No explicit MCTS/tree search; CoT is the reasoning structure (the paper notes ToT-style structures as future work). For embodied planning, the 'plan' is the CoT (a list of sub-goals) that is iteratively revised.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-CoT-step: retrieval and revision are interleaved at the granularity of each chain-of-thought step (e.g., one pseudo-code block, one outline section, one sub-goal). Not per-token, per-sentence, per-tool-call, or per-answer.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not a CBR method; no case adaptation). The analogous operation is execution-/knowledge-free LLM-prompted revision: the LLM rewrites its own draft thought step conditioned on freshly retrieved documents and the revised prefix.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Raw retrieved document/passage text (code snippets/notebooks, Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft page content, or Google search result content) prepended to the prompt as factual context. No distilled strategy, free-text workflow, executable skill, structured note, or latent representation; the injected items are raw documents and the output is the revised free-text/code thought step.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw document/passage (un-distilled factual text/code retrieved from the corpus or web). Not a distilled strategy/insight, state-aware guideline/rule, reusable workflow, procedural skill, demonstration, or hint.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Causal step-by-step revision is the main robustness mechanism: revising each step one-by-one (rather than revising the whole CoT at once) avoids introducing errors at otherwise-correct steps; an ablation (causal vs non-causal) confirms the causal/iterative approach is more reliable. Step-conditioned query refinement also reduces irrelevant retrieval by targeting intermediate, easier-to-retrieve facts. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator/self-reflection, reason-in-documents refinement, or distractor-aware SFT. The paper explicitly notes (Limitations) that performance still relies on the quality of the external knowledge base and that an inferior/irrelevant KB can yield unhelpful retrieved content.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (no episodic / skill-library / workflow / procedural / graph / latent agent memory). The external corpus/web is a static knowledge source, not a written-to agent memory).
- **write back**: False: RAT does not store new experiences, cases, or skills into any memory; it only reads from a static external corpus or the live web during inference.
- **online growth**: No: the retrievable store (codeparrot/github-jupyter index, Minecraft Wiki/DigMinecraft pages, Google web) does not grow as a function of the system's own generation; it is a fixed/external knowledge source.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back; no memory is maintained or updated).
- **failure experience usage**: N/A / none: no storage or retrieval of past failed experiences. The method does correct hallucinations in the current draft (a within-episode self-correction using retrieved facts), but nothing is persisted as failure memory.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate; effectively append-only-none).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No: retrieval and per-step triggering follow a fixed schedule with off-the-shelf similarity top-k (or Google search); not an RL-/value-trained policy and not an M-MDP/soft-Q-learning case-selection policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No: single-model, single private retrieval pipeline; no memory/experience shared across agents or heterogeneous frameworks.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> Code generation: HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+. Mathematical reasoning: GSM8K and GSM-HARD (GSMHard). Creative writing: open-ended tasks including survey/summarization (e.g., the 'summarize the American Civil War according to a timeline' case), evaluated by human Elo/TrueSkill win-rate. Embodied planning: 100 Minecraft tasks (ranging from simple objectives to challenging diamond objectives) evaluated through MC-TextWorld (Lin et al. 2023).
- **benchmark family**:
> code (HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+) + math/QA-style (GSM8K, GSM-HARD) + open-ended creative writing (custom, human-rated) + embodied (Minecraft via MC-TextWorld). Spans the code and embodied (Minecraft) families plus math reasoning and open-ended generation; not the standard web/tool/memory-agent benchmark families.
- **baselines**:
> DIRECT (the base LLM answering directly, no retrieval/CoT); zero-shot CoT (Kojima et al. 2022, 'let's think step by step'); RAG with n retrieved examples in single-shot (RAG-1 shot) and multi-shot (RAG-5 shot) configurations (Lewis et al. 2020). All baselines use the same base model per setting and no benchmark examples as demonstrations. Ablation baselines additionally include RAG-1 (question-as-query) and CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query).
- **key metrics**:
> Code generation: pass@k (pass@1, pass@5). Mathematical reasoning: accuracy (per-question, aligned with GSM8K). Embodied planning: plan execution success rate in MC-TextWorld (executability) and human Elo/TrueSkill rating (plausibility). Creative writing: human Elo evaluation -> TrueSkill rating score (Herbrich et al. 2006) and win rate. Reported relative improvements vs DIRECT are also a headline summary metric.
- **headline result**:
> Relative average improvements of RAT over DIRECT across base models/tasks: +13.63% on code generation, +16.96% on mathematical reasoning, +19.2% on creative writing, and +42.78% on embodied (Minecraft) task planning. Concrete examples: on HumanEval (GPT-4 base) RAT reaches pass@1 69.33% / pass@5 88.40% (vs DIRECT 57.32% / 78.66%, i.e. +20.94% / +12.38% relative on pass@1/pass@5); on GSM8K RAT 71.36% vs DIRECT 65.85% (GPT-3.5); on Minecraft embodied planning (GPT-4) RAT achieves 76.67±8.02% executability and a 29.37 TrueSkill plausibility rating (+42.78% relative), the best among all methods.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Retrieval-strategy ablation (Table 3, HumanEval/HumanEval+): RAG-1 (question-as-query) < CoT+RAG (whole-CoT-as-query) < RAT (continuously-modified reasoning-thought parts as queries); RAT yields +8.7 percentage points pass@1 and +7.9 pp pass@5 over the RAG-1 baseline on HumanEval, showing iterative query refinement drives the gain. (2) Causal vs non-causal reasoning ablation (Table 4, CoT baseline): the causal method (iteratively interleaving reasoning and retrieval, revising step-by-step) beats CoT by +11.9 pp pass@1 and +4.6 pp pass@5 on HumanEval and outperforms the non-causal variant (use initial reasoning to retrieve all steps at once then generate final answer), establishing the value of sequential, causal reason-and-retrieve. (3) Cross-model generalization (Table 1): RAT improves CodeLlama-7b, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4; the largest gains are with GPT-4 (better in-context learning from retrieved text), while CodeLlama-7b shows degradation on MBPP+ (pass@1 -5.05% relative), attributed to weaker in-context learning of smaller models. (4) Case analyses on Minecraft (crafting-table materials) and the American Civil War timeline illustrate how step-wise retrieval recovers intermediary facts and corrects detail-level hallucinations that classical RAG misses.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No: only end-to-end task metrics (pass@k, accuracy, executability, TrueSkill/win-rate) are reported. No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are measured for the retriever.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mostly outcome metrics (final code pass@k, math accuracy, generation quality ratings). Some process-oriented signal is captured via embodied-planning executability (plan execution success rate, a step-wise feasibility proxy) and via qualitative case analyses of intermediate-step correctness/hallucination, but there is no formal scored reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A as a new-benchmark contribution; RAT uses existing benchmarks (HumanEval/HumanEval+/MBPP/MBPP+, GSM8K/GSM-HARD, MC-TextWorld Minecraft 100-task suite) plus a custom set of open-ended creative-writing tasks evaluated by human Elo/TrueSkill. The Minecraft evaluation uses 100 tasks ranging from simple to diamond-level objectives. A benchmark-contamination pre-processing step (following Guo et al. 2024) removes exact solutions from the code library; discussed in Appendix D.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Chain-of-Thought / zero-shot CoT prompting (Wei et al. 2022; Kojima et al. 2022 'let's think step by step'); Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020 RAG); iterative/interleaved retrieval-with-reasoning predecessors -- IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2022, CoT to generate better queries), IRGR / entailment-tree iterative retrieval-generation reasoner (Ribeiro et al. 2022), and ITRG (Feng et al. 2023, retrieval based on last-step generation); embedding/text-encoder retrieval (Sentence-BERT, Reimers & Gurevych 2019; OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002). Base models: CodeLlama-7b (Roziere et al. 2023), gpt-3.5-turbo (Ouyang et al. 2022), GPT-4 (OpenAI 2023). Evaluation infra: MC-TextWorld (Lin et al. 2023), TrueSkill (Herbrich et al. 2006).
- **contrasts with**:
> Classical single-query RAG (RAG-1/RAG-5) which uses one query (the task prompt / question) and tends to summarize retrieved content, over-focusing on the final-target item and missing intermediary facts; zero-shot CoT alone which hallucinates intermediate steps (e.g., wrong crafting materials, wrong dates); prior reasoning-augmented RAG (IRCoT, IRGR, ITRG) which 'simply adopt a single query' or retrieve for single-step QA. RAT's distinctions: (1) generate a full zero-shot CoT first, then (2) retrieve using evolving reasoning + draft answers as queries in an autoregressive way, and (3) causally revise each thought step one-by-one rather than revising the whole CoT at once or retrieving everything up front.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving) -- iterative/test-time retrieval interleaved with chain-of-thought reasoning. RAT sits in the lineage of reasoning-interleaved RAG (IRCoT, ITRG, IRGR) and is contemporaneous with active/adaptive RAG (FLARE, Self-RAG, Adaptive-RAG), but is distinguished by being a zero-shot prompting strategy that generates a draft CoT and then iteratively, causally revises each thought step with step-conditioned retrieval, extending RAG from short-form QA to diverse long-horizon generation (code, math, writing, embodied Minecraft planning).

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- context_budget_and_selection_count
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- venue

<a id="item-rankrag"></a>
### 34. RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs

2024  ·  NeurIPS 2024  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02485)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: NeurIPS 2024 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37). Preprint arXiv:2407.02485 (cs.CL), submitted 2 Jul 2024.
- **authors affiliation**:
> Yue Yu (Georgia Tech, work done during an internship at NVIDIA), Wei Ping (NVIDIA, corresponding), Zihan Liu (NVIDIA), Boxin Wang (NVIDIA), Jiaxuan You (NVIDIA), Chao Zhang (Georgia Tech), Mohammad Shoeybi (NVIDIA), Bryan Catanzaro (NVIDIA). Primary affiliations: NVIDIA and Georgia Tech.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02485

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: QA (knowledge-intensive NLP): open-domain QA, multi-hop QA, fact verification, conversational QA, and domain-specific (biomedical) RAG QA.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline-trained, single-LLM, retrieve-rerank-generate RAG for knowledge-intensive QA. The setting is non-interactive (single forward QA per question, no environment loop, no multi-agent). Supervision is available: a two-stage instruction fine-tuning pipeline (Stage-I general SFT on 128K examples; Stage-II unified instruction tuning blending QA + ranking data). At test time the model operates zero-shot on the target tasks (no task-specific demonstrations or fine-tuning). One LLM serves both as reranker and as answer generator.
- **what is retrieved**: Documents / passages (chunked text contexts, e.g. Wikipedia passages, or MedCorp biomedical corpus passages) relevant to the question. No demos/trajectories/skills/tools are retrieved.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus (e.g., December 2018/2020 Wikidump for general QA; MedCorp for biomedical). No agent-written or growing/episodic memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking objective: the LLM reranker selects the top-k (k much smaller than N, e.g. k=5) most relevant contexts from N retrieved candidates. The retrieval-augmented ranking training task asks the model to identify ALL relevant passages among 5, but at inference the goal is a fixed-k high-recall shortlist for generation, not a variable-size precision-driven set.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method)
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is an instruction-tuning RAG/reranking method.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document / passage (chunked text context; conversational documents are cut into 150-word chunks during ranking-data construction).
- **index source**: Static corpus, offline-constructed: pre-indexed document collections (Wikidump for general QA; MedCorp for biomedical). The store is frozen; not online/test-time-induced.
- **index structure topology**: Flat vector index (dense embedding retriever over the corpus, e.g. Dragon/DPR/Contriever/MedCPT) plus BM25 sparse index used for hard-negative mining during training. No graph/hierarchical/cluster organization.
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid two-stage: (1) first-stage retriever is a dense embedding model (Dragon by default; also tested DPR, Contriever; MedCPT for biomedical) — off-the-shelf; (2) second-stage reranker is the instruction-tuned LLM itself acting as an LLM-as-reranker (relevance scored by probability of generating 'True'). BM25 (sparse) is also used during training data construction.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> First-stage retriever: none (off-the-shelf, frozen). Reranker (the LLM): supervised instruction-tuning on relevance-labeled ranking data — MS MARCO gold (q,c+) pairs vs BM25-mined hard negatives (q,c-), plus synthetic conversational relevance pairs (4-gram recall of chunk vs gold answer >0.5 relevant, <0.1 irrelevant), and retrieval-augmented ranking labels (contexts containing the answer = relevant). Signal is binary relevance supervision (True/False classification / relevant-passage identification), not RL/preference/LM-feedback.
- **query construction**: Raw input question used directly (with task-specific instruction template). For conversational QA, the previous dialogue turns are used as context with the current question. No decomposition, sub-query generation, or query expansion.
- **query granularity**: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single query per question drives both retrieval and reranking; no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot (single retrieval pass per question), followed by a single reranking pass, then generation. No iterative or active retrieval.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieval and reranking are always performed for every question (no learned trigger, confidence gating, or agent-initiated request).
- **reranking**:
> Yes — this is the central contribution. The same instruction-tuned LLM performs context reranking: it scores each (question, passage) pair by the probability of generating 'True' to the relevance prompt, then keeps the top-k (k much smaller than N). It is an instruction-tuned LLM-as-reranker (pointwise relevance scoring), not a separate cross-encoder.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Rerank-then-truncate: the LLM reranks N retrieved contexts and retains only the top-k for generation, filtering out irrelevant/distractor passages. Training also includes hard-negative-aware retrieval-augmented QA to make generation robust to irrelevant context. No decompose/compress/distill step.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools retrieved)
- **index content separation**: N/A (no progressive disclosure / index-then-content separation)
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no tool index/protocol)
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no tools)

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation: the reranked top-k contexts are concatenated with the question and fed back into the same RankRAG LLM to generate the final answer. Ranking labels and retrieval-augmented data also act as a training signal during instruction tuning (the dual capability is learned jointly).
- **planning integration**: Retrieve-then-rerank-then-generate, single-shot (no planning/search loop). The pipeline is: (1) retriever fetches top-N; (2) RankRAG LLM reranks to top-k; (3) RankRAG LLM generates answer from top-k. No MCTS/tree search, no per-step interleaving.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: a single retrieve-rerank-generate pass produces the final answer; retrieval is not interleaved with reasoning steps or CoT.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not a CBR / case-adaptation method)
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw passages/contexts (verbatim text) injected into the prompt as 'Passage 1: ... Passage k: ...'. No distilled strategy, workflow, program, or latent token.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw document/passage text (lowest abstraction); no distilled strategy, guideline, workflow, or skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retriever/distractor-aware SFT plus a learned reranking filter: (1) retrieval-augmented QA training mixes gold context with BM25 top-retrieved hard-negative ('distractor') contexts so the generator learns to be robust to irrelevant context; (2) context-ranking and retrieval-augmented ranking tasks train the LLM to explicitly identify relevant contexts, and at inference the reranker discards low-relevance distractors before generation.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (static corpus RAG; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory written by the agent).
- **write back**: False — the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills; the corpus and model are fixed after offline training.
- **online growth**: No — the retrievable store is frozen after offline indexing; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
- **write back trigger**: Never (no write-back mechanism).
- **failure experience usage**:
> No experience-memory storage. However, during training, hard-negative (non-answer-containing) BM25-retrieved contexts are used as negative/irrelevant examples for both the ranking task (q,c- pairs) and the robustness of retrieval-augmented QA. This is offline negative-example supervision, not stored runtime failure experience.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no stored entries to mutate; append-only/dedup/refine not applicable).
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partially: context selection is performed by an instruction-tuned LLM reranker (a learned relevance classifier), not a fixed similarity top-k over the embedding scores. However, it is supervised binary-relevance learning, not an RL-optimized or value-based retrieval policy. The first-stage retriever remains fixed similarity top-N.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No — single-model, single-agent; no cross-agent/cross-framework memory or experience sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> General-domain (9 datasets): NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikimQA (open-domain/multi-hop QA, KILT splits where applicable), FEVER (fact verification, KILT), Doc2Dial, TopiOCQA, INSCIT (conversational QA). Biomedical (Mirage benchmark, 5 datasets): MMLU-Med, PubMedQA, BioASQ, MedQA, MedMCQA. Ranking evaluation uses MS MARCO passage ranking. Also Llama2-backbone evaluation on the same 9 datasets.
- **benchmark family**: QA / multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikimQA), fact verification (FEVER), conversational QA (Doc2Dial, TopiOCQA, INSCIT), domain-specific biomedical RAG (Mirage), and passage-ranking (MS MARCO). Not in the web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL families.
- **baselines**:
> Without RAG: InstructGPT, PaLM 2, FLAN-LaMDA, GLaM, Claude 2, Mixtral-8x22B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V2 Chat, GPT-3.5-turbo-0613, GPT-4-0613. With retrieval: Atlas, Raven, Self-RAG, RECOMP, InstructRetro, RePlug, RA-DIT, Llama-3-Instruct (8B/70B), Llama3-ChatQA-1.5 (8B/70B, primary open-source SOTA baseline), GPT-3.5-turbo RAG, GPT-4-0613 RAG, GPT-4-turbo-2024-0409 RAG; reference InstructGPT/CodeX pipelines (GenRead, Retrieve-Read, ReFeed). Reranking baselines (ranking module study): BERT-, T5-, Llama3-rankers fine-tuned on full MS MARCO, BGE-ranker (off-the-shelf), GPT-3.5/GPT-4 as rerankers, and ChatQA-1.5-as-reranker.
- **key metrics**:
> Exact Match (EM) for OpenQA (primary), Accuracy (TriviaQA, PopQA), F1 (HotpotQA, 2WikimQA, and ConvQA: Doc2Dial/TopiOCQA/INSCIT), Accuracy for FEVER and biomedical multiple-choice (Mirage). Ranking module evaluated by Recall (top-k recall). Efficiency reported as relative time overhead vs accuracy gain.
- **headline result**:
> Zero-shot, Llama3-RankRAG significantly outperforms Llama3-ChatQA-1.5 and GPT-4 on nine knowledge-intensive benchmarks: RankRAG 8B average 52.6 vs ChatQA-1.5 8B 49.6; RankRAG 70B average 56.1 vs ChatQA-1.5 70B 53.6 (and vs GPT-4-0613 RAG 43.5). E.g. on NQ EM 54.2 (70B) and 50.6 (8B). It also matches GPT-4 on five biomedical Mirage benchmarks without biomedical fine-tuning (RankRAG 70B avg 78.06 vs GPT-4-0613 79.97).
- **ablations**:
> Table 3 (Llama3-8B): removing reranking drops average from 52.6 to 49.8 (largest single component effect); w/o retrieval-augmented QA (RQA) -> 51.6; w/o retrieval-augmented ranking (RAR) -> 51.8; replacing the unified scheme with RAFT-style training (Lin et al. RA-DIT) -> 48.1; Stage-I SFT only -> 42.2. Ranking-module study (5.5): with only ~5k ranking data (~1% of MS MARCO) RankRAG already attains strong recall and outperforms dedicated BERT/T5/Llama3 rerankers trained on 10x more data and BGE-ranker (>1M pairs); using ChatQA-1.5 to rerank HURTS performance (ranking data in tuning is necessary). Backbone study (Table 4): consistent +7.8%/+6.4%/+6.3% average gains over ChatQA on Llama2 7B/13B/70B. Retriever robustness across Dragon/DPR/Contriever (Fig 6a). Efficiency (Fig 10a): reranking N=20->100 improves EM by 5.9%-9.1% with only 0.9x-6.0x added time (far below the naive 20x-100x).
- **evaluation decoupling**: Yes — intrinsic ranking metrics (Recall) for the ranking module are reported separately (Table 6, §5.5, Appendix E.1) from end-to-end QA task metrics (EM/F1/Acc in Table 2).
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome metrics (final answer EM/F1/Acc). The ranking module is evaluated intrinsically via top-k Recall (an intermediate process-quality metric for context selection), and a qualitative case study (Table 7) inspects retrieved-context quality, but there is no per-step reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reranking adds time overhead = N*t2/(t1+t3), where computing each relevance score needs generating just one token over a short input. Empirically, reranking N=20 to 100 yields +5.9% to +9.1% EM at only 0.9x to 6.0x added time (far below the 20x-100x naive expectation). Even N=20 improves over no-reranking. Training cost: RankRAG-8B = 32 A100 GPUs x 10h (4h Stage-I + 6h Stage-II); RankRAG-70B = 128 A100 GPUs x 16h (4h + 12h). Data-efficient: ~5k (~1%) ranking examples already strong.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Reranked-then-truncated, fixed-k: retriever fetches top-N (N=100 for 8B, N=30 for 70B by default); the LLM reranker keeps top-k for generation (default k=5; ablations vary k in {5,10,20} for baselines reporting best). Max generated tokens capped per task (32 for OpenQA, 128 for ConvQA, 8 for others). Training uses 5 contexts per retrieval-augmented sample.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey)
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (RankRAG is a method; it reuses existing benchmarks rather than constructing one. Uses KILT splits for NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA, December 2018 Wikidump (2020 for PopQA) as corpus, and the Mirage biomedical benchmark with MedCorp/MedCPT.)

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> ChatQA-1.5 / ChatQA (Liu et al., 2024) context-rich QA instruction-tuning blend and ConvQA datasets (HumanAnnotatedConvQA, SyntheticConvQA); Llama2/Llama3 backbones; Dragon dense retriever (Lin et al., 2023); MS MARCO passage ranking (Bajaj et al., 2016); LLM-as-ranker line (RankGPT/Sun et al. 2023, Qin et al. 2024, Ma et al. 2023); general instruction-tuning (FLAN, Self-Instruct, Unnatural Instructions, OpenAssistant, Dolly, SODA, ELI5).
- **contrasts with**:
> Separate expert reranker pipelines (BERT/T5/monoT5/BGE-ranker cross-encoders) and LLMs fine-tuned solely on large ranking data; RAFT-style retrieval-augmented fine-tuning of RA-DIT (Lin et al., 2024) which treats each retrieved context separately; standard retrieve-then-generate RAG (ChatQA-1.5, Self-RAG, RECOMP, RePlug, InstructRetro, Atlas/Raven); end-to-end retriever-LLM co-training (REALM, Atlas) which the paper argues complicates training and requires re-indexing.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving / knowledge-intensive QA): a retrieval-augmented generation method that unifies the reranking and generation stages within one instruction-tuned LLM. Positioned in the RAG-pipeline-improvement / context-filtering lineage (instruction-tuned RAG LLMs and LLM-as-reranker), extending the ChatQA RAG-instruction-tuning line with a unified ranking-and-generation objective.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- code_url

<a id="item-repoformer"></a>
### 35. Repoformer - Selective Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Completion

2024  ·  ICML 2024  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10059)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2024
- **venue**: ICML 2024 (International Conference on Machine Learning) - Oral (acceptance rate 1.5%). Proceedings: PMLR v235 (https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/wu24a.html). Preprint: arXiv:2403.10059 (v1 15 Mar 2024, v2 4 Jun 2024).
- **authors affiliation**: Di Wu (University of California, Los Angeles - UCLA), Wasi Uddin Ahmad, Dejiao Zhang, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Xiaofei Ma (all AWS AI Labs). Work done with/at Amazon; code released under amazon-science.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10059 (DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2403.10059; DBLP journals/corr/abs-2403-10059). Proceedings: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/wu24a.html . Project page: https://repoformer.github.io/
- **code url**: https://github.com/amazon-science/Repoformer (Apache-2.0; data + inference code + CrossCodeLongEval benchmark). Training code based on https://github.com/amazon-science/ContraCLM.
- **maintained repo url**: N/A (single per-paper code repo; no maintained leaderboard or living paper list).

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: code (repository-level code completion: line, API-invocation, code-chunk, and function-body completion in user repositories).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-agent, supervised setting. The system completes one or more consecutive lines Y in a file given the in-file left context X_l, right context X_r, and the set of other repository files F. RAG follows the four-stage RG-1 pipeline of Zhang et al. 2023 (indexing, query formation, retrieval, generation). The central question is whether to retrieve cross-file context at all: the authors show retrieval helps only ~20% of instances and harms ~20%, so they make retrieval selective. Repoformer is a single code LM, fine-tuned via self-supervision, that serves simultaneously as (a) the selective-RAG policy (decides whether to retrieve by emitting a special token) and (b) the generation model. It is trained once on permissively-licensed repositories from the Stack and then frozen at inference. It can also act as a plug-and-play selective-retrieval policy in front of larger black-box generation models (StarCoderBase-7B/16B, Code Llama, CodeGen25, ChatGPT/gpt-3.5-turbo).
- **what is retrieved**: Cross-file code snippets (code chunks): fixed-size spans of consecutive lines extracted from other files F in the same repository (CC = cc_1...cc_k). Not documentation, demos, or trajectories - purely in-repository code context.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: the target repository's own files, indexed per-repository as a static snapshot. No growing/episodic agent memory; the retrievable store is frozen per repository and does not grow during deployment.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking (k=10 most-similar code chunks). The retrieval set size is fixed; the novelty is at the per-instance decision level (retrieve k=10 vs retrieve nothing), governed by a learned self-evaluation policy. Not minimal-complete-set recovery nor precision-driven variable-k within retrieval.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: Retrieve=yes (selective, self-triggered); Reuse=yes (retrieved chunks injected as prompt context for robust generation); Revise=no (no case adaptation/revision); Retain=no (no write-back). [Retrieve, Reuse] only.
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False - the work frames itself as selective retrieval-augmented generation (selective RAG) / adaptive RAG for code; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not present itself as case-based reasoning.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> token/snippet: a fixed-size code chunk of consecutive lines (chunk size = 20 lines for line/API/chunk completion, 50 lines for function completion; stride = half the chunk size). After retrieval, fragment alignment (Lu et al. 2022) replaces each top chunk with the chunk immediately following it.
- **index source**:
> Static, offline-constructed per-repository store: all files in F are partitioned into fixed-size sliding-window code chunks at indexing time. No online/test-time induction or growth. (Training-data labels are induced offline by simulating RAG over 18k filtered Stack repositories.)
- **index structure topology**: Flat similarity index over sliding-window code chunks within a repository (bag-of-tokens for Jaccard / dense vectors for UniXcoder). No dependency graph, knowledge graph, or hierarchical category structure.
- **retriever type**:
> Sparse lexical by default: Jaccard similarity over token sets (chosen for speed and strong performance, following Zhang et al. 2023). Also evaluated dense retrievers - UniXcoder cosine similarity and OpenAI-embedding cosine similarity (CCEval) - and CodeBLEU; Jaccard was not outperformed by these on the main tasks. The retriever itself is off-the-shelf (not trained).
- **retriever learning signal**:
> none for the retriever (off-the-shelf Jaccard / UniXcoder / OpenAI embeddings, no training). The LEARNED component is the selective-retrieval POLICY inside the code LM: it is trained by self-supervised LM-feedback - the ground-truth retrieve/abstain label is obtained by contrasting the LM's own completion quality (Edit Similarity vs the ground truth Y) with vs without retrieval augmentation (label positive if retrieval improves ES by more than threshold T=0).
- **query construction**:
> The query to the in-repository retriever is formed from the in-file context (X_l and X_r). During training data creation, the target Y is additionally included in the query for 50% of instances (oracle-in-query), to align with both non-iterative and iterative use where a draft prediction Y' is used to re-query. The selective decision itself is made by the LM from X_l and X_r before any retrieval.
- **query granularity**:
> task-level / one-shot at the completion point: a single retrieval decision and (if triggered) a single retrieval is made for each completion instance after observing X_l, X_r. No multi-step / per-token re-querying (the paper notes single-iteration RAG already captures most gains of iterative RAG).
- **when to retrieve**: adaptive (learned router) + one-shot: a learned self-evaluation policy decides per instance whether to retrieve once. Retrieval is selective rather than always-on; when triggered it is a single (one-shot) retrieval.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Learned self-assessment via a reflection-style token: after observing X_l, X_r the LM emits the end-of-current-file token <eof> and then predicts a special token <cc> (retrieve) or an empty token (abstain). In practice retrieval is triggered when p(<cc>) exceeds a threshold T (Threshold/SelectiveT, e.g. T=0.2 for line/API/chunk, T=0.15 for function) or greedily if <cc> is the most likely token (Greedy/SelectiveG). This single forward-pass signal jointly encodes (1) whether the LM already knows the answer (self-knowledge, a la Kadavath et al. 2022) and (2) whether cross-file info is likely needed. Contrasted with trial-retrieval (retriever similarity) and trial-generation (token-uncertainty/entropy) heuristics, which the paper shows are less effective and incur retrieval/generation latency.
- **reranking**: No dedicated reranking stage. Top-k chunks are taken by retriever similarity; fragment alignment (use the following chunk) is the only post-retrieval reordering/transformation. No cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Minimal: fragment alignment (replace each retrieved chunk with the immediately-following chunk, per Lu et al. 2022) and concatenation into the prompt up to the context budget. The key refinement is at the decision level (selectively NOT retrieving) plus training the LM for robustness to noisy contexts, rather than distilling/compressing/decomposing the retrieved text. No distractor-filtering module.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A - no tools/skills/tool-docs; retrieved units are raw code chunks.
- **index content separation**: N/A - no progressive-disclosure / lightweight-index-then-content separation; retrieved chunks are used directly.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A - no live tool index or integration protocol (no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling). Repository index is a static per-repo snapshot.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A - no inter-tool dependency modeling (no tools).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation: if retrieval is triggered, the retrieved cross-file chunks CC are placed after the special token <cc> and concatenated with X_l and X_r in a fill-in-the-middle-style prompt; the same code LM then generates Y. If abstaining, the LM generates from X_l, X_r only. The selective decision and the generation are produced in a single left-to-right pass (an extension of fill-in-the-middle). Crucially, the framework also doubles as a training signal: a self-supervised multi-task objective (L_eval for the <cc> self-assessment + L_gen for code generation, total = lambda*L_eval + L_gen, lambda=1.0) teaches the LM both to self-trigger and to robustly use noisy CC.
- **planning integration**:
> retrieve-then-generate, gated by a self-triggered decision: there is no explicit planner/tree-search. The pipeline is: observe in-file context -> LM self-evaluates (one forward pass) -> optionally retrieve once -> LM completes. In the online-serving latency model, the decision (P1), no-retrieval generation (P2), and retrieve+generate (P3) are issued in parallel and the system keeps whichever the decision selects.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-answer / per-completion: a single self-assessment + at most one retrieval per completion instance; retrieval is not interleaved per CoT-step or per-token.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not framed as CBR). Retrieved chunks are used as verbatim in-context augmentation; robustness to them is acquired via training rather than explicit case revision.
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw code chunks (verbatim consecutive lines from other repo files), injected as plain in-context text after the <cc> token. No distilled strategy, workflow, program-skill, or latent representation.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw code (concrete, low-abstraction): contiguous code line spans from sibling files in the repository, akin to demonstration-style raw context rather than a distilled insight or guideline.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retriever-aware / robustness-oriented fine-tuning: the self-supervised multi-task objective trains the LM to (a) abstain from retrieval when CC would not help or would harm (performance-oriented self-evaluation) and (b) robustly leverage potentially noisy CC when retrieved (L_gen conditions on CC for positively-labeled instances). Analyses (Figure 6) show Repoformer has fewer/smaller performance drops from CC than StarCoderBase, and robustness holds under dense retrieval with a different context distribution (Table 8). Labels are derived by contrasting the LM's own output quality, making it a distractor-/noise-aware SFT.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none - no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory. Uses a static per-repository code index plus the fine-tuned LM's parametric knowledge.
- **write back**: False - the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills at inference time. (Training data labels are mined offline once; nothing is written back during deployment.)
- **online growth**: False - the retrievable store is a frozen per-repository snapshot and the LM is frozen after fine-tuning; neither grows during deployment.
- **write back trigger**: never - no write-back event at inference time.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Not stored as runtime experience. During OFFLINE training-label creation, both helpful and unhelpful/harmful retrievals are used contrastively: an instance is labeled negative (abstain) when retrieval does not improve (or hurts) the LM's completion ES, and positive (retrieve) when it does. This success-vs-no-gain contrast is the supervision signal, but no failure cases are retained in an inference-time memory.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A - no stored entries are mutated (no memory); the per-repo index is static.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Yes (partially): the WHEN-to-retrieve decision is a learned self-evaluation policy trained via self-supervised LM-feedback (contrastive ES labels) and applied through a threshold on p(<cc>). It is not an RL/value-based policy and the WHAT-to-retrieve step remains fixed similarity top-k; but the retrieval-gating decision is genuinely learned rather than a fixed similarity rule.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> No cross-agent memory sharing. However, the learned selective policy generalizes across generation models: Repoformer-1B serves as a plug-and-play selective-RAG policy in front of heterogeneous larger LMs (StarCoderBase-7B/16B, CodeGen25-7B, Code Llama-7B/16B, ChatGPT), improving their accuracy while cutting latency ~25%.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> RepoEval (Zhang et al. 2023; line completion: 16 repos / 1600 instances; API completion: 16 repos / 1600 instances; function completion: 16 repos / 455 instances, unit-test verifiable). CrossCodeLongEval (new benchmark introduced by this paper, built from 1500 raw Python repos from CrossCodeEval; chunk completion: 944 repos / 5000 instances; function completion: 1460 repos / 5000 instances). CrossCodeEval (Ding et al. 2023; line completion across Python, Java, C#, TypeScript) used for multilingual generalization.
- **benchmark family**: code (repository-level code completion: RepoEval / CrossCodeEval / CrossCodeLongEval family).
- **baselines**:
> Primary comparisons (same generation model, StarCoder family): (1) No Retrieval (in-file X_l + X_r only); (2) Always Retrieving (single-iteration RG-1 RAG pipeline of Zhang et al. 2023, the state-of-the-art prompting baseline). Generation models compared/used as backbones: StarCoderBase-1B/3B/7B, StarCoder-16B, CodeGen-Mono-2B/16B, CodeGen25-7B, Code Llama-7B/16B, ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613). Selective-policy alternatives compared in appendices: trial-retrieval (retriever similarity score: BM25/sparse, UniXcoder, CodeBLEU) and trial-generation (token uncertainty / entropy) heuristics; conceptually contrasted with SKR (Wang et al. 2023) and Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024).
- **key metrics**:
> Exact Match (EM), Edit Similarity (ES = 1 - Levenshtein/max-length, reported x100), and unit-test pass rate (UT) for function completion. Efficiency metrics: %RAG (fraction of instances where retrieval is performed) and Speedup (SU) vs always-retrieving. Decision-quality metrics: abstention precision and calibration of the selective decision.
- **headline result**:
> 16B Repoformer with threshold selective RAG sets state-of-the-art repository-level code completion, outperforming the strongest StarCoder-16B always-retrieving baseline by ~3% averaged across tasks; Repoformer outperforms same-sized StarCoderBase always-retrieving by more than 3 absolute ES points on multiple tasks, and Repoformer-3B matches/surpasses always-retrieving StarCoder-16B on several tasks. Efficiency headline: selective retrieval yields up to 70% inference speedup in online serving (with dense retrieval / large repos) without harming accuracy; threshold selection improves BOTH accuracy and latency vs always retrieving. Concretely (RepoEval, 1B, Table 3) SelectiveG reaches 18-19% %RAG with 61-69% speedup at ~1 ES drop; SelectiveT keeps/improves ES with 27-28% speedup.
- **ablations**:
> Section 5.1 proof-of-concept: on RepoEval API/function completion, retrieval improves only ~20% of instances, leaves >60% unchanged, and HARMS ~20% - consistent across CodeGen-Mono 2B/16B, StarCoderBase-1B, StarCoder-16B (motivates selectivity). Section 6 ablations (StarCoderBase-1B): (A1) merging L_eval and L_gen into one cross-entropy down-weights L_eval so p(<cc>)~=1 and selective decisions become meaningless (always retrieves); (A2) removing L_eval slightly improves RAG accuracy but loses the selective ability (so L_eval adds selectivity at little RAG cost); (A3) further removing CC (pure fill-in-the-middle) matches in-file completion but degrades RAG performance, showing training-with-CC is necessary; (A4) placing <cc>/CC inside the fill-in-the-middle infilling span (marked by <cc_end>) badly hurts function completion by breaking pretrained FIM semantics. Other analyses: threshold insensitivity (T=0.4 still matches always-retrieving with 50% latency cut); abstention precision >0.8 on all tasks (0.78 for RepoEval function); robustness to dense vs sparse retrieval; generalization to Java/C#/TypeScript (Repoformer-M) and to larger black-box generation models.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Partial. End-to-end task metrics (EM/ES/UT) are the primary report. Intrinsic retrieval ranking metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) are NOT the focus; instead the paper decouples the DECISION quality (retrieval abstention precision and calibration of p(<cc>)) and the retrieval budget (%RAG) from end-to-end accuracy, and separately analyzes retrieval helpfulness distribution (Figure 3, Table 1).
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Both. Outcome metrics: EM/ES/UT of the final completion. Process/decision metrics: precision of retrieval-abstention decisions (>0.8), calibration of the selective prediction, %RAG, and per-instance analyses of whether CC helps/harms - i.e., the quality of the intermediate retrieve/abstain decision is evaluated, not only final code correctness.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Central contribution. The selective decision costs only a single forward pass (T_d < T_g < T_r + T_g). Reported: SelectiveT gives 27-28% speedup with equal/better accuracy and SelectiveG 61-69% speedup at ~1 ES drop on RepoEval line/API (Repoformer-1B); as a plug-and-play policy for larger LMs, Repoformer-1B cuts latency ~24-32% while improving accuracy (Table 4). With dense retrieval on large repos (retrieval = >80% of pipeline latency) a ~20% RAG budget translates to >70% end-to-end speedup. Note: sparse retrieval on moderate repos is already as costly as 3B-LM generation, motivating the savings.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed k=10 retrieved code chunks when retrieval is triggered; chunk size 20 lines (line/API/chunk) or 50 lines (function), stride = half chunk size; max sequence length 2048 during fine-tuning; max generated tokens follow RepoEval conventions. The novel budget control is the per-instance binary gate set by threshold T on p(<cc>) (e.g. T=0.2 line/API/chunk, T=0.15 function), tuning the fraction of instances that retrieve (%RAG) and thus the accuracy-latency trade-off; k itself is fixed (not adaptive within retrieval).
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> CrossCodeLongEval (introduced here): built from 1500 raw Python repositories from CrossCodeEval by sampling new blanks (to avoid CrossCodeEval's bias of removing instances StarCoderBase-1B answers correctly without retrieval). Chunk-completion split: 944 repos / 5000 instances (avg |Y| ~1.47 lines / 19.2 tokens); function-completion split: 1460 repos / 5000 instances (avg |Y| ~9.5 lines / 111.2 tokens). Construction = algorithmic sampling of code chunks (Poisson-length) and function bodies + Jaccard RAG simulation; answer verifiability is reference-based (EM/ES) for chunk and reference-based for function (RepoEval function split is unit-test verifiable). Released with the code under Apache-2.0.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> RG-1 single-iteration RAG pipeline and RepoEval from RepoCoder (Zhang et al. 2023); fill-in-the-middle training (Bavarian et al. 2022); StarCoder/StarCoderBase (Li et al. 2023) and CodeGen/CodeGen25 (Nijkamp et al.) code LMs; LM self-knowledge / 'language models know what they know' (Kadavath et al. 2022); Jaccard / UniXcoder (Guo et al. 2022) retrieval and fragment alignment (Lu et al. 2022, ReACC); the Stack (Kocetkov et al. 2022) for training repos; ContraCLM (Jain et al. 2023) training infrastructure; CrossCodeEval (Ding et al. 2023).
- **contrasts with**:
> Always-retrieving RAG for code completion (RepoCoder/Zhang et al. 2023, and structured-context fine-tuned methods like RepoFusion/Shrivastava et al., CoCoMIC/Ding et al. 2024). Among adaptive-RAG works, explicitly contrasted with SKR (Wang et al. 2023, needs extra module + knowledge store of unhelpful instances) and Self-RAG (Asai et al. 2024, distills a smaller LM using GPT-4 oracle labels): Repoformer needs no extra module, no knowledge store, and no oracle-LM labels - it self-supervises from the LM's own contrastive output quality. Also contrasted with uncertainty-triggered RAG (Jiang et al. 2023 FLARE, Li et al. 2023) and trial-retrieval relevance gating (Drozdov et al. 2022), which the paper shows are less robust across completion lengths and incur retrieval/generation latency.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task-solving), code-domain selective/adaptive RAG. Direct descendant of RepoCoder (RG-1 / RepoEval) in repository-level code completion; introduces the code-domain 'when-to-retrieve' question, paralleling QA-domain adaptive/self-RAG (Self-RAG, SKR, FLARE, Adaptive-RAG) but powered by self-supervised contrastive ES labels rather than oracle-LM distillation. Predecessor to later selective/efficient repo-level RAG and RL-based code retrieval methods (e.g. RLCoder).

<a id="item-guideline-forest"></a>
### 36. Guideline Forest (Guideline Forest: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning with Branching Experience-Induced Guidelines)

2025  ·  arXiv 2506.07820  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07820)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**: Jiaxiang Chen (Fudan University; equal contribution), Zhuo Wang (Fudan University & SII; equal contribution), Mingxi Zou (Fudan University), Qifan Wang (Meta), Zenglin Xu (Fudan University & SAIS; corresponding/senior author). Primary affiliation: Fudan University.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.07820 (PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.07820 ; HTML v3: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.07820v3 ; DOI: https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2506.07820)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Multi-step LLM reasoning: mathematical reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500) and code generation (MBPP, HumanEval). Framed as improving reasoning quality (not knowledge-grounding QA, not embodied/web agents). Tasks are reasoning/code-generation with verifiable final answers.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline-to-online, single-model (with an optional multi-model collaboration extension) supervised setting. A training phase uses labeled (question, answer) pairs to build a memory of verified gold reasoning trajectories; an inference phase retrieves from this frozen memory and reasons over a new problem. Supervision is available (ground-truth labels used both to verify/regenerate training trajectories and to filter what gets stored). Two LLMs are used in the pipeline: GPT-4o-mini for reasoning generation and GPT-4o for verification. The default deployment is single-agent step-wise branch reasoning over one model; an optional Multi-Inference Collaboration extension assigns different guideline branches to different LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B) and aggregates their step-level candidates by weighted voting. The memory grows during training in a closed loop but is frozen for the reported test-time evaluation.
- **what is retrieved**:
> experiences / trajectories: verified, label-consistent 'gold reasoning' trajectories (problem + step-wise solution + embeddings) of past solved training problems. These retrieved trajectories are then abstracted into structured 'guidelines' (reusable, high-level step-wise reasoning plans) that steer the new reasoning. So the retrieved unit is a past reasoning trajectory; the USED unit is a distilled guideline induced from it.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING / episodic experience memory the system itself writes (a repository M_mem of verified gold reasoning trajectories built during a training/collection phase via a closed-loop self-improving process). Explicitly contrasted with conventional RAG that retrieves a static external knowledge corpus: here retrieval targets accumulated REASONING EXPERIENCE, not docs/KB. Construction is offline-induced during training then frozen at test time; growth happens within the training loop, so grounding is a self-built growing memory (dominantly experience-grounded, not a static external corpus).
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k retrieval objective: for each test problem the system retrieves the top-k (default k=3) most semantically similar verified positive samples by cosine similarity, then aggregates their solution steps into a guideline. The ablation (Fig.4a / retrieval-scale study) frames k as a precision/quality trade-off (too few -> overly specific/misaligned paths, too many -> generalization noise), with k=3 best, but the mechanism is still a fixed-size top-k, not a completeness-driven minimal-set or variable-size recommendation.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: yes, Retain: yes]. Retrieve: top-k cosine retrieval of verified gold trajectories. Reuse: trajectories are abstracted into guidelines and reused to steer step-wise reasoning (not verbatim ICL; an induced/adapted reuse). Revise: a stepwise self-refinement mechanism revises intermediate outputs, and label-guided regeneration revises incorrect training trajectories. Retain: verified trajectories are appended to memory (closed-loop growth). All four canonical CBR phases are effectively realized, though under non-CBR terminology.
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
