> False - the paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed via retrieval-augmented generation/reasoning, exploratory reasoning (CoT/ToT/FoT), ensemble/collaborative inference, and a latent-trajectory marginalization formulation. It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain CBR mechanisms (storing past solved cases, retrieving similar ones, abstracting/adapting, retaining new solutions) under another name.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Full reasoning trajectory / case (problem + step-wise solution): the retrieved unit is a verified gold reasoning trajectory z=(z_1,...,z_T) paired with its problem x. From the top-k retrieved trajectories the system induces guideline(s) g=(g_1,...,g_T), an abstract step-wise reasoning plan. So retrieval granularity = full trajectory (problem-solution episode); the derived/used granularity = guideline-rule (per-step reasoning plan).
- **index source**:
> Growing, offline-induced memory repository M_mem built during a training/collection phase from labeled training data (GSM8K 500, MATH-500 ~700 across categories, MBPP 100, HumanEval 30 training instances). Construction is a closed self-improving loop (CoT -> label-guided regeneration -> optional ToT exploration -> optional memory-guided refinement; only correct trajectories retained). The store grows during training and is then frozen for test-time inference. Not a static external corpus; not built at test time.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat dense vector index over trajectory/problem embeddings (text-embedding-3-small embeddings; stored as problem, steps, embeddings; cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor retrieval). No graph, hierarchy, or cluster topology described. (The 'forest' in the name refers to the branching reasoning structure at inference, not to the index topology.)
- **retriever type**: Dense retriever using off-the-shelf OpenAI text-embedding-3-small embeddings with cosine similarity for top-k nearest-neighbor search over the gold-reasoning memory. Not BM25, not learned/RL-trained, not generative.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf frozen text-embedding-3-small embeddings; fixed cosine top-k; no contrastive training, no LM-feedback, no RL). The supervision/quality signal is applied to WHAT populates the index (only label-consistent, verified-correct gold trajectories are retained via label-guided generation and GPT-4o verification), not to the retriever's ranking function.
- **query construction**:
> Raw problem statement is used as the query/key. At inference the new input problem x is embedded with text-embedding-3-small and matched against stored problem/trajectory embeddings by cosine similarity. No query decomposition, expansion, intent extraction, or thought-conditioning of the retrieval query (retrieval is a single one-shot lookup per problem; the per-step branching/aggregation that follows does not re-query the memory).
- **query granularity**:
> Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval is performed per test problem using the whole problem as the query to fetch the top-k gold trajectories, from which guidelines are induced. The subsequent multi-branch step-wise reasoning does NOT issue fresh per-step retrievals against the memory; branching/aggregation operate on the already-induced guidelines.
- **when to retrieve**:
> One-shot: retrieval from the gold-reasoning memory happens once per problem at the start of inference (to induce the guidelines). It is not iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or router-gated. (Within the training loop, a memory lookup is also used to help refine hard training cases, but that is part of memory construction, not test-time retrieval.)
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule / unconditional: one retrieval is triggered at the beginning of solving each new problem (to build its guideline set). No token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated request triggers retrieval. (During training, retrieval from M_mem is triggered when verified trajectories are insufficient / for harder instances, a construction-time heuristic.)
- **reranking**:
> None - no explicit reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker). The top-k positive samples are taken directly by cosine similarity. (A separate step-level aggregation selects among candidate reasoning branches, but that is candidate-step selection during generation, not retrieval reranking.)
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Decompose-then-recompose / distillation into guidelines: the retrieved trajectories are not injected verbatim but are abstracted via a Guideline Generation Prompt into a concise core-problem + step-wise reasoning plan, then expanded via a Guideline Rewriting Prompt into 3 diverse branch variants. This is a distill-then-diversify refinement of retrieved content (not simple rerank/compression, and no explicit distractor filtering at retrieval time).
- **tool document engineering**: N/A - no tools/skills or tool descriptions are indexed or retrieved. Retrieval items are natural-language reasoning trajectories embedded with text-embedding-3-small.
- **index content separation**:
> Partial / induced-abstraction rather than progressive disclosure: stored entries hold problem + steps + embeddings; what is injected at inference is the INDUCED guideline (a distilled abstraction), not the raw heavy trajectory. There is no explicit lightweight-index-then-load-heavy-content (SOP-index-then-content) mechanism; the abstraction is generated on the fly via prompting rather than stored as a separable index layer.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A - not a tool-retrieval system; no live tool index or RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling protocol. The memory is an internally managed dense vector store that grows during the training loop only.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A - no tools retrieved, so no inter-tool dependency modeling.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Case adaptation + prompt augmentation (guideline-steered generation): retrieved gold trajectories are abstracted into structured guidelines (high-level step-wise plans), rewritten into M (~3) diverse branch variants, and each guideline step is injected into the LLM prompt (Guideline Execution Prompt) to steer the corresponding reasoning step. Thus retrieval is used as an instructional scaffold that guides step-wise generation, not as verbatim few-shot exemplars and not as a training signal (no weight updates at inference).
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-plan-then-branch: a single retrieval induces a guideline set, which is the high-level plan; reasoning then proceeds per-step in a multi-branch manner where each guideline branch independently proposes a candidate step z_t^(m), each candidate is optionally self-refined, and the M candidates are aggregated into a single unified step z_hat_t that becomes shared context for the next step. This is a step-wise interleaved branch-and-aggregate procedure (forest-of-paths) rather than MCTS/tree search; complexity O(MT) for M branches over T steps.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**:
> Per-CoT-step: branching, self-refinement, and aggregation are interleaved at each reasoning step (each guideline branch proposes a candidate step; candidates are refined and aggregated per step). Retrieval from memory, however, is per-problem (once), so retrieval-vs-reasoning interleaving is coarse (one retrieval) while the branch/aggregate search is fine-grained per step.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted abstraction + diversification + execution-feedback-style self-correction: the retrieved case is (1) abstracted into a guideline via an LLM prompt (not verbatim ICL), (2) rewritten into multiple perspective variants, (3) executed step-by-step with a lightweight self-correction/refinement at each step and aggregation-based selection among branches. No RL reuse-finetuning; adaptation is prompt-driven (induce -> rewrite -> execute -> refine -> aggregate).
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled strategy / guideline (free-text structured step-wise plan): what is injected is an induced guideline with a 'Core Problem' and numbered reasoning steps (e.g., <step 1>, <step 2>, ...), rewritten into 3 diverse variants. Not raw trajectory text, not an executable program/skill object, not latent/soft tokens. (For code tasks the guideline is still a natural-language reasoning plan; the final answer is code.)
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled reusable reasoning workflow / guideline: the paper explicitly distinguishes concrete instance-specific trajectories (what is stored/retrieved) from abstract reusable guidelines (what steers reasoning). The operative abstraction level is a distilled strategy/reusable step-wise plan (mid-high abstraction), deliberately capturing general reasoning structure rather than exact solutions.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Several: (1) memory contains only verified, label-consistent gold trajectories (incorrect trajectories discarded; GPT-4o verification) so the retrieval source is clean; (2) retrieval-scale ablation tunes k=3 to balance specificity vs generalization noise; (3) guideline abstraction strips instance-specific details, reducing overfitting to a single retrieved case; (4) multi-branch diversity + step-wise aggregation (confidence-based scoring/voting) provides ensemble-like robustness against individual-path errors; (5) step-wise self-refinement corrects intermediate errors before they accumulate. No retriever-side relevance evaluator or distractor-aware SFT at retrieval time.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Episodic experience memory of verified gold reasoning trajectories (a 'reasoning experience repository' M_mem). Stored as concrete episodic trajectories (problem + steps + embeddings); guidelines are derived from it at inference rather than stored as a separate skill-library/workflow/graph/latent memory.
- **write back**:
> True - all verified (label-consistent, correct) reasoning trajectories are appended to the memory repository: M_mem <- M_mem U {(x^(i), z^(i)*)} (Eq.2), forming a self-improving loop where accumulated experience continuously expands the reasoning repository. Write-back happens during the training/collection phase.
- **online growth**:
> Partial - the store GROWS during the training/collection (closed-loop self-improving) phase as more verified trajectories are added, but it is FROZEN for the reported test-time inference (guidelines extracted from training samples guide test inference; no evidence the memory is written during test-time deployment). So growth is offline/training-time, not test-time-online.
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success only (label-verified): a trajectory is written to memory iff it produces the correct ground-truth answer (verified, with GPT-4o verification). Incorrect initial trajectories are first regenerated via label-guided generation (best-of-n, up to three rounds) and ToT exploration for harder instances; only the resulting correct trajectories are retained, and failed cases are discarded. No per-step or unconditional write-back; no storing of failures.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success-only. Failed/incorrect trajectories are explicitly discarded and never stored or retrieved. There is no failure/negative-experience memory and no success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval. Errors are handled transiently via label-guided regeneration during construction and step-wise self-refinement at inference, but failures are not retained as corrective cases.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Append-only growth: verified trajectories are appended to M_mem (Eq.2). No described dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forget-prune of existing stored entries; the repository monotonically accumulates. (Individual stored trajectories are not mutated in place after writing.)
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No - retrieval/case-selection is a fixed off-the-shelf cosine-similarity top-k (text-embedding-3-small), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, or trained selector). Selection signals (label-consistency for retention, k tuning, branch aggregation) are heuristic/supervision-based, not a trained retrieval policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Optional cross-model sharing via the same induced guidelines: the Multi-Inference Collaboration extension assigns the (shared) guideline branches to different LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B), each of which generates step-level candidates following its assigned guideline; these are aggregated by weighted voting (Eq.4, uniform weights w=1), reaching e.g. 90.32% on number-theory tasks. This is sharing of reusable guidelines/experience across heterogeneous models (model-agnostic, transferable priors), though the memory itself is a single shared repository, not per-agent private memories.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> GSM8K (grade-school math word problems; 500 train / 1,319 test), MATH-500 (competition math across 7 categories: algebra, precalculus, prealgebra, counting & probability, geometry, intermediate algebra, number theory; ~100 train sampled per category, full benchmark for test), MBPP (Python program synthesis; 100 train / 341 test, following AFlow), HumanEval (Python code generation; 30 train / 130 test, following AFlow).
- **benchmark family**: QA/math reasoning (GSM8K, MATH-500) + code generation (MBPP, HumanEval). Spans the math-reasoning and code families (SWE-bench-style repo tasks are NOT used; MBPP/HumanEval are function-level code-gen). No web/embodied/tool/memory-RL benchmarks.
- **baselines**:
> Direct: IO (input-output prompting). Exploratory reasoning: CoT (Wei et al. 2022), CoT-SC / Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022), ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b), ToT (Yao et al. 2023a), FoT / Forest-of-Thought (Bi et al. 2024). Search-based: AFlow (Zhang et al. 2024, MCTS-based agentic workflow generation). Also compared across backbones (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct) and against guideline-enhanced versions of CoT/ReAct/ToT.
- **key metrics**:
> Solve Rate (%) for math (GSM8K, MATH-500) = fraction of problems with correct final answer; pass@1 for code (MBPP, HumanEval) = fraction passing all test cases on a single generated solution. Plus tokens-per-problem and an accuracy-cost utility 'Acc-1kTok' = Acc - Tokens/1000 for the efficiency analysis.
- **headline result**:
> With GPT-4o-mini, Guideline Forest reaches GSM8K 93.5%, MATH-500 69.2%, MBPP 81.6%, HumanEval 95.4% (avg 84.9%), outperforming all baselines on average (best baseline AFlow 84.1 avg) and achieving the best single results on GSM8K, MATH-500, and HumanEval (on MBPP 81.6% is slightly below AFlow's 83.4%). Most-cited single figure: MATH-500 69.2% vs ToT 65.2 / FoT 65.8 / AFlow 65.6 with GPT-4o-mini.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Mechanism ablation on MATH-500 subdomains (Table 4): Full 69.20 vs w/o multi-guideline 61.39, w/o aggregation 62.19, w/o refinement 64.63 - all three components contribute (e.g., Geometry 41.66 -> 53.66 with multi-path; Prealgebra 76.83 -> 80.20 with refinement). (2) Retrieval scale (Fig.4a): k=3 positive samples is optimal (too few -> overly specific, too many -> generalization noise). (3) Path diversity (Fig.4b): multi-path > single-path. (4) Stepwise refinement (Fig.4c): ~+4% avg. (5) Aggregation strategy (Fig.4d): stepwise aggregation > final-step-only, ~+7% absolute. (6) Backbone scaling (Table 2): improves with GPT-4o > GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-32B. (7) Guideline-enhanced baselines (Table 5): CoT 57.8->59.8, ReAct 58.0->66.0, ToT 65.2->66.0; Ours 69.8. (8) Multi-model collaboration (Fig.5): cooperation best, 90.32% on number theory. (9) Cost ablation (Table 3, Num.Th.): GF 12.6k tokens / 85.48% / Acc-1kTok 72.88, best utility.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No - only end-to-end task metrics (Solve Rate / pass@1) plus token-cost are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) are reported separately; the retrieval-scale ablation (k) is measured by downstream solve rate, not by retrieval quality.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome-focused (final Solve Rate / pass@1). Some process-adjacent analyses: training-accuracy-vs-iteration curve (Fig.3) showing improvement from CoT -> label guidance -> ToT stages; step-wise aggregation/refinement ablations probing intermediate-step quality; and qualitative case studies (Fig.6, Appendix) illustrating step-level reasoning and refinement. No formal step-wise retrieval-accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k retrieval: top-k=3 positive samples retrieved per problem (k=3 optimal per ablation); guideline rewritten into M~3 diverse branches executed per step. Maximum input lengths capped at 400 tokens for MATH-500/GSM8K and 600 tokens for MBPP/HumanEval. Selection is fixed-k by cosine similarity (not adaptive/precision-driven, not reranked-then-truncated).
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A - not a survey/taxonomy paper.
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A - uses existing benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH-500, MBPP, HumanEval), not a benchmark-construction paper. Train/test splits used: GSM8K 500/1319, MATH-500 ~100-per-category train / full test, MBPP 100/341, HumanEval 30/130.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> RAG (Edge et al. 2024 GraphRAG; Guo et al. 2024 LightRAG; SlimRAG 2025) reframed from knowledge to reasoning retrieval; CoT (Wei et al. 2022) and CoT-SC/Self-Consistency (Wang et al. 2022); ToT (Yao et al. 2023a) used both as a baseline and as a structured-exploration component during training; FoT/Forest-of-Thought (Bi et al. 2024) for branching reasoning; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b); AFlow (Zhang et al. 2024) for workflow/data-split protocol; ensemble learning (bagging/boosting/random forests/mixture-of-experts) as the conceptual basis for branch aggregation; BoostStep (Zhang et al. 2025a, step-level case-library retrieval) and AdaS (Hu et al. 2024) as related step-retrieval/adaptive-compute work.
- **contrasts with**:
> Exploration-based reasoning (CoT, ToT, FoT) that builds trajectories from scratch per instance with unguided test-time search and no experience reuse; workflow/search-based methods (AFlow, HaIR-ICL via MCTS, WorkflowLLM) that learn fixed/heuristic workflows with high search cost and limited transfer; conventional RAG that retrieves external knowledge documents (vs retrieving reasoning experience); pure test-time sampling ensembles (Self-Consistency, multi-LLM Avengers/SMACS) that lack experience-grounded structured branching. Guideline Forest instead retrieves verified reasoning trajectories, distills reusable guidelines, and aggregates step-wise at O(MT) cost.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for reasoning / task-solving) intersecting experiential/episodic-memory reasoning. Lineage: RAG (knowledge retrieval) -> reasoning retrieval / experience reuse; CoT -> ToT/FoT branching -> Guideline Forest, which adds a verified-gold-reasoning memory plus guideline induction and step-wise branch-and-aggregate. Positioned as 'reasoning-experience retrieval': retrieving and reusing verified gold trajectories abstracted into structured branching guidelines that drive reasoning, bridging RAG, exploratory reasoning, and ensemble/collaborative inference.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- code_url
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- venue

<a id="item-marag-r1"></a>
### 37. MARAG-R1: Beyond Single Retriever via Reinforcement-Learned Multi-Tool Agentic Retrieval

2025  ·  arXiv 2510.27569  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27569)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: arXiv:2510.27569 (cs.CL); preprint, submitted 31 Oct 2025; no peer-reviewed venue as of retrieval
- **authors affiliation**: Qi Luo, Xiaonan Li (equal contribution), Yuxin Wang, Tingshuo Fan, Yuan Li, Xinchi Chen, Xipeng Qiu (corresponding); School of Computer Science, Fudan University
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.27569

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: QA / RAG / tool-use: corpus-level reasoning and information aggregation (GlobalQA: TopK/Count/Sort/MinMax) plus multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline-trained, single-agent LLM that operates interactively at inference: the model interleaves reasoning with calls to four retrieval tools over a static document corpus until it has gathered sufficient evidence, then produces a final answer. Supervision is available via query-answer pairs (with gold supporting-document IDs) used to build expert trajectories (SFT) and to define rewards (RL). The central problem framing is that a single retriever with fixed top-k is a bottleneck for corpus-level (global) reasoning that requires complete document coverage and aggregation.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Documents (corpus passages/documents) retrieved/operated on via four tools: semantic search, keyword search, document filtering (metadata/logical constraints), and aggregation (statistical/structural operations such as count, rank, set union/min/max). The retrieved unit is documents/document-IDs.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus (the model retrieves from a fixed document collection via specialized tools; no agent-written growing memory).
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Completeness-oriented: explicitly targets recovery of the complete minimal set of supporting documents for corpus-level synthesis, moving beyond fixed top-k. A document-coverage reward R_E = F1(D_pred, D*) over document IDs rewards retrieving all necessary documents while minimizing irrelevant ones; evaluated with Document F1@k (D-F1@20).
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: false. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document (problem operates at the document / document-ID granularity); tools also expose tool-API actions (semantic search, keyword search, filter, aggregate) over those documents.
- **index source**: Static corpus, built offline; not online/test-time induced. The retrievable store is the fixed GlobalQA (and multi-hop QA) corpora; tool indices (dense embeddings via BGE, keyword index) are constructed over this static corpus.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat document index accessed through multiple tool interfaces: a dense/semantic vector index (BGE embeddings), a keyword-matching index, plus a metadata/constraint filter and an aggregation operator over document sets. Not a graph or hierarchy (the paper explicitly contrasts with graph-based RAG which loses document-level identifiers).
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid multi-tool: dense semantic retriever (BGE/Qwen3 embeddings), keyword/sparse-style matching retriever, a filter model (Qwen3-4B used as filtering model), and an aggregation operator; an LLM policy coordinates which tool to call (tool-as-action). The individual retrievers are off-the-shelf; the coordination is learned.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> The underlying retrievers (BGE / Qwen3 embeddings) are off-the-shelf (none / not retraining). The TOOL-COORDINATION POLICY (the LLM deciding how/when to call each tool) is learned via two-stage training: SFT on GPT-4-generated expert trajectories (with rejection sampling) followed by reinforcement learning (RLOO) using a composite reward (answer F1 + document-coverage F1 + tool-exploration reward).
- **query construction**:
> Thought-conditioned, model-generated tool calls: at each step the model emits intermediate reasoning R_t and a tool invocation C_t (e.g., a semantic-search query, a keyword query, a filter constraint, or an aggregation operation over previously retrieved document sets); sub-queries are decomposed per subquery and combined via explicit set operations (Union, Min, etc.).
- **query granularity**: Step/state-level: queries/tool-calls are constructed iteratively at each reasoning step within a trajectory (multi-step, up to a max number of retrieval steps), rather than a single one-shot query at t=0.
- **when to retrieve**: Iterative / adaptive (learned router): the model autonomously decides at each step whether and which tool to invoke, interleaving reasoning and retrieval until sufficient evidence is gathered. The when/how is learned via SFT+RL (learned policy), not a fixed schedule.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Agent-initiated tool requests produced by the learned policy: the model itself emits a tool call as part of its generated trajectory. The tool-exploration reward (R_T) shapes how many calls to make (rewarding sufficient-but-not-excessive calls relative to the expert trajectory's call count), so the trigger is a learned, reward-shaped decision rather than token-confidence or a complexity classifier.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Filtering/selection via the Document Filter tool (metadata/logical-constraint filtering, Qwen3-4B as filtering model) and the Aggregation tool (set operations such as union, count, min/max to synthesize/condense evidence). The policy iteratively narrows and combines document sets; no separate compression/distillation module is reported.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: Static tool index (fixed offline corpus and tools); tools are invoked via the model's generated tool calls (function-calling-style interleaved actions), not via a live external protocol such as RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP. No CRUD auto-sync.
- **tool dependency awareness**:
> Partial/implicit: tools are chained so that outputs of one feed another (e.g., Union of semantic+keyword search results, then Aggregation/Min over the combined set), and the learned policy sequences them; but there is no explicit inter-tool dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation within an interleaved reasoning-retrieval trajectory: retrieved documents (D_t) are appended to the context after each tool call and used by the model to reason in subsequent steps and produce the final answer. The policy that selects/sequences tools is itself trained as a learning signal (RL reward).
- **planning integration**:
> Per-step interleaved retrieve-and-reason inside a search loop: the agent autonomously plans, retrieves, and integrates over multiple steps (S_t = (R_t, C_t, D_t)), progressively gathering and consolidating evidence; no MCTS/tree search. Plan and retrieval are intertwined (agentic RAG) rather than plan-then-retrieve.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-tool-call within a rollout: each reasoning step produces one tool invocation followed by retrieved documents, interleaving thinking and retrieval step by step until the final answer.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (no retrieved-case adaptation; this is not CBR). The closest analog is RL-reuse-finetuning of the tool-coordination policy.
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw documents / document IDs injected into context (the method explicitly preserves document-level boundaries and identifiers, contrasting with graph methods that lose provenance). Aggregation produces structured set-operation outputs (e.g., the min document ID).
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw document-level evidence (and their IDs); not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill. The contribution emphasizes preserving fine-grained factual/numerical detail and provenance versus graph abstractions.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Reward-shaped training: the document-coverage F1 reward (R_E) penalizes irrelevant retrievals (precision term) while rewarding recall, and the tool-exploration reward (R_T) penalizes redundant/excessive calls; the Document Filter narrows the search space. Appendix A reports stable performance beyond ~10 retrieval steps, attributed to RL helping balance retrieval depth with over-retrieval noise control. No explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection module.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (no persistent episodic/skill/workflow memory; retrieval is over a static corpus within a single episode).
- **write back**: false. The system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into a persistent memory; evidence is gathered per-query within a trajectory and discarded after answering.
- **online growth**: false. The retrievable store is a fixed static corpus; it does not grow during deployment/test time.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back to a memory store; only model parameters are updated during the offline SFT+RL training phase).
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no stored-memory entries to mutate; not applicable since there is no growing memory store).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: true. Tool selection/sequencing (the retrieval policy) is a learned RL-optimized policy: SFT cold-start (MARAG-CS) then RLOO RL with a composite reward, rather than a fixed similarity top-k. The paper frames learning 'both how and when to use' the tools as the core contribution.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A / no. Single-agent private policy; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: GlobalQA (four task types: TopK, Count, Sort, MinMax) for corpus-level reasoning; 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA for multi-hop generalization. Backbone models: Qwen2.5-3B/7B/14B-Instruct; retriever BGE; filter model Qwen3-4B; TopK=20.
- **benchmark family**: QA / corpus-level aggregation (GlobalQA, from the GraphRAG line) + multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA).
- **baselines**:
> StandardRAG (single-round retrieval, Lewis et al. 2021), ITER-RETGEN (Shao et al. 2023), IRCoT (Trivedi et al. 2023), HyperGraphRAG (Luo et al. 2025), Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025), ReCall (Chen et al. 2025; same multi-tool suite but optimized with answer-level reward only). Internal variants: MARAG (prompt-only, untrained multi-tool), MARAG-CS (SFT-only cold start), MARAG-R1 (SFT+RL).
- **key metrics**: F1 (token-level answer accuracy) and Document F1@k / D-F1@20 (document-coverage/execution F1 between retrieved and gold document sets at k=20). For multi-hop QA: EM and F1. Average number of tool calls reported as an efficiency/behavior metric.
- **headline result**:
> On GlobalQA with Qwen2.5-14B, MARAG-R1 achieves average F1 31.22 and D-F1@20 42.11, the best across all baselines and the SFT-only MARAG-CS (28.92 / 39.83); consistent SOTA across 3B (26.40 F1 / 37.05 D-F1@20) and 7B (28.60 / 38.44). ReCall (same tool suite, answer-only reward) scales only from 6.41 to 14.25 avg F1 (3B->14B) vs MARAG-R1's 26.40->31.22.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Reward/stage ablation (Qwen2.5-14B, Table 2): w/o SFT 14.25 F1 / 20.00 D-F1@20 (largest drop, -17.0 F1 / -22.1 D-F1@20); w/o Answer Reward 13.78 / 24.48 (-17.4 F1 / -17.6 D-F1@20); w/o Document Reward 28.87 / 39.53 (-2.4 / -2.6); w/o Tool-Calls Reward 29.45 / 39.54 (-1.8 / -2.6) vs Full 31.22 / 42.11. (2) Tool ablation (Qwen2.5-7B, Table 4, Full 27.35/38.19): w/o Aggregation 10.48/19.54 (largest, -16.9 F1/-18.7 D-F1); w/o Keyword 13.03/24.08 (-14.3/-14.1); w/o Semantic 20.21/25.13 (-7.1/-13.1); w/o Document Filter 22.57/32.14 (-4.8/-6.0). (3) Tool-call count (Table 3): MARAG-R1 6.32 calls, MARAG-CS 6.27, ReCall 4.53, MARAG 2.81. (4) Appendix: retriever-scale (Qwen3 0.6B->8B: 31.22/42.11 -> 32.31/43.06) and filter-scale (Qwen3-4B->14B: 31.22 -> 31.82 F1) show graceful scaling; retrieval-step analysis shows stable performance beyond ~10 steps.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Yes (partially): document-level coverage (D-F1@20, an intrinsic retrieval/coverage metric over document IDs) is reported separately from token-level answer F1 (end-task), and average tool-call counts are reported separately. However, both are produced end-to-end by the same agent rather than via a decoupled retriever-only evaluation.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Both: outcome (answer F1, EM) plus process/intermediate metrics — D-F1@20 (document-coverage/execution F1, treated as correctness of intermediate reasoning steps), average tool-call count, and training-dynamics analysis (training entropy/reward vs test F1/D-F1@20 correlation). Reward design itself includes process-level terms (document-coverage and tool-exploration rewards).
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reports average tool calls per query as the main cost proxy: MARAG-R1 6.32 calls (vs MARAG-CS 6.27, ReCall 4.53, MARAG 2.81); the tool-exploration reward explicitly penalizes excessive calls to balance exploration with efficiency, and Appendix A shows performance saturating beyond ~10 retrieval steps (robust to over-retrieval). RL uses 5 sampled rollouts per query (RLOO). No wall-clock latency, token, or dollar-cost numbers reported.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed per-tool TopK=20 for retrieval; D-F1 evaluated at k=20 (D-F1@20). The number of documents in context grows with the number of tool calls (effectively budget-capped by the max retrieval-step setting); k per call is fixed rather than adaptive. No explicit token-budget cap reported.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (not a benchmark paper). Uses existing GlobalQA (TopK/Count/Sort/MinMax, from the GraphRAG line), 2WikiMultiHopQA, and HotpotQA; specific train/test set sizes are not detailed in the paper text.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> RLOO / REINFORCE-style RL (Ahmadian et al. 2024); RL-for-retrieval agents Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025) and ReSearch/ReCall (Chen et al. 2025); agentic ReAct (Yao et al. 2023); GlobalQA benchmark from GraphRAG (Edge et al. 2025); BGE embeddings (Xiao et al. 2023); Qwen2.5/Qwen3 backbones; chunk-free/landmark-embedding retrieval (Luo et al. 2024); SFT cold-start from GPT-4 expert trajectories. Shares first-author lineage with R3-RAG (Li/Luo et al. 2025).
- **contrasts with**:
> Single-retriever fixed-top-k Workflow RAG (StandardRAG, ITER-RETGEN, IRCoT); graph-based RAG (GraphRAG, HyperGraphRAG, HippoRAG, KG-RAG — criticized for losing document-level provenance/identifiers); RL-RAG methods optimized with answer-only sparse reward (Search-R1, ReCall) — MARAG-R1 adds process-level rewards (document-coverage + tool-exploration) and a multi-tool suite.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving): agentic / reinforcement-learned RAG. Extends RL-trained iterative-retrieval agents (Search-R1, ReCall, ReSearch, R3-RAG) by coordinating MULTIPLE complementary retrieval tools (semantic/keyword/filter/aggregate) via SFT+RL with process-level rewards, explicitly targeting corpus-level/global retrieval and aggregation rather than local top-k multi-hop QA.

### 38. R1-Searcher: Incentivizing the Search Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

2025  ·  arXiv 2503.05592  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05592)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**: Huatong Song, Jinhao Jiang, Yingqian Min, Jie Chen, Zhipeng Chen, Wayne Xin Zhao, Lei Fang, Ji-Rong Wen. Primary affiliation: Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China; with DataCanvas Alaya NeW (Lei Fang). Correspondence: Wayne Xin Zhao.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05592
- **code url**: https://github.com/RUCAIBox/R1-Searcher
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/RUCAIBox/R1-Searcher (follow-up: https://github.com/RUCAIBox/R1-Searcher-plus for R1-Searcher++)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: QA (open-domain / knowledge-intensive multi-hop question answering with autonomous tool/search invocation during reasoning).
- **problem setting**:
> Train a single LLM to autonomously decide when to invoke an external search system and how to integrate retrieved documents into its chain-of-thought to answer multi-hop questions. Setting is interactive (the model emits queries and the retrieval environment returns documents mid-generation), single-agent, and supervision is outcome-only (final-answer correctness via F1 plus format/retrieval rewards); no process rewards, no SFT cold start, and no intermediate-step annotations are used. Works from both an Instruct model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) and a Base model (Qwen-2.5-7B-Base) trained purely with RL.
- **what is retrieved**: Documents: 100-word Wikipedia passages (with titles) from a static corpus retrieved during reasoning; in the online-search generalization test, summarized web pages from Google Web Search.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus (2019 English Wikipedia from KILT, ~29M passages); generalizes at test time to online Google Web Search. Not a growing/episodic agent memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k ranking per query (top documents returned by the dense retriever and injected verbatim); the model issues multiple queries iteratively to cover all hops, but each individual retrieval call is fixed top-k. No explicit minimal-set/completeness objective is optimized.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle over a case base).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: false. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document (100-word Wikipedia passage chunk with title); retrieved set injected between <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tags.
- **index source**: Static offline corpus: English Wikipedia (KILT 2019 dump) segmented into 100-word passages, ~29M passages; index is fixed and not grown online.
- **index structure topology**: Flat dense vector index over passage embeddings (BGE-large-en-v1.5 embeddings); standard ANN/flat similarity index, no graph or hierarchy.
- **retriever type**: Dense retriever (BGE-large-en-v1.5 text embeddings); the LLM itself acts as a learned query generator but the document scorer is an off-the-shelf dense retriever. Online variant uses Google Web Search API + GPT-4o-mini summarization.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> none for the retriever itself (BGE-large-en-v1.5 is frozen / off-the-shelf). The LLM's query-generation and retrieve-or-not policy is trained by outcome-based RL (Reinforce++ with modifications): Stage-1 retrieval reward (binary on whether any retrieval is invoked) + format reward; Stage-2 F1 answer reward + format reward. So the learned signal is on the policy that drives retrieval, not on the embedding model.
- **query construction**: Thought-conditioned keyword query generated by the LLM during its <think> reasoning; the model emits a search query (keywords only, constrained to a single triple/fact) enclosed in <begin_of_query>...<end_of_query>. Queries are produced autonomously as reasoning proceeds.
- **query granularity**: step/state-level: queries are generated at intermediate reasoning steps whenever the model is uncertain, allowing multiple sequential queries within one rollout (up to a maximum retrieval count of 8).
- **when to retrieve**: adaptive / agent-initiated and iterative: the model itself decides at each reasoning step whether to emit a query, and can retrieve multiple times within a single solution (max 8 retrievals). Learned via RL rather than a fixed schedule.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Agent-initiated request: retrieval fires when the LLM generates the <end_of_query> tag during reasoning (the generation pauses, the query is extracted, documents are fetched and inserted). The decision to emit a query is a learned RL policy behavior triggered by the model's own uncertainty, not an explicit confidence/attention threshold.
- **reranking**: None. Top documents from the dense retriever are used directly; no separate reranking stage is reported.
- **retrieved context refinement**: none for local Wikipedia retrieval (documents injected verbatim within tags). For the online-search generalization setting only, retrieved web pages are summarized/compressed by GPT-4o-mini before integration due to page length.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A. There is no tool/skill description indexing; retrieval is over Wikipedia document passages, not tool docs. The single search 'tool' is invoked via special query tags with no docstring engineering.
- **index content separation**: N/A. No progressive-disclosure index/content separation; passages are retrieved and loaded directly.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A. Local index is static (Wikipedia); the search tool is invoked via a custom tag-based protocol (<begin_of_query>/<end_of_query>), not RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling. Online variant calls the Google Web Search API but the index is the live web with no CRUD auto-sync.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A. Single retrieval tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> prompt augmentation as a training signal loop: retrieved documents are inserted into the model's ongoing reasoning context (<begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents>) and the model continues reasoning conditioned on them; the entire retrieve-and-reason trajectory is optimized end-to-end by outcome RL (reward maximization).
- **planning integration**:
> per-step interleaved inside a single autoregressive reasoning loop: retrieve-then-reason cycles repeat within one rollout (RAG-based rollout). The model plans, queries, reads documents, and continues reasoning iteratively until producing the final <answer>. Not MCTS/tree search (explicitly contrasted with MCTS test-time scaling baselines).
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-reasoning-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval is woven into the chain-of-thought at the point each search query is emitted, so multiple retrieve-read-reason cycles occur per solution.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not CBR; no retrieved-case adaptation step). The closest analogue is RL-finetuning of how retrieved documents are used, but no case revision mechanism.
- **retrieved item representation**: raw retrieved passages (verbatim Wikipedia text inside <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tags) injected into the reasoning context; in the online setting, GPT-4o-mini summaries of web pages.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: raw document passage (factual evidence text); not distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retrieval Mask-based Loss Calculation: <begin_of_documents>...<end_of_documents> tokens are treated as special tokens and masked out of the RL loss so retrieved (environment) tokens do not influence policy gradients; combined with strict format rewards (iteratively refined to prevent reward hacking such as fabricating documents without querying). Robustness to noisy/irrelevant retrieval emerges from end-to-end outcome RL exploration rather than an explicit relevance evaluator.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). Retrieval targets a fixed external corpus; learned 'memory' is implicit in the model's RL-updated weights, not an external retrievable store.
- **write back**: false. The system does not write new experiences/cases/skills into any external memory store at inference time; learning is baked into model weights via RL training only.
- **online growth**: false. The retrievable store (Wikipedia index) is fixed; it does not grow during deployment. Only the online-search variant queries the live web, but no agent memory is accumulated.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back mechanism; the retrievable store is static and no episodic memory is maintained).
- **failure experience usage**:
> No explicit storage/retrieval of failed experiences as memory. During RL training, incorrect rollouts receive low/negative reward (e.g., F1=0, or -2 format penalty for malformed output) and thus shape the policy via gradient updates (success+failure used as contrastive RL signal), but failures are not stored as retrievable cases.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no external memory store to mutate). The policy is updated by RL gradient steps over a single training epoch; no append/dedup/refine of stored entries.
- **retrieval as learned policy**: true (partial): the decision of WHEN to retrieve and WHAT query to issue is a learned RL policy (Reinforce++ with RAG rollout and retrieval-masked loss). The document scoring/ranking itself remains a fixed off-the-shelf dense retriever (BGE), not RL-optimized.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A / single-agent. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing; one model trained and evaluated independently.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki), Musique, Bamboogle. Training data selected from HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA training sets (~8148 samples total). HotpotQA and 2Wiki are in-domain; Musique and Bamboogle are out-of-domain. Bamboogle also used for online-search generalization (Google API).
- **benchmark family**: QA / multi-hop (open-domain multi-hop QA).
- **baselines**:
> Naive Generation; Standard RAG; Branching: SuRe, REPLUG; Summarization: LongLLMLingua, RECOMP, Selective-Context; Adaptive Retrieval: SKR; RAG-CoT: Self-Ask, Iter-RetGen, IRCoT; Test-Time Scaling (MCTS): CR-Planner, ReARTeR; Reasoning models with standard RAG: Marco-o1-Qwen-7B, Skywork-o1-Llama-3.1-8B. Backbones for baselines: GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Online-search comparison: Search-o1 (32B backbone).
- **key metrics**: Cover Exact Match (ACC_R / CEM) and LLM-as-Judge (ACC_L, using GPT-4o-mini); ablations also report EM and F1. Online-search section reports CEM.
- **headline result**:
> On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct backbone, R1-Searcher outperforms the strongest baseline ReARTeR by 48.2% on HotpotQA, 21.7% on 2WikiMultiHopQA, and 4.0% on Bamboogle (relative improvement, LLM-as-Judge ACC_L). Qwen-2.5-7B-Base trained RL-from-scratch (no cold start) reaches the best overall results (e.g., HotpotQA ACC_R 0.654 / ACC_L 0.750; 2Wiki 0.636 / 0.650; Bamboogle 0.528 / 0.544; Musique 0.282 / 0.314), surpassing closed-source GPT-4o-mini baselines.
- **ablations**:
> (1) GRPO vs Reinforce++ as the RL algorithm: GRPO gives longer responses, more retrievals, and better OOD (Bamboogle) generalization; Reinforce++ is better on in-domain (HotpotQA/2Wiki) (Table 3, avg CEM 59.0 vs 58.9). (2) RL vs SFT: RL substantially beats SFT on both in-domain and OOD (e.g., Qwen-Base-RL avg CEM 60.6 vs SFT 50.1; Llama-Instruct-RL 58.2 vs SFT 48.2); SFT relies on internal knowledge and retrieves at worse timing/relevance. (3) Answer reward type (EM vs CEM vs F1): F1 is best (avg CEM 60.6) with up to +52.6% over EM (39.7); EM too strict for open-ended answers. (4) Format reward strictness needed to prevent reward hacking (e.g., fabricating documents without querying; Stage-1 needed for Llama to retrieve at all). (5) Training-data difficulty: including hard (>20 rollout) questions ('w. Difficult') improves avg CEM by ~3.4% over 'w/o Difficult' (60.8 vs 58.8). (6) Data diversity: HotpotQA+2Wiki mixture beats either alone by up to +10.9% avg CEM (60.6 mixture vs 54.6 HotpotQA / 43.6 2Wiki).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (CEM/ACC_R, LLM-as-Judge/ACC_L, EM, F1) are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics such as Recall@k or nDCG are reported (the retriever is fixed off-the-shelf).
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome metrics (final-answer correctness). Process-level signals are reported qualitatively/analytically (response length, number of retrievals during training logs, case studies on retrieval timing/relevance) but not as scored process-quality metrics.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> R1-Searcher is positioned as more efficient than MCTS-based test-time scaling (ReARTeR/CR-Planner) which 'incurs significant overhead due to increased retrieval invocations.' Max retrieval count capped at 8 per solution; 16 rollouts per sample during training, train batch 256, rollout batch 64, 1 epoch, lr 2e-6, DeepSpeed Zero-2. Number of retrievals tracked in training logs (harder data / GRPO -> more retrievals). No explicit latency/token-cost numbers vs accuracy reported.
- **context budget and selection count**: Fixed-k per retrieval call (top documents from dense retriever, each a 100-word passage); model may issue up to 8 retrieval calls per solution (maximum retrieval count = 8). No adaptive/precision-driven k or reranked-then-truncated budgeting reported.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (primary research paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). For reference: training corpus is KILT 2019 English Wikipedia segmented into 100-word passages (~29M passages); RL training set ~8148 selected samples from HotpotQA + 2WikiMultiHopQA, categorized into easy/medium/difficult by rollout count (Stage-1: 350 medium; Stage-2: ~4561 HotpotQA + ~3581 2Wiki).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Reinforce++ (base RL algorithm, modified with RAG-based rollout + retrieval mask-based loss); DeepSeek-R1 / R1-Zero-style outcome-based RL for reasoning (incentivizing capability via RL without SFT); GRPO (compared as alternative). Backbones: Qwen-2.5-7B-Base and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Evaluation infra: FlashRAG; corpus from KILT Wikipedia; retriever BGE-large-en-v1.5; ReARTeR evaluation framework conventions.
- **contrasts with**:
> MCTS / test-time scaling RAG methods (ReARTeR, CR-Planner) which it outperforms while avoiding heavy retrieval overhead; SFT/distillation cold-start approaches (it uses RL only, no cold start); RAG-CoT prompting methods (Self-Ask, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen); branching (SuRe, REPLUG) and summarization (LongLLMLingua, RECOMP, Selective-Context) RAG; adaptive retrieval (SKR); reasoning models with standard RAG (Marco-o1, Skywork-o1); Search-o1 (online search with larger 32B backbone, which it beats by 11.4% CEM on Bamboogle).
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task solving). Part of the early-2025 lineage of RL-trained agentic search / search-augmented reasoning LLMs (alongside Search-R1, DeepResearcher, and its own follow-up R1-Searcher++), which train LLMs end-to-end with outcome RL to interleave retrieval with reasoning, descending from R1/R1-Zero-style RL-for-reasoning and from iterative RAG-CoT methods.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document/passage (Wikipedia text passages; top-5 per query enclosed in <result></result> tags).
- **index source**: Static offline-built corpus: pre-indexed Wikipedia (Dec. 2018) via FlashRAG; embeddings/index preprocessed offline; the retrievable store is frozen and does not grow during training or test time.
- **index structure topology**: Flat dense vector index (E5-base-v2 embeddings over Wikipedia passages, FlashRAG/FAISS); no graph or hierarchical organization.
- **retriever type**: Dense (E5-base-v2 dense retriever, off-the-shelf); a BM25/keyword option is not the primary configuration.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf E5-base-v2, frozen). The learned component is the LLM policy that decides when and how (query formulation) to retrieve; the policy is trained by RL (GRPO) on a final-outcome reward (F1-based answer reward + format reward). The retriever is not trained.
- **query construction**:
> Thought-conditioned: the policy LLM generates a natural-language search query inside <search></search> tags during its <think> reasoning; queries are produced free-form by the model as a function of the question and prior retrieval results (supports query refinement / self-correction of queries).
- **query granularity**: Step/state-level: queries are emitted at each reasoning step where the model decides to search (multiple search queries per rollout), rather than one-shot at t=0.
- **when to retrieve**: Iterative and agent-initiated/adaptive: the model decides at each step whether to emit a <search>; the rollout alternates think -> search -> result -> think until an <answer> / eos. When-and-how-to-search is learned, not on a fixed schedule.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Agent-initiated request: retrieval is triggered when the generation produces a </search> tag (the policy emits a search query as part of its text-based thinking). The decision to search is learned through RL rather than from a confidence threshold, learned complexity classifier, or reflection tokens.
- **reranking**: None reported; the dense retriever's top-5 passages are returned directly without a separate reranking stage.
- **retrieved context refinement**: None / minimal: retrieved top-5 passages are inserted verbatim into the reasoning context (enclosed in <result></result>); no decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. The only special handling is loss masking of retrieved tokens during training.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (search is a single fixed tool; no per-tool description engineering). Tool invocation is conveyed via a simple prompt template instructing use of the wikipedia search tool with <search></search> tags.
- **index content separation**: N/A (no progressive-disclosure index vs content separation; flat dense index).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (single search tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation as part of an RL training signal: retrieved results are concatenated back into the rollout as context for further reasoning; the whole reason-with-search rollout is optimized via GRPO toward a final-answer reward (retrieved tokens are masked out of the policy-gradient loss so the policy is not trained to imitate retrieved text).
- **planning integration**: Inside a search loop / per-step interleaved: search is woven into the reasoning chain itself (think -> search -> result -> think -> ... -> answer). There is no separate planner module; the reasoning chain is the plan and retrieval is an integral component of it.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-reasoning-step / per-search-call within a rollout: each <think> step may issue one <search> call, and retrieval results condition subsequent reasoning; interleaving is at the level of individual thinking steps rather than per-token or per-final-answer.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not a CBR/case-adaptation method).
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw retrieved passages (top-5 Wikipedia text snippets) injected verbatim inside <result></result> tags; no distillation into strategy/guideline/program form.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw document/passage (concrete retrieved Wikipedia text), not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retriever-aware / RL training: the policy is trained end-to-end with GRPO so it learns to reason over (and self-correct against) imperfect retrieval; retrieved-result tokens are masked in the loss to prevent the policy from being biased toward retrieved text. Reflection/self-correction (e.g., recognizing a failed query and reformulating) emerges naturally from RL rather than from an explicit relevance evaluator.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (no episodic store, skill library, or persistent memory; retrieval is against a static external corpus).
- **write back**: False; the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into any memory. Learning is captured in the policy LLM's weights via RL, not in a retrievable store.
- **online growth**: False; the retrievable Wikipedia store is frozen (built offline) and does not grow during deployment or test time.
- **write back trigger**: never (no write-back to a retrievable memory; the only updating is offline RL policy-weight updates from final-outcome rewards).
- **failure experience usage**:
> No explicit storage/retrieval of failed experiences. During RL, low-reward rollouts (including format-incorrect or wrong-answer ones) receive lower normalized advantage in GRPO (reward 0 / 0.1 / F1), implicitly discouraging failure patterns, but failures are not stored as retrievable cases. Reflection/self-correction within a rollout is an emergent behavior, not a stored failure rule.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: Yes (partially): the decision of WHEN to retrieve and HOW to formulate the query is a learned RL policy (GRPO-optimized LLM) rather than a fixed similarity top-k schedule. The underlying passage ranking for a given query remains a fixed off-the-shelf dense top-k retriever.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No; single-agent, single-policy. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: HotpotQA (full dev, 7405), 2WikiMultiHopQA (full dev, 12576), MuSiQue (full dev, 2417; also the sole training source, train set 19938 samples), Bamboogle (test, 125). Retrieval environment: Wikipedia (Dec. 2018) via FlashRAG with E5-base-v2, top-5.
- **benchmark family**: Multi-hop QA (open-domain multi-hop question answering over Wikipedia).
- **baselines**:
> No RAG / Naive Generation (instruction-tuned model answers directly), Naive RAG (concatenate retrieved passages with question then answer), Iter-RetGen (iterative retrieve-generate synergy), IRCoT (interleaved retrieval with chain-of-thought). Prompt-based baselines use instruction-tuned Qwen2.5 models of the same size for fair comparison. Backbones: Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.
- **key metrics**: Exact Match (EM, %) and LLM-as-a-Judge (LJ, %, using gpt-4o-mini as judge). Training/analysis metrics: training & validation reward, response length, average number of search operations per rollout.
- **headline result**:
> ReSearch outperforms all baselines on all four multi-hop QA benchmarks. Average improvement over the best baseline: +15.81% EM / +17.56% LJ for 7B models and +14.82% EM / +15.46% LJ for 32B models (absolute improvements over baselines range 8.9%-22.4%). Best single configuration (ReSearch-Qwen-32B-Instruct): e.g., Bamboogle 56.80 EM / 67.20 LJ; HotpotQA 46.73 EM / 67.70 LJ; MuSiQue 26.40 EM / 38.56 LJ; 2Wiki 44.90 EM / 50.30 LJ.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No; only end-to-end task metrics (EM, LJ) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome-based (final-answer EM and LLM-as-a-Judge). Process is examined qualitatively/diagnostically (number of search operations, response length, reward curves, and a case study of reflection/self-correction) but not scored as a quantitative process-quality metric.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Response length (tokens excluding retrieval results) is reported as a proxy for test-time reasoning cost and grows during training; the average number of search operations per rollout also grows during training (more retrieval calls = more cost but higher accuracy). Top-5 passages retrieved per query. Training cost: 8x8 (=64) NVIDIA H800 GPUs, full-parameter optimization with gradient checkpointing, 2 training epochs on MuSiQue (19938 samples). No explicit latency/API-cost-vs-accuracy frontier table is given.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k retrieval: top-5 passages per search query. Multiple search calls allowed per rollout, so total injected context grows with the number of searches. Inference context length 8192 (per ReCall serving config). No adaptive/precision-driven k or explicit token-budget cap on injected items is reported beyond fixed top-5.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (not a benchmark paper; uses existing datasets). Evaluation sizes: HotpotQA dev 7405, 2WikiMultiHopQA dev 12576, MuSiQue dev 2417, Bamboogle test 125; original context documents discarded so only Q-A pairs are used with an open-ended Wikipedia retrieval environment.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> DeepSeek-R1 / OpenAI-o1-style RL-for-reasoning (rule-based reward, RL without supervised reasoning steps); GRPO (DeepSeekMath / Group Relative Policy Optimization) as the RL algorithm; verl RL framework; FlashRAG retrieval toolkit with E5-base-v2 retriever; Qwen2.5 (7B/32B, base and instruct) backbones.
- **contrasts with**:
> Prompt/heuristic-based multi-step RAG methods (Iter-RetGen, IRCoT) and naive RAG / no-RAG baselines; self-reflection RAG such as Self-RAG; SFT-based imitation of reasoning-with-search trajectories (ReSearch uses no supervised reasoning/search data). Concurrent RL-search work (e.g., Search-R1) is in the same line; ReSearch emphasizes treating search as an integral part of the reasoning chain trained purely via outcome RL.
- **lineage**:
> Part of the B (RAG / task-solving) lineage of RL-trained reason-with-search / agentic-RAG methods (alongside Search-R1): LLM policy learns interleaved reasoning + retrieval from outcome rewards over a static corpus, rather than relying on prompting heuristics or growing experiential memory. Direct predecessor in spirit to the authors' own successor framework ReCall, which generalizes search to arbitrary tool calls.

- dynamic_index_and_protocol

### 40. Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning

2025  ·  COLM 2025  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: COLM 2025 (Second Conference on Language Modeling); preprint arXiv:2503.09516 (v1 Mar 2025, v5 Aug 2025)
- **authors affiliation**:
> Bowen Jin, Zhenrui Yue, Dong Wang, Jiawei Han (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Hansi Zeng, Hamed Zamani (Center for Intelligent Information Retrieval, University of Massachusetts Amherst); Jinsung Yoon, Sercan O. Arik (Google Cloud AI Research). Lead author: Bowen Jin (UIUC).
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.09516
- **code url**: https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/PeterGriffinJin/Search-R1

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Open-domain question answering (general QA and multi-hop QA) treated as interleaved reasoning-and-search; search engine is used as a tool during step-wise reasoning.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, single-agent setting: a single policy LLM is trained with reinforcement learning to autonomously decide when and what to search during step-by-step reasoning, issuing multiple search queries to a real-time retrieval engine over multiple turns until it emits a final answer. Supervision is weak/outcome-only (the gold answer enables a rule-based EM reward); no per-step or trajectory-level annotation is required. The search engine is modeled as part of the environment, so rollouts interleave LLM-generated tokens with retrieved tokens. Training merges NQ and HotpotQA training sets; evaluation covers both in-domain and out-of-domain QA datasets.
- **what is retrieved**: Documents/passages (top-k Wikipedia passages) returned by the search engine in response to LLM-generated natural-language search queries.
- **retrieval grounding**: STATIC external corpus: retrieval targets a fixed 2018 Wikipedia dump as the knowledge source; there is no agent-written growing/episodic memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k ranking: a fixed number of passages (default top-3) is retrieved per query; the system relies on multi-turn querying rather than completeness-of-set or precision-driven variable-size retrieval. The retriever itself is off-the-shelf and not optimized for completeness.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False: the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: document (Wikipedia passage); the top-k retrieved passages are injected as a block enclosed in <information> and </information> tokens.
- **index source**: Static corpus, offline-built: a fixed prebuilt dense index over the 2018 Wikipedia dump. The retrievable store is frozen and does not grow during training or deployment.
- **index structure topology**: Flat vector (dense) index over Wikipedia passages (E5 embeddings); no graph/hierarchical/cluster organization reported.
- **retriever type**: Dense retriever (E5) as the default search engine; the framework is retriever-agnostic and the released code also supports BM25 and online web search, but the main experiments use a frozen dense E5 retriever.
- **retriever learning signal**: None (off-the-shelf, frozen): the retriever (E5) is not trained or adapted; only the policy LLM is optimized by RL. The learning signal (outcome reward) flows to the LLM's query-generation and reasoning policy, not to the retriever.
- **query construction**: Thought-conditioned: the LLM generates a free-text search query inside <search>...</search> tokens during reasoning, conditioned on the question and prior reasoning/retrieved context. Queries are emitted autonomously by the learned policy rather than copying the raw input.
- **query granularity**: Step/turn-level: a separate query is constructed at each reasoning step where the model decides to search, supporting multiple queries across turns within a single rollout (multi-turn, multi-query).
- **when to retrieve**: Iterative / agent-initiated: the LLM decides when to retrieve by emitting <search></search> tokens during reasoning; retrieval can occur multiple times per rollout up to a maximum action budget B.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Agent-initiated request: retrieval is triggered when the policy LLM generates the </search> token; the surrounding system loop detects this token, extracts the enclosed query, calls the search engine, and appends results in <information></information>. The decision is a learned behavior shaped by the outcome reward, not a fixed schedule or external confidence/uncertainty signal.
- **reranking**: None reported; the top-k passages from the dense retriever are used directly without a separate reranking stage.
- **retrieved context refinement**: None: retrieved passages are inserted verbatim into the rollout within <information></information> tokens with no decomposition, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. Robustness is instead handled at the training-loss level via retrieved-token loss masking.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A: the single tool is a search engine invoked via natural-language queries; no tool/skill descriptions are indexed or engineered.
- **index content separation**: N/A: no lightweight-index-then-content / progressive-disclosure separation; retrieved passages are loaded directly.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: Static index for the main experiments (frozen 2018 Wikipedia dump via a local retrieval server); the released code additionally supports online web search, but the paper's evaluation uses a static dense index, not a live-synchronized/MCP tool store.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A: single tool (search engine); no inter-tool dependency modeling.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt/context augmentation as a training signal: retrieved passages are appended to the ongoing rollout sequence as additional context for subsequent generation, and the whole interleaved trajectory is optimized end-to-end by RL (PPO/GRPO) with an outcome reward. Retrieved tokens are masked out of the policy-gradient loss.
- **planning integration**:
> Inside a search loop with per-step interleaving: retrieval is woven into an iterative reason-then-(optionally)-search loop (retrieve-as-you-reason). The LLM alternates <think> reasoning, <search> query, <information> retrieved context, and finally <answer>, dynamically adjusting how many search calls to make based on problem complexity.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-reasoning-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: each search call is interleaved between reasoning steps (turns), and multiple search-call turns can occur within a single rollout.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (no case adaptation; not CBR). Retrieved context is used verbatim and the policy adapts via RL fine-tuning rather than case revision.
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw retrieved passages (verbatim document text) injected as natural-language context enclosed in <information></information> tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw passage/document (no distillation or abstraction into strategies, guidelines, workflows, or skills).
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Retrieved-token loss masking: the policy-gradient (and KL) loss is computed only over LLM-generated tokens, masking out retrieved tokens so the model is not optimized to imitate retrieved content; this stabilizes training and improves robustness to retrieved context (ablation shows avg EM 0.431 with mask vs 0.343 without on Qwen2.5-7B-base). No explicit relevance evaluator, self-reflection, or distractor-filtering module.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: none (static external corpus only; no episodic/skill/workflow/procedural/graph/latent memory the agent writes to).
- **write back**: False: the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills back into any retrievable memory; only the policy LLM weights are updated by RL.
- **online growth**: False: the retrievable store (Wikipedia index) is frozen and does not grow during training or deployment.
- **write back trigger**: Never: there is no memory write-back mechanism.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Outcome-reward learning, not stored experience: failed rollouts receive reward 0 (EM) and successes receive 1, and both shape the policy via RL advantage estimation, but no failed or successful trajectories are explicitly stored or retrieved as memory. Rejection-sampling baseline uses success-only trajectories, but Search-R1 itself uses outcome rewards over all sampled rollouts (success and failure) without an experience store.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (no memory store; only model parameters are updated by gradient RL).
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partly: the DECISION of when to search and WHAT query to issue is a learned RL policy (PPO/GRPO) embedded in the LLM, but the underlying passage-selection (retriever ranking) is a fixed top-k dense retriever that is not itself learned. So query/timing policy is learned; document ranking is fixed top-k.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: N/A / single-agent: a single policy LLM with no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: NQ (Natural Questions), TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle (seven QA datasets). Knowledge corpus: 2018 Wikipedia dump; retriever: E5; top-3 passages. Training on merged NQ + HotpotQA train sets.
- **benchmark family**: QA (general single-hop: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA) and multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle).
- **baselines**:
> Without retrieval: Direct Inference, Chain-of-Thought (CoT). With retrieval (inference-time): RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1. Fine-tuning-based: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), R1 (RL fine-tuning without search, base and instruct), and Rejection Sampling (with search engine, using the same multi-turn rollout mechanism). All baselines use the same retriever, same number of retrieved docs, same corpus, same training data, and same pretrained LLMs for fair comparison.
- **key metrics**: Exact Match (EM) of the final answer against gold (rule-based string match); the same EM is also the outcome reward used for RL training. Auxiliary training-dynamics metrics: response length, number of valid search calls, training reward.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Retrieved-token loss masking: with mask avg EM 0.431 vs without mask 0.343 on Qwen2.5-7B-base (PPO), confirming masking drives stability/gains. (2) PPO vs GRPO: GRPO converges faster but can collapse after many steps; PPO is more stable; final rewards comparable (PPO chosen as default; e.g. 7B-base PPO 0.431 vs GRPO 0.350). (3) Base vs Instruct: instruct models converge faster and start higher, but final performance is similar after RL. (4) Response length and number of valid search calls: response length follows a decrease-then-increase-then-stabilize trend; valid search-call count grows over training as the model learns to search more. (5) Appendix studies: number of retrieved passages, GRPO group size, case studies (R1 vs Search-R1).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No: only end-to-end task EM is reported; intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are not reported separately (the retriever is frozen off-the-shelf).
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome (final-answer EM). Some intermediate process behavior is analyzed descriptively in training-dynamics studies (response length, number of valid search calls) but not scored as a quality metric; reward itself is purely outcome-based.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Discussed qualitatively via training dynamics rather than as a hard cost-vs-accuracy curve: number of valid search calls increases over training (more retrieval as performance improves), and response length grows due to appended retrieved passages. PPO is favored for stability over GRPO (which converges faster but can collapse). An appendix studies the number of retrieved passages. No explicit API-dollar-cost or latency/speedup numbers reported in the main text.
- **context budget and selection count**: Fixed-k: default 3 retrieved passages per search call across all retrieval-based methods (following Lin et al. 2023); rollouts are capped by a maximum action/search budget B. An appendix ablates the number of retrieved passages.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (uses existing QA datasets; not a new benchmark). Training merges NQ + HotpotQA train sets; evaluation on test/validation splits of seven datasets with EM.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> DeepSeek-R1 / DeepSeek-R1-Zero outcome-reward RL for reasoning (Guo et al. 2025); policy-gradient RL methods PPO (Schulman et al. 2017) and GRPO (Shao et al. 2024); standard RAG (Lewis et al. 2020); dense retrieval with E5 (Wang et al. 2022) over the Karpukhin et al. 2020 Wikipedia dump; implemented on the veRL RL training framework. Positioned as a search-augmented extension of R1-Zero-style RL.
- **contrasts with**:
> Inference-time RAG (single-round retrieve-then-generate), IRCoT and ReAct (prompting-based iterative retrieval, not RL-optimized), Search-o1 (inference-time agentic search), Toolformer/SFT and rejection-sampling (supervised trajectory imitation requiring high-quality labeled or filtered trajectories), and R1 (RL reasoning without a search engine). Search-R1 differs by learning search behavior end-to-end via outcome-reward RL with retrieved-token masking, requiring no annotated search trajectories.
- **lineage**:
> Group B (RAG for task-solving): an RL-trained, multi-turn, interleaved reason-and-retrieve QA agent grounded in a static external corpus; sits in the agentic-RAG / RL-for-search lineage extending DeepSeek-R1-Zero outcome-reward RL to retrieval-augmented reasoning, alongside contemporaneous works such as R1-Searcher and ReSearch.
