<a id="item-instructrag-planning"></a>
### 58. InstructRAG: Leveraging Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Instruction Graphs for LLM-Based Task Planning

2025  ·  arXiv 2504.13032  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13032)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: SIGIR 2025 (Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval); preprint arXiv:2504.13032. DOI: 10.1145/3726302.3730009. Accepted as Oral / full-score paper.
- **authors affiliation**: Zheng Wang, Shu Xian Teo, Jun Jie Chew, Wei Shi — all at Huawei Singapore Research Center, Singapore.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.13032
- **code url**:
> N/A (no official public code repository released; the author's homepage lists only Paper/Slides/Media links for this paper, with no Code link. The popular GitHub repo weizhepei/InstructRAG is a DIFFERENT, unrelated ICLR 2025 paper 'Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Self-synthesized rationales' and must not be confused with this work.)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: LLM-based task planning / agent planning. Spans multi-hop QA reasoning (HotpotQA), embodied tasks (ALFWorld), web shopping (Webshop), and scientific reasoning (ScienceWorld). Framed as grounding the thought-action-observation (TAO) planning process via RAG.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, multi-step agent planning following the thought-action-observation (TAO) / ReAct paradigm, where retrieval grounds the LLM's generation of thoughts and actions. Supervision is available: the method is trained offline on 'seen' tasks (split into support set for graph construction and query set for agent training) and then few-shot adapts to 'unseen' tasks. It is a multi-agent system (two cooperating learned agents: an RL-Agent and an ML-Agent) sitting around a single planner LLM (which may be trainable, e.g. GLM-4, or frozen, e.g. GPT-4o mini, DeepSeek-V2). Meta-learning setup with explicit train/few-shot-adapt/test stages.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Instruction paths — i.e., ordered sequences of correct past actions (instructions such as Search[Scott Derrickson], Lookup[nationality], Goto[shelf 6], Take[vase 2]) drawn from successful past task-solving experiences. New paths can also be composed by traversing/combining instructions across graph nodes (enlargeability), so retrieved paths need not have existed verbatim in the database.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING / induced memory of the agent's own past successful experiences (an instruction graph built offline from a support set), which is further EXPANDED at few-shot-adaptation time when the testing support set is inserted into the graph. It is not an external static document corpus or KB; it is a self-constructed episodic-experience store. Best characterized as a growing experience memory (induced offline + extended at adaptation time), not a frozen external corpus.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> The RL-Agent retrieves K candidate instruction PATHS (K=3 by default, a tunable hyperparameter), then the ML-Agent selects exactly ONE single best path to inject as the planning exemplar. So the operative objective is precision-driven single-best-path selection (1 of K) optimized by downstream end-to-end task metric, rather than a fixed top-k list returned to the LLM or an explicit minimal-set-completeness objective. The path itself must be complete enough to solve the question, but the retrieval target is the single most effective path.
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is framed as RAG-for-task-planning within a multi-agent meta-reinforcement-learning framework. It realizes some CBR-like mechanisms (retrieve-and-reuse of past solution paths, composition of new solutions) under different terminology (instruction graph, enlargeability, transferability).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Instruction path = a full (or composed sub-)trajectory of discrete actions, i.e., a workflow-routine / action-sequence. The atomic stored element is an instruction (a single action like Search[topic]); paths over these instructions (organized as graph nodes of clustered instructions and edges of tasks) are the retrieval unit. So: sub-trajectory / workflow-routine of actions, retrieved as a path over a KG-style instruction graph.
- **index source**:
> Growing memory induced offline from the training support set's successful instruction paths (graph constructed once during data pre-processing), then further extended at few-shot-adaptation time by inserting the testing support set into the graph (G -> G'). Not a static external corpus; not grown from query-set/test-query solutions online.
- **index structure topology**:
> A directed instruction GRAPH G(V,E). Each node is a SET of similar instructions (clustered via AKNN + cosine-similarity threshold delta); each edge is a SET of tasks (with associated questions) that traverse between two instruction nodes. Nodes act as junctions enabling new path combinations. This is a graph/dependency topology over actions, distinct from a flat vector index.
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid: AKNN dense-embedding similarity search (HNSW, Malkov & Yashunin) for instruction matching + graph traversal (DFS) controlled by a LEARNED RL policy (the RL-Agent) that decides node inclusion/exclusion, followed by a LEARNED dense bi-encoder selector (the ML-Agent, CLIP-style text encoders) for final single-path selection. So: dense + learned-policy + learned-bi-encoder hybrid.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> Two learned components with distinct signals. (1) RL-Agent: trained with downstream-task-effectiveness as RL reward — warm-start via binary cross-entropy on on-path/off-path node labels, then policy gradient (REINFORCE) where the reward r = Delta(A-hat, A) is the end-to-end LLM answer quality (e.g., F1 on HotpotQA). (2) ML-Agent: contrastive learning (InfoNCE-style QPA loss + QPM binary-classification loss in pre-training; fine-tuning uses contrastive loss with the best end-to-end-scored path as positive and hard negatives from the K retrieved paths). Both are meta-learned (MAML-style) for fast adaptation. So: RL/value-from-downstream-effectiveness for the policy + contrastive (similarity + downstream-best) for the selector.
- **query construction**:
> The raw input question Q-hat is the query. For the RL-Agent's MDP state, the query embedding v_{Q-hat} is compared (cosine similarity) against (a) the most similar instruction in a node, (b) the most similar task on the in-edge (task embedding = average of its questions' embeddings), and (c) the most similar question within the closest task. For the ML-Agent, the question is encoded by a transformer text encoder ([EOS]-token representation) and matched against path encodings. No explicit sub-query decomposition or synthetic query expansion.
- **query granularity**:
> Task-level / question-level (one query per input question Q-hat at planning time). There is also a two-level structure internally (a per-node step-level RL traversal decision builds paths, and a path-level selection), but the externally issued query is at the question/task level, issued once before planning.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot (plan-time): for each input question, the RL-Agent retrieves K candidate paths and the ML-Agent selects one path, which is injected into the prompt up front to guide the entire TAO planning sequence. Retrieval is not re-triggered per TAO step at inference.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule — retrieval is performed once per question at planning time (no token-confidence, uncertainty, reflection-token, or agent-initiated dynamic trigger). Internally the RL-Agent's per-node include/exclude decision is governed by its learned policy over cosine-similarity states, but this is path construction, not a learned WHEN-to-retrieve trigger.
- **reranking**:
> Effectively yes: a two-stage selection. Stage 1 the RL-Agent retrieves/builds K candidate paths via learned graph traversal; Stage 2 the ML-Agent (a learned CLIP-style bi-encoder, meta-learned) acts as a learned reranker/selector that picks the single most relevant path by question-path cosine similarity. Not a classic cross-encoder; it is a learned bi-encoder selection trained with contrastive + downstream-effectiveness signals.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Selection/reranking down to a single best path (decompose-then-recompose at the graph level: instructions are recombined into new paths, then one path is selected). No reason-in-documents distillation or compression of the path text itself; the selected path is injected as a structured plan. Noise is handled implicitly via diverse instruction combinations rather than an explicit relevance-filter module.
- **tool document engineering**:
> N/A — instructions/actions are not tool docstrings; they are action templates (e.g., Search[topic], Lookup[entity], Goto[loc], Take[obj]). Instruction text is embedded directly (via the embedding model used for AKNN) and clustered into nodes by cosine similarity with threshold delta=0.4; no synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field tool embedding.
- **dynamic index and protocol**:
> N/A — no live tool index, no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool integration protocol. The 'instructions' are environment actions in ReAct-style task environments, not external API tools. The graph is static after offline construction except for the one-time extension with the testing support set at adaptation time.
- **tool dependency awareness**:
> Partial in a planning (not tool) sense: predefined transition rules may constrain the RL-Agent's action space (e.g., on HotpotQA, disallow Lookup before a Search on the topic — following KnowAgent), capturing prerequisite/ordering constraints between actions. The graph edges also encode legal action transitions. But there is no tool-dependency graph, shared-auth, or bipartite tool KG.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation as a planning exemplar. The single selected instruction path P-hat is written into a 4-part prompt: (1) Task Description (the question), (2) Instruction Definitions (semantics of each action type), (3) Planning Path (the retrieved/composed path as a structured step-by-step plan), and (4) Demonstrations (example planning paths). The LLM then generates the answer following the TAO process grounded in this plan. The path's downstream effectiveness is also fed back as the RL-Agent reward (training signal).
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-plan with one-shot exemplar injection: the RL-Agent + ML-Agent retrieve and select a path BEFORE the LLM plans, and that path is provided as an in-context plan/exemplar guiding the whole TAO rollout. Not interleaved per-step at inference, not inside MCTS/tree search at planning time. (Internally the RL-Agent does a DFS tree traversal over the instruction graph to build candidate paths, but that is the retrieval module, separate from the LLM's planning.)
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer / per-question (one retrieval-and-selection per question, then the LLM completes the full TAO plan). Retrieval is not woven per-CoT-step, per-sentence, or per-tool-call at inference time.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Primarily verbatim-ICL-exemplar reuse of the selected path, augmented by graph-level recomposition (new paths are synthesized by combining stored instructions across junction nodes via RL-guided traversal, enabling coverage of questions never seen verbatim — 'enlargeability'). No per-instance LLM-prompted rewriting or execution-feedback repair of an individual retrieved case at test time; adaptation to new tasks is via MAML-style few-shot meta-update of the two agents' parameters.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> A free-text structured planning path (an ordered sequence of action instructions, e.g., Search[..]->Lookup[..]->Search[..]->Lookup[..]) injected as the 'Planning Path' section of the prompt, alongside instruction definitions and demonstrations. It is a free-text workflow/plan, not a latent token, not an executable program.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: A reusable workflow / action-sequence routine (mid-level): more abstract than a single demonstration (it is a composable path that can be recombined across tasks) but still concrete action-level instructions rather than a distilled natural-language strategy or guideline.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Robustness arises from the diverse instruction combinations enabled by the graph plus the learned RL-Agent path-construction and ML-Agent path-selection, which help pick appropriate paths and downweight bad ones; the agents are trained against downstream effectiveness (reward = answer quality), implicitly disfavoring paths that yield poor answers. Demonstrated empirically: with 50% erroneous historical paths injected, InstructRAG's F1 drops only ~11.1% (37.17 -> 33.04) vs. RAP dropping from 29.82 -> 21.72. No explicit self-reflection relevance evaluator or distractor-aware SFT module.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Graph-structured experience memory (an instruction graph of past successful action paths) — i.e., a workflow/procedural memory organized as a directed graph (nodes = instruction sets, edges = task sets). Best tagged: graph + procedural/workflow.
- **write back**:
> Yes, but only at construction/adaptation time, not during deployment inference. Successful instruction paths from the training support set are written into the graph during offline construction, and the testing support set's paths are inserted into the graph (G -> G') during the few-shot adaptation stage. New query-set solutions produced during testing are NOT written back into the graph.
- **online growth**:
> No (not during test-time inference). The store grows in two discrete offline/adaptation phases (initial offline construction from training support set; one-time extension with the testing support set at few-shot adaptation). It does not continuously grow from solved test queries during deployment.
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success only, at dataset-preparation/adaptation time: only instruction paths that correctly solve their question (verified against ground truth) are inserted into the graph. There is no per-step, reflective, or human-validated online write trigger during inference; failed paths are excluded from the clean graph (and are only added artificially in the noise-robustness experiment).
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success-only for the memory store: the graph is built from correct/successful instruction paths only; failed paths are deliberately excluded (failed paths are injected only in the noise-robustness stress test, not used as a learning signal). However, the ML-Agent's contrastive fine-tuning uses hard NEGATIVES (the non-best among the K retrieved paths and paths from other questions) as a discriminative signal, and the RL-Agent learns from low rewards on poor paths — so negative/failure signals are used in TRAINING the retrievers, but failed experiences are not stored as retrievable corrective rules.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Append-only with dedup-style merging into node sets: new instructions are either merged into an existing similar node (if cosine similarity >= delta, e.g., identical instructions merge with similarity 1.0) or create a new node (if < delta); tasks are appended to edge sets. Existing stored instructions/paths are not mutated, refined, overwritten, or pruned/forgotten. The graph topology grows monotonically; trainable agent parameters (not memory entries) are what get updated via meta-learning.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Yes. Retrieval is explicitly a LEARNED policy: the RL-Agent models graph traversal as a Markov Decision Process and learns pi_theta(a|s) (include/exclude node) via warm-start (BCE) + REINFORCE policy gradient with end-to-end reward; the ML-Agent learns a contrastive selection policy; both are meta-trained (MAML, Finn et al. 2017). This is decidedly NOT fixed similarity top-k.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> No cross-agent/cross-framework memory sharing in the collective-memory sense. It is a multi-agent system (RL-Agent + ML-Agent cooperating around one planner LLM via a shared reward loop), and the single instruction graph is shared between these two cooperating modules, but there is no sharing of memory across multiple independent agents or heterogeneous agent frameworks. Memory is a single shared private store for one InstructRAG instance.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> HotpotQA (multi-hop QA, ~113K Wikipedia QA pairs; F1), ALFWorld (embodied household tasks; success rate), Webshop (web-shopping navigation; reward 0-1), ScienceWorld (elementary-school scientific reasoning; reward 0-1, used for cross-dataset generalization with training on HotpotQA).
- **benchmark family**: QA / multi-hop (HotpotQA); embodied (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld); web (Webshop). Mix of multi-hop QA, embodied, and web-agent families.
- **baselines**: ReAct, WKM (World Knowledge Model), Reflexion, GenGround, and RAP (Retrieval-Augmented Planning; identified as the best baseline). All run on the same three backbone LLMs (GLM-4, GPT-4o mini, DeepSeek-V2) with matched retrievers/setups. WKM not reported on HotpotQA.
- **key metrics**:
> F1 score (HotpotQA), success rate (ALFWorld), reward score 0-1 (Webshop, ScienceWorld). Plus runtime/efficiency: graph construction time (s), training time (hours), few-shot adaptation time (mins/task), testing time (s), and number of graph nodes. All main results reported statistically significant (t-test, p<0.05).
- **headline result**:
> Up to 19.2% improvement over the best existing approach (RAP) on HotpotQA. Concretely, on unseen tasks: improvements of 19.2% (HotpotQA), 9.3% (ALFWorld), and 6.1% (Webshop) over RAP. Best absolute numbers with DeepSeek-V2 on unseen tasks: HotpotQA F1 37.17 (vs RAP 29.82), ALFWorld success 81.34 (vs RAP 72.39), Webshop reward 74.00 (vs RAP 72.72).
- **ablations**:
> Component ablation on HotpotQA (DeepSeek-V2, F1=37.17 full): w/o Instruction Graph 32.87 (graph contributes ~11.6%); w/o RL-Agent 33.45 (RL-Agent ~11.1%); w/o warm-start in RL-Agent 34.37; w/o policy gradient in RL-Agent 36.18; w/o ML-Agent 34.78 (ML-Agent ~6.9%); w/o pre-training in ML-Agent 36.19; w/o fine-tuning in ML-Agent 36.24. Parameter studies: threshold delta swept 0.0-1.0 (best at 0.4, F1=37.17; #nodes grows 5->725; delta=1.0 collapses graph to individual paths losing recombination), and K (candidate paths) swept 1-5 (F1 converges at K=3=37.17; testing time grows with K). Noise robustness (Table 4): stable up to 50% erroneous paths (only -11.1%). Cross-dataset generalization (Table 2): HotpotQA->ScienceWorld beats RAP by 6-10%. Seen-task gains (Table 3): +21.9%/+10.8%/+10.4%. Few-shot scaling (Fig 2): effectiveness stable across #tasks; converges around 80% of samples.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No — the paper reports end-to-end task metrics (F1 / success rate / reward) only. It does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k, nDCG, or path-retrieval-completeness reported separately). The RL reward is itself the end-to-end metric, so retrieval quality is measured only through downstream task performance.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Predominantly outcome-only (final answer F1 / task success / reward). No separate process-quality metrics such as reasoning faithfulness, step-wise retrieval accuracy, or trajectory-quality scoring are reported; intermediate path quality is captured only implicitly via the end-to-end reward used to train the agents.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k retrieval of K=3 candidate paths (tuned; converges at 3), then exactly ONE selected path injected into the prompt. The prompt is a fixed 4-part structure (Task Description, Instruction Definitions, Planning Path, Demonstrations). No explicit token-budget cap or reranked-then-truncated scheme; effectively a single-path budget. graph construction threshold delta=0.4; RL-Agent reward discount 0.99, lr 0.001.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A — this is a method paper, not a survey.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A — uses existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one. (Context: HotpotQA ~113K QA pairs; meta-learning task splits defined per dataset, e.g. HotpotQA's 12 answer types split 6 seen / 6 unseen; Webshop split 60% categories train / rest test; ALFWorld uses its provided seen/unseen split; ScienceWorld used entirely as unseen cross-dataset transfer.)

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> ReAct / thought-action-observation (TAO) planning paradigm (Yao et al. 2022b); RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024, retrieval-augmented planning over stored experiences) as the closest predecessor it improves on; MAML model-agnostic meta-learning (Finn et al. 2017) and meta-ICL methods (MetaICL/MAML-en-LLM/MTIL) for transferability; REINFORCE (Williams 1992) for the RL policy; CLIP-style dual text encoders (Radford et al. 2021) for the ML-Agent; HNSW/AKNN (Malkov & Yashunin 2018) for instruction indexing; KnowAgent (Zhu et al. 2024) for action-transition rules. Also relates to the authors' own RAG line (M-RAG ACL'24, EMG-RAG EMNLP'24).
- **contrasts with**:
> RAP (stores past experiences as independent context/action-observation trajectories and retrieves by AKNN similarity without enlargeability/transferability — InstructRAG instead organizes them in a recombinable graph and learns retrieval); GenGround (generate-then-ground for multi-hop reasoning, search-engine dependent); PlanRAG (plan-then-retrieve, decision-QA / video-game domain specific); RAT (iterative CoT revision); plain prompting/fine-tuning planners ReAct, Reflexion, WKM, FireAct, NAT, ETO that are bounded by the LLM's own knowledge and do not leverage a structured retrievable experience store.
- **lineage**:
> Sits in the experience/memory-augmented LLM-planning lineage (Group C: RAG planning) — a structured-memory planner that retrieves over an induced graph of past task paths and adds a learned RL retrieval policy + meta-learned selector. Bridges retrieval-augmented planning (RAP/RAT/GenGround/PlanRAG) with multi-agent meta-reinforcement learning, distinguished by (i) graph-organized recombinable instruction paths (enlargeability) and (ii) MAML-based fast task transfer (transferability).

### 59. MINDSTORES: Memory-Informed Neural Decision Synthesis for Task-Oriented Reinforcement in Embodied Systems

2025  ·  arXiv 2501.19318  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19318)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**: Anirudh Chari* and Suraj Reddy* (equal contribution), Aditya Tiwari, Richard Lian, Brian Zhou. arXiv lists affiliations as MIT (Chari, Reddy, Lian), Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (Tiwari), and Harvard University (Zhou); the project page lists all authors under a37.ai.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19318

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Embodied planning / decision-making: LLM high-level planning for an embodied agent in an open-world Minecraft environment (MineDojo), with a low-level behavior-cloning controller executing actions.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, online, single-agent embodied planning in the open-world MineDojo (Minecraft) simulator. The LLM acts as a zero-shot high-level planner ('brain') that decomposes goals into step-by-step plans, while a behavior-cloning controller ('body') maps plans to 42 discrete low-level actions. No model fine-tuning; learning happens entirely through an accumulating natural-language experience database. Supervision is the environment's task-completion reward/done signal (self-supervised via outcomes); each task evaluated over 30 trials with randomized initial states (seed 42). Long-horizon tasks (episodes 3,000-12,000 steps) with irreversible-error dynamics and task dependencies (e.g., stone tools required before iron mining).
- **what is retrieved**: Past experiences stored as natural-language (state, task, plan, outcome) tuples; also LLM-generated insights synthesized from those retrieved experiences. Both successful and failed past episodes are stored and retrievable.
- **retrieval grounding**: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes during deployment. The (state,task,plan,outcome) experience database is built online from the agent's own interactions; it is not a static external corpus.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k similarity retrieval objective. The system retrieves the k most similar past experiences (optimal k=5; tested k=1,3,5,10,20) ranked by weighted cosine similarity; there is no notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> Realizes a Retrieve-Reuse-Retain CBR cycle without naming it: Retrieve (top-k similar (s,t,p,o) experiences), Reuse (LLM adapts retrieved cases/insights into a new plan), Retain (writes the new experience tuple back). Revise is present as plan refinement via outcome prediction but operates on the new plan rather than mutating stored cases. Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial (new-plan revision, not stored-case revision), Retain: yes].
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it is framed via cognitive 'mental models' (Craik 1952) and 'experience-augmented planning'. It realizes CBR-like mechanisms under different terminology.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: A (state, task, plan, outcome) experience tuple — i.e., a case (problem-context-solution-result) represented as natural-language paragraphs. Effectively a full episode/trajectory-level experience record rather than a token snippet or single demo.
- **index source**: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The database starts empty (or per-task small, e.g., 26 entries for Wooden Door) and grows from the agent's own executed episodes during deployment (e.g., to 355 entries for Minecart in the continuous-building experiment).
- **index structure topology**: Flat vector index. Each of state/task/plan/outcome is embedded with Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, treated as 768-dim, L2-normalized) and stored in a FAISS IndexFlatL2 (flat L2 / cosine-similarity) index. No graph or hierarchical structure.
- **retriever type**: Dense retriever (off-the-shelf sentence-embedding similarity search). Sentence-BERT embeddings + FAISS cosine/L2 nearest-neighbor search.
- **retriever learning signal**: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a frozen pretrained Sentence-BERT encoder with fixed manually-set field weights (lambda_s=0.4, lambda_t=0.4, lambda_p=0.2); it is not trained or learned via any task/LM/RL signal.
- **query construction**:
> Raw natural-language descriptions of the current state and task form the query keys; for outcome prediction the proposed plan is added. Similarity is computed as a weighted sum over fields (state, task, and optionally plan), each embedded by the same sentence transformer. State/task descriptions and the plan are themselves produced by LLM prompts over the structured environment JSON.
- **query granularity**: Two-level retrieval. (1) State/task-level retrieval (weights on s and t) to inform plan generation; (2) plan-conditioned retrieval (weights on s, t, p) to predict the proposed plan's outcome before execution.
- **when to retrieve**:
> Iterative. Retrieval is invoked at plan-generation time (state/task neighbors) and again inside the plan-refinement loop for outcome prediction (plan neighbors), repeated each time the plan is revised until predicted success, and re-triggered for each new sub-task within the observe-retrieve-synthesize-act-log cycle.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule tied to the planning loop: retrieve at each new sub-task/state for plan generation, and retrieve again to predict outcomes whenever a candidate plan is (re)generated. The refinement loop continues (re-retrieving and revising) while the predicted outcome is not 'success'. There is no learned router, token-confidence, or attention-based trigger.
- **reranking**: None. A single weighted-cosine-similarity top-k ranking is used; no separate reranking stage (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker).
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> LLM insight synthesis (a form of reason-over-documents distillation): the LLM analyzes the retrieved k experiences to produce 'insights' about common failure modes to avoid, successful strategies to adapt, and environmental dynamics, which are then injected alongside the raw retrieved experiences into the plan-generation prompt. No explicit compression, distractor filtering, or decompose-recompose beyond this analysis step.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; experiences are NL episode tuples, not tool/API documents).
- **index content separation**: N/A. No lightweight-index-vs-heavy-content separation; the embedded NL experience tuples are both the index keys and the retrieved content.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol; not a tool-retrieval system).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A as a tool-retrieval mechanism. (Task/crafting dependencies such as 'stone pickaxe before iron mining' are handled implicitly by the LLM reasoning over retrieved experiences and insights, not via an explicit dependency graph over retrievable tools.)

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation plus LLM-based case adaptation. Retrieved experiences and synthesized insights condition the LLM's plan generation; retrieved similar past plans/outcomes drive an outcome-prediction step that triggers iterative plan revision before execution.
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-plan with an iterative predict-and-refine loop. Pipeline (Algorithm 1): retrieve top-k state/task experiences -> LLM analyze_experiences (insights) -> LLM generate_plan -> loop{ retrieve similar plans -> analyze_outcomes -> if predicted success break, else revise_plan } -> execute_plan -> add new experience to database. Closed loop: observe, retrieve, synthesize, act, log.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-plan / per-sub-task: retrieval and outcome-prediction are interleaved at the granularity of generating and revising a high-level plan for the current sub-task (before execution), not per CoT-token or per individual low-level action.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation plus prediction-driven revision: the LLM synthesizes insights from retrieved cases and generates a plan (case reuse/adaptation), then iteratively revises the plan based on predicted outcomes from similar past plans before execution (a predicted-feedback-driven revision, not execution-feedback within the same loop and not RL fine-tuning).
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw natural-language experience tuples (state, task, plan, outcome paragraphs) injected verbatim into the prompt, supplemented by LLM-distilled free-text insights derived from them. Experiences are deliberately natural language rather than vectors or symbolic representations.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw natural-language trajectory/experience (state-task-plan-outcome case), additionally abstracted at use-time into distilled strategy/insight statements (e.g., causal rules like 'stone tools are prerequisites for iron mining') by the LLM analysis step.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Outcome-prediction-based self-validation: before execution, the system predicts the proposed plan's likely outcome from similar past plans and iteratively revises plans predicted to fail, which guards against acting on misleading retrieved context. The LLM insight-analysis step also serves to filter/interpret retrieved experiences. No retriever-aware training or explicit distractor-aware SFT.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Episodic experience memory (natural-language (state,task,plan,outcome) experience database). Framed as a persistent 'mental model'.
- **write back**: True. After executing a plan, the new experience tuple (s_t, t_t, p_t, outcome) is added to the database D for future retrieval (Algorithm 1: D.add(...)).
- **online growth**: Yes. The store grows during deployment/test-time as the agent executes tasks; the continuous-building experiment shows the database expanding from 26 entries (Wooden Door) to 355 entries (Minecart) without resetting between tasks.
- **write back trigger**:
> On every executed episode (success and failure alike): after plan execution the resulting experience tuple, including failure descriptions in the outcome field, is stored. Writes occur per executed plan/sub-task outcome rather than only on success or only after explicit self-critique.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success and failure both stored and retrieved. The outcome field explicitly records the execution result and a failure description if applicable; the LLM analyzes retrieved experiences specifically to identify 'common failure modes to avoid' (e.g., 'wooden pickaxes break mining iron'), enabling counterfactual/corrective reasoning from negative experiences.
- **memory evolution update**: Append-only. New experience tuples are added to the FAISS index; the paper describes no dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or pruning of existing entries (it notes future work on experience pruning and hierarchical memory as a limitation).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed weighted-similarity top-k over off-the-shelf embeddings, not a learned or RL-optimized policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No. Single-agent private experience database; no sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> MineDojo (Minecraft simulation environment, Fan et al. 2022). 53 Minecraft tasks across 8 complexity tiers MT1-MT8 (MT1 Basic, MT2 Tool, MT3 Hunt and Food, MT4 Dig-down, MT5 Equipment, MT6 Tool-Complex, MT7 IronStage, MT8 Challenge/Diamond), grouped into Basic (MT1-MT2), Intermediate (MT3-MT5), Advanced (MT6-MT8). Observation space: RGB view, GPS, inventory; 42 discrete actions. Behavior-cloning controller (MineCLIP-based) trained on human demonstrations.
- **benchmark family**: embodied (Minecraft / MineDojo).
- **baselines**:
> DEPS (Describe-Explain-Plan-Select; Wang et al. 2024c) — primary baseline, using the authors' own DEPS implementation without the experience database for fair comparison; Voyager (Wang et al. 2023); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023). Single-Shot (DEPS without iterative refinement) and No-Experience (retrieval removed) serve as internal ablation baselines.
- **key metrics**:
> Success Rate (% task completion across 30 trials); Learning Efficiency / Novel Learning Iterations (iterations or time-steps to skill mastery); Complexity Scaling (success vs MT tier); Retrieval Impact (success rate vs k); Continuous Learning (steps per task as the database grows).
- **headline result**:
> 9.4% mean improvement in open-world planning success rate over DEPS across MineCraft tasks (MT1-MT8), with the largest gains on intermediate-complexity tasks (e.g., +20.0% on MT3 Painting: 96.7% vs 76.7%; +11.0% average across intermediate tasks). Both systems reach 0% on the MT8 diamond task.
- **ablations**:
> (1) No Experience: removing the retrieval/experience component reduces the method to DEPS-like single-shot planning, removing the gains. (2) Fixed k values (k=1,3,5,10,20): k=5 found optimal overall; simple tasks improve steadily with k while complex tasks need larger k, and advanced tasks (Minecart, Diamond) remain near-unachievable regardless of k. (3) Single-Shot: disabling iterative plan refinement (i.e., DEPS) lowers success. Also the field-weight choice (lambda_s=0.4, lambda_t=0.4, lambda_p=0.2) was set via these studies. Table 4 isolates the effect of outcome prediction (MINDSTORES with prediction vs DEPS without) per tier.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate, learning iterations, steps) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately. Retrieval is examined only indirectly via success-rate-vs-k curves.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome metrics (task success rate). Some process-adjacent efficiency metrics are reported: novel-learning iterations to mastery and time-steps/steps-to-completion (Tables 3 and 4, Figures 4 and 6), which capture learning/planning efficiency but not reasoning faithfulness or step-wise retrieval accuracy.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (not a benchmark paper; it uses MineDojo's existing tasks). For reference, it evaluates on 53 MineCraft tasks across MT1-MT8, 30 trials each, episodes 3,000-12,000 steps; best-system difficulty signal: MT8 diamond = 0% for all methods, indicating the hardest tasks remain unsolved.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> DEPS (Describe, Explain, Plan and Select; Wang et al. 2024c) — MINDSTORES keeps DEPS's iterative verbal-feedback planning foundation and adds a persistent experience database. MineDojo (Fan et al. 2022) environment and MineCLIP/behavior-cloning controller. Sentence-BERT (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) embeddings and FAISS for retrieval. GPT-4 as the LLM planner/reasoner. Conceptually grounded in Craik's (1952) mental-models theory.
- **contrasts with**:
> Zero-shot/no-memory LLM planners that start fresh each episode (DEPS, ProgPrompt, Inner Monologue); skill-library/code-memory agents with opaque, non-interpretable representations (Voyager's code snippets, PaLM-E's latent vectors); feedback-loop agents lacking persistent cross-episode memory (Reflexion, ReAct); memory-augmented planners with shallow/non-causal reasoning evaluated mainly on narrow benchmarks like ALFRED (ExpeL, E2CL, AdaPlanner); latent/symbolic world-model and tree-search methods (PIGLeT, RAP, DreamerV3, LATS).
- **lineage**:
> Group C (RAG planning): experience/memory-augmented LLM planning for embodied agents. Sits in the lineage of zero-shot LLM open-world planners (Inner Monologue -> DEPS -> Voyager) extended with growing episodic natural-language experience memory; closely related to experiential-learner memory planners (Reflexion, ExpeL, AdaPlanner, E2CL), distinguished by storing interpretable (state,task,plan,outcome) NL tuples retrieved for plan refinement and outcome prediction in an open-world (MineDojo) setting.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- code_url
- context_budget_and_selection_count
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- venue

<a id="item-webragent"></a>
### 60. WebRAGent / GAE-Retriever (Multimodal Trajectory Retrieval and Retrieval-Augmented Web Agent; UATD + GAE-Bench)

2025  ·  OpenReview 2025 (GAE-Bench/UATD)  ·  [paper](https://openreview.net/forum?id=L1VPZFbAcu)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**:
> Core GAE-Retriever/UATD/GAE-Bench paper 'Universal Retrieval for Multimodal Trajectory Modeling' accepted as a poster at the Workshop on Computer-Use Agents @ ICML 2025 (WCUA 2025; OpenReview id wNFgL1c6It, Submission 37) and posted as arXiv:2506.22056 (cs.AI, 27 Jun 2025). The extended WebRAGent version 'WebRAGent: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multimodal Web Agent Planning' was submitted to ICLR 2026 (OpenReview id L1VPZFbAcu, Submission 17081, 19 Sept 2025) and REJECTED (Program Chairs decision 26 Jan 2026; scores 2/6/4/4). A further-revised version 'Learning Multimodal Trajectory Representations for Web Agent Planning' (OpenReview id XZputtLpjz, Mar 2026) exists. Task-specified venue label: OpenReview 2025 (GAE-Bench/UATD).
- **paper url**: https://openreview.net/forum?id=L1VPZFbAcu (ICLR 2026 WebRAGent submission; core paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.22056 and https://openreview.net/forum?id=wNFgL1c6It)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: web (GUI web-agent planning) plus multimodal information retrieval for agent trajectories. The retriever (GAE-Retriever) targets GUI agent trajectory retrieval across web/mobile/desktop sources; the downstream agent (WebRAGent) is a retrieval-augmented web-navigation agent.
- **problem setting**:
> Two coupled settings. (1) Offline supervised multimodal trajectory retrieval: given a query that can be text, a state (screenshot), a full trajectory, or a sub-trajectory, retrieve the matching state/trajectory/sub-trajectory from a candidate corpus; a VLM-based retriever is trained with contrastive learning on labeled positive pairs derived from human-annotated demonstrations (single-agent, supervision = labeled retrieval pairs from UATD/GAE-Bench-lite). (2) Interactive, single-agent retrieval-augmented web-agent planning: WebRAGent is a complete web agent (planner = GPT-4.1 in DOM mode, OpenAI computer-use-preview in Vision mode) that, at each step, retrieves step-level experience knowledge from a trajectory knowledge base via GAE-Retriever, reranks it with an LLM (GPT-4o), and conditions next-action prediction on the retrieved textual or visual exemplars. It runs in live, dynamic web environments (Online-Mind2Web), uses chain-of-thought reasoning, explicit history memory, and an LLM-as-judge reward module; the only difference between the non-retrieval baseline and WebRAGent is the presence/absence of the retrieval module.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Multimodal GUI agent experience: states (screenshots), full trajectories, sub-trajectories/intervals, and step-level demonstrations (observation + action). In WebRAGent the retrieved unit is step-level experience knowledge from two knowledge bases: D_text (natural-language description of observation o~ + demonstration action a~ for the step) and D_vision (the step screenshot + structured action: operation type, target bounding box, input value). At the benchmark level, queries/targets are states, trajectories, or sub-trajectories.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> STATIC external corpus (a curated demonstration/trajectory store). The retrievable store is the Unified Agent Trajectory Dataset (UATD)/GAE-Bench candidate set built offline from human-annotated demonstrations across five GUI sources; WebRAGent retrieves from this fixed trajectory knowledge base. It is NOT a growing/episodic memory the agent writes during deployment (no online write-back of new trajectories).
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking objective. The retriever is trained and evaluated with InfoNCE contrastive loss and Recall@1/5/10; WebRAGent retrieves a top-k candidate set (Top-k=5 or 10 used on Online-Mind2Web) that is then LLM-reranked. There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven recommendation objective.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes (learned dense multimodal retrieval + LLM rerank of past demonstrations), Reuse: yes (retrieved step-level exemplars injected into the planner, with an explicit Reuse-Level decision for high-level vs element-level adaptation), Revise: partial (the planner adapts/borrows strategy from analogous exemplars and an LLM-as-judge reward triggers reset-and-recover, but there is no formal per-case revise-and-store step), Retain: no (no write-back of new cases into the corpus)].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The work frames itself as multimodal trajectory representation learning / retrieval-augmented generation for web agents; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes Retrieve/Reuse mechanisms (and references skill abstraction, Agent Workflow Memory, SkillWeaver, RaDA, Synapse) under a RAG/representation-learning framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Heterogeneous multimodal units: single state s_i (a screenshot observation), full trajectory tau, or trajectory sub-sequence tau_{i:j} (ranging from a single state-action pair to the whole trajectory). In WebRAGent specifically, the retrieved unit is a step-level (observation, action) demonstration record (full-trajectory / sub-trajectory at training time; per-step exemplar at agent inference time).
- **index source**:
> Static corpus, offline-induced. UATD is built offline from five open-source GUI benchmarks (Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct): 7,747 human-annotated demonstrations and 82,793 states. GAE-Bench (714,628 positive pairs via 12 extraction patterns) and GAE-Bench-lite (trajectories capped at <10 steps; 514,956 train / 21,805 in-domain / 27,139 out-of-domain, 574,222 candidates) are derived offline. The WebRAGent retrieval database is the UATD trajectory store. Frozen at deployment (no online growth).
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat vector index over VLM embeddings (dense nearest-neighbor by maximum dot-product similarity). Candidate sets are organized by retrieval-target type (state / trajectory / interval) per data source (Table 5), and GAE-Bench has a typed task structure (6 tasks / 12 subtasks), but there is no graph or learned hierarchy in the retrieval index itself.
- **retriever type**:
> Learned dense multimodal retriever (VLM-as-retriever). GAE-Retriever is a contrastive embedding model built on VLM2Vec with a Qwen2-VL (Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct) backbone, embedding multimodal trajectories via the last-token final-layer representation. Used together with an LLM-based reranker (GPT-4o) in WebRAGent (hybrid retrieve-then-LLM-rerank).
- **retriever learning signal**:
> Contrastive on similarity labels (downstream/task-supervised). GAE-Retriever is trained with the InfoNCE contrastive objective over positive retrieval pairs from GAE-Bench-lite, using large in-batch negatives enabled by GradCache. Positives include gold trajectories (q->tau_equiv from UATD ground truth) and silver trajectories (q->tau_sim, entity-substituted hard positives forcing procedural/skill-level invariance). Trained with LoRA (rank 8) on Qwen2-VL-Instruct, 16x H800 GPUs, accumulated batch size 2,048, 256 steps (~1,044 GPU hours), lr 5e-5. Not RL; not LM-feedback; not preference/Bradley-Terry.
- **query construction**:
> Query q-tilde is the raw input combined with a task-specific instruction (one of the 12 GAE-Bench instruction templates) plus a contextual trajectory description; the key/value follow a recursive grammar over states, actions, sub-trajectories, and full trajectories. In WebRAGent the query is the current state/context aligned to the agent's present step (state-conditioned, step-level retrieval). No automatic sub-query decomposition; entity substitution is used only to synthesize silver TRAINING pairs, not query-time expansion.
- **query granularity**:
> Both / two-level. At benchmark level queries span task-level (q->tau, q->s), state/step-level ((q,s)->s', (q,s)->tau), and trajectory-level ((q,tau)->tau', (q,tau)->s). In WebRAGent retrieval is step/state-level: step-level experience knowledge aligned with the current state is retrieved at each planning step.
- **when to retrieve**:
> Iterative (per-step) in WebRAGent: retrieval is performed at each planning step using the current state, followed by LLM reranking, before the next action is predicted. (The retriever benchmark itself is a one-shot query->candidate task.) No uncertainty-triggered or learned-router gating; retrieval runs on a fixed per-step schedule.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule (per-step, unconditional). WebRAGent issues a retrieval + rerank call at every planning step (one GAE-Retriever encoding + embedding retrieval + LLM rerank per step). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated trigger.
- **reranking**:
> Yes. An LLM-based reranker (GPT-4o) refines the GAE-Retriever Top-k candidates. The reranking prompt (Appendix E.2, Snippet 6) explicitly instructs the LLM to rank by (1) visual similarity of the screenshot, (2) consistency of UI elements/layout, and (3) semantic relevance of the task description. Reranking is the dominant inference-time cost (3.54 s/step without cache vs 0.39 s/step retrieval; reduced to ~0.0002 s/step with a two-level LLM-side cache, 9.24x speedup). Reported: with reranking, setting Top-k=5 improves R@1 by ~36% and Top-k=10 by ~54% on Online-Mind2Web.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Rerank + compression. Post-retrieval processing = LLM-based reranking (cross-encoder-style relevance refinement) plus engineering optimizations (image compression / optimized encoding to reduce token consumption) before the retrieved exemplars are injected into the planner. No reason-in-documents distillation or decompose-then-recompose.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (not a tool/API retrieval method; retrieved items are GUI trajectory states/steps, not tool documents).
- **index content separation**:
> Partial: GAE-Retriever produces a lightweight dense embedding index for fast nearest-neighbor retrieval, after which heavier content (full screenshots + structured actions / textual descriptions) is loaded and LLM-reranked. Token selection separates salient UI tokens from redundant background, and image compression/two-level caching are used to manage on-demand heavy-content loading. There is no formal progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content protocol.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (the trajectory store is a static internally-managed corpus, not a live tool registry with MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful/function-calling sync).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation / case (exemplar) reuse. Reranked step-level textual (D_text) or visual (D_vision) knowledge is injected into the planner's prompt to guide chain-of-thought reasoning and next-action prediction. The planner prompt includes a 'Reuse Level Decision' mechanism instructing the agent to identify HIGH_LEVEL similarity (borrow intent/strategy) when element-level details do not match, so silver/analogous exemplars provide structural guidance rather than verbatim copying. No fine-tuning of the planner on retrieved items; everything is in-context. (At the retriever level, the learned embeddings are the artifact validated downstream.)
- **planning integration**:
> Per-step interleaved, retrieve-then-plan within an agent loop. At each step WebRAGent observes (DOM or screenshot), retrieves + reranks step-level experience knowledge aligned to the current state, then the planner (GPT-4.1 DOM mode / computer-use-preview Vision mode) performs long-horizon task decomposition and execution via CoT with explicit history memory and an LLM-as-judge reward. Not one-shot exemplars at plan time; not MCTS/tree search.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-step (per planning step within the rollout): one retrieval+rerank+inject cycle per action decision. Not per-CoT-token or per-sentence.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation of retrieved exemplars: the planner reuses retrieved step-level demonstrations as guidance, applying a 'Reuse Level Decision' (HIGH_LEVEL strategy borrowing vs element-level reuse) so that analogous/silver trajectories provide structural/procedural guidance rather than verbatim solutions; an LLM-as-judge reward enables execution-feedback-driven recovery (reset-and-recover) within the episode. No RL reuse-finetuning of the planner.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Surface forms injected: (i) D_text - natural-language description of the observation plus the demonstration action for the step; (ii) D_vision - the step screenshot plus a structured action (operation, target bounding box, value). These are raw/lightly-structured per-step demonstration records, not distilled free-text strategies, executable programs, or latent tokens. (The retriever internally encodes trajectories as dense latent embeddings, but injected knowledge is human-readable text/image exemplars.)
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Mixed: both raw single demonstrations / state-action steps (low-level interaction details: operation type, target bounding box, value, screenshot) AND higher-level procedural/strategy guidance. The training design (silver trajectories) deliberately pushes the embedding to capture skill-level procedural similarity ('Search -> Filter -> Add-to-Cart') decoupled from specific parameters, and the planner is prompted to extract both high-level plans and low-level interaction patterns from retrieved exemplars.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> (1) LLM-based reranking of Top-k candidates filters/orders noisy retrievals by visual+layout+semantic relevance. (2) 'Reuse Level Decision' prompt mechanism instructs the agent to treat non-matching exemplars as HIGH_LEVEL structural guidance, preventing silver/analogous trajectories from acting as noisy supervision. (3) Silver-trajectory contrastive training teaches procedural invariance and improves OOD generalization (robustness to distribution shift). (4) Token selection (UI-connected RGB-space graph) suppresses redundant visual tokens. No explicit retriever-aware planner SFT or self-reflection relevance gate.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Procedural / experience store (static demonstration knowledge base). The retrievable store is a fixed library of human-annotated GUI trajectories (UATD) treated as reusable procedural experience; not an episodic memory the agent grows, not a graph, not latent memory.
- **write back**:
> No. WebRAGent does not store its own newly generated trajectories/experiences back into the retrieval corpus; the trajectory knowledge base (UATD) is built offline and used read-only at deployment. (It does maintain a within-episode explicit history memory for the running task, but this is not written back to the retrievable store.)
- **online growth**: No. The retrieval store is frozen after offline induction from UATD; it does not grow during deployment/test-time.
- **write back trigger**:
> Never (for the retrievable trajectory store). No event causes a write into the retrieval corpus; new agent experiences are not consolidated. (Within a single episode the agent keeps a CoT/history memory and computes an LLM-as-judge reward score per step, but neither is persisted as a new retrievable case.)
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success-only / demonstration-based. The retrieval corpus consists of human-annotated successful demonstrations; failed agent trajectories are not stored or contrastively retrieved. The step-level LLM-as-judge reward (scores from {1,3,7,9,10}; categories doing/finished/loop) steers the running agent (e.g., reset-and-recover on loops) but is not used to mine or store failure cases for retrieval.
- **memory evolution update**: N/A (static store). Stored entries are not mutated after offline construction (no append/dedup/merge/refine/forget at deployment); the corpus is fixed.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partial: case-SELECTION is via a LEARNED dense retriever (GAE-Retriever, contrastively trained VLM embeddings) plus an LLM reranker, rather than an off-the-shelf fixed similarity model. However retrieval is NOT an RL- or value-optimized sequential policy (no M-MDP / soft Q-learning); it is a learned-embedding top-k + LLM rerank.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Cross-framework transfer demonstrated (not shared private memory). GAE-Retriever is shown to be plug-and-play: integrated into the SeeAct agent framework it yields an 8-10% success-rate gain (SeeAct 49.0% -> +D_text 57.0% -> +D_vision 59.0% on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset), demonstrating that the retrieved trajectory knowledge transfers across heterogeneous agent frameworks. The retrieval corpus itself is a shared static resource, not per-agent private growing memory.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> Retrieval evaluation: GAE-Bench / GAE-Bench-lite over five sources - Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct (Recall@1/5/10; in-domain and out-of-domain splits). Downstream web-agent evaluation: Online-Mind2Web (a representative 100-task subset selected via two-stage stratified sampling from the original set, balanced across websites/categories and easy/medium/hard difficulty). SeeAct cross-framework study also on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset.
- **benchmark family**: web (Mind2Web / WebArena / WebLINX / GUIAct / AutoWebGLM for offline trajectory retrieval; Online-Mind2Web for the live downstream agent). Plus a new multimodal-retrieval benchmark family introduced by the paper itself (GAE-Bench).
- **baselines**:
> Retrieval baselines (zero-shot, three groups): (1) Multimodal backbone models - Qwen2-VL-2B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B; (2) Multimodal retrieval models - LamRA-Ret, ColQwen2-v1.0, GME-Qwen2VL-2B, UniSE-MLLM, VLM2Vec-Qwen2VL-2B, VLM2Vec-V2.2 (strongest baseline); (3) Multimodal trajectory/GUI planning models - UGround-V1-2B, ShowUI-2B, UI-TARS-2B-SFT, TongUI-3B. Downstream (WebRAGent): non-retrieval agent with the SAME planner (GPT-4.1 DOM / computer-use-preview Vision), same observation/action/reward/prompts, differing only by the retrieval module; SeeAct (added in rebuttal) as a cross-framework baseline (+/- retrieval). Also text-only retrieval (q->tau) vs multimodal retrieval comparison (Appendix D.5).
- **key metrics**: Retrieval: Recall@1/5/10. Downstream web agent: task Success Rate (%) on Online-Mind2Web, broken down by Easy/Medium/Hard difficulty. Efficiency: seconds/step for retrieval vs reranking vs total, and cache speedup. Reranking effect: relative R@1 improvement at Top-k=5 / Top-k=10.
- **headline result**:
> WebRAGent improves web-agent task Success Rate by over 15% (reported as 15-22%, and 16-22% in the later revision) versus the non-retrieval baseline on the 100-task Online-Mind2Web subset, using identical planners (GPT-4.1 DOM / computer-use-preview Vision) and differing only in the retrieval module. For the retriever itself, GAE-Retriever surpasses all baselines on every dataset, with Recall@1 consistently >10.0; e.g., Recall@10 of 76.3 on AutoWebGLM and 67.9 on GUIAct, improving Recall@1 over the strongest baseline VLM2Vec-V2.2 by up to 7.1 points (GUIAct) / 6.4 points (AutoWebGLM), with an average +10.22-point improvement across five datasets over the best baseline (up to +12.9 Recall@1 per the conclusion).
- **ablations**:
> (1) Cross-framework plug-and-play (SeeAct, 100-task Online-Mind2Web): SeeAct 49.0% -> +D_text 57.0% -> +D_vision 59.0% (8-10% gain), with visual knowledge best on Medium (60.52%) and Hard (25.00%) tasks. (2) Textual vs visual RAG: both effective; visual exemplars help more on fine-grained Medium/Hard operations. (3) Multimodal vs text-only retrieval (Appendix D.5, Table 11): multimodal/state-conditioned retrieval beats text-only q->tau by ~22%. (4) Reranking Top-k effect on Online-Mind2Web: Top-k=5 improves R@1 by ~36%, Top-k=10 by ~54%. (5) Inference efficiency (Appendix D.7, RTX A6000): retrieval 0.39 s/step vs reranking 3.54 s/step; with two-level LLM cache total drops to 0.383 s/step (9.24x speedup), ~10% added latency/step. (6) Retriever per-task analysis: semantic tasks (q->tau, q->s) easiest; (q,tau)->tau' and (q,s)->tau hardest; GAE-Retriever sometimes higher OOD than IND, indicating generalizable representations. (7) Token Selection vs alternatives (Appendix D.8). Open issue raised by reviewers: no isolated ablation separating the silver-data contribution.
- **evaluation decoupling**: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@1/5/10, in-domain and out-of-domain, per task/subtask) are reported separately from the end-to-end web-agent Success Rate on Online-Mind2Web, explicitly linking better trajectory representations to better downstream agent performance.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mixed. Downstream metric is outcome-level task Success Rate, but reported by difficulty stratum (Easy/Medium/Hard) and accompanied by qualitative step-level case studies (Appendix F) marking where retrieved knowledge is cited at each critical step, plus a step-level LLM-as-judge reward signal and per-step latency analysis. Retrieval side reports ranking-quality (process) metrics.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reported. Retrieval augmentation adds ~10% latency per step. Per-step cost: retrieval 0.3877 s, reranking 3.5374 s, total 3.9251 s without cache; with a two-level LLM-side cache + compressed image encoding, total 0.3830 s/step (9.24x speedup), reranking near-negligible on cache hits. Training cost: 16x NVIDIA H800, LoRA rank 8, accumulated batch 2,048, 256 steps, ~1,044 GPU hours. The 15-22% success gain is argued to justify the modest added retrieval cost.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Reranked-then-truncated fixed-k: GAE-Retriever returns Top-k candidates (Top-k=5 or 10 on Online-Mind2Web) which the LLM reranker refines; the top reranked step-level exemplar(s) (textual or visual) are injected into the planner prompt. Trajectory length capped at <10 steps in GAE-Bench-lite to fit VLM context windows; token selection further reduces visual tokens to keep high-resolution multi-image trajectories within budget. No adaptive/precision-driven variable-k.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> UATD: 7,747 human-annotated demonstrations and 82,793 states unified from five GUI sources (Mind2Web 1,468 tasks/9,621 states; AutoWebGLM 140/620; WebArena 201/1,221; WebLINX 485/6,882; GUIAct 5,453/64,449); screenshots kept at original resolution, target elements as bounding boxes, missing screenshots rendered via gpt-4o-mini HTML completion + Playwright, state descriptions auto-annotated (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18). GAE-Bench: 714,628 positive retrieval pairs from 12 extraction patterns over 6 retrieval task types (text-to-state, text-to-trajectory, state-to-state, state-to-trajectory, trajectory-to-state, trajectory-to-trajectory). GAE-Bench-lite (<10-step trajectories): 514,956 train / 21,805 in-domain / 27,139 out-of-domain, 574,222 candidates; plus a GAE-Bench-lite(mini) candidate partition. Silver trajectories built via NER -> entity-type-preserving substitution -> query rewrite. Answer verifiability: ground-truth positive pairs are derived from human demonstrations (gold) plus synthesized silver positives. Difficulty signal: even the strongest GAE-Retriever reaches Recall@1 only ~10-26 and the hardest subtasks ((q,tau)->tau', (q,s)->tau) remain low.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> VLM2Vec (Jiang et al., 2025; Qwen2-VL backbone embedding model) extended to trajectory contrastive learning; GradCache (Gao et al., 2021) for large-batch contrastive training under memory limits; token selection via UI-connected RGB-space graph (inspired by Raposo et al. 2024 mixture-of-depths and ShowUI / Lin et al. 2024a); AGUVIS (Xu et al., 2024) for screenshot-as-observation unified GUI formulation; ShowUI action schema for the unified action space; source datasets Mind2Web, AutoWebGLM, WebArena, WebLINX, GUIAct; Online-Mind2Web for live evaluation; SeeAct (Zheng et al. 2024) as the cross-framework integration target. Conceptually relates to RaDA (Kim et al. 2024), Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024), Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al. 2024c), SkillWeaver (Zheng et al. 2025), and retrieval-augmented RL (Goyal et al. 2022).
- **contrasts with**:
> CLIP-based / single-image multimodal retrievers (CLIP, BLIP, composed video retrieval) - unsuitable for long multi-image high-resolution (~1000x1000) GUI trajectories; text/DOM-only trajectory retrieval (RaDA matching textual trajectory descriptions, Synapse matching DOM/HTML states) - argued to miss visual semantics (layout, icon status, rendering); end-to-end pure-vision GUI agents such as AGUVIS that aggregate trajectories to train action policies (next-action labels) rather than a trajectory RETRIEVER; and screenshot-only retrievers (UniSE-MLLM) which underperform. Also positioned as introducing a 'representation layer' missing from reactive-generation GUI agents.
- **lineage**:
> Group C (RAG + planning) with strong overlap into retrieval-augmented web-agent and trajectory/experience-retrieval lines (B/D). It advances the RaDA -> Synapse -> Agent-Workflow-Memory line of retrieval-augmented web-agent planning by (a) introducing the Multimodal Trajectory Retrieval task and the UATD/GAE-Bench infrastructure, (b) training the first VLM-based multimodal trajectory retriever (GAE-Retriever) with token selection + GradCache, and (c) wrapping it in WebRAGent, a DOM+vision retrieval-augmented web agent validated on Online-Mind2Web. Distinctive emphasis: a static, supervised, learned multimodal trajectory-retrieval layer (vs growing episodic memory) feeding per-step LLM-reranked exemplars to a strong web-agent planner.
