<a id="item-cbr-ddi"></a>
### 72. CBR-DDI (Case-Based Reasoning Enhances the Predictive Power of LLMs in Drug-Drug Interaction)

2025  ·  arXiv 2505.23034  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23034)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**:
> Guangyi Liu (Dept. of Electronic Engineering, Tsinghua University), Yongqi Zhang (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou), Xunyuan Liu (Tsinghua University), Quanming Yao (Tsinghua University; corresponding author). Lead/primary affiliation: Tsinghua University.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23034

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Scientific decision-making / biomedical prediction: drug-drug interaction (DDI) type prediction, framed as a reasoning/classification task for LLMs (decision-making in a scientific domain).
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-agent, non-interactive inference. Given a query drug pair (u,v), predict the interaction type r from a fixed relation set. Two evaluation regimes for emerging/unseen drugs: S1 (one emerging drug vs. one existing drug) and S2 (two emerging drugs), plus S0 (both drugs seen) in the appendix. Supervision: ground-truth interaction labels exist in training data and are used to construct cases and to verify/revise predictions; the LLMs themselves are NOT fine-tuned (plug-and-play). A GNN module (EmerGNN-style) is trained on the biomedical KG. The knowledge repository of cases is induced offline.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Cases: structured problem-solution units, each a drug pair enriched with (i) LLM-generated functional drug descriptions, (ii) GNN-extracted drug-association representation, (iii) an LLM-distilled interaction-mechanism explanation, and (iv) the interaction-type label. Effectively distilled pharmacological 'cases' rather than raw demos.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID. Cases are drawn from a knowledge repository induced offline from historical/training DDI data (a growing/refinable store updated via representative sampling), while drug-association facts are grounded in a STATIC external biomedical KG (HetioNet) via a trained GNN. Retrieval combines semantic (LLM-description embeddings) and structural (KG-subgraph GNN) signals.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-K case ranking (K=5 reference cases by default; K=1,5 studied in retrieval ablations). For TWOSIDES the task is cast as top-5 recommendation (Recall@5/NDCG@5); for DrugBank single-label classification. Not a minimal-set-completeness objective.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] - all four canonical CBR phases are implemented: Retrieve (hybrid LLM-GNN case retrieval), Reuse (dual-layer knowledge-enhanced prompting / analogical reasoning), Revise (verify prediction vs. ground-truth label and prompt revisions for errors), Retain (representative-sampling refinement and storage of revised cases in the repository).
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> True. The work explicitly frames itself as case-based reasoning, citing classical CBR literature (Aamodt & Plaza-style clinical CBR, Kolodner-lineage, Althoff et al. 1998, Bichindaritz & Marling 2006, Hennessy & Hinkle 1992) and motivating from clinical decision-support CBR; method named CBR-DDI.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: case (problem-solution): a drug-pair case combining functional drug descriptions, KG-derived drug-association representation, distilled interaction-mechanism text, and the interaction-type label.
- **index source**:
> Hybrid offline-induced + dynamically-refined store. The case repository is constructed offline from historical/training DDI data (LLM distills mechanisms; GNN encodes associations) and is dynamically refined at use time via verification-driven revision and representative sampling. Drug-association evidence comes from a static external biomedical KG (HetioNet) through a trained GNN.
- **index structure topology**:
> Hybrid: a case repository organized/clustered by DDI category (representative cluster centroids per interaction type via text-embedding clustering of mechanisms) backed by dense vector indices for semantic (description embeddings) and structural (GNN subgraph embeddings) similarity; drug associations sit on a knowledge-graph topology queried by an attention-based subgraph GNN.
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid. Combines dense semantic retrieval (LLM-generated drug-description embeddings via a text embedding model, RoBERTa-style) with structural retrieval over KG subgraph representations produced by an attention-based GNN (EmerGNN). Retrieval score s(p,c)=lambda*SemanticSim + (1-lambda)*StructSim with cosine similarity.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> Mixed. The semantic side uses an off-the-shelf text embedding model (no contrastive training reported). The structural side uses a GNN (EmerGNN) trained on the KG for the DDI task, so the structural similarity component carries downstream-task-effectiveness signal; the fusion weight lambda is a tuned hyperparameter rather than a learned policy. No RL/preference learning for retrieval.
- **query construction**:
> For a query drug pair (u,v): an LLM generates concise functional descriptions D_p=(D_u,D_v) (intent/feature extraction), embedded for semantic similarity; in parallel the GNN encodes the KG subgraph connecting u and v (using description embeddings as node features) to produce h_p for structural similarity. Both form the retrieval key.
- **query granularity**: Task-level / one-shot at t=0: a single retrieval is issued per query drug pair. It is a two-channel (semantic + structural) query but not multi-step or trajectory-level.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot (single retrieval per query before reasoning). Not iterative or uncertainty-triggered.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per query drug pair before prompting (no confidence/attention/router trigger).
- **reranking**:
> Single-stage ranking by the weighted hybrid score s(p,c)=lambda*SemanticSim+(1-lambda)*StructSim, then top-K selection; no separate cross-encoder reranking stage. Candidate interaction TYPES are separately pre-filtered to top-N by GNN scores (a form of candidate pruning, distinct from case reranking).
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Pre-injection refinement at two levels: (i) candidate-answer pre-filtering to top-N interaction types by GNN scores to reduce label-space noise/distractors; (ii) top-P attention-weighted relational paths selected from the GNN as high-quality factual evidence (instead of heuristic triplet retrieval). The repository itself is also distilled via representative sampling. No reason-in-documents distillation per query.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; cases are engineered by LLM-distilling interaction mechanisms and GNN-encoding associations, but this is case engineering not tool-document engineering).
- **index content separation**:
> Partial: described as a 'lightweight' knowledge repository; representative sampling compresses the store to cluster centroids (over 90% size reduction on DrugBank), separating a compact representative set from the full case pool. No explicit progressive-disclosure index-then-content protocol.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no external tool API/MCP/RapidAPI integration). The case repository is dynamically refined (verification + representative sampling) but not a live tool index.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling). The method does model inter-drug structural dependencies via KG relational paths, but not tools.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation via case reuse / analogical adaptation: retrieved cases' interaction-mechanism text plus GNN-extracted drug-association facts and filtered candidate types are assembled into a dual-layer knowledge-enhanced prompt; the LLM synthesizes them to produce the predicted mechanism M_p and interaction type T_p. No fine-tuning; in-context learning only.
- **planning integration**: Retrieve-then-reason (one-shot exemplars/cases at prediction time). Retrieval feeds a single dual-layer prompt that the LLM uses to generate the mechanism explanation and interaction-type prediction; no multi-step planning, tree search, or interleaved per-step retrieval.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: a single retrieval-and-reasoning pass produces one prediction (mechanism + type) per query drug pair.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted analogical adaptation of retrieved cases (in-context), combined with execution-/label-feedback-driven revision in the Revise step: predictions are verified against ground-truth labels and erroneous cases are revised (re-prompted with the correct label to regenerate the mechanism) before being retained.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled, structured natural-language case: free-text interaction-mechanism explanation + functional drug descriptions + structured KG relational paths (e.g., Fosphenytoin -binds-> CYP3A4 -binds-> Diphenhydramine) + candidate interaction-type label set. Injected as text in the prompt.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Distilled strategy/insight at the case level: generalizable pharmacological interaction-mechanism patterns abstracted from historical drug-pair cases (not raw trajectories, not single demonstrations), paired with state-aware factual evidence (drug-association paths).
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Multiple guards: (i) hybrid semantic+structural retrieval to ensure retrieved cases share both functional and structural relevance; (ii) attention-weighted top-P path selection to filter low-quality KG triplets; (iii) top-N candidate-answer pre-filtering to suppress irrelevant label distractors; (iv) representative sampling to remove redundant/noisy cases from the repository; (v) verification-and-revision to correct erroneous stored cases.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Hybrid episodic + graph: a case repository (episodic/case memory of pharmacological cases) refined dynamically, grounded by a graph (biomedical KG of drug associations encoded by a GNN).
- **write back**: True. New/resolved cases (with verified or revised interaction mechanisms) are written into the knowledge repository; the store is dynamically refined.
- **online growth**:
> Partial / controlled growth. The repository can incorporate new resolved cases and adapt to new discoveries, but representative sampling deliberately controls (compresses) growth; experiments evaluate on a largely offline-induced, sampled repository rather than unbounded test-time accumulation.
- **write back trigger**:
> Reflective / on-verification: for each LLM prediction, correctness is verified against the ground-truth label (from training data or expert feedback); correct cases are retained and incorrect ones are revised (re-prompted with the correct label) before storage. Effectively on-success-and-failure with correction.
- **failure experience usage**: Failures are corrected rather than stored as negatives: erroneous predictions trigger label-grounded revision so the corrected (positive) case is retained. No explicit success-vs-failure contrastive retrieval or failure-only corrective rules reported.
- **memory evolution update**: Refine-overwrite + dedup-merge + forget-prune: cases are revised/overwritten upon error correction, semantically similar cases are clustered and merged to representative centroids (dedup), and redundant cases are pruned (over 90% reduction on DrugBank).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Case selection is fixed similarity-based top-K (weighted hybrid score with a tuned lambda); not an RL/learned retrieval policy. The structural-similarity GNN is trained on the task but the case-selection rule itself is not a learned policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No. Single-agent private repository. The framework is plug-and-play across different backbone LLMs (Llama3.1-8B/70B, DeepSeek-V3), but there is no cross-agent/cross-framework memory sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> DrugBank (Wishart et al. 2018; multi-class, 86 interaction types) and TWOSIDES (Tatonetti et al. 2012; multi-label, 200 side effects). Evaluated under S1 (emerging vs existing drug) and S2 (two emerging drugs) settings; S0 (both existing) in appendix. External KG: HetioNet (Himmelstein & Baranzini 2015).
- **benchmark family**: Biomedical / scientific decision-making (drug-drug interaction prediction); a domain-specific benchmark family (not in the QA/web/embodied/tool/code/memory taxonomy). Knowledge-graph-grounded relational prediction.
- **baselines**:
> Traditional (non-LLM): MLP, ComplEx, MSTE, Decagon, SumGNN, EmerGNN, TIGER. LM/LLM-based: TextDDI (fine-tuned RoBERTa), DDI-GPT (referenced in comparison table), Base LLM (zero-shot), Naive-CBR (fingerprint-similarity 10-shot case retrieval), K-Paths (Abdullahi et al. 2025, heuristic KG-path prompting). Backbone LLMs: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, DeepSeek-V3-671B.
- **key metrics**: DrugBank: Accuracy and macro-F1. TWOSIDES (recommendation framing): Recall@5 and NDCG@5. Aggregate improvement reported as Delta_avg (average accuracy+recall improvement across the two datasets). Repository-size (#Case) reported for the sampling ablation.
- **headline result**:
> CBR-DDI achieves state-of-the-art performance with a ~28.7% accuracy improvement over the Naive-CBR baseline (and 463% over the base LLM). Best DrugBank S1 results: with DeepSeek-V3, F1=74.38 (Acc 71.05); with Llama3.1-70B, Acc=71.36 / F1=70.85, vs. strongest non-LLM baseline EmerGNN (DrugBank S1 Acc 68.10 / F1 65.78).
- **ablations**:
> (1) Dual-layer knowledge augmentation (Table 3, Llama3.1-70B): full (DrugBank S1 Acc 71.4) vs w.o.case (factual-only, 68.3) vs w.o.asso (regularity/case-only, 69.4); removing either layer degrades performance, and retrieved cases (regularity) are more critical than KG associations alone. (2) Representative sampling (Table 4): cuts repository size by >90% (DrugBank S1 35,255 -> 2,139 cases) with comparable/slightly-improved accuracy (71.36 -> 71.05). (3) Hybrid retriever weight lambda (Figure 4): retrieval accuracy peaks at a balanced semantic+structural mix, confirming both channels matter. (4) Effect of #cases K and #paths P (appendix): accuracy rises then saturates/decreases with larger K/P.
- **evaluation decoupling**: Partial. End-to-end task metrics (Acc/F1/Recall@5/NDCG@5) are primary, but the hybrid-retriever ablation reports intrinsic retrieval accuracy (majority-label of top-K under varying lambda), decoupling retrieval quality from final task performance for that study.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome (final interaction-type prediction). Some process signals are examined qualitatively (case studies show retrieved cases, extracted association paths, generated mechanism explanations, interpretability) and the retrieval-accuracy ablation; no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness metric.
- **context budget and selection count**: Fixed-k injection: K=5 reference cases, P=5 association paths, candidate answers capped at top-N (3 for DrugBank, 10 for TWOSIDES; varied among {3,5,10}). No explicit token-budget cap reported; selection is fixed-k then truncated by candidate pre-filtering.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (uses existing datasets, not a newly constructed benchmark). For reference: DrugBank split 1,461/79/161 train/valid/test drugs, 86 relations, 137,864 training edges; TWOSIDES 514/30/60 drugs, 200 relations, 185,673 training edges; HetioNet used as external KG.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> EmerGNN (Zhang et al. 2023; attention-based subgraph GNN for emerging-drug DDI, reused for structural similarity and association-path extraction); classical CBR for clinical decision support (Aamodt & Plaza lineage, Althoff et al. 1998, Bichindaritz & Marling 2006); in-context learning / few-shot prompting (Brown et al. 2020); KG-grounded DDI (HetioNet); recent CBR+LLM integration work (Wilkerson & Leake 2024; Guo et al. 2024).
- **contrasts with**:
> Naive-CBR (fingerprint-similarity case retrieval giving only labels, no pharmacological insight), K-Paths (Abdullahi et al. 2025, heuristic KG-path prompting that may inject irrelevant/redundant info), TextDDI and DDI-GPT (fine-tuned small-LM classifiers, limited LLM compatibility/interpretability), and pure GNN/feature DDI methods (EmerGNN, SumGNN, TIGER, Decagon, MSTE, ComplEx, MLP) that require task-specific training.
- **lineage**: Group D: case-based planning / case-based reasoning lineage (explicit CBR with full Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle), applied to a scientific decision-making domain; hybrid LLM+GNN retrieval over a dynamically-refined case/experience memory grounded in a biomedical KG.

<a id="item-cbr-llm-driving"></a>
### 73. CBR-LLM: Case-Based Reasoning Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Decision Making in Realistic Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios

2025  ·  arXiv 2506.20531  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20531)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: arXiv:2506.20531 [cs.AI] (submitted 25 Jun 2025; comments note '12 pages, 10 figures, under-review conference'). A peer-reviewed journal version was subsequently published in Safety Science (Elsevier), DOI 10.1016/j.ssci.2026.107234.
- **authors affiliation**: Wenbin Gan, Minh-Son Dao, Koji Zettsu. Big Data Integration Research Center, National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT), Tokyo, Japan.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.20531
- **code url**:
> N/A (no official code repository released; the paper provides no code/GitHub link and no associated repo could be located). The naturalistic near-miss dataset is from Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (https://web.tuat.ac.jp/~smrc/en/about.html), with only a 1000-sample subset used due to copyright constraints.

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Decision-making for autonomous/assisted driving: evasive-maneuver recommendation in safety-critical driving scenarios (SCDSs) from egocentric dashcam video. Multimodal (video-to-text scene understanding) + LLM reasoning; framed as Knowledge Representation and Reasoning (KR) combining symbolic case memory with neural reasoning.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-agent, open-loop decision-support task. Input is a ~15s dashcam near-miss video; a dual-task scene-understanding model converts it into (a) a detailed driving-risk classification (one of 7 risk types) and (b) a free-text spatial-temporal risk event caption. Given this, the system retrieves similar past resolved cases from a curated, evolving case base and an LLM (via Chain-of-Thought) recommends a single evasive maneuver from a fixed maneuver set plus a justification. Supervision: each video is manually annotated with a ground-truth human-driver evasive maneuver (semantic annotations are manually verified for correctness). Evaluation is offline against human-expert maneuvers; no closed-loop vehicle control, no online interaction, no agent learning during deployment is tested (continual case-base growth is described conceptually / as future work).
- **what is retrieved**:
> Past resolved driving CASES (experiences) of safety-critical scenarios. Each case is a structured problem-solution record: Key = {risk type, scene event caption}; Value = risk-analysis results {road context, other-car position, other-car action, event context, ego-car evasive maneuver, ego-car maneuver justification}. Used as CBR few-shot exemplars (in-context demonstrations) for the LLM.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID, leaning toward a GROWING/episodic case memory: the retrievable store is a curated case base of human-driver experiences (resolved SCDSs) rather than a static doc/KB/API corpus. The case base is explicitly designed to evolve and incrementally absorb newly analyzed experiences over time; in the evaluated setting it is built offline (900 cases held out as the case base) and queried by similarity, with continual online growth presented as a designed property / future deployment behavior.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking objective: retrieve the k most similar same-risk-type cases (k in {1,3,5} few-shot examples) by embedding cosine similarity. Not a minimal-complete-set objective and not a precision-driven variable-size recommendation; k is a fixed hyperparameter (with similarity-based selection compared against random selection).
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] partially: Retrieve=yes (similarity-based same-risk-type case recall); Reuse=yes (retrieved cases injected as few-shot exemplars and adapted to the current scene via LLM CoT reasoning); Revise=partial/implicit (the LLM adapts the recalled cases' decision logic to the new context and produces a justification, but there is no execution-feedback or outcome-verification revision loop in the experiments); Retain=designed-but-not-evaluated (the case base is stated to evolve / incrementally update with new experiences, but online retention is not experimentally demonstrated).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> case (problem-solution record): a complete resolved SCDS case with key {risk type, scene event caption} and value {road context, other-car position/action, event context, ego-car evasive maneuver, justification}. The event caption is embedded as a single dense vector for similarity; the full case is reused as a few-shot exemplar.
- **index source**:
> Growing/episodic curated case base, offline-induced in the evaluated split (900 of 1000 annotated SCDS scenarios stored as past-experience cases; 100 held out as test queries). Designed to grow online by incrementally adding newly analyzed experiences; this online growth is described as a designed property rather than experimentally measured.
- **index structure topology**:
> Metadata/context-keyed flat vector index: cases are embedded by their event caption into vectors (via the nomic-embed-text embedding model) and similarity search is performed, but retrieval is constrained/partitioned by risk type (recall restricted to the same risk category). So effectively a risk-type-keyed (category-partitioned) flat dense vector store; not a knowledge graph or hierarchical app->API index.
- **retriever type**: Dense retriever: open embedding model 'nomic-embed-text' embeds scene event captions into vectors, with vector cosine-similarity matching, constrained to the same risk type. Not BM25, not learned/RL, not LLM-as-retriever, not generative.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a fixed pretrained open embedding model (nomic-embed-text) with cosine-similarity top-k selection; it is not trained with contrastive similarity labels, LM-feedback, downstream-task reward/preference, RL, or value-based signals. Case selection is fixed similarity (plus a hard same-risk-type filter), compared against random sampling as a control.
- **query construction**:
> Two-stage query construction from the dashcam video: (1) a dual-task scene-understanding model predicts the risk type and a structured risk assessment; (2) semantic components (risk category, conflict type, driving context) are encoded and passed to an LLM (DeepSeek-R1) that synthesizes a narrative scene event caption. The event caption (plus risk type) forms the query/key; the caption is embedded for similarity retrieval. Intent/risk extraction is thus performed before retrieval.
- **query granularity**: Task-level (one-shot at decision time): a single query (risk type + event caption) is formed once per SCDS event and used for a single retrieval pass. It is event-based (one event = one decision) rather than per-frame, per-step, or trajectory-level re-querying.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot: retrieval is performed once per detected SCDS event, before the LLM reasoning/decision step. No iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or learned-router re-retrieval within the reasoning loop.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule / event-triggered: retrieval fires once whenever an SCDS (risk) event is detected by the upstream dual-task model; there is no token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, learned-complexity, or reflection-token trigger. (Detection of a non-safe scene by the risk-prediction stage is the gating condition.)
- **reranking**: No dedicated reranking stage. Candidates are selected by embedding cosine-similarity within the same risk type and the top-k are used directly as few-shot examples; no cross-encoder, RRF, or hierarchy-aware reranker is applied.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Minimal: a hard same-risk-type filter (category constraint) plus similarity top-k selection acts as a coarse relevance/distractor filter before the cases are inserted as few-shot exemplars. No decompose-then-recompose, reason-in-documents distillation, or compression of the retrieved cases.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tools/APIs are retrieved; retrieved items are driving cases). Cases are keyed on a manually-defined structured schema (risk type + event caption) and embedded with nomic-embed-text; no synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned embeddings.
- **index content separation**:
> Partial: each case is split into a lightweight Key part (risk type + event caption) used for similarity retrieval and a Value part (full risk-analysis decision logic) that carries the reusable content; only the key/caption is embedded for matching while the value supplies the decision reasoning. This key/value separation is a mild form of index-vs-content separation, though both are stored together per case.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol such as RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling). LLMs are accessed locally via Ollama API for generation, not as a retrievable tool store.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no tools; no inter-tool dependency modeling).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation via case-based few-shot in-context learning: retrieved same-risk-type cases are inserted as few-shot exemplars into a dynamically generated prompt (system prompt + task prompt + CBR few-shot examples). The LLM then performs Chain-of-Thought reasoning to adapt the recalled decision logic to the current scene and outputs a structured JSON maneuver recommendation + justification (case adaptation realized through LLM reasoning).
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-reason (one-shot exemplars at decision time): pipeline is scene-understanding -> CBR retrieval -> dynamic prompt assembly -> single LLM CoT decision. Retrieval supplies few-shot exemplars once before a single CoT reasoning pass that produces the final maneuver; no MCTS/tree-search, no per-step interleaved retrieval, no plan-then-retrieve loop.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-answer: one retrieval feeds one CoT reasoning pass that yields one maneuver decision per SCDS event. Retrieval is not interleaved per CoT step, per sentence/token, or per tool-call.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation: retrieved cases are provided as in-context exemplars and the LLM adapts their decision logic to the current scene through a designed Chain-of-Thought process (overview road context -> analyze other-car position/action spatial-temporally -> summarize event context -> infer maneuver -> justify). No execution-feedback-driven revision, critic-guided revision, or RL reuse-finetuning.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Raw case content as free-text/structured exemplars: retrieved cases are surfaced as structured key-value records (risk type, event caption, road context, other-car position/action, event context, ego-car maneuver, justification) injected verbatim as few-shot examples; the LLM's own output is a structured JSON decision with justification.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Raw cases / single demonstrations (problem-solution records of past SCDSs). The retrieved unit is a concrete prior driving experience (not a distilled strategy, abstract rule, reusable workflow, or procedural skill); abstraction/generalization happens downstream in the LLM's CoT adaptation.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Mainly a same-risk-type retrieval constraint plus similarity-based selection to avoid injecting irrelevant cases. The paper empirically shows that a single irrelevant (randomly selected) example can degrade performance below zero-shot, motivating similarity+same-category retrieval as the noise-robustness mechanism; risk-aware prompting (structured risk annotations) further grounds reasoning. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, self-reflection filter, or distractor-aware SFT.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: episodic case memory (curated, evolving case base of past driving experiences). It is a structured experiential case store rather than a skill-library, workflow memory, procedural memory, knowledge graph, or latent memory.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Not used as a distinct mechanism. The case base stores resolved SCDSs with the executed (successful) human-driver evasive maneuvers; failed/negative experiences are not separately stored or retrieved as contrastive or corrective rules. Effectively success-only (human-resolved) cases.
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Case selection is a fixed embedding-similarity top-k within the same risk type (compared against random sampling); it is not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy (no M-MDP, soft Q-learning, preference learning, or value-based retrieval).
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No. Single-agent system with one shared case base; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience/memory sharing is described.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> Real-world naturalistic near-miss driving dataset from Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology (>220,000 dashcam near-accident video segments, each ~15s = 10s before + 5s after the trigger, with descriptive tags). Due to copyright, a 1000-sample subset is used, balanced across 7 risk types (~143 each). For the CBR-augmented evaluation, 100 samples (~14 per risk type) are held out as test cases and the remaining 900 form the case base. No public agentic-RAG benchmark is used.
- **benchmark family**:
> Decision-making / autonomous-driving domain benchmark on a private real-world dashcam SCDS dataset; does NOT map to standard families (not QA / multi-hop / web / embodied (ALFWorld etc.) / tool (ToolBench) / code (SWE-bench) / memory (LoCoMo) / decision-RL (D4RL)). Closest normalized label: real-world driving decision-making / risk-scenario understanding (egocentric dashcam video).
- **baselines**:
> Internal comparisons rather than external SOTA methods: (1) eight open-source LLMs of varying size as backbones (Mistral 7B, Mistral-Nemo 12B, Mixtral 8x7B, Phi-4 14B, DeepSeek-R1 14B, Gemma2 27B, Qwen2.5 32B, Llama3.3 70B); (2) prompt-setting baselines: risk-unaware vs risk-aware prompting; (3) in-context-learning baselines: zero-shot vs 1/3/5-shot, and random case selection vs similarity-based (same-risk-type) CBR retrieval. The key contrast is similarity-based CBR retrieval vs random sampling and vs zero-shot.
- **key metrics**:
> Decision alignment: Micro-accuracy / micro-average accuracy of the recommended evasive maneuver vs the ground-truth human-driver maneuver. Text quality (Event Context and Ego-car Maneuver Justification, assessing interpretability / alignment with expert reasoning): BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, CIDEr. Variances reported in brackets.
- **headline result**:
> Llama3.3-70B achieves the highest maneuver-decision accuracy: micro-accuracy 0.9412 (~0.941) under the risk-aware setting (vs 0.9369/0.937 risk-unaware); abstract/intro cite 0.9412 as the top alignment with human-like decisions. In the CBR-augmented setting, Llama3.3-70B reaches 0.94 accuracy with similarity-based 5-shot retrieval, and similarity-based case retrieval consistently outperforms random sampling across models.
- **ablations**:
> Several controlled comparisons act as ablations: (Q1) vanilla LLM size comparison (8 models) showing larger instruction-tuned models do better; (Q2) risk-aware vs risk-unaware prompting (risk-aware generally improves accuracy across 5 top models, e.g., Gemma2 27B 0.893->0.918, Qwen2.5 32B 0.875->0.898, Llama3.3 70B 0.937->0.941; Phi-4 14B slightly drops, underperforming on adjacent-vehicle conflicts); (Q3) CBR augmentation ablation over selection method (random vs similarity) x shots (0/1/3/5): similarity-based selection consistently beats random; a single irrelevant (random 1-shot) example often drops below the zero-shot baseline; more similar examples monotonically help; DeepSeek-R1 is a notable exception where more few-shot examples degrade performance (consistent with the DeepSeek-R1 paper). Per-risk-type breakdowns are given in Tables 4-5.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Partial. Decision-outcome accuracy (maneuver micro-accuracy) is reported separately from generation-quality metrics (BLEU-4/METEOR/ROUGE-L/CIDEr on event context and justification). However, intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval precision) are NOT reported; retrieval quality is assessed only indirectly via downstream accuracy (similarity vs random selection).
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Both outcome and (linguistic) process quality: the final maneuver decision is scored by accuracy (outcome), while the intermediate event-context understanding and the maneuver justification are scored with NLG metrics (a proxy for reasoning/interpretability quality). No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-accuracy metric.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (this is a system/method paper, not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> Source: Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology naturalistic near-miss dashcam dataset (>220,000 ~15s near-accident segments with descriptive tags). Used subset: 1000 samples balanced across 7 SCDS risk types (~143 each), each manually verified for semantic-annotation correctness and manually labeled with the ground-truth human-executed evasive maneuver (one maneuver per video from an 8-option maneuver set). Split: 900 cases as the case base, 100 (~14/type) as test queries for the CBR evaluation. Semantic annotations (risk type via a two-stage safe/risk-then-7-class predictor; event captions synthesized by DeepSeek-R1) are human-verified. Best system score (difficulty signal): up to 0.94 maneuver accuracy (Llama3.3-70B). Answer verifiability: maneuver labels are human-annotated ground truth; dataset is private/copyright-restricted, limiting reproducibility.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Authors' prior open Case-Based Reasoning driving-assistance framework (Gan, Dao, Zettsu 2022, IEEE BigData) and their dashcam scene-understanding / risk-prediction pipeline (e.g., Drive-CLIP 2024; MM-TrafficRisk, Dao et al. 2023; SCVLM, Shi et al. 2024). Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al. 2022). DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025) for caption synthesis. nomic-embed-text embedding model. Ollama for local LLM serving. Classic CBR retrieve-reuse paradigm + LLM in-context learning / RAG.
- **contrasts with**:
> Rule-based collision-avoidance decision systems (Li et al. 2021) and end-to-end imitation/RL driving (Chen et al. 2024) lacking interpretability and long-tail robustness; prior LLM-for-driving works operating in simulators or drone-based full-observability BEV settings (DiLu/Wen et al. 2023, Fu et al. 2024; DriveMLM/Wang et al. 2023; LMDrive/Shao et al. 2024; DriveGPT4/Xu et al. 2024); knowledge/RAG-driven LLM driving methods (Cai et al. 2024 'Driving with regulation'; SafeDrive/Zhou et al. 2024; SACA/Zhao et al. 2025). CBR-LLM is positioned as egocentric dashcam (partial-observability, realistic) + experiential case retrieval, contrasting full-observability simulator/BEV approaches; and within its own experiments, similarity-based CBR retrieval is contrasted with random sampling and zero-shot, and risk-aware vs risk-unaware prompting.
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based planning / case-based reasoning). An applied CBR+LLM decision-making system that implements Retrieve + Reuse (and a designed-but-untested Retain/evolving case base) of the CBR cycle: it uses similarity-based same-category case recall as in-context few-shot exemplars adapted by LLM Chain-of-Thought, in the safety-critical autonomous-driving domain from egocentric dashcam video. Sits in the CBR-meets-LLM-ICL line (alongside CaseGPT, CBR-RAG) but is distinguished by its multimodal video grounding, explicit risk-aware prompting, and human-experience case base, while lacking a learned retrieval policy and an experimentally evaluated case-adaptation/retention loop.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- context_budget_and_selection_count
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- explicit_cbr_grounding
- memory_evolution_update
- online_growth
- write_back
- write_back_trigger

<a id="item-cdmem"></a>
### 74. CDMem (Context-Dependent Memory Framework for LLM-Centric Agents)

2025  ·  NAACL 2025 Industry  ·  [paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-industry.80/)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: NAACL 2025 (Volume 3: Industry Track), Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the ACL: Human Language Technologies; pages 1055-1069; DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.naacl-industry.80
- **authors affiliation**: Pengyu Gao (Independent Researcher), Jinming Zhao (Qiyuan Lab, corresponding author), Xinyue Chen (Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics), Yilin Long (Peking University). Pengyu Gao and Jinming Zhao contributed equally.
- **paper url**: https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-industry.80/
- **code url**: https://github.com/piri-gao/CDMem

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Interactive decision-making / embodied text-game agents (navigation and manipulation in situated virtual textual environments).
- **problem setting**:
> Online, interactive single-agent decision-making over multi-trial episodes. An LLM-centric agent (GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4o) interacts with situated text environments, generating reasoning-and-action trajectories. The system is an online learning architecture that continuously learns and updates memory during deployment (no separate offline training phase, unlike Expel/AutoGuide). 5 trials per environment, max 20 interaction steps per trial. Supervision is from environment success/failure feedback (verbal/textual), not labeled gold demonstrations.
- **what is retrieved**: Multilevel knowledge: expert-encoded raw trajectories (CD-exemplars), short-term task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections, environmental summaries), and long-term insights (environmental insights, success- and failure-related task insights).
- **retrieval grounding**: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes during deployment (online learning). The retrievable store is induced and continuously updated at test time from the agent's own trajectories; not a static external corpus.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed-count retrieval driven by similarity/match: retrieves a fixed number of exemplars (all methods use two exemplars) and a fixed number L of insights re-ranked by cosine similarity. It is context-match-gated (intersection of env-match and task-match prioritized) rather than a complete-minimal-set or precision-driven variable-size objective.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] — Retrieve (context-dependent graph index matching), Reuse (retrieved exemplars/insights injected into prompt for action decisions), Revise (short-term reflection on success/failure refines experiences; long-term encoding consolidates), Retain (online write-back into Env-Index/Task-Index). Not framed as CBR by the authors.
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The work is framed via human cognitive memory psychology (context-dependent effect, encoding/storage/retrieval) and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it realizes CBR-like retrieve-reuse-revise-retain mechanisms under a memory-framework framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Multiple units organized by a graph index: (i) raw interaction trajectories / expert-compressed trajectories used as exemplars (CD-exemplars); (ii) task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections); (iii) distilled guideline-style insights (environmental insights and success/failure task insights). Effectively trajectory + experience + guideline-rule granularities keyed by environment-type and task-type.
- **index source**: Online/test-time-induced growing memory. Memory is encoded from the agent's own trials during deployment via multistage encoding (expert -> short-term -> long-term every B tasks) and stored into the context-dependent index; the store grows and updates online.
- **index structure topology**:
> Graph-structured, context-dependent index composed of two dictionaries: Env-Index (environment-dependent long-term memories) and Task-Index (task-dependent, split into Success and Failure sub-dictionaries). Keys are environment/task descriptions (types predefined by domain experts); values are short-term-memory + raw-trajectory pairs. Retrieval matches on environment-type and task-type cues (metadata/context-keyed graph).
- **retriever type**: Hybrid: LLM-as-retriever for index matching (prompt-based Index Matching Module M_match selects best environment/task type) plus dense embedding cosine-similarity (text-embedding-3-small) for non-LLM re-ranking of insights.
- **retriever learning signal**: None (off-the-shelf). The index-matching is a zero-shot prompted LLM module; the re-ranking uses fixed cosine similarity over off-the-shelf embeddings (text-embedding-3-small). No trained/contrastive/RL retriever.
- **query construction**: The current trial's environment description and task goal are used as the query/cue. The prompt-based Index Matching Module takes the current task and environment as input and outputs the best-matching environment-type and task-type, which serve as keys to access the graph index.
- **query granularity**: Task-level (one-shot at the start of a new trial): retrieval is performed per new trial conditioned on its environment description and task goal, not per reasoning step.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot per trial: at the inference/start of a new trial the agent retrieves relevant exemplars and insights once and injects them into the working-memory prompt for the episode.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule (deterministic): retrieval is triggered at the start of each new trial via the index-matching module on the current task/environment cues; there is no token-confidence, uncertainty, or learned-router trigger.
- **reranking**:
> Yes. A non-LLM-based sorting/re-ranking algorithm (Rerank, Algorithm 3) computes cosine similarity between each candidate insight and the short-term memories of the current environment/task and sums the scores to prioritize the most relevant insights. Exemplars are prioritized by env-task intersection match.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> rerank (cosine-similarity-based insight sorting) plus context-match filtering (prioritize exemplars in the env/task intersection, fall back to Task-Index then default Reflexion exemplars). The encoding stages also distill/compress trajectories before storage (expert encoding compresses raw trajectories).
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tool/API retrieval; not a tool-use setting).
- **index content separation**:
> Yes (partial): the graph index keys are lightweight environment/task descriptions while the heavy content (raw trajectories and short-term memories) is stored as the dictionary values and recalled on demand after match; expert encoding compresses raw trajectories into a lighter knowledge chunk before storage.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol; memory index is updated in-process online).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; not a tool-use setting).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation / case reuse: retrieved CD-exemplars, environmental insights, and success/failure task insights are organized together with the current trial and task experiences into a working-memory-style prompt and fed to the LLM to make action decisions.
- **planning integration**:
> One-shot retrieve-then-act at the start of each trial: relevant exemplars and insights are retrieved and assembled into the prompt (working memory) which then drives interleaved ReAct-style reasoning-and-action decisions across the episode. Not inside MCTS/tree search; not per-step retrieval.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-trial (per-episode): retrieval happens once per trial and the retrieved context conditions the whole reasoning-acting rollout; reasoning and acting themselves are interleaved (ReAct) but without per-step re-retrieval.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation plus execution-feedback-driven revision: retrieved insights/exemplars guide the LLM's action decisions (verbatim-style ICL exemplars), and short-term encoding revises experiences by reflecting on successful (build 'Successful Shortcut') and unsuccessful (classify error type: planning/search/operation) trajectories; long-term encoding consolidates these into cross-task insights.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Mixed surface forms injected as text: raw/expert-compressed trajectories (exemplars), distilled free-text insights/guidelines (environmental insights, success/failure task insights), and structured task experiences (successful shortcuts, failure-type reflections, environmental summaries).
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Multilevel: raw trajectory (exemplars), expert-compressed trajectory, short-term task experiences/shortcuts, and distilled cross-task insights/guidelines (environmental and task insights) — spanning concrete demonstrations up to abstract state-aware guideline-like insights.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Context-dependent indexing restricts retrieval to environment/task-type-matched memory (key-cue gating) to avoid irrelevant recall; insight re-ranking by cosine similarity to current short-term memories filters and prioritizes relevant insights; authors report insights significantly reduce agent hallucinations (e.g., correct item-usage context in ALFWorld). No explicit retriever-aware adversarial training.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: graph (context-dependent graph-structured index) combining episodic trajectories, short-term experience, and long-term distilled insights/guidelines.
- **write back**: True. New encoded memories (short-term experiences and, after batching, long-term insights) are written back into the Env-Index and Task-Index dictionaries; trajectories are retained as exemplars.
- **online growth**: True. CDMem is explicitly an online learning framework; the retrievable store grows and updates during deployment as the agent encounters novel environments/tasks (contrasted with offline Expel/AutoGuide).
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success-and-failure plus batched reflective consolidation: short-term encoding writes after each trial reflecting separately on successful and unsuccessful trajectories; long-term Memory Encoding Module fires every B tasks (batch size, e.g. default 1; experiments up to 11) to consolidate accumulated short-term memories into long-term insights and update the indices.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success + failure are stored and used separately. The Task-Index has explicit Success and Failure sub-dictionaries; short-term encoding produces 'Successful Shortcuts' from successes and error-type (planning/search/operation) reflections from failures; long-term task insights summarize positive and negative examples separately (common mistakes and remedies from failures).
- **memory evolution update**:
> append-and-consolidate: short-term memories appended to per-key lists; when a list reaches batch size, long-term encoding processes (consolidates/abstracts) entries into long-term insights stored in the indices, and long-term encoding 'updates memory indexes to maintain relevance and accuracy' (delta-update / re-consolidation rather than pure append-only).
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Retrieval is a fixed prompted index-matching + fixed cosine-similarity re-ranking; it is not an RL/learned retrieval policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No. Single-agent private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing described.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: ALFWorld (134 test environments, composed of 9 rooms and 6 task types, following the ReAct/Reflexion/Expel split) and ScienceWorld (50-task test set: 10 task types whose oracle trajectory average length < 20 steps, top 5 variants each).
- **benchmark family**: embodied / interactive decision-making text environments (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld).
- **baselines**: ReAct (no-memory baseline), Reflexion, Expel-Online, AutoGuide-Online. (Expel and AutoGuide are originally offline; the paper compares against their online variants.)
- **key metrics**: Task success rate (%) on ALFWorld; average score on ScienceWorld. Also reports computational cost (API calls per sample, total API calls, monetary cost) and success-rate-vs-number-of-trials curves.
- **headline result**:
> Using GPT-4o-mini, CDMem reaches 85.8% success rate on ALFWorld and 56.0 (56.02) score on ScienceWorld, surpassing state-of-the-art online LLM-centric methods. With Configuration 2 (memory components on GPT-4o), ALFWorld success rate reaches 90.0%, nearly 10 points above Expel-Online's 80.3%; on ScienceWorld CDMem's 56.02 exceeds AutoGuide-Online's 44.84 by over 10 points.
- **ablations**:
> ALFWorld ablations (Table 1): full CDMem 85.8; w/o expert encoding 72.3 (~10pt drop, largest impact alongside env insights); w/o task-encoding 84.3; w/o env-encoding 74.3 (~10pt drop); w/o CD-Exemplars 80.6 (~5pt drop). ScienceWorld ablations (Table 2): full 56.0; w/o task-encoding 40.9; w/o env-encoding 54.7 (only ~2pt drop). Batch-size study (Table 6): SR stable across batch sizes 1-11 (83.6-86.4), demonstrating CDMem tolerates larger insight-extraction batches than Expel/AutoGuide. Analyses: expert encoding before short-term encoding yields more accurate successful-shortcut summaries; env/task insights reduce hallucinations.
- **evaluation decoupling**: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate / score) plus cost are reported; no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) for the index-matching or re-ranking are reported.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome-based (success rate / score). Some process-oriented analysis is provided: success-rate-vs-trial-number curves (improvement between trial 0 and trial 1) and qualitative hallucination-reduction analysis, but no quantitative step-wise retrieval/planning accuracy.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reported (Table 3, ALFWorld vs Reflexion): CDMem uses 4 API calls per sample vs Reflexion's 2; 1155 total API calls vs 781; monetary cost $0.51 vs $0.33 for processing the dataset. Authors frame CDMem as efficient given its accuracy gains; batch-size analysis shows insight extraction remains effective at larger batches, reducing long-term-encoding cost.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k injection: all methods use two exemplars; a fixed number L of insights is retrieved then re-ranked by cosine similarity (reranked-then-selected). Max 20 interaction steps per trial. Exemplar selection prioritizes env-task intersection, falling back to Task-Index then default Reflexion exemplars.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> ALFWorld test set reuses the established 134-environment split (9 rooms x 6 task types) from ReAct/Reflexion/Expel. ScienceWorld test set is newly constructed: from 30 ScienceWorld task types, select 10 types with oracle average trajectory length < 20, take top 5 variants each -> 50 environments; answer verifiability via environment-defined success/score. Best-system scores (CDMem 85.8% ALFWorld GPT-4o-mini; 56.0 ScienceWorld) signal task difficulty.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Reflexion (verbal RL reflection; CDMem's short-term encoding extends it and uses its default exemplars as fallback), ReAct (interleaved reasoning+acting backbone and ALFWorld test split), Expel and AutoGuide (offline experience/insight and state-aware guideline extraction, extended to online here).
- **contrasts with**:
> Expel-Online and AutoGuide-Online (offline experience/guideline learners; CDMem is online and continuously self-improving), Reflexion (reflects only on failures and uses fixed exemplars; CDMem reflects on successes and failures with context-dependent exemplars), and memory methods like MemoryBank/ChatDB/TiM that retrieve directly from the whole memory pool without an efficient context-dependent index.
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based / experience-based planning): online experience/memory-based LLM agents that retrieve self-generated trajectories, experiences, and distilled insights to improve interactive decision-making; sits in the Reflexion -> Expel/AutoGuide lineage, adding human-memory-inspired multistage encoding and a context-dependent graph index for online learning.

<a id="item-cops"></a>
### 75. CoPS: Empowering LLM Agents with Provable Cross-Task Experience Sharing

2025  ·  ICLR 2025  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16670)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**:
> ICLR 2025 (Poster). Listed as 'ICLR 2025 Poster' in the OpenReview ICLR.cc/2025/Conference submissions (Submission #12611, forum id=9W6Z9IeLzc). An earlier version was also a poster at the NeurIPS 2024 Language Gamification Workshop (LanGame, forum id=8DLW1saLEY, Submission #18). Preprint arXiv:2410.16670 (cs.LG; cs.AI), submitted 22 Oct 2024 (v1).
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16670
- **code url**: https://github.com/uclaml/COPS

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: LLM-agent sequential reasoning / interactive decision-making across embodied household tasks (ALFWorld), web shopping (WebShop), and multi-hop knowledge-intensive QA (HotPotQA). Spans embodied, web, and QA agent domains.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, single-agent gradient-free sequential decision-making formalized as a task space M, state space S, action space A where state s is a text history and an experience tau is a complete trial (success reward r=1, else 0). The agent solves each task over up to 10 trials with cross-trial and cross-task experience sharing. CoPS is designed to work in two settings: (1) OFFLINE, where the agent has access to an external static dataset/memory bank of pre-collected experiences (possibly from other tasks/agents); and (2) ONLINE, where the agent gathers its own experiences through environment interaction and appends them to the memory bank after each trial. No parameter updates (pure in-context). Supervision is the binary environment success signal r(tau). A theoretical framework analyzes OfflineCoPS (pessimism principle) and OnlineCoPS (optimism principle) with provable suboptimality / regret bounds depending on LLM pretraining quality and distribution matching.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Past experiences = complete prior-task trial trajectories (tau, full text trials) from a memory bank. Successful cross-task experience trajectories are selected and concatenated as in-context demonstrations. The retrievable unit is the whole trial trajectory; the method explicitly supports experiences from DIFFERENT tasks than the current one (cross-task sharing).
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID by design / GROWING in the main experiments. The memory bank D may be a static external pre-collected dataset (offline setting) OR a self-grown episodic store the agent writes to after each trial (online setting). In the reported Alfworld/Webshop/HotPotQA experiments the bank is grown online over 10 trials per task (and shared across tasks), so it functions as a growing/episodic memory; the offline variant treats it as a static corpus. No external KB/doc corpus is retrieved.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Distribution-matching / fixed-size sampling objective rather than a deterministic top-k ranking or a completeness/minimal-set objective. CoPS solves p_hat = argmax_p E_{tau~p}[r(tau)] - d(p, Dec(.|s1)) (a pessimism-regularized reward-maximizing distribution over the bank), then samples k experiences i.i.d. from p_hat(tau) proportional to r(tau)*exp(-c*cos-distance). k is a fixed in-context memory size (k=5 in experiments; plateaus at k=3). It is a fixed-k selection but via stochastic distribution-matched sampling, not similarity argmax top-k (the c->infinity limit recovers nearest-neighbor; c=0 is uniform over successes).
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes (distribution-matched, pessimism-based selection of prior-task experience trajectories from the memory bank), Reuse: yes (concatenated raw experiences used as in-context demonstrations for the new task), Revise: no (retrieved trajectories are used verbatim and not adapted/edited per case at solve time), Retain: yes in the online setting (new trial experiences appended to the memory bank); no in the offline setting].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper frames itself as cross-task experience sharing / experience-assisted sequential reasoning grounded in offline-RL pessimism and online-learning optimism principles (citing Jin et al. 2021 pessimism, Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011 optimism, Lin et al. 2023 in-context RL theory). It does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'; it realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under an experience-sharing / RAG-for-decision-making framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: full trajectory: a complete trial / experience tau (the full text of a prior task's trial, including the thought-action-observation sequence). Multiple selected trajectories tau^1..tau^k are concatenated into one experience collection T = tau^1 | ... | tau^k.
- **index source**:
> Growing memory (online setting, used in the headline experiments) or static external dataset (offline setting); hybrid construction. The bank D is unrestricted and may contain experiences for different tasks or different solution strategies for the same task. In the online experiments the bank is initialized and grown from the agent's own trials across tasks; the method also supports a pre-collected/external (e.g., from other agents or RL systems) static bank.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat store of trajectory experiences. Each experience is embedded with a language embedding model (gte-Qwen2 7B) into a Euclidean vector; selection scores experiences by cosine distance to a decoder-produced reference experience tau^{s1}. No graph, hierarchy, or cluster structure; it is a flat memory bank with embedding-based scoring.
- **retriever type**:
> Dense embedding-based selection (off-the-shelf gte-Qwen2 7B Instruct embeddings) combined with a reward-weighted, pessimism-regularized sampling distribution. Not BM25, not a learned/trained retriever, not LLM-as-retriever; the LLM itself supplies the 'decoder' reference experience but selection is embedding cosine + reward weighting.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> none (off-the-shelf embedder) plus reward weighting; the selection rule is theoretically derived (pessimism principle from offline RL), not trained. The embedding function e is a fixed pretrained model (gte-Qwen2 7B); the selection probability p_hat(tau) is proportional to the binary task reward r(tau) times exp(-c*cosine-distance to the decoder reference). There is no contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning, no RL-trained retriever; the only 'signal' is the binary success reward used as a multiplicative weight and the embedding similarity.
- **query construction**:
> Raw initial-state-conditioned reference. CoPS uses a 'decoder' (Dec) that, given the current initial state s1, outputs a reference experience tau^{s1} from the bank that starts with the same initial state s1 (most recent one if several) - reflecting how the LLM would solve the task without intervention. The query/key is therefore the embedding of this decoder reference experience tau^{s1} (an LLM-behavior proxy for the current task), not a hand-built query; experiences are scored by cosine distance to it.
- **query granularity**:
> task-level / trial-level (one-shot per trial at t=0). The decoder reference and the experience selection are computed once at the start of each trial from the initial state s1; the selected experience collection T is then fixed for the whole step-by-step rollout of that trial. (Contrasts with RAP, which re-retrieves per stage within a trial.)
- **when to retrieve**:
> one-shot per trial. Selection is performed once at the beginning of each trial (each of the up to 10 trials per task triggers a fresh selection), then the concatenated experiences are kept fixed during the within-trial step-by-step action generation. No within-trial uncertainty-triggered or adaptive re-retrieval.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> fixed schedule (per-trial). Selection is triggered unconditionally at the start of every trial; there is no confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier/reflection-token trigger and no agent-initiated mid-trial retrieval. The paper highlights that because the prompt prefix is shared/fixed across trials, this enables prefix-caching efficiency (vs RAP's frequent per-stage embedding queries).
- **reranking**:
> No separate reranking stage. Experiences are scored once by the reward-weighted exp(-c*cosine-distance) distribution p_hat and sampled; there is no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker. The scalar c interpolates between uniform sampling over successes (c=0) and deterministic nearest-experience selection (c->infinity).
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> None / minimal. Selected successful experience trajectories tau^1..tau^k are concatenated verbatim into a single trajectory T and placed at the beginning of the prompt; no compression, decomposition, distillation, or distractor-filtering is applied. The reward-weighting (only successful, r=1, experiences receive positive probability) acts as an implicit relevance/quality filter at selection time rather than a post-retrieval refinement.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; tools/environments are fixed per benchmark - ALFWorld actions, WebShop search/HTML, HotPotQA Wikipedia search).
- **index content separation**: N/A. No separation of a lightweight index from heavy content; experiences are embedded for scoring and the full selected trajectories are loaded into the prompt.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool index; environment interaction is via each benchmark's native action interface).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> prompt augmentation: the concatenated selected experience collection T = tau^1 | ... | tau^k is prepended to the prompt, and the agent then generates each action a_h ~ LLM(. | T, s_h) conditioned on T and the current state. No fine-tuning or latent-token injection; experiences are reused in-context as demonstrations of how to solve (cross-task) trials.
- **planning integration**:
> retrieve-then-plan, one-shot exemplars at trial start. Per trial, CoPS (1) selects k distribution-matched successful experiences via the pessimism objective, (2) concatenates them into T, then (3) runs the LLM agent step-by-step (a_h ~ LLM(.|T,s_h)) until success or the step budget H. No MCTS/tree search (explicitly contrasted with LATS's tree search), no hierarchical subtask decomposition, no per-step re-retrieval. Across trials, the online memory bank grows and the selection improves, giving cross-trial/cross-task improvement.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**:
> per-trial / per-episode (per-answer at the trial level). Experience selection and prompt augmentation happen once per trial; within a trial the selected context is fixed while the agent emits a multi-step thought-action-observation rollout. Not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Verbatim ICL exemplar reuse: selected experience trajectories are concatenated and injected as-is as in-context demonstrations; there is no explicit case adaptation/revision, execution-feedback rewriting, critic-guided revision, or fine-tuning of the retrieved cases. Adaptation to the current task happens implicitly through the LLM conditioning on T plus the principled distribution-matched selection that picks experiences closest to the current task's decoder distribution.
- **retrieved item representation**: raw trajectory: selected experiences are injected as raw full prior trials (concatenated text trajectories of thought/action/observation steps) used as in-context demonstrations. No distillation into guidelines, no executable skills, no latent tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> raw trajectory (concrete full prior-trial demonstrations). CoPS deliberately reuses successful raw experience trajectories as demonstrations rather than distilling them into higher-level strategies, insights, or workflows; its novelty is the principled distribution-matched SELECTION of these raw trajectories, not their abstraction.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Pessimism-based distribution matching: the selection objective penalizes distribution shift from the LLM's own decoder distribution (d(p, Dec(.|s1))), keeping selected experiences close to what the LLM would naturally do for the current task, which provably guards against risky out-of-distribution / poorly-matched experiences. Reward weighting restricts positive selection probability to successful (r=1) experiences. The scalar c tunes the adaptability-vs-robustness trade-off (smaller models benefit from a small nonzero c). Theoretically, the suboptimality/regret is bounded by the LLM pretraining error times a chi-square distribution-mismatch term, formalizing robustness to distribution shift.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: episodic experience bank (a memory bank D of full prior trials). Can be a self-grown online episodic store or an external static dataset; not a skill-library, workflow, graph, or latent memory.
- **write back**:
> Yes (in the online setting). After completing a trial, the agent appends the new experience trajectory to the memory bank D for future use (Algorithm 1, online line: 'the agent updates the memory bank D by adding the new experience'). In the offline setting the bank is a fixed pre-collected dataset (no write-back).
- **online growth**: Yes (online setting, used in the main Alfworld/Webshop/HotPotQA experiments): the bank grows trial-by-trial during deployment as new trials are added, enabling cross-trial improvement over the 10 trials and cross-task sharing. In the offline-setting variant the bank is static.
- **write back trigger**:
> on-trial-completion (every finished trial is appended in the online setting), i.e., per-trial append regardless of success/failure outcome of that trial (the experience's reward r(tau) is stored alongside and used to weight future selection). It is not reflective/critique-gated and not human-validated; storage happens automatically at the end of each trial. (Offline: never / no write-back.)
- **failure experience usage**:
> Failures are stored (every trial, including failed ones with r=0, is appended to the online bank) but are effectively NOT reused for prompting: the selection probability p_hat(tau) is proportional to the reward r(tau), so r=0 (failed) experiences get zero selection probability and only successful experiences are surfaced as demonstrations. So failures are recorded but not used as negative/contrastive demonstrations; no failure-derived corrective rules. Baselines like Reflexion/LATS instead reflect on failures.
- **memory evolution update**:
> append-only. New trial experiences (with their rewards) are added to D; stored experiences are not merged, deduplicated, refined, overwritten, or pruned in the method (the decoder simply prefers the most-recent same-initial-state experience). The Limitations section notes that outdated/poorly-aligned experiences can hurt and suggests dynamic memory management as future work, implying no automatic forgetting/pruning.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partly principled-but-not-learned: experience selection IS a theoretically optimized SELECTION POLICY (the pessimism/optimism-principled distribution p_hat over the bank derived from offline/online RL theory with provable suboptimality/regret), but it is NOT a trained/RL-updated parametric policy and NOT a fixed similarity top-k either. It is a closed-form reward-weighted, distribution-matched sampling rule (r(tau)*exp(-c*cosine)) with theoretical guarantees, sitting between fixed top-k and learned RL retrieval.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Cross-TASK sharing within a single agent is the central contribution: experiences from previously solved (different) tasks are shared and selected for new tasks. The offline setting also allows ingesting experiences from EXTERNAL sources (e.g., other agents / RL systems / pre-collected datasets), enabling a form of cross-source experience sharing, but the method is single-agent and does not implement collaborative multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing (multi-agent extension is listed as future work).

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: ALFWorld (134 tasks, simulated household, textual feedback), WebShop (50 products, catalog of >1M items, HTML page + search engine interaction), and HotPotQA (100 multi-hop QA tasks, Wikipedia retrieval). Each algorithm is evaluated over up to 10 trials per task.
- **benchmark family**: embodied (ALFWorld); web (WebShop); QA / multi-hop (HotPotQA).
- **baselines**:
> Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2024, reflection-driven multi-trial self-improvement, up to 3 recent same-task reflections), RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024, retrieval-augmented planning with per-stage top-k trajectory-fragment in-context demonstrations), and LATS (Zhou et al. 2023, Language Agent Tree Search, tree-structured search with reflection). React is cited as the underlying ICL agent foundation but is not a main results baseline.
- **key metrics**: Task success rate (%) - success after up to 10 trials (ALFWorld over 134 tasks, WebShop over 50 products x10 trials each, HotPotQA over 100 QA tasks). Sample-efficiency metric: total number of generated tokens (Table 3, WebShop) as a compute/efficiency proxy.
- **headline result**:
> CoPS consistently outperforms SOTA baselines across all three benchmarks and both model sizes. ALFWorld: 94% (Llama 3.1 8B) and 100% (70B), vs Reflexion 86%/94% and RAP 70%/93% - notably CoPS with the small 8B model (94%) matches Reflexion's 70B (94%). WebShop: 50% (8B) / 56% (70B), vs RAP 42%/42% (best baseline), a +8% (8B) and +14% (70B) absolute gain; Reflexion 30%/30%, LATS 24%/32%. HotPotQA: 63% (8B) / 65% (70B), vs Reflexion 56%/61% and LATS 55%/64%. Efficiency: on WebShop with Llama 3.1 8B, LATS generates 1,555,365 tokens vs CoPS 314,336 (>=5x fewer), under matched runtime.
- **ablations**:
> Two hyperparameters ablated on ALFWorld (Llama 3.1 8B and 70B): (1) Scaling factor c in {0,1,5,10} with k=5 fixed - for the smaller 8B model a small nonzero c (e.g., c=1) generally yields the best performance, balancing adaptability vs robustness; larger models are less sensitive. This empirically matches Theorem 5.4's insight that more powerful LLMs should align more strongly with the decoder distribution. (2) Number of in-context experiences k from 1 to 10 with c=0 - performance improves up to k=3 then plateaus for both model sizes, so >3 experiences give minimal gains. Final hyperparameters (Table 5): ALFWorld k=5,c=5 (both sizes); WebShop k=5,c=0; HotPotQA k=5,c=5 (8B) and k=5,c=0 (70B).
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No. Only end-to-end task success rate (and token-count efficiency) is reported; no intrinsic retrieval/selection metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, selection completeness) are reported separately - selection quality is evaluated indirectly through downstream success and the theoretical suboptimality/regret bounds.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome (binary task success rate, r(tau) in {0,1}). A sample-efficiency / process-cost proxy is reported (total generated tokens, Table 3) and trends over the 10 trials are shown (Figure: success rate vs trial index). No step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality metric. Theoretical guarantees (suboptimality gap, regret) provide a process-level analysis but are not empirical metrics.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Strong efficiency emphasis. On WebShop, CoPS generates far fewer tokens than tree-search LATS (8B: 314,336 vs 1,555,365, ~5x; 70B: 113,849 vs 1,058,752, ~9x) under matched runtime, and the fixed shared prompt prefix across trials maximizes prefix-caching in modern LLM-serving (SGLang), giving efficiency gains over RAP's frequent per-stage embedding queries. CoPS also achieves higher accuracy with the smaller 8B model than baselines need 70B for (ALFWorld 94% 8B = Reflexion 70B), i.e., better accuracy-per-compute. No dollar/latency figures, but token counts and serving-efficiency arguments are central. Token counts for Reflexion/RAP on WebShop are also tabulated (8B: 159,131 / 107,504; 70B: 125,406 / 109,245).
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k selection, budget-capped by k. In experiments k=5 in-context experiences per trial (Table 5), though the ablation shows performance plateaus at k=3. Selection is reward-weighted distribution-matched sampling of k trajectories (proportional to r(tau)*exp(-c*cosine)) rather than reranked-then-truncated; the scalar c (in {0,5} across benchmarks) controls how peaked the selection distribution is. The selected experiences are concatenated and prepended; prompt budget is bounded by k trajectories.
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (uses existing benchmarks: ALFWorld 134 tasks; WebShop 50 products evaluated x 10 trials; HotPotQA 100 QA tasks; up to 10 trials per task).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> React (Yao et al. 2022b, ICL agent foundation); RAP (Kagaya et al. 2024, retrieval of in-context demonstrations for agents - CoPS adds principled selection and avoids per-stage manual splitting); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2024); LATS (Zhou et al. 2023); pessimism principle in offline RL (Jin et al. 2021); optimism principle in online decision-making (Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011); in-context RL / LLM-agent statistical theory (Lin et al. 2023; He et al. 2024; Park et al. 2024 on regret of LLM agents); Raparthy et al. 2023 (high-quality experiences as ICL demonstrations from external RL systems); gte-Qwen2 embeddings (Li et al. 2023b); SGLang serving with prefix caching (Zheng et al. 2023); Llama 3.1 (Dubey et al. 2024).
- **contrasts with**:
> Reflection-driven reasoning (Reflexion, LATS) that relies only on pretrained-model knowledge and same-task self-reflection, limiting novel-scenario performance and risking hallucination; experience-assisted reasoning that depends on manually-curated or external-expert experiences and lacks clear principles for selecting representative examples (RAP - which also needs frequent per-stage embedding queries and benchmark-specific manual trajectory splitting, and lacks an effective selection algorithm); resource-intensive tree-search methods (LATS) with poor sample efficiency; fine-tuning-based agent learning (Feng et al. 2024) with high compute cost. CoPS instead offers a single, theoretically grounded, benchmark-agnostic, distribution-matched cross-task selection rule.
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based / experience planning): a theory-grounded experience-selection LLM agent in the lineage of retrieval-augmented / experience-assisted planners (React -> Reflexion / RAP -> CoPS). It advances the sub-topic by providing a provable pessimism-based (offline) / optimism-based (online) experience-selection policy with suboptimality and regret bounds, distinguishing it from heuristic similarity-top-k experience retrieval (RAP) and from insight-distillation experience agents (e.g., ExpeL).

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):
