<a id="item-cer"></a>
### 76. Contextual Experience Replay (CER): Contextual Experience Replay for Self-Improvement of Language Agents

2025  ·  ACL 2025  ·  [paper](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.694.pdf)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**:
> ACL 2025 (Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Long Papers, pp. 14179-14198). Also released as preprint arXiv:2506.06698 (submitted 7 Jun 2025). An earlier version was submitted to ICLR 2025 under the title 'Contextual Experience Replay for Continual Learning of Language Agents' (OpenReview id RXvFK5dnpz).
- **authors affiliation**:
> Yitao Liu (Princeton University; work done while a student researcher at Princeton, now a PhD student at The University of Hong Kong / xlang-ai), Chenglei Si (Stanford University), Karthik Narasimhan (Princeton University), Shunyu Yao (Princeton University). Lead author Yitao Liu; corresponding contact lyitao17@gmail.com.
- **paper url**: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.694/

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: LLM-agent sequential decision-making / web navigation (web agents). Text-based web navigation (WebArena) and multimodal/visual web navigation (VisualWebArena). Decision-making / web domain.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, single-agent, training-free (no parameter updates) continual self-improvement of an LLM web-navigation agent at inference time. The agent (a ReAct-style policy built on GPT-4o in BrowserGym) solves multi-step web tasks with a large state/action space and no environment-specific prior knowledge. CER distills reusable experiences (environment dynamics + decision-making skills) from past trajectories into a dynamic in-context memory buffer, retrieves relevant ones for each new task, and 'replays' them in the context window. Three settings are studied, distinguished by the source/time of trajectories: OFFLINE (a fixed training set of trajectories collected in advance via human annotation or LLM self-guided exploration, then frozen), ONLINE (no trajectories initially; the agent learns from its own past-task trajectories during inference, looping distill->retrieve->solve), and HYBRID (offline learning first, then continued online self-evolution). Supervision: ground-truth rewards are NOT required to function (a key claimed advantage over AutoGuide/AutoManual/AWM); CER distills from both successful and failed trajectories. Backbone: GPT-4o-2024-0513 (also tested with Llama-3.1-70B), temperature 0.1, max 30 steps per task.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Distilled experiences of two kinds: (1) environment DYNAMICS - summaries of web pages with their content, inferred possible usages, and corresponding URL (state knowledge enabling state-aware decisions / direct URL navigation); and (2) SKILLS - common decision-making patterns/workflows, each with a brief abstract summary (e.g. 'Navigate to forum {forum name}') plus step-by-step guidelines containing natural-language summaries and concrete action examples. Both are distilled from past (successful and failed) trajectories and stored in the dynamic experience buffer.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes itself (with offline and hybrid variants). The retrievable store is a dynamic experience buffer populated by distilling experiences from trajectories: in the online setting it grows at test time from the agent's own past-task trajectories; in the offline setting it is built from a fixed pre-collected trajectory set and then frozen; hybrid combines both. Not a static external corpus (docs/KB/API); it is a self-generated/self-distilled experience memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking objective with a precision flavor: the LLM retriever selects the top-k most useful and informative experiences (capped at k_d=5 dynamics and k_s=5 skills in the WebArena/VisualWebArena implementation), and is explicitly instructed to 'select not more than max skills/pages'. No formal minimal-complete-set recovery objective; selection is a budgeted top-k of the most helpful experiences, not a fixed retrieval ranking benchmark.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes (LLM-as-retriever selects top-k relevant dynamics/skills per task), Reuse: yes (experiences replayed in context to guide ReAct decisions), Revise: partial (experiences are distilled/abstracted and de-duplicated at write time; retrieved experiences themselves are reused as-is without per-case solution adaptation at solve time), Retain: yes (distilled experiences merged into the dynamic buffer, growing online)].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper frames itself via experience replay (citing Lin-style replay, Schaul et al. Prioritized Experience Replay 2016, Rolnick et al. 2019 experience replay for continual learning) and the Recognition-Primed Decision model (Klein 1998); it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or use the term case-based reasoning. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under an experience-replay / continual-learning / self-improvement framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Two experience-level units: (a) a single environment-dynamics entry = a page summary (page contents + possible usages + URL), and (b) a single skill = a workflow-routine / guideline (sub-goal summary + step-by-step guideline with natural-language steps and concrete action examples). So the retrieved unit is a distilled experience (workflow-routine / guideline-rule / state-summary), not a raw full trajectory.
- **index source**:
> Growing memory; construction time varies by setting: online -> online/test-time-induced (buffer grows from self-generated past-task trajectories during inference); offline -> offline-induced and then frozen (built from a pre-collected human-annotated or LLM-explored trajectory set); hybrid -> hybrid (offline-induced then online-grown). Not a static external corpus.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat experience buffer organized as two separate lists/pools: a dynamics pool (page summaries keyed by content/usage/URL) and a skills pool (workflow guidelines). Selection is done by the LLM reading the task goal, website descriptions, and ALL available dynamics/skills in the buffer (no learned vector index, no graph or explicit hierarchy described; experiences are presented to the model as enumerated id'd items). Effectively metadata/context-keyed flat lists rather than a dense vector index.
- **retriever type**:
> LLM-as-retriever: a VLM (GPT-4o) is prompted with the task goal, website descriptions, and all dynamics/skills in the buffer, and outputs the top-k useful experience ids to retrieve. Separate retrieval prompts for dynamics and for skills (Figs. 5-6). Not BM25/dense-embedding-based; selection is performed by the language model itself.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> none (off-the-shelf / prompted): the retrieval module is an un-finetuned GPT-4o prompted to pick the most useful experiences for the current task goal. There is no contrastive training, no LM-feedback fine-tuning, no Bradley-Terry/preference learning, and no RL-trained retrieval policy; retrieval relevance is judged zero-shot by the LLM via instructions in the retrieval prompt.
- **query construction**:
> The query is the current task's goal plus the website descriptions, passed (as natural language) to the LLM retrieval module, which breaks the task into a few steps and selects pages/skills helpful for each step. No embedding query; intent is decomposed by the retriever LLM (the retrieval prompt instructs it to 'break the task down into a few steps and then select pages/skills').
- **query granularity**:
> task-level (one-shot at t=0): retrieval is performed once per new task, conditioned on the task goal, before solving; the retrieved dynamics/skills are replayed into the context for that whole task. (The retriever internally decomposes the task into steps to choose experiences, but the retrieval call itself is task-level, not per-step re-retrieval.)
- **when to retrieve**: one-shot: for each new task, CER runs the retrieval+replay module once (after any distillation from prior trajectories) and augments the context before the agent acts. No iterative/uncertainty-triggered or learned-router mid-episode retrieval is described.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> fixed schedule: retrieval is triggered unconditionally at the start of every new task (the buffer is queried, top-k dynamics/skills are selected and injected). There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned-complexity-classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-episode trigger.
- **reranking**: None as a separate stage. The single LLM-as-retriever pass simultaneously filters and selects the top-k useful experiences; there is no downstream cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranker applied after retrieval.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Refinement happens primarily at DISTILLATION/write time rather than post-retrieval: experiences are distilled into abstract, generalized form (e.g. 'navigate to forum {forum name}' with variable placeholders), de-duplicated against existing buffer entries to avoid repetitive distillation, and split into dynamics vs skills. At retrieval, the LLM selects/filters the most useful top-k (a relevance-filtering step). Selected structured experiences are then programmatically mapped (f) into natural-language descriptions before injection. No compression or reason-in-documents distillation of fetched items beyond this selection + format mapping.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval method; web actions are issued via BrowserGym action space, e.g. click/fill/goto, not a retrievable tool/API index).
- **index content separation**:
> Partial: experiences are stored as structured entries (dynamics: name+contents+usages+URL; skills: name+steps) and only the selected top-k are programmatically expanded into natural-language descriptions and loaded into context at solve time, so a lightweight selectable index is separated from on-demand full content (akin to a shortcut-list-then-content pattern). Not a formal SOP-index-then-content design.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (not a tool-retrieval system; environment interaction is via the BrowserGym web action API / accessibility tree, not RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling tool stores).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> prompt augmentation (in-context replay): the k selected experiences E={E_1,...,E_k} are transformed via a programmatic mapping f into natural-language experience descriptions E_NL=f(E), then integrated into the model context C via g, yielding an augmented context C'=g(C,E_NL). The underlying ReAct decision policy then conditions on these replayed dynamics/skills to issue better actions. No fine-tuning or latent-token injection; everything is textual in-context learning.
- **planning integration**:
> retrieve-then-plan with one-shot exemplars at plan/task time: for each task CER retrieves and injects relevant dynamics + skills into the ReAct agent's context, after which the agent runs its normal multi-step ReAct (think-act-observe) loop (max 30 steps). Experiences guide both state navigation (dynamics, incl. direct URL goto) and action selection (skills). No MCTS/tree search inside CER itself (though it is shown to compose with a sampling+reranking 'single-turn tree search' surrogate). Retrieval is task-level, not interleaved per planning step.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-answer (per-task/per-episode): retrieval and experience replay occur once before the ReAct rollout for a task; the injected dynamics/skills stay fixed across the multi-step reasoning/acting of that episode. Not per-CoT-step, per-sentence/token, or per-tool-call.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Verbatim in-context replay with LLM-prompted generalization at distillation rather than per-case solve-time adaptation: retrieved dynamics/skills are injected as-is (after programmatic NL formatting) and the ReAct policy adapts them implicitly via reasoning. The 'adaptation' is front-loaded into distillation, where the LLM abstracts experiences with variable placeholders so they apply broadly; no execution-feedback-driven revision of a retrieved case at solve time.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled free-text experience descriptions injected into the system prompt: (a) environment-dynamics entries formatted as 'Dynamics i: <page name> / contents / potential usages / URL', and (b) skill entries formatted as 'Skill i: <name> / Steps:' with natural-language steps interleaved with concrete executable action examples (e.g. click(id), fill(id, text), goto(url)). So a structured-note / free-text-workflow representation containing both NL summaries and concrete action snippets (not raw trajectories, not latent tokens).
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled, abstract/generalized: experiences are explicitly required to be abstract and broadly applicable (variables/placeholders like {forum name} instead of literal values). Two complementary abstraction types - state-aware environment dynamics (page/state knowledge + URLs) and reusable decision-making skills/workflows (sub-goal-level procedures with step guidelines). Higher abstraction than raw trajectories; the paper argues (cross-template SR) that improvement comes from fine-grained generalizable experiences, not memorized whole trajectories.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Several: (1) Robustness to noisy/incorrect trajectories is shown empirically (Sec. 5.6 / Table 7): CER distills from both successful and failed trajectories and still beats the baseline; using ground-truth-filtered success-only (CER_success) gives only a modest gain (33.5 vs 31.4 avg), evidencing tolerance to noisy experiences, credited to the LLM's implicit reasoning and the flexible natural-language representation. (2) The retrieval LLM filters out useful experiences for the current task (relevance selection). (3) De-duplication at distillation avoids redundant/repetitive experiences. (4) Abstraction/generalization of experiences reduces overfitting to specific tasks.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Workflow/procedural + episodic-derived semantic memory: a dynamic experience buffer holding distilled environment dynamics (state/semantic knowledge of pages) and skills (procedural workflows). It is an abstracted experience memory (not raw episodic trajectories, not a skill-program library of executable code, not a graph).
- **write back**:
> Yes. The distillation module D writes new distilled experiences (dynamics + skills) into the dynamic buffer epsilon. In online/hybrid settings, after completing each task the agent distills experiences from the just-finished trajectory and merges them into the buffer; in offline, distillation from the pre-collected trajectory set populates the buffer once.
- **online growth**:
> Yes in online and hybrid settings: the buffer grows at test/inference time from self-generated past-task trajectories (loop between distillation stage B and inference stage C). In the pure offline setting the buffer is built from a fixed training trajectory set and then frozen (no growth during inference).
- **write back trigger**:
> on-success-and-failure, per-task (reflective distillation): after each completed task (online/hybrid) or for each trajectory in the offline set, the distillation module distills dynamics and skills and merges them into the buffer. Writes occur regardless of success/failure (CER does NOT require ground-truth reward to write); the model is shown existing buffer experiences to avoid repetitive distillation. Not per-step and not human-validated (human only supplies optional offline trajectories).
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success+failure used together: CER explicitly distills fine-grained skills and environment dynamics from BOTH successful and failed trajectories (a stated contribution and a contrast with reward-dependent prior work). Ablation (Table 7) shows the success-only variant CER_success (using ground-truth evaluators to keep only successful trajectories) is only slightly better (33.5 vs 31.4 average), so distillation from failed cases is not a bottleneck and failures contribute useful dynamics/skills. Failures are not stored as separate corrective negative rules; they are mined for reusable dynamics/skills like successes.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Append-and-merge with de-duplication: new distilled experiences are merged into the buffer continually across time, and the distillation model is provided the existing buffer to avoid repetitive/duplicate distillation (so it appends genuinely new dynamics/skills rather than rewriting all). The paper contrasts CER with Agent Workflow Memory, which rewrites the whole workflow memory; CER instead continuously merges new experiences (incremental append/merge rather than full-overwrite). No explicit forget/prune or per-entry refine-overwrite mechanism is described.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No. Case/experience selection is performed by a prompted (un-finetuned) GPT-4o acting as the retriever; it is not an RL-/value-optimized or contrastively-trained retrieval policy. (Selection is LLM-judged top-k rather than fixed embedding top-k, but it is not a learned policy in the trained-parameters sense.)
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> No. Single-agent private memory: one agent accumulates and replays its own distilled experience buffer. The paper does show generalization across task templates and compatibility/composition with other off-the-shelf agent methods (e.g. sampling+reranking 'tree search' surrogate), but not memory sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024b; 812 tasks across 5 sites/domains: Shopping, Shopping Admin/CMS, Forum/Reddit, Gitlab, Map) and VisualWebArena (Koh et al. 2024a; 910 multimodal tasks across Classifieds, Shopping, Forum). Environment: BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024), with Set-of-Marks (SoM) image annotation for VisualWebArena. Backbones: GPT-4o-2024-0513 (main), Llama-3.1-70B (open-source validation on the Gitlab split).
- **benchmark family**: web (WebArena; VisualWebArena - realistic interactive web navigation / multimodal web agents).
- **baselines**:
> GPT-4o w/ BrowserGym (ReAct-format) reproduced by the authors as the primary comparable baseline; WebArena original agent (Zhou et al. 2024b); AutoEval (Pan et al. 2024); VisualWebArena original agent (Koh et al. 2024a); Tree Search (Koh et al. 2024b) on VisualWebArena; SteP (Sodhi et al. 2024) listed for reference only (uses human-designed per-website policies, not autonomous, so excluded from fair comparison). For synergy: trajectory sampling + reranking (a single-turn surrogate of Tree Search). For open-source: ReAct baseline with Llama-3.1-70B. Related-work contrasts: ExpeL, Synapse, Voyager, Generative Agents, Learn-by-interact, AutoGuide, AutoManual, Agent Workflow Memory (AWM).
- **key metrics**:
> Task success rate (SR, %) overall and per website/domain; relative SR improvement over baseline; cross-template success rate (ct-SR); stability (% of baseline-solved tasks retained) and plasticity (% additional tasks solved vs baseline); token efficiency (Delta input tokens, Delta tokens %, Delta SR %).
- **headline result**:
> On WebArena, CER_hybrid reaches 36.7% average SR, relatively improving the GPT-4o w/ BrowserGym baseline (24.3%) by 51.0% (per-site: Shopping 32.8, CMS 41.2, Forum 41.2, Gitlab 37.2, Map 30.4). On VisualWebArena, CER_online reaches 31.9% average SR (Classifieds 27.0, Shopping 38.1, Forum 24.4), outperforming the Tree Search method (26.4%) by ~20.8% relative with dozens-of-times fewer token costs. CER offline/online/hybrid on WebArena = 33.4 / 33.2 / 36.7 average SR.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Token efficiency (Table 3): vs ReAct baseline (24.3 SR), CER adds only +5.8% / +11.2% / +17.3% input tokens for offline/online/hybrid while raising SR by +37.8% / +36.7% / +52.5% relative - large gains for minor token overhead. (2) Cross-template SR / stability & plasticity (Table 4, Forum): CER ct-SR 60.0 vs baseline 44.7, stability 93%, plasticity 141% (41% new task types solved), showing improvement comes from generalizable fine-grained experiences, not memorizing whole trajectories. (3) Open-source model (Table 5, Gitlab, Llama-3.1-70B): CER_hybrid 22.0 vs ReAct 17.3 (~+26.5% relative; smaller gain than GPT-4o, attributed to weaker formatting/skill distillation). (4) Synergy (Table 6, Forum): CER 37.7, Sampling 43.1, CER w/ sampling 52.6 (+39.5% over CER w/ ReAct) - composes with performant methods. (5) Robustness / success-only (Table 7, full WebArena): CER 31.4 vs CER_success 33.5 - distilling from failed trajectories is not a bottleneck; robust to noisy trajectories. (6) Division of dynamics vs skills (Table 8, Forum): CER 37.7 vs CER-skills 33.3 vs CER-dynamics 35.1 - both components matter and synergize. (7) Offline data source (Table 9, Forum): human annotations vs self-guided exploration; human-annotated offline (33.3) and hybrid (41.2) beat exploration-based (offline 31.6, hybrid 35.1), and hybrid w/ human annotations (41.2) surpasses online-only (37.7); noisy unstructured exploration trajectories can mislead, showing goal-oriented trajectories matter.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No. Only end-to-end task SR (and derived ct-SR/stability/plasticity/token metrics) are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) are reported separately, since retrieval here is LLM-judged experience selection for in-context replay rather than a ranked-retrieval benchmark.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome (success rate / reward). Some process-oriented analyses are reported: cross-template SR (generalization), stability vs plasticity (knowledge retention vs acquisition), token-cost analysis, and qualitative case study (e.g. WebArena task 31 showing how distilled dynamics+skills enable correct navigation/sorting). No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality metric.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> A central selling point: CER adds only modest input-token overhead (Delta tokens +5.8% offline / +11.2% online / +17.3% hybrid) for large relative SR gains (+37.8% / +36.7% / +52.5%) (Table 3). On VisualWebArena it beats Tree Search (which samples 20x at each step over up to 5 steps with GPT-4o as a value function) using a max of only 30 steps per task and 'at least 3 times fewer tokens' (text says 'dozens of times fewer token costs' relative to the search budget). No explicit dollar/latency figures.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed/budget-capped top-k: in the WebArena & VisualWebArena implementation, k_d=5 (max dynamics) and k_s=5 (max skills) are retrieved/replayed; retrieval prompts explicitly cap selection ('select not more than max skills/pages'). Experiences are kept abstract/compact and the added tokens are small (single-digit to ~17% of input). Selection count is fixed-k (not adaptive/precision-driven beyond the cap), retrieved-then-injected.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (uses existing benchmarks: WebArena 812 tasks / 5 sites; VisualWebArena 910 tasks / 3 sites). Offline training trajectories were newly collected: ~5-10 human-annotated gold tasks per WebArena website (~5% of test set, filtered to avoid test overlap), or alternatively 10 LLM self-guided exploration trajectories (max 30 steps each).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> ReAct (Yao et al. 2023b, base think-act-observe policy and output format) and BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024, web environment/observation); experience replay for RL/continual learning (Lin; Schaul et al. 2016 Prioritized Experience Replay; Rolnick et al. 2019); memory/experience LLM agents (Generative Agents - Park et al. 2023; Voyager - Wang et al. 2024a; ExpeL - Zhao et al. 2023; Synapse - Zheng et al. 2023); Set-of-Marks visual grounding (Yang et al. 2023); Recognition-Primed Decision model (Klein 1998); benchmarks WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024b) and VisualWebArena (Koh et al. 2024a).
- **contrasts with**:
> Methods requiring ground-truth reward to function before learning - AutoGuide (Fu et al. 2024), AutoManual (Chen et al. 2024), Agent Workflow Memory/AWM (Wang et al. 2024b) - CER works without ground-truth rewards and from both success and failure; AWM specifically lacks a retrieval module and rewrites the whole workflow memory, whereas CER retrieves and continually merges. Methods that store raw long observation-action pairs as exemplars (ExpeL, Synapse) - CER instead distills fine-grained, abstract dynamics/skills better suited to complex environments. Compute-heavy search methods (Tree Search, Koh et al. 2024b) - CER is much cheaper in tokens. SteP (Sodhi et al. 2024) - relies on human-designed per-website policies (not autonomous). Parameter-update/training-based agent learning - CER is training-free.
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based / experience planning): a training-free, in-context experience-replay LLM web agent in the lineage of experience/insight-memory agents (ReAct -> Reflexion/ExpeL -> Agent Workflow Memory -> CER). It advances test-time continual self-improvement by distilling environment dynamics + decision-making skills from both successful and failed trajectories into a dynamic in-context buffer (write-back + LLM-as-retriever replay), without ground-truth reward and without parameter updates, validated on realistic web-navigation benchmarks.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

<a id="item-evolver"></a>
### 77. EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle

2025  ·  arXiv 2510.16079  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16079)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: Accepted by ICML 2026 (per arXiv comment and official repo, paper accepted at ICML 2026, ~2026-05-01). Preprint arXiv:2510.16079 (cs.CL / cs.AI), submitted 17 Oct 2025 (v1), last revised 16 May 2026 (v3).
- **authors affiliation**:
> Rong Wu (Zhejiang University; Shanghai AI Laboratory), Xiaoman Wang (East China Normal University) - these two contributed equally; Jianbiao Mei (Zhejiang University; Shanghai AI Laboratory), Pinlong Cai (Shanghai AI Laboratory), Daocheng Fu (Shanghai AI Laboratory; Fudan University), Cheng Yang (Shanghai AI Laboratory; Central South University), Licheng Wen (Shanghai AI Laboratory; Shanghai Innovation Institute; Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Xuemeng Yang (Shanghai AI Laboratory), Yufan Shen (Shanghai AI Laboratory), Yuxin Wang (University of Science and Technology of China), Botian Shi (Shanghai AI Laboratory, corresponding author). Primary affiliation: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (with Zhejiang University). Code/contact: KnowledgeXLab (wurong1159@zju.edu.cn).
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.16079
- **code url**:
> https://github.com/KnowledgeXLab/EvolveR (official; redirected from the paper's stated https://github.com/Edaizi/EvolveR). MIT License, Python, built on verl. Model weights: https://huggingface.co/Edaizi/EvolveR (EvolveR-3B); data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Edaizi/EvolveR-NQ-HotpotQA.

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: QA / agentic decision-making: knowledge-intensive open-domain and multi-hop question answering with tool use (search engine), framed as an LLM-agent self-evolution problem. Primary focus is multi-hop QA; method is positioned as a general experience-driven lifecycle paradigm.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, single-agent, closed-loop self-evolving agent with parameter updates. The agent operates in a Think-Act-Observe loop over an action space of {<search_experience>, <search_knowledge>, <answer>}. The lifecycle alternates two phases that share the same trajectories: (1) Offline Self-Distillation, where the policy parameters are FROZEN and the agent's own model distills its past success/failure trajectories into abstract reusable strategic 'principles' that are curated into an Experience Base E (with semantic dedup, merge/integration, dynamic utility scoring, and pruning); (2) Online Interaction, where the agent solves tasks, actively retrieves distilled principles to guide reasoning, and accumulates new behavioral trajectories. The loop is closed by a Policy Evolution mechanism that uses GRPO reinforcement learning on the online trajectories (composite outcome + format reward) to update the policy. Supervision: ground-truth answers provide a sparse binary outcome (Exact Match) reward; a dense format/shaping reward encourages balanced reasoning and search. A cold-start SFT stage (~700 NQ+HotpotQA samples, LoRA, trajectories from GPT-4o) teaches the interaction format before RL. In-domain training data (NQ, HotpotQA train splits) builds the experience base; out-of-domain datasets are used only for evaluating generalization. Trained on 8x A100 (80GB) GPUs; full 3B lifecycle ~39.4 hours.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Two distinct retrieval targets during online interaction: (1) distilled strategic PRINCIPLES (guiding principles from successes, cautionary principles from failures) from the agent's own internal Experience Base E (these are the self-learned experiences central to the method); and (2) factual DOCUMENTS from an external knowledge base / search engine (Wikipedia corpus) via <search_knowledge>. The experience principles (abstracted guidelines/rules paired with structured knowledge triples) are the novel retrieval unit; documents are standard RAG-style factual retrieval.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID. The agent retrieves from (a) a GROWING/episodic internal Experience Base E that the agent writes itself (self-distilled principles, grown during training across the closed loop), and (b) a STATIC external knowledge corpus (Wikipedia, via a search engine / dense retriever) for factual grounding. The defining novelty (experience principles) targets a self-written, evolving memory; the knowledge search targets a fixed external corpus.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking objective for both retrieval streams: <search_experience> returns top-k_e = 3 principles from E; <search_knowledge> returns top-k_d = 3 documents. No completeness / minimal-set objective and no precision-driven variable-size recommendation; selection is fixed top-3 nearest-neighbor by embedding similarity. (The agent may issue multiple search calls per episode, but each call is fixed-top-3.)
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes (embedding top-3 retrieval of principles from E via <search_experience>), Reuse: yes (principles applied as heuristic guidance in the agent's reasoning, plus RL reinforces effective reuse), Revise: partial/yes (principles are merged/integrated and their utility scores updated, and the self-distillation ability improves over time; but a retrieved principle is used as-is as guidance rather than per-instance adapted), Retain: yes (distill new principles, dedup/merge, score, prune into E)]. All four CBR phases are present in spirit, with Reuse mediated by an RL-trained policy.
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper frames itself as an 'experience-driven self-evolution lifecycle' / self-evolving agents / experiential learning and continual learning; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'. It realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms (with abstraction into principles) under a self-evolution + RL framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> guideline-rule / principle (problem-solving strategic principle): each retrieved experience unit is a distilled abstract principle = a one-sentence natural-language description plus several structured (subject, predicate, object) knowledge triples, tagged as guiding (from success) or cautionary (from failure), and carrying a metric score and usage/success counts. The complementary knowledge-search unit is a document (Wikipedia passage). So the primary novel unit is a distilled strategic guideline-rule; the secondary unit is a document.
- **index source**:
> Hybrid. The Experience Base E is a GROWING memory induced online/across the closed training loop from the agent's own trajectories (offline self-distillation phases interleaved with online interaction); principles are added/merged/pruned over time (grows to ~50k principles during training). The external knowledge index is a STATIC pre-built corpus (Wikipedia-18 corpus with e5 embeddings, served via a local FAISS/Pyserini retrieval server, following Search-R1).
- **index structure topology**:
> Experience Base: flat vector index of principle embeddings (BGE-M3 embeddings) for cosine-similarity nearest-neighbor search, implemented with Milvus (paper) / a vector DB; each principle additionally carries metadata (metric score, usage/success counts) and structured knowledge triples, and is linked to its source trajectories via the Merge operation (a loose, per-principle trajectory-linking structure rather than a global graph). External knowledge base: flat dense vector index (e5 embeddings over Wikipedia, FAISS Flat index). Overall: flat vector indices with metadata/score keying; not a hierarchical or global knowledge graph (though principles embed local triples).
- **retriever type**:
> Dense (embedding-based) nearest-neighbor retriever for both streams. Experience retrieval uses BGE-M3 embeddings with cosine similarity (Milvus); knowledge retrieval uses dense e5 embeddings over Wikipedia (FAISS), following Search-R1. Off-the-shelf embedders (not a learned retriever); however, the agent's policy that DECIDES when/what to query is RL-trained (GRPO), so query issuance is a learned policy while the similarity matching itself is fixed dense ANN.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> The embedding-based matching is off-the-shelf (no contrastive fine-tuning of BGE-M3 or e5). However, the decision of WHEN and WHAT to retrieve is learned: the agent's policy is trained via GRPO reinforcement learning with a composite reward (sparse outcome EM reward + dense format reward that explicitly rewards using <search_experience> and <search_knowledge> diversity and balanced reasoning steps). Thus the retrieval-action policy is RL/task-effectiveness-optimized, while the underlying similarity retriever is fixed similarity. Additionally, principle selection over time is shaped by a utility-based dynamic metric score s(p) = (c_succ+1)/(c_use+2) that prunes low-utility principles (utility/effectiveness signal on the store, not on the embedder).
- **query construction**:
> Agent-generated, thought-conditioned queries. Inside its <think> reasoning, the agent issues a <search_experience> query (often expressed as candidate principle triples / intent it is looking for) to fetch relevant principles, and/or a <search_knowledge> query (a natural-language search query) for facts. Queries are free-form natural-language strings produced by the policy mid-reasoning, conditioned on the current state/question; not raw-input-only and not fixed templates.
- **query granularity**:
> step/state-level (within-episode, two-stream): the agent can issue retrieval queries at any point in its multi-turn Think-Act-Observe loop, conditioned on its current reasoning state, and can search multiple times per episode (converging to ~2 experience searches and ~4 knowledge searches per trajectory). Not a single one-shot task-level retrieval; retrieval is interleaved per reasoning step / per tool-call.
- **when to retrieve**:
> Iterative / agent-initiated (adaptive within the loop): retrieval is triggered by the agent's own decision to emit a <search_experience> or <search_knowledge> action during reasoning, and can occur multiple times per episode. The learned policy (RL-shaped) governs the timing; there is no fixed schedule, no token-confidence trigger.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> agent-initiated request: the agent autonomously decides to issue <search_experience> / <search_knowledge> actions from within its <think> reasoning. The format reward shapes this behavior (rewarding diverse and sufficient search use), so the trigger is a learned, policy-driven action rather than an external confidence/uncertainty/attention signal or a learned complexity classifier.
- **reranking**:
> None. Both experience and knowledge retrieval return the top-3 by embedding similarity directly with no separate cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking stage. (Principle ordering/prioritization is influenced over time by the dynamic metric score, but there is no per-query reranking module described.)
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Minimal at retrieval time for the online phase: retrieved principles (with their scores and triples) and retrieved documents are injected into context as observations (<experience>...</experience> and <information>...</information>) and consumed by the agent's reasoning; they are loss-masked during the policy update. The heavy refinement happens at WRITE time on the experience store (distillation into abstract principles, semantic deduplication, merge/integration, utility scoring, and pruning), not as post-retrieval document distillation/compression at query time. So online: none/light; offline curation: distill + dedup + filter.
- **tool document engineering**:
> N/A for tool retrieval. The experience-principle 'documents' are engineered, though: trajectories are distilled by the agent's own policy into a structured principle = NL description + (subject,predicate,object) triples, with semantic deduplication, merge/integration, and a dynamic utility metric_score, before being embedded (BGE-M3) and indexed. This is principle/experience engineering rather than tool-docstring engineering.
- **index content separation**:
> Partial. Each principle stores a compact description + triples + score as the retrievable/indexed unit, with the merge step LINKING source trajectories to a principle (heavier raw trajectory content is associated but the lightweight principle is what is retrieved and injected). This is a light-index-then-(optionally)-associated-content pattern, though the paper does not emphasize progressive disclosure.
- **dynamic index and protocol**:
> N/A as a tool store. The external knowledge tool is a fixed local Wikipedia search engine (FAISS/Pyserini retrieval server, following Search-R1), not an MCP/RapidAPI/RESTful live tool index. The internal Experience Base is a dynamically updated vector DB (Milvus) of self-distilled principles with CRUD-like add/merge/prune operations, but it stores experiences, not external tool APIs.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation + training signal. (1) Prompt augmentation: retrieved principles provide heuristic strategic guidance that shapes the agent's <think> monologue and steers subsequent <search_knowledge> actions; retrieved documents provide factual grounding. (2) Training signal: because online trajectories are conditioned on retrieved principles, the GRPO update learns a policy of how to effectively utilize the agent's own distilled wisdom (reinforcing the link between retrieving high-quality principles and producing high-reward outcomes). Retrieved-token loss is masked (not directly absorbed into parameters); an exp-absorb ablation that unmasked principle tokens slightly hurt performance.
- **planning integration**:
> Per-step interleaved within an agentic reasoning/acting loop (retrieve-while-think). The agent runs a multi-turn Think-Act-Observe loop and weaves principle retrieval and knowledge retrieval into its reasoning at chosen steps, then answers. Plans are not produced one-shot; principles act as retrieve-then-reason heuristic guidance that influences the agent's next actions inside the loop. No explicit MCTS/tree search; integration is inside an interleaved search-and-reason loop optimized by RL.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**:
> per-CoT-step / per-tool-call within a rollout: retrieval (experience and knowledge) is interleaved at the granularity of individual reasoning steps and tool-calls within a single episode (multiple <think>, <search_experience>, <search_knowledge> actions per trajectory before the final <answer>).
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Primarily LLM-prompted/policy-guided reuse rather than per-case solution rewriting: a retrieved principle is applied verbatim as heuristic guidance that conditions the agent's reasoning and subsequent actions, and the RL-trained policy learns to apply principles effectively (RL-reuse-finetuning). Adaptation/revision happens at the store level (offline self-distillation revises and merges principles, utility scoring prunes weak ones) rather than rewriting a retrieved case at solve time.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled strategy/guideline (free-text rule) paired with structured knowledge triples: each principle is injected as a natural-language description plus (subject, predicate, object) triplets, tagged guiding/cautionary, and annotated with its metric score (e.g. 'type: guiding, metric score: 0.67, description: ...'). Knowledge results are injected as raw document passages. The novel surface form is the distilled strategic principle (structured note + triples), not a raw trajectory or executable program.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled strategy/insight, specifically state-aware strategic guidelines/rules (e.g. 'For comparison questions, gather data on both items before concluding'; 'When determining character relationships in a series, avoid assuming actors based solely on character recognition; confirm with verified role descriptions'). Explicitly NOT raw trajectories - the paper contrasts itself with 'learning by raw trajectories' and emphasizes abstraction into reusable principles. The complementary knowledge units are raw documents (low abstraction).
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Multiple: (1) utility-based DYNAMIC SCORING and PRUNING - each principle's metric score s(p)=(c_succ+1)/(c_use+2) tracks historical effectiveness; principles below threshold theta_prune=0.3 are periodically pruned (manual annotation shows this cuts incorrect/misleading principles from 24% to 8% and raises 'ideal' principles from 26% to 82%). (2) Semantic DEDUPLICATION + a two-stage matching/merge (embedding pre-filter at theta_sim=0.85 then LLM binary equivalence judgment) keeps E compact and avoids redundant/noisy entries. (3) RL-conditioned policy learns to selectively use helpful principles. (4) Retrieved tokens are loss-masked (an exp-absorb variant that unmasks them degraded performance, attributed to noisy/irrelevant top-k principles). Scalability test to ~50k principles shows stable, non-collapsing performance, evidencing robustness to long-term noise.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Procedural / strategic experience memory: an Experience Base E of distilled abstract problem-solving principles (guiding + cautionary) with structured triples and utility scores. It is derived from episodic trajectories but stored as abstracted procedural/strategic knowledge rather than raw episodes. Plus an external static factual knowledge store (not a learned/grown memory).
- **write back**:
> Yes. The offline self-distillation phase writes newly distilled principles into E (add as new entry if novel, else Merge the new trajectory under the most similar existing principle). It also updates per-principle usage/success counts and metric scores, and prunes low-utility principles. So the system actively stores, merges, scores, and removes experiences.
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success-and-failure, reflective (during the offline self-distillation phase). After collecting trajectories online, the agent reviews each trajectory by outcome: successful trajectories yield a guiding principle, failed trajectories yield a cautionary principle (Exact-Match correctness determines outcome). New principles trigger dedup/merge writes; usage/success counts update when principles are used; low-score principles trigger pruning sweeps. Writes occur in the offline reflection phase, not per-step during the answer-producing rollout.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success + failure, used contrastively/correctively. Successful trajectories distill into GUIDING principles; FAILED trajectories distill into CAUTIONARY principles (explicit 'what to avoid' rules with failure-pattern triples). Both kinds are stored in E and retrievable. Additionally, the RL/GRPO update itself leverages both positive and negative rollouts (learn what to do from successes, what to avoid from failures), which the paper argues is why GRPO beats SFT-on-successes-only (0.382 vs 0.357 on 3B).
- **memory evolution update**:
> Link-and-evolve with dedup-merge and forget-prune: new principles are deduplicated (semantic pre-filter + LLM equivalence) and either added or Merged under an existing principle (linking the new source trajectory and strengthening it with new evidence); each principle's metric score and usage/success counts are continuously updated; principles whose score falls below theta_prune=0.3 are periodically pruned (forget). Longitudinal analysis shows later-created principles have higher average metric scores (0.462 -> 0.500), indicating the store and the distillation ability co-evolve. Not append-only.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Partially. The similarity matching (BGE-M3 / e5 cosine top-k) is a fixed non-learned retriever, but the DECISION to retrieve and WHAT to query (issuing <search_experience>/<search_knowledge> with policy-generated queries) is an RL-LEARNED policy (GRPO with a reward that explicitly incentivizes effective experience/knowledge search), and principle prioritization in the store is governed by a learned utility score. So case-selection/use is partly a learned policy layered on fixed similarity retrieval, not pure fixed top-k.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> No. Single-agent private memory: one EvolveR agent distills, curates, retrieves, and learns from its own Experience Base. No sharing across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks (the paper notes inspiration from multi-agent memory frameworks like G-Memory but does not implement cross-agent experience sharing).

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> Seven QA benchmarks. In-domain (train splits used to build the experience base): Natural Questions (NQ) and HotpotQA (multi-hop). Out-of-domain (generalization only): TriviaQA, PopQA (general QA), and 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle (multi-hop). External retrieval over a Wikipedia-18 corpus. Models: Qwen2.5 family (0.5B, 1.5B, 3B, 7B).
- **benchmark family**: QA / multi-hop QA (open-domain single-hop: NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA; multi-hop: HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle). No web/embodied/tool/code/memory/decision-RL benchmark families.
- **baselines**:
> Three paradigms, all on Qwen2.5 base models: (1) Prompting-based (no parameter updates): Direct Inference, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), RAG, IRCoT, Search-o1. (2) SFT-based: standard SFT, Rejection Sampling. (3) RL-based (direct competitors): Search-R1 (base and instruct variants; with search engine), DeepSeek-R1-style R1-base / R1-instruct (reasoning without search). The closest competitor is Search-R1.
- **key metrics**:
> Primary: Exact Match (EM) after standard normalization (main results). Secondary: F1 Score (reported in the model-scale generalizability analysis). Auxiliary diagnostics: average action counts per trajectory (<think>, <search_knowledge>, <search_experience>), top-3 retrieval search latency (seconds), experience-base size (number of principles), and principle quality annotation percentages.
- **headline result**:
> On the QA benchmark suite, EvolveR achieves the best average EM, outperforming all baselines including the strong RL agent Search-R1: average EM 0.382 on Qwen2.5-3B (vs 0.325 for Search-R1-instruct) and 0.417 on Qwen2.5-7B (vs 0.385 for Search-R1-instruct). It secures best scores on in-domain NQ (0.434/0.462 at 3B/7B), out-of-domain PopQA, and the adversarial Bamboogle, while staying competitive elsewhere.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Self- vs teacher-distillation (Table 2): scale-dependent reversal - GPT-4o-mini teacher distillation helps small models (0.5B: 0.220 teacher vs 0.150 self), but at 3B self-distill (0.382) BEATS teacher-distill (0.370), validating 'cognitive alignment'. (2) Experience retrieval at inference (Table 3): disabling exp-retrieve (same trained model) drops 3B avg from 0.382 -> 0.340 (and far more on smaller models, e.g. 0.150 -> 0.078 at 0.5B), showing retrieval is indispensable. (3) Component attribution (Table 4, 3B): none 0.134; RL-only 0.325; distill+retrieve no-RL 0.357; distill+RL no-retrieve 0.340; full (distill+retrieve+RL) 0.382 - retrieval and RL are complementary. (4) Memory configuration (Table 5): no-base 0.325 < teacher-distilled 0.370 < self-distilled 0.382. (5) RL vs SFT on the same successful trajectories (Table 8): GRPO 0.382 > SFT 0.357 (~7% relative), because RL uses both successes and failures. (6) Pruning-threshold sensitivity (Table 9): robust across theta_prune in {0.1,0.3,0.7,0.9} (avg ~0.265-0.276 at 1.5B). (7) Experience internalization (Table 11): unmasking principle tokens (exp-absorb) slightly hurts (0.382 -> 0.371). (8) Principle-quality annotation (Table 6) and scalability to ~50k principles (Table 7) confirm scoring/pruning efficacy and stability.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Partial. The end-to-end task metric (EM, plus F1) is the primary report. Intrinsic retrieval-ranking metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are NOT reported. However, intrinsic experience-store quality IS reported separately via manual principle-quality annotation (Ideal/Vague/Incorrect % by score tier) and principle-quality-by-creation-phase metric scores, plus retrieval latency vs accuracy as the base scales - so experience-curation quality is decoupled, but classic retrieval IR metrics are not.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mostly outcome (EM/F1), but with notable process-level analysis: longitudinal tracking of action frequencies (<think>/<search_knowledge>/<search_experience> per trajectory across training, converging to ~6 reasoning / ~4 knowledge / ~2 experience), principle-quality annotation (process artifact quality), principle metric-score evolution over training intervals, and a qualitative rollout case study. No formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness score.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reported. Training cost: full Qwen2.5-3B lifecycle (cold-start SFT + GRPO RL) ~39.4 hours on 8x A100 (80GB). Experience-retrieval latency (Milvus): ~0.06s for top-3 over ~14k principles, scaling to only ~0.20s at ~50k principles - negligible vs LLM generation. RL rollout: G=8 trajectories per prompt, batch 128 prompts; vLLM-accelerated. Accuracy stays stable/peaks (avg EM up to 0.410 at 45k) as the base grows, showing favorable scalability/cost vs accuracy. Knowledge retrieval is top-3 docs per call; the agent converges to ~4 knowledge + ~2 experience searches per trajectory.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed-k, budget-capped. Per <search_knowledge> action: top-k_d=3 documents; per <search_experience> action: top-k_e=3 principles. Max input sequence length 8192 tokens, max response 1024 tokens. The agent may issue multiple searches per episode (no fixed total cap; format reward gives a diversity score and a quantity bonus up to 6 searches). Cold-start uses ~700 SFT samples. Selection is fixed top-3 retrieved-then-used (not adaptive/precision-driven k).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (uses existing QA benchmarks: NQ, HotpotQA, TriviaQA, PopQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue, Bamboogle; external Wikipedia-18 corpus; follows Search-R1 / O2-Searcher data setup). Does not construct a new benchmark.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Search-R1 (Jin et al. 2025; RL-trained search agent, interaction format, retrieval setup, ~700-sample cold-start, top-3 doc retrieval) and O2-Searcher (Mei et al. 2025; same group, search-based agent) as the agentic-RL backbone; GRPO from DeepSeekMath (Shao et al. 2024) and DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025; cold-start + RL recipe) for policy optimization; ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) Think-Act-Observe loop and Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) for the experiential/self-reflection lineage; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) and Memento (Zhou et al. 2025) as prior experience/reflection-memory agents; structured-memory frameworks Mem0 (Chhikara et al. 2025) and G-Memory (Zhang et al. 2025) for the description+triples principle representation; BGE-M3 embeddings; verl RL framework; LLaMA-Factory + LoRA; vLLM; Milvus.
- **contrasts with**:
> Four LLM-agent learning paradigms the paper explicitly positions against (Figure 1): (1) Stateless Execution (standard agents that discard experience, e.g. ReAct, CoT - 'operational amnesia'); (2) Learning by Raw Trajectories (retrieving un-distilled past trajectories - mimics solutions, fails to abstract); (3) Learning via External Scribing (relying on a powerful EXTERNAL teacher LLM to distill insights, e.g. ExpeL / Memento - treats reflections as transient hints, leaves intrinsic policy unchanged); EvolveR contrasts by self-distilling its own experiences into abstract principles AND evolving its policy via RL (closed loop). Also contrasts with standard RAG/Search-R1 (fixes external-knowledge gaps but does not learn from the agent's own interaction strategy) and with SFT-on-successes (cannot leverage failures).
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based / experience-driven planning agents): a 2025/2026 self-evolving agent that fuses experience-memory distillation (ExpeL/Reflexion lineage) with agentic search-RL (Search-R1/O2-Searcher/GRPO). It advances the experience-planner line from raw-trajectory recall (ExpeL) and external-teacher reflection (ExpeL/Memento) toward a fully self-contained closed loop that (a) self-distills its own trajectories into abstract, scored, curated strategic principles and (b) co-evolves the policy via RL on the same experience-guided trajectories - distinguishing it from both static RAG planners and memory-only experiential agents.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- online_growth

<a id="item-mael"></a>
### 78. MAEL (Multi-Agent cross-task Experiential Learning)

2025  ·  arXiv 2505.23187  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23187)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2505.23187, cs.CL; marked 'Work in Progress'); not yet peer-reviewed
- **authors affiliation**:
> Yilong Li (Peking University), Chen Qian (Shanghai Jiao Tong University), Yu Xia, Ruijie Shi, Yufan Dang, Zihao Xie, Weize Chen, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun (Tsinghua University), Ziming You (Peking University), Cheng Yang (Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications), Weichuan Liu (Siemens), Ye Tian, Xuantang Xiong, Lei Han (Tencent Robotics X). Equal contribution: Yilong Li, Chen Qian. Corresponding authors: Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23187

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Multi-agent LLM collaboration spanning QA/multi-domain reasoning (MMLU), arithmetic reasoning (GSM-8K), code synthesis (HumanEval), long-form/commonsense generation (CommonGen-Hard), and project-level software development / code generation (SRDD). General task-solving with decomposition + critique rather than a single domain.
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, multi-agent (graph of N LLM agents on an undirected collaboration network). Two-phase: an offline-style 'experiential learning phase' over a training corpus (30 training tasks per dataset) where reward annotations are computed per decision step, followed by an inference phase on held-out tasks. Supervision is available during the learning phase via task-specific reward/metric functions (e.g., accuracy, pass@k, composite quality scores). Each agent maintains its own distributed experience pool. The setting is cross-task transfer: learning from previously solved tasks to improve future structurally-similar tasks.
- **what is retrieved**: Per-agent past 'experiences' = step-level input-output pairs annotated with a quality reward, of the form (state s_t, action a_t, reward r_t), used as few-shot examples. At task-wise granularity, a complete high-quality solution trace is retrieved.
- **retrieval grounding**: GROWING / episodic memory the agents write. Each agent's experience pool is built (induced) during the experiential learning phase from the system's own collaboration traces; it is not a static external corpus/KB.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k ranking (effectively top-1): the single top-ranked experience entry by the combined similarity-and-reward retrieval score is appended to the agent input. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable size.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> Retrieve: yes (reward-weighted similarity retrieval of past experiences). Reuse: yes (injected as few-shot exemplars guiding decomposition/communication). Revise: partial (the workflow has a critique/refinement loop that revises current solutions, but retrieved cases are not explicitly adapted/revised before reuse — they are used verbatim). Retain: yes (write-back of new (s,a,r) experiences during the learning phase). 4-flag: [Retrieve=Yes, Reuse=Yes, Revise=Partial, Retain=Yes].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The work does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames experiences via a neural-network/backpropagation analogy (agents as neurons, experience pools as learnable weights, forward/backward passes) and the term 'experiential learning'. It realizes CBR-like retrieve-reuse-retain mechanics under a different framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> (state, action, reward) tuple = a single agent input-output pair annotated with a quality reward (step-level experience). Under task-wise retrieval the unit is a full high-quality solution trace for the task; under step-wise retrieval the unit is the per-decision-step experience tuple.
- **index source**:
> Growing memory induced online during a dedicated experiential learning (training) phase from the multi-agent system's own forward-pass collaboration traces over a 30-task training set per dataset; experiences are accumulated incrementally over the training dataset. Frozen at inference (no write-back at test time noted).
- **index structure topology**:
> Distributed per-agent flat experience pools: each agent (node v_i) owns its own pool p_i organized as a flat collection of (s,a,r) entries searched by embedding similarity. The agents themselves are organized on an undirected graph collaboration network, but the retrievable store within each agent is a flat vector-keyed index.
- **retriever type**: Dense embedding retriever (cosine similarity over text-embedding-ada-002 embeddings) combined with a reward weighting; off-the-shelf embedder, not learned.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None for the embedder itself (off-the-shelf text-embedding-ada-002). The ranking signal is a hand-designed weighted combination of cosine similarity and the stored task-effectiveness reward (downstream step quality), retrieval_score = alpha*similarity + (1-alpha)*reward with alpha=0.5 by default. The reward component is derived from task-specific downstream quality metrics, so selection is biased by downstream-task-effectiveness but the retriever is not trained.
- **query construction**: Raw agent input at the current decision step (the subtask description / state s_t) is embedded and used as the query. For task-wise retrieval the original task description is used as the query for the whole task; for step-wise retrieval each step's input is the query.
- **query granularity**: Both supported as variants: task-level one-shot query (MAEL_Task, query = original task description, applied throughout the task) and step/state-level query (MAEL_Step, a fresh query at each decision step).
- **when to retrieve**: Variant-dependent: one-shot at task start (MAEL_Task) or iterative per-decision-step (MAEL_Step). Retrieval happens on a fixed schedule at each agent decision step, not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router gated.
- **retrieval trigger signal**: Fixed schedule: retrieval is performed deterministically at each critical decision step (task solve, solvability judge, task decompose, solution critique, solution aggregate) for MAEL_Step, or once at task start for MAEL_Task. No confidence/uncertainty/learned-classifier trigger.
- **reranking**: No separate neural reranking stage; ranking is a single weighted-scoring step combining cosine similarity and stored reward (a similarity+reward weighted score), then top-1 selection.
- **retrieved context refinement**: None beyond the similarity+reward scoring and top-1 selection; the retrieved experience entry is appended verbatim to the agent input. No decomposition/distillation/compression/distractor-filtering of retrieved context is described.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; experiences are agent interaction traces, not tool documents).
- **index content separation**: N/A (no lightweight-index-vs-heavy-content separation; experiences are stored and retrieved as whole (s,a,r) entries / traces).
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no tool index or tool-integration protocol; not a tool-retrieval method).
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling).

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation: the top-ranked experience (s_j, a_j, r_j) is appended to the agent input s_t as a few-shot example, and the augmented input is fed to the agent to generate the response. It guides subtask decomposition strategy and inter-agent communication/solving/refinement/aggregation.
- **planning integration**:
> Per-step interleaved within a divide-and-conquer + solver-critique collaboration workflow. Retrieval is woven into each stage of the recursive task-solving workflow (Decompose -> Solve -> Critique -> Aggregate); experiences guide both task decomposition and inter-agent communication. This is a retrieve-at-each-step (MAEL_Step) or retrieve-once-then-plan (MAEL_Task) integration, not inside an explicit MCTS/tree search.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-decision-step / per-agent-action within a collaboration rollout (for MAEL_Step), i.e., retrieval at each of the workflow's critical decision steps (decompose, solve, critique, aggregate). For MAEL_Task it is per-task (one retrieval reused across the whole rollout).
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Verbatim ICL exemplar: the top-ranked retrieved experience is appended unchanged to the agent input as a few-shot example (no explicit LLM-prompted adaptation, execution-feedback revision, or RL reuse-finetuning of the retrieved case itself). Solution revision happens via the separate solver-critique refinement loop, not by adapting the retrieved case.
- **retrieved item representation**: Raw stored input-output trajectory pair (state-action text) annotated with a numeric reward, injected as a free-text few-shot exemplar; under task-wise retrieval it is the raw historical solution trace. Not distilled into abstract rules or executable skills.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Raw trajectory / raw demonstration (a concrete past input-output pair or full solution trace), not a distilled strategy, abstract guideline, or procedural skill.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Reward-weighted similarity scoring biases retrieval toward high-quality (high-reward) and relevant experiences, providing implicit robustness. The paper empirically reports robustness: even Low-Reward & Low-Similarity retrieval still beats no-experience (e.g., +6.7% on HumanEval), but there is no explicit relevance-evaluator, self-reflection filter, or retriever-aware training to guard against noise.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Episodic (per-agent distributed experience pools of (state, action, reward) interaction traces); analogized to learnable weights of a neural-network-like agent graph.
- **write back**:
> True (during the experiential learning phase). Agents store new (s_t, a_t, r_t) experiences into their individual experience pools via a backpropagation-style backward pass: P <- P union {(s_t,a_t,r_t)}. However, write-back occurs only in the dedicated training/learning phase, not during test-time inference.
- **write back trigger**:
> On every traversed critical decision step during the learning-phase forward/backward pass (per-step), regardless of success or failure. Each step's (input, output, reward) is stored after the forward pass computes its reward; storage is reward-annotated but not gated on success only. Effectively per-step write during training.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Experiences are stored with their rewards including low-reward (lower-quality) ones, not success-only; the reward annotation lets retrieval prefer high-reward experiences. The paper analyzes 'Low Reward' vs 'High Reward' retrieval, showing low-reward experiences still help, but there is no explicit failure-only corrective-rule mechanism or contrastive success/failure usage; failures are simply stored as low-reward entries and down-weighted at retrieval.
- **memory evolution update**: Append-only: experiences are accumulated (P <- P union {(s_t,a_t,r_t)}) over the training set. No dedup-merge, delta-update, refine-overwrite, or forgetting/pruning of stored entries is described.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed similarity+reward weighted top-1 scoring rule (alpha=0.5), not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. The framing uses RL-like terms (state, action, reward, forward/backward pass) but the experience pools act as non-parametric 'weights' and the retriever is not trained.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Per-agent private memory: each agent (node) maintains its own individual/distributed experience pool; experiences are NOT pooled into a shared global memory across agents. Sharing across heterogeneous frameworks is not addressed. Coordination is via the graph edges, but experience pools are agent-specific.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: MMLU; GSM-8K (GSM); HumanEval; CommonGen-Hard; SRDD (Software Requirement Description Dataset, project-level software development).
- **benchmark family**: QA/multi-domain knowledge (MMLU); arithmetic reasoning (GSM-8K); code (HumanEval function-level; SRDD project/repository-level software development); long-form/commonsense generation (CommonGen-Hard). No standard web/embodied/tool/memory-RL benchmark families used.
- **baselines**: Single-agent: GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5-sonnet. Multi-agent: AutoGen (Wu et al. 2023), EvoMac/EvoMAC (Hu et al. 2025). Internal variants: MAEL_NoExp (no experience), MAEL_Task (task-wise retrieval), MAEL_Step (step-wise retrieval).
- **key metrics**:
> Accuracy (MMLU, GSM-8K); pass@k (HumanEval); official composite metric for CommonGen-Hard (grammar, fluency, relevance, logical consistency, concept coverage); SRDD quality = product of completeness, executability, consistency. Efficiency: completion token consumption and number of convergence rounds/dialogue turns. Also code-scale metrics (cyclomatic complexity, lines, tokens, functions, files).
- **headline result**:
> MAEL outperforms single-/multi-agent baselines on most of 5 datasets; average score: MAEL_NoExp 65.67, MAEL_Task 69.69, MAEL_Step 66.52 vs GPT-4o-mini 60.78 and AutoGen 55.18. On SRDD, MAEL_Step quality 76.43 (+20.21% over AutoGen baseline, +9.2% over MAEL_NoExp) and reduces average dialogue rounds to convergence by 26%. On CommonGen-Hard, MAEL_Task cuts token usage by 49% vs MAEL_NoExp while improving quality by 12.04 points (new SOTA). (Default backbone: GPT-3.5, temperature 0.2, 4-node topology, 30 training tasks per dataset.)
- **ablations**:
> (1) Three retrieval strategies compared (No-Exp / Task-wise / Step-wise) across all datasets and on SRDD quality breakdown; MAEL_Step best on SRDD, MAEL_Task best on average. (2) Factors-affecting-retrieval ablation (Table 4): 2x2 of High/Low Similarity x High/Low Reward on HumanEval and CommonGen — both factors help individually; combining High Reward & High Similarity gives largest gain (HumanEval 73.3->90.0, +12.5% relative; CommonGen +10.1%); even Low&Low beats no-experience (+6.7% on HumanEval). (3) Experience-pool scaling (Fig 3): performance vs pool size (0/10/20/30 tasks) on HumanEval (76.7->90.0, non-monotonic dip at 20) and CommonGen (34.5->46.5). (4) Efficiency analysis (Fig 2): token consumption and convergence rounds reductions. (5) Code scale/complexity metrics (Table 3). Note experience hurts slightly on MMLU and GSM (low solution overlap / low complexity).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness of retrieval) are NOT reported separately; evaluation is end-to-end task performance plus the similarity/reward-factor ablation, but retrieval quality is measured only through downstream task scores.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Both. Outcome: task accuracy/pass@k/quality. Process: number of convergence rounds / dialogue turns to converge, token consumption per inference, per-step solution-quality progression over iterations (case study Fig 4), and intermediate SRDD sub-metrics (completeness, executability, consistency) plus code-scale/complexity statistics.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reported. Experience retrieval reduces completion-token consumption and convergence rounds across nearly all datasets: CommonGen-Hard MAEL_Task cuts token usage 49% vs MAEL_NoExp (with +12.04 quality); SRDD MAEL_Step reduces average dialogue rounds to convergence by 26% (with +9.25 quality). Values normalized relative to MAEL_NoExp for SRDD due to its much higher cost. Retrieval cost itself (embedding/lookup) not separately quantified.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed top-1 selection: the single top-ranked experience entry is appended to the agent input as a few-shot example (top-k=1). Workflow budget controlled via fixed hyperparameters: max refinement rounds 2 (simple: MMLU/HumanEval/GSM) or 3 (complex: CommonGen-Hard/SRDD), and max task-decomposition layers 1 or 2 respectively; 4-node topology; 30 training tasks per dataset. No explicit token-budget cap on injected context described.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> ChatDev / Experiential Co-Learning (Qian et al. 2024a,b) for software-developing agents and graph/linear MAS workflows; AutoGen (Wu et al. 2023) and AgentVerse/CAMEL/MetaGPT MAS frameworks; EvoMAC (Hu et al. 2025) self-evolving MAS (also a baseline); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023, also source of CommonGen-Hard) for iterative critique; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2024) 'LLM agents are experiential learners' for experience accumulation; neural-network/backpropagation analogy (forward/backward pass).
- **contrasts with**:
> Myopic MAS frameworks that solve each task from scratch without cross-task transfer (AutoGen, AgentVerse, CAMEL, MetaGPT). Self-evolving MAS that adapt topologies at test-time without a dedicated experience-accumulation training phase (EvoMAC/Hu et al. 2025; EvoFlow/Zhang et al. 2025). MAEL distinguishes itself by (a) a dedicated training phase accumulating historical cross-task experience and (b) assigning fine-grained step-level rewards to each experience for reward-weighted retrieval.
- **lineage**:
> Group D (case-based / experiential planning): experience/case-based planners that learn from prior task episodes. Sits in the lineage of experience-accumulation agents (ExpeL, Reflexion, Experiential Co-Learning / ChatDev) extended to graph-structured multi-agent collaboration with per-agent reward-weighted episodic retrieval; positioned within the self-evolving MAS line (vs EvoMAC) but emphasizing offline cross-task experiential learning rather than test-time topology evolution.
