- **how retrieved used**: prompt augmentation. Retrieved top-k relevant memory notes (with their structured attributes and linked notes) are concatenated into the LLM's context to ground the answer to the current question. No fine-tuning, no latent-token injection; everything is in-context.
- **planning integration**:
> retrieve-then-answer (one-shot at query time). This is a QA/memory pipeline rather than a multi-step planner: for each question, retrieve top-k notes once, then generate the answer conditioned on them. The 'agentic' loop (note construction -> link generation -> memory evolution) runs on the WRITE/storage side as memories are ingested, not as an interleaved plan-time search. No MCTS/tree search, no per-step interleaved retrieval during answering.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-answer (per-question). Retrieval and memory injection occur once before generating the answer to a question and remain fixed for that answer. Not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted, applied to the MEMORY rather than to a single retrieved case: (1) note construction uses an LLM (template Ps1) to generate keywords/tags/context for each new interaction; (2) link generation uses an LLM (Ps2) to decide connections among the top-k nearest notes; (3) memory evolution uses an LLM (Ps3) to rewrite the context/keywords/tags of existing neighbor notes when a new note arrives, replacing the old note. There is no execution-feedback revision of a retrieved answer and no RL reuse-finetuning; reuse at answer time is verbatim-context injection.
- **retrieved item representation**: Structured note (free text + metadata): injected items are human-readable notes carrying original content plus LLM-generated keywords, tags, and a contextual description, optionally with linked notes. Not raw trajectories, executable programs, or latent/soft tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Enriched/distilled note (single self-contained knowledge unit). It sits above a raw logged turn (because keywords/tags/contextual description abstract and re-describe the interaction) but below a generalized reusable workflow or procedural skill; it is an atomic, contextually-enriched experience note whose abstraction evolves over time via memory evolution.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> (1) Moderate top-k retrieval to balance context richness against retrieved noise (hyperparameter study shows gains plateau/decline at large k due to noise). (2) LLM-driven memory evolution that continuously refines/consolidates the contextual descriptions of existing notes, sharpening clusters (t-SNE shows more coherent clustering than base memory) and reducing dispersion. (3) Adversarial QA category in evaluation tests the ability to reject unanswerable queries. There is no retriever-aware contrastive training or explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection-filter on retrieved items.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: graph-structured episodic memory: a growing network of episodic interaction notes interconnected by LLM-generated semantic links (Zettelkasten knowledge network), stored as enriched structured text plus embeddings. Not a skill-library, procedural-policy, or latent memory.
- **write back**:
> Yes. Every new interaction is written back as a structured memory note (content + LLM-generated keywords/tags/context + embedding + links); the system additionally writes back UPDATES to existing neighbor notes during memory evolution. Closed loop: construct note -> retrieve neighbors -> generate links -> evolve neighbors -> store.
- **online growth**: Yes. The memory store grows continuously during deployment as interactions arrive (new notes added, links formed, neighbor notes evolved). Not frozen after an offline induction phase; the official library persists growth in ChromaDB.
- **write back trigger**:
> always-on per-interaction (unconditional). A note is written for every incoming interaction regardless of success/failure (no success/failure gating, since this is QA-conversation memory rather than trajectory outcome memory); the same add event also triggers link generation and evolution of related historical notes. Not on-success-only, not reflective-after-critique, not human-validated.
- **failure experience usage**:
> N/A / not distinguished. A-Mem stores conversational interactions as memory regardless of any task success/failure signal; it does not separate or contrastively use failed vs successful trajectories (no notion of negative/corrective experiences). Memory quality is improved via evolution/linking, not via failure labeling.
- **memory evolution update**:
> link-and-evolve (refine-overwrite of existing entries). This is the work's defining mechanism: when a new note is added, the LLM may update the contextual descriptions, keywords, and tags of retrieved neighbor notes, and the evolved note replaces the original in the store (Eq. 7). Combined with dynamic link generation, the network self-organizes and continuously refines its understanding. Not purely append-only; supports delta-update/refine-overwrite of historical memories plus link formation. (CRUD update/delete also supported in the library.)
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No. Note selection (for linking and for answering) is fixed cosine-similarity top-k over frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings, not an RL- or value-optimized learned retrieval policy. The agentic behavior is LLM-prompted note enrichment/linking/evolution, not a trained retrieval policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: No. Single-agent private memory: one agent constructs and evolves its own A-Mem note network over its conversation history. No sharing of memory across multiple agents or heterogeneous frameworks is claimed.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> LoCoMo (long-term conversational QA; ~9K tokens/dialogue, up to 35 sessions; 7,512 QA pairs across five categories: Multi-Hop, Temporal, Open-Domain, Single-Hop, Adversarial) as primary; DialSim (QA from long-term multi-party TV-show dialogues - Friends, The Big Bang Theory, The Office; ~1,300 sessions over five years, ~350K tokens) as secondary. Backbones: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B (six foundation models in main tables), plus DeepSeek-R1-32B, Claude-3 Haiku, Claude-3.5 Haiku in the appendix. Scaling tested up to 1,000,000 memory entries.
- **benchmark family**: memory / long-context conversational QA (LoCoMo, DialSim). Within the survey's normalization this is the memory benchmark family (LoCoMo-style long-term conversation memory), with QA / multi-hop sub-types. No web, embodied, tool, code, or decision-RL benchmarks.
- **baselines**:
> LoCoMo (full-context backbone LLM with no memory mechanism / full preceding conversation in prompt), ReadAgent (episode pagination + memory gisting + interactive look-up), MemoryBank (dynamic memory with Ebbinghaus-forgetting-curve updating and user-portrait building), and MemGPT (OS-inspired tiered virtual-context memory: main context = RAM, external context = disk). On DialSim only LoCoMo and MemGPT are compared. Mem0 (graph-DB memory) is discussed in the introduction/related work as motivation but is not a main results baseline.
- **key metrics**:
> Primary: F1 score (answer accuracy, harmonic mean of precision/recall) and BLEU-1 (unigram overlap). Efficiency: average answering token length per question; plus memory usage (MB) and retrieval time (microseconds) in the scaling study; processing time per memory op; per-op API cost. Appendix adds ROUGE-L, ROUGE-2, METEOR, and SBERT Similarity. A per-model average Ranking is also reported.
- **headline result**:
> On LoCoMo, A-Mem achieves the best average ranking across all six foundation models and roughly doubles (>=2x) baseline performance on complex Multi-Hop reasoning for GPT models, while using only ~1,200-2,500 answering tokens vs ~16,900 for full-context baselines (85-93% token reduction). Example (GPT-4o-mini): Temporal F1 45.85 vs MemGPT 25.52 / LoCoMo 18.41; overall best average ranking 1.2. On DialSim, A-Mem F1 = 3.45, a 35% improvement over LoCoMo (2.55) and 192% over MemGPT (1.18), and best across all six metrics (ROUGE-L 3.54, ROUGE-2 3.60, METEOR 2.05, SBERT 19.51).
- **ablations**:
> (1) Module ablation (GPT-4o-mini, LoCoMo, Table 3): removing both Link Generation (LG) and Memory Evolution (ME) collapses performance (Multi-Hop F1 9.65, Single-Hop 13.28, Adversarial 15.32); adding LG only (w/o ME) recovers most (Multi-Hop 21.35, Single-Hop 39.17, Adversarial 44.16); full A-Mem is best (Multi-Hop 27.02, Temporal 45.85, Single-Hop 44.65, Adversarial 50.03), showing LG is the critical foundation and ME provides essential refinement. (2) Retrieval-k hyperparameter sweep (k = 10/20/30/40/50, Figure 3): performance rises then plateaus/slightly decreases at large k, most evident on Multi-Hop and Open-Domain (context-richness vs noise tradeoff). (3) Scaling study (Table 4): linear O(N) memory usage identical to baselines; A-Mem retrieval time grows only 0.31->3.70 microseconds from 1K to 1M entries (slightly slower than MemoryBank but far faster than ReadAgent's 43.6->120,069 microseconds). (4) Memory analysis: t-SNE shows A-Mem embeddings form more coherent clusters than base memory (without LG+ME).
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No. Only end-to-end QA metrics (F1, BLEU-1, ROUGE, METEOR, SBERT) plus efficiency metrics (token length, memory usage, retrieval time) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval completeness) are separated from the downstream QA outcome; the closest decoupled signal is the retrieval-k hyperparameter sweep and the structural t-SNE memory analysis.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mostly outcome-level (answer F1/BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR/SBERT). Some structural/process-adjacent analysis is provided qualitatively: the t-SNE memory-organization visualization (clustering coherence from LG+ME) and the per-category breakdown (e.g., multi-hop reasoning), plus efficiency proxies (tokens, retrieval latency). No step-wise retrieval accuracy or reasoning-faithfulness metric.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Strongly emphasized. A-Mem uses ~1,200 tokens per memory operation (answering ~1,126-2,520 tokens depending on model) vs ~16,900 for full-context LoCoMo/MemGPT, an 85-93% token reduction via selective top-k retrieval; each memory op costs <$0.0003 on commercial APIs. Processing ~5.4 s with GPT-4o-mini, ~1.1 s with local Llama-3.2-1B on one GPU. Scaling (Table 4): O(N) memory, retrieval time 0.31->3.70 microseconds across 1K->1M entries (orders of magnitude faster than ReadAgent). So large accuracy gains come with much lower inference cost than full-context baselines, despite multiple LLM calls during memory construction.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed top-k, default k=10 for query-time retrieval (tuned per LoCoMo category, swept over 10/20/30/40/50 in analysis), with top-k nearest-neighbor selection also used at link-generation time. Budget is effectively capped by the small retrieved-note set, yielding ~1,126-2,520 answering tokens. Not adaptive/precision-driven k and not reranked-then-truncated; k is a manually set hyperparameter (default 10, library default also k=10, recommended 3-10).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (no new benchmark constructed; uses existing LoCoMo - 7,512 QA pairs over five categories, ~9K-token dialogues up to 35 sessions - and DialSim - ~1,300 sessions, ~350K tokens, from three TV shows).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Agent memory line: MemGPT (OS-style tiered context, Packer et al.), MemoryBank (Ebbinghaus-forgetting memory, Zhong et al.), ReadAgent (gist memory + interactive look-up), SCM (Self-Controlled Memory); structured/graph memory Mem0 (motivation/contrast). Conceptually inspired by the Zettelkasten note-taking method (Luhmann). Uses RAG foundations (Lewis et al.; standard dense-retrieval indexing) and the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence encoder for embeddings; evaluated on LoCoMo (Maharana et al.) and DialSim benchmarks; deployed via Ollama/LiteLLM and (in the library) ChromaDB.
- **contrasts with**:
> Memory systems with predefined/fixed structures and workflows that the agent must specify in advance: MemGPT (OS-style tiered context), MemoryBank, ReadAgent, SCM, and especially Mem0-style graph-database memory (predefined schemas/relationships limit adaptability). Also contrasts with agentic RAG (which is agentic only in the retrieval phase over a STATIC knowledge base) - A-Mem instead places agency in autonomous memory storage, linking, and evolution.
- **lineage**:
> Group F (decision/memory line) - self-organizing agentic memory. Within the LLM-agent memory lineage (MemGPT -> MemoryBank/ReadAgent/SCM -> Mem0 graph memory -> A-Mem), A-Mem's distinctive contributions are (a) Zettelkasten-inspired note construction with LLM-generated keywords/tags/contextual descriptions, (b) autonomous LLM-driven link generation forming an interconnected, schema-free knowledge network, and (c) memory evolution that rewrites/refines existing historical notes when new memories arrive (self-organizing memory). It is a 2025 episodic-memory method emphasizing dynamic self-organization over fixed-structure storage and over static-corpus agentic RAG.

<a id="item-ace"></a>
### 138. ACE (Agentic Context Engineering)

2025  ·  arXiv 2510.04618  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: ICLR 2026 (arXiv:2510.04618, submitted Oct 2025)
- **authors affiliation**:
> Qizheng Zhang, Changran Hu, Shubhangi Upasani, Boyuan Ma, Fenglu Hong, Vamsidhar Kamanuru, Jay Rainton, Chen Wu, Mengmeng Ji, Hanchen Li, Urmish Thakker, James Zou, Kunle Olukotun. Affiliations: Stanford University (Zhang, Zou, Olukotun), SambaNova Systems Inc. (Hu, Upasani, Ma, Hong, Kamanuru, Rainton, Wu, Ji, Thakker), UC Berkeley (Li). Equal contribution: Qizheng Zhang and Changran Hu.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618
- **code url**: https://github.com/ace-agent/ace (Apache-2.0; project page https://ace-agent.github.io/)
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/ace-agent/ace

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Agentic / interactive agents (tool-use, API understanding, code generation, environment interaction) and domain-specific reasoning (financial analysis, plus medical reasoning and text-to-SQL). Spans agent and domain-specific reasoning rather than open-domain QA.
- **problem setting**:
> Context adaptation: improving LLM behaviour by modifying the input context (system prompts, agent memory, evidence) rather than updating model weights. Studied in two modes: offline adaptation (optimize a system prompt / playbook on a training split, then evaluate on a test split with pass@1) and online adaptation (evolve agent memory at test time as samples stream in). Single LLM is used for all three roles (Generator/Reflector/Curator) to avoid knowledge transfer. Adaptation can use ground-truth labels OR rely solely on natural execution feedback (e.g. code execution success/failure), making it work with and without labeled supervision. Single-agent private context; not multi-agent shared memory.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Structured, itemized 'bullets' from an evolving context 'playbook': reusable strategies/insights, domain concepts, formulas/calculations, tool-use guidelines, and common failure modes (mistakes to avoid), each tagged with helpful/harmful counters. The entire curated playbook is loaded into context (rather than top-k retrieved per query).
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes and curates online (an evolving playbook). Built from the agent's own execution traces; not a static external document/KB corpus. Offline-warmup can initialize it, but it grows during deployment, so effectively growing-memory (HYBRID offline-init + online-growth).
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Not a fixed top-k ranking objective. ACE deliberately accumulates a comprehensive, detailed playbook (the whole curated context is injected, capped by a token budget) to preserve complete domain knowledge and avoid brevity bias / context collapse, prioritizing completeness and detail over concise selection.
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The paper frames itself as 'context adaptation' / 'agentic context engineering' and 'evolving playbooks', inspired by Dynamic Cheatsheet and LLM memory frameworks (A-MEM). It does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner or claim case-based reasoning.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**: guideline-rule / strategy bullet (a 'bullet' = small itemized unit such as a reusable strategy, domain concept, formula, or common failure mode, plus metadata: unique ID + helpful/harmful counters). Conceptually similar to a memory entry in Dynamic Cheatsheet / A-MEM.
- **index source**: Growing memory induced online/at test-time from the agent's execution traces; can be offline-induced via offline warmup on a training split, then continues to grow online. Hybrid offline-init + online/test-time-induced.
- **index structure topology**:
> Sectioned / category-keyed itemized list (a structured playbook with labeled sections such as STRATEGIES & INSIGHTS, FORMULAS & CALCULATIONS, COMMON MISTAKES TO AVOID), each holding ID-tagged bullets with helpful/harmful counters. Not a vector index or knowledge graph; effectively a hierarchical (section -> bullet) structured store. A de-dup step compares bullets via semantic embeddings.
- **retriever type**: LLM-as-context-manager / no learned dense retriever in the classic sense. The full playbook is supplied to the Generator; the Generator itself flags which bullets were useful or misleading. De-duplication uses semantic embeddings for similarity comparison during grow-and-refine.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None for a trained retriever (off-the-shelf). Bullet utility is tracked via non-learned helpful/harmful counters updated by the Reflector from execution feedback; selection/curation is driven by LM-feedback (Reflector insights) and natural execution outcomes rather than a contrastively trained or RL-trained retriever.
- **query construction**:
> No explicit query is formed for retrieval; the whole curated playbook is injected as part of the Generator's input context. The Generator, while solving a new query, marks which bullets were helpful/misleading, which provides the feedback signal for the Reflector. Effectively task/query-conditioned usage of a global context rather than per-query retrieval.
- **query granularity**: Task-level: the playbook is provided as context for each task/query (one shared evolving context), with adaptation done per-sample (batch size 1) to construct delta updates.
- **when to retrieve**: One-shot per task for usage (whole playbook injected at the start of solving a query). Adaptation/update is iterative across samples (online) or epochs (offline).
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule for context injection (playbook always provided to Generator). For updates, the trigger is execution/reflection-based: after the Generator produces a trajectory, the Reflector critiques it (using execution feedback such as code success/failure, or GT labels when available) and proposes corrective delta bullets that the Curator merges.
- **reranking**: No retrieval reranking stage. Instead, a grow-and-refine de-duplication/pruning step periodically (proactively after each delta, or lazily when the context window/token budget is exceeded) prunes redundant bullets via semantic-embedding similarity.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Curation/refinement of the context store: Reflector distills concrete insights from successes/errors (optionally across multiple refinement rounds, default up to 5); Curator merges compact delta bullets via deterministic, non-LLM logic; grow-and-refine performs de-duplication, pruning, and in-place counter updates, capped by a playbook token budget.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A. ACE does not engineer tool/API descriptions for indexing; the AppWorld setting uses the official ReAct tool interface. Bullets may contain tool-use guidelines and readily-usable code snippets, but these are curated from execution traces, not from tool docstrings.
- **index content separation**:
> N/A / partial. There is no lightweight-index-then-load-content split; the curated playbook itself (with section headers and ID-tagged bullets) is the content loaded into context. Metadata (IDs, helpful/harmful counters) is lightweight, but heavy content is not separately deferred.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A. Tool integration follows the AppWorld official ReAct implementation; ACE does not introduce a live-synchronized tool index, RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling protocol, or CRUD auto-sync of a tool store.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A. ACE does not model inter-tool dependency graphs; tool-use knowledge is captured implicitly as free-text strategy/failure-mode bullets in the playbook.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**: Prompt augmentation: the evolved playbook (curated strategies, formulas, failure modes) is injected into the Generator's input context as a comprehensive system prompt / agent memory, guiding reasoning and tool use. No weight updates.
- **planning integration**:
> One-shot context injection at plan/act time: the playbook conditions the ReAct agent's multi-turn reasoning and tool use. The playbook is updated between episodes/samples (online) or epochs (offline) rather than inside a tree/MCTS search. Effectively retrieve(load playbook)-then-plan/act, with the playbook itself evolving from execution feedback.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-task / per-episode: the whole playbook conditions an entire ReAct rollout. Updates are per-sample (a delta context distilled from each sample); not per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled strategy / structured note: free-text itemized bullets (strategies, domain concepts, formulas, common mistakes) tagged with IDs and helpful/harmful counters, sometimes including readily-usable code/tools; organized into a structured playbook. Not raw trajectories or latent tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Distilled strategy/insight and state-aware guideline/rule (reusable heuristics, domain concepts, formulas, common failure modes) abstracted from raw trajectories; more abstract than a raw trajectory but more detailed/comprehensive than a terse summary.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Reflector-based self-reflection separates evaluation/insight extraction from curation; helpful/harmful counters and grow-and-refine de-duplication/pruning limit redundancy and harmful bullets; ACE is shown robust to weak/noisy reflectors and degrades gracefully (staying above base model except under fully adversarial updates every iteration). Effectiveness still depends on feedback quality (degrades without reliable GT/execution signals).

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: Workflow/procedural playbook memory (structured, itemized strategy store) functioning as agent memory; non-parametric, append-and-refine. Closest to skill-library/workflow + episodic-insight memory.
- **write back**: True. The system stores new experiences/insights as delta bullets into the playbook: Curator integrates Reflector-distilled lessons, appending new-ID bullets and updating existing ones in place.
- **online growth**: Yes. In online adaptation the playbook grows during deployment/test-time as samples stream in; offline warmup can pre-populate it, but it continues to expand and refine online (grow-and-refine).
- **write back trigger**:
> Reflective (after self-critique): each sample's Generator trajectory is critiqued by the Reflector (using execution feedback and/or GT labels), and the Curator writes delta bullets. Triggered on both successes and failures (the Reflector distills insights from successes and errors), batch size 1, optionally over multiple epochs offline.
- **failure experience usage**: Both success and failure are used: the Reflector distills concrete insights from successes AND errors; bullets include 'common mistakes to avoid' (failure-mode/corrective rules), and helpful/harmful counters track which bullets help vs. mislead. Not success-only.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Delta-update + dedup-merge + forget-prune + link-and-evolve: incremental delta updates (localized bullet edits) instead of monolithic rewrite; new-ID bullets appended, existing bullets updated in place (e.g. incrementing counters); grow-and-refine performs semantic-embedding de-duplication and pruning (proactive or lazy when token budget exceeded). Explicitly avoids full-context rewriting to prevent context collapse.
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Context curation is not an RL/learned policy; it is LLM-prompted reflection + deterministic non-LLM merging with counter-based heuristics and embedding de-duplication. (Paper notes GEPA's RL comparison, but ACE itself is not RL-trained.)

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> AppWorld (agent benchmark: API understanding, code generation, environment interaction; test-normal and test-challenge splits); FiNER and Formula/XBRL-Formula (financial analysis over XBRL; from FinLoRA/loukas2022finer & wang2025finlora); plus additional domain tasks from StreamBench: DDXPlus (medical reasoning) and BIRD-SQL (text-to-SQL).
- **benchmark family**: Web/agent (AppWorld) + tool/code/environment-interaction; domain reasoning: finance (FiNER, Formula), medical (DDXPlus), text-to-SQL (BIRD-SQL). Mix of agent (AppWorld) and domain-specific reasoning families.
- **baselines**:
> Base LLM (no context engineering / default prompts); In-Context Learning (ICL, few/many-shot, agarwal2024many); MIPROv2 (DSPy prompt optimizer, auto='heavy'); GEPA (Genetic-Pareto reflective prompt optimizer, DSPy, auto='heavy'); Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC, online test-time memory, CU variant). For AppWorld all methods are built on the official ReAct implementation. Contextual leaderboard reference: IBM CUGA (GPT-4.1, top-1 production agent) - cited as contextual reference, not a methodological baseline.
- **key metrics**:
> AppWorld: Task Goal Completion (TGC) and Scenario Goal Completion (SGC) on test-normal and test-challenge, plus average; pass@1 in offline. FiNER/Formula/DDXPlus: accuracy (exact-match). BIRD-SQL: LLM-as-a-judge (GPT-4o-mini). Efficiency: adaptation latency, number of rollouts, token dollar cost (ingestion/generation).
- **headline result**:
> On AppWorld (DeepSeek-V3.1-671B base), ReAct+ACE reaches 59.4% average (+17.0 over ReAct's 42.4) offline with GT labels, matching the top-ranked production agent IBM CUGA (60.3%, GPT-4.1) and surpassing it on test-challenge with online adaptation; +10.6% average over selected baselines on agents and +8.6% on finance. Online without GT labels ACE improves AppWorld up to +17.1%.
- **ablations**:
> Ablation on AppWorld (Table 3) over three factors: (1) Reflector with iterative refinement (ACE's addition beyond Dynamic Cheatsheet), (2) multi-epoch adaptation, (3) offline warmup. ReAct + ACE without Reflector or multi-epoch already gives +12.7 average (55.1 vs 42.4); adding each component yields further gains, confirming all are key. Additional studies: incremental context update (Appendix A.5, shown to be the key enabler vs monolithic rewrite that causes context collapse), robustness to reflection quality (Appendix A.4: robust to weak/noisy reflectors), hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix A.6).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (no Recall@k/nDCG): there is no top-k retrieval to score. Evaluation reports end-to-end task metrics (TGC/SGC/accuracy) plus efficiency metrics; context-collapse case study reports token count vs accuracy over adaptation steps.
- **process vs outcome metrics**: Primarily outcome metrics (task/scenario goal completion, accuracy). Process is examined qualitatively via the context-collapse case study (token count vs accuracy per adaptation step) and ablations, but not via formal step-wise faithfulness/process scores.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> ACE substantially cheaper than adaptive baselines: offline AppWorld -82.3% adaptation latency and -75.1% rollouts vs GEPA (and -80.8%/-83.6% input/output token usage vs GEPA in offline adaptation); online FiNER -91.5% adaptation latency and -83.6% token dollar cost vs Dynamic Cheatsheet; ~86.9% lower adaptation latency on average vs existing adaptive methods (per repo). At eval time ACE uses more raw input tokens (richer playbook) but billed cost is mitigated by KV caching reuse.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Budget-capped: whole curated playbook injected, capped by a playbook token budget (default 80,000 tokens in the released code). Grow-and-refine prunes/dedups to stay within budget (proactively or lazily when window exceeded). No fixed top-k selection; budget + de-duplication govern size. Reflector refinement rounds and offline epochs default to 5 in the paper (repo defaults: max_num_rounds=3, num_epochs=1).
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (not a survey; ACE is a method paper).
- **benchmark construction and size**: N/A (not a benchmark paper). Uses existing benchmarks; notes AppWorld difficulty: at submission the best leaderboard system achieved only 60.3% average accuracy. FiNER labels tokens with one of 139 fine-grained XBRL entity types; Formula tests numerical financial reasoning.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Dynamic Cheatsheet (suzgun2025dynamic) - agentic test-time external-memory design ACE is directly inspired by; ReAct (yao2023react) - base agent loop; LLM memory frameworks like A-MEM (xu2025mem) for the memory-entry/bullet concept; DSPy ecosystem (MIPROv2, GEPA) for prompt-optimization baselines; long-context LLMs (DeepSeek-V3.1) for scaling comprehensive contexts.
- **contrasts with**:
> Monolithic-rewrite context optimizers and concise prompt optimizers: GEPA (brevity-as-strength reflective prompt evolution), MIPROv2 (Bayesian prompt optimization), ICL (fixed demonstrations), and Dynamic Cheatsheet's full-rewrite memory (which can cause context collapse). ACE contrasts by using structured incremental delta updates + grow-and-refine to avoid brevity bias and context collapse, and by adapting weights-free without labeled supervision via execution feedback.
- **lineage**:
> Group F (decision/memory/RL) - self-improving LLM agents via evolving non-parametric memory/context. Sits in the test-time context-adaptation / agent-memory lineage (Dynamic Cheatsheet, Reflexion, GEPA, TextGrad), extending memory frameworks (A-MEM) toward structured, incrementally-updated 'playbook' memory for self-improving agents.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- adaptation_mechanism
- cbr_cycle_coverage
- cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing

<a id="item-agent-kb"></a>
### 139. Agent KB (AGENT KB) - Leveraging Cross-Domain Experience for Agentic Problem Solving

2025  ·  arXiv 2507.06229  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06229)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**:
> Xiangru Tang, Tianrui Qin, Tianhao Peng (co-first authors), Ziyang Zhou, Daniel Shao, Tingting Du, Xinming Wei, Peng Xia, Fang Wu, He Zhu, Ge Zhang, Jiaheng Liu, Xingyao Wang, Sirui Hong, Chenglin Wu, Hao Cheng, Chi Wang, Wangchunshu Zhou (senior). Affiliations: Yale University, OPPO (OPPO-PersonalAI), UW-Madison, UNC Chapel Hill, Stanford University, Bytedance, Nanjing University, All Hands AI, DeepWisdom, Microsoft Research, Google DeepMind.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06229
- **code url**:
> https://github.com/OPPO-PersonalAI/Agent-KB (official; Apache-2.0; ~431 stars as of mid-2025; Python-dominant. Contains Agent-KB-GAIA (smolagents/open_deep_research) and Agent-KB-SWE-bench subprojects). Anonymous reproducibility mirror cited in paper: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Agent-KB/
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/OPPO-PersonalAI/Agent-KB (official repo; last push Aug 2025). No separate maintained leaderboard/paper-list.

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Agentic problem solving spanning reasoning and software engineering: general/long-horizon tool-use and web research QA (GAIA), expert/scientific QA (Humanity's Last Exam Bio/Chem, GPQA), and code repair (SWE-bench Lite). Cross-domain experience transfer across heterogeneous agent frameworks (planning + tool-use + code).
- **problem setting**:
> Inference-time, training-free (no retraining/fine-tuning) memory layer that enables experience sharing across multiple heterogeneous agent frameworks (smolagents, OWL, SWE-Agent, OpenHands). Interactive multi-pass agentic solving: each task is attempted in three sequential passes (pass@1 retrieves cross-task experiences; pass@2 enriches Agent KB with failure diagnoses from the first attempt; pass@3 revisits unresolved cases with the expanded pool). Supervision is task-level outcome (exact-match correctness / SWE-bench test passage); both successful and failed runs are normalized into experiences. The knowledge base is bootstrapped offline from 80 human seed trajectories plus automatic rollouts (~9.5k experiences) and continues to grow online across passes/frameworks. Frameworks contribute to and consume the same shared KB via lightweight REST/RPC APIs without architectural changes.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Structured 'experiences' distilled from heterogeneous agent trajectories: (a) workflow-level experiences = high-level reusable problem-solving strategies/plans and agent_experience guideline lists (planning stage), and (b) execution-level experiences/snippets = targeted diagnostic fixes and correction hints derived from execution traces (feedback stage). Each experience unit E = <pi, gamma, S, C> = (task embedding, goal-constraint predicates, action-reasoning pairs {(a_i, r_i)}, cross-framework metadata).
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID: a structured experience knowledge base that is bootstrapped offline (human seeds + automatic rollouts over benchmark datasets) and GROWS online during multi-pass deployment as frameworks write back new experiences (additions, conflict resolution, eviction). It is the agent ecosystem's own distilled trajectory memory rather than a static external document corpus; tool-level web search exists in the base agents but the defining retrieval targets the shared experience KB.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k retrieval (default top-k = 3; SWE-bench retrieve prompt asks for 3-5 entries). After hybrid scoring/reranking the top-k candidates are deduplicated, then refined. The objective is precision-driven small-set selection: ablation (Fig 5b) shows hybrid retrieval peaks around k=3 and remains robust across top-k settings; it is not a recall/completeness objective over a minimal needed set.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve, Reuse(=Refine/adapt), Revise(=feedback-driven refinement), Retain(=write-back)] - the paper explicitly restructures the classic CBR Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle into a Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop with cross-agent write-back. Mapping: Retrieve = hybrid BM25+embedding retrieval; Reuse/Revise = Refine step adapts (entity mapping, tool substitution, step reordering) plus feedback-stage diagnostic correction; Retain = self-evolving memory addition/dedup/eviction with utility scores. All four phases are effectively realized.
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> Partial/True-with-reframing. The work explicitly references case-based reasoning for LLM agents (cites Hatalis et al. 2025 'Review of case-based reasoning for LLM agents') and the classic Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle, but deliberately reframes its own pipeline as a 'Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop with write-back across agents' rather than branding itself as CBR. It does not center Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner as its primary framing; it positions itself as a cross-framework shared memory infrastructure that restructures the CBR cycle.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Structured experience unit (a distilled problem-solution-experience case): E = <pi (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 task embedding), gamma (goal-constraint predicates), S = {(a_i, r_i)} action-reasoning pairs, C (cross-framework metadata)>. Surfaced either as a workflow-level reusable plan/guideline (planning) or an execution-pattern fix/hint (feedback). Effectively (question, agent_plan/agent_experience, [search_agent_plan/experience]) JSON entries.
- **index source**:
> Hybrid construction. Offline bootstrap: 80 human seed trajectories (60 BrowseComp/HopRAG-style browsing + 20 SWE-Gym-style coding) drive automatic rollouts by smolagents/OWL/SWE-Agent/OpenHands over BrowseComp, MultiHopRAG, HLE, WebWalkerQA, RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval, yielding ~9k workflow summaries + ~7k execution snippets (~9.5k experience entries). Online growth: the same KB is enriched at test time across passes (failure diagnoses added in pass@2/3) and across frameworks via shared APIs.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat experience store with a calibrated hybrid index: a lexical (BM25) inverted index over text plus a dense vector index of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 task embeddings, fused by a weighted score (alpha=0.5). Entries carry framework-compatibility metadata C and goal-constraint predicates gamma used as filters. Conceptually 'hierarchical' in that it stores workflow-level vs execution-level (planning vs feedback) experiences, but the retrievable structure is a metadata-keyed flat hybrid index rather than a knowledge graph.
- **retriever type**:
> Hybrid: lexical BM25 shortlisting + dense semantic ranking (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence-transformer embeddings, cosine), combined via calibrated weighted score fusion (sigma_hyb = alpha * sigma_text + (1-alpha) * sigma_sem, alpha=0.5). An LLM is used as a ranker/curator during deduplication (knowledge curation) but the retrieval scorer itself is BM25 + embedding hybrid.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None (off-the-shelf) for the retriever: BM25 and a frozen all-MiniLM-L6-v2 encoder; the hybrid fusion weight alpha and disagreement-gate threshold beta are fixed hyperparameters (0.5 / 0.8), not learned. The only learned/adaptive signal is at the memory-management level: each stored experience maintains a utility score u_j <- u_j + eta(r_j - u_j) updated from a reward signal r_j (retrieval success / execution gain) to drive eviction - a value/utility update over entries, not a trained retrieval policy.
- **query construction**:
> Reason step constructs the query. Planning stage: the Reason module reads the task description, surfaces key requirements/challenges and produces structured queries (keyword/concept lists, e.g. 'EC numbers; virus testing method; SPFMV; SPCSV; ...') targeting reusable subroutines/success patterns. Feedback stage: the Reason module analyzes execution traces/critic highlights to derive queries from observed errors (rather than the task description). So queries are LLM-reasoned/intent-extracted and decomposed into searchable components, distinct per stage.
- **query granularity**:
> Two-level / dual-phase: a task-level query at the planning stage (one query from the task description per pass), and a trajectory/feedback-level query at the feedback stage (derived from execution traces and critic highlights). Re-issued across the three sequential passes. Not per-CoT-step or per-token.
- **when to retrieve**:
> Iterative across two fixed stages per attempt and across three sequential passes: retrieve at the planning stage (before/while forming the plan) and again at the feedback stage (after initial execution, conditioned on error traces). Within a benchmark instance, this repeats over pass@1/pass@2/pass@3. It is a fixed two-stage schedule, not uncertainty-triggered active retrieval and not a learned router.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule tied to pipeline stage: (1) planning stage trigger = arrival of a new task description; (2) feedback stage trigger = completion of an execution attempt whose trace/critic indicates errors/bottlenecks (re-engaged for unresolved cases in pass@2/pass@3). No token-level confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, or reflection-token trigger.
- **reranking**:
> Yes. After BM25 lexical shortlisting, candidates are reranked by semantic task similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and combined via calibrated weighted hybrid fusion (alpha=0.5), i.e. a weighted-score fusion reranking; top-k are then deduplicated. An LLM ranker is additionally used during memory deduplication/curation (comparing reasoning quality, completeness, transferability) but that is for write-time curation, not query-time reranking.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Refine stage + dedup. Retrieved candidates are not replayed verbatim; the Refine step adapts abstract action patterns to currently available tools/APIs using metadata C, and when multiple experiences are retrieved it synthesizes them into one coherent workflow via entity mapping, tool substitution, and step reordering. A disagreement gate filters feedback-stage refinements. Top-k candidates are deduplicated before refinement. (rerank + decompose/recompose + adaptation + gating).
- **tool document engineering**:
> N/A for tool indexing. Agent KB indexes distilled experiences, not tool/API documents. Tool/API compatibility is handled at refine time via standardized action vocabularies and metadata C (tool substitution / entity mapping) rather than via synthetic-query augmentation or instruction-tuned tool embeddings.
- **index content separation**:
> Yes (partial). The KB exposes lightweight REST/RPC APIs and stores compact structured experience units (task embedding pi + predicates gamma + metadata C + action-reasoning pairs S) that are retrieved cheaply, while the heavy native execution happens in the base framework. It separates workflow-level (planning) experiences from execution-level (feedback) snippets, and curated human seeds are stored but never retrieved directly (they only seed generation), giving a lightweight-index-then-content flavour.
- **dynamic index and protocol**:
> Live, evolving experience store synchronized across frameworks via lightweight REST endpoints / RPC calls (submit + retrieve experiences); experiences gathered in one framework become instantly available to others. Self-evolving with CRUD-like operations (addition, LLM-ranked conflict resolution/deduplication, utility-based eviction). Integration protocol is HTTP/REST + RPC APIs (not RapidAPI/MCP); it is a tool-agnostic memory service rather than a tool registry.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A. Retrieval does not model inter-tool dependency graphs or prerequisites. Cross-framework tool compatibility is handled heuristically at refine time (tool substitution, entity mapping, step reordering using metadata C), not via a dependency graph or dependency-aware reranking.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation + case/experience adaptation. Retrieved experiences are injected as concise actionable suggestions/guidelines that (a) seed the agent's initial plan with cross-domain workflows (planning stage) and (b) supply targeted diagnostic fixes applied to live execution (feedback stage). The base agent is left unchanged; Agent KB intercepts only the planning and feedback points. No training signal / no weight updates (training-free).
- **planning integration**:
> Plan-then-retrieve-then-refine, dual-phase and looped with execution. Planning stage: Reason summarizes the task -> Retrieve selects experiences -> Refine synthesizes them into an executable plan rho returned to the native framework. The framework executes; then the Feedback stage runs a second Reason-Retrieve-Refine cycle over the execution trace to produce a refined plan rho', gated by the disagreement gate. Repeated across pass@1/2/3. Retrieval interfaces at plan time and post-execution feedback time, not inside MCTS/tree search.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-stage / per-pass: one retrieval+refine at planning (per-plan) and one at feedback (per-execution-trace), repeated across three passes. Coarser than per-CoT-step or per-token interleaving; closer to per-answer/per-attempt with a planning vs feedback split.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation + execution-feedback-driven revision. Retrieved experiences are adapted (not replayed) in the Refine step via entity mapping, tool substitution, and step reordering to fit available tools/APIs and domain constraints; the feedback stage performs execution-feedback-driven revision of the plan, and a disagreement gate (cosine of plan embeddings >= beta=0.8) blocks revisions that diverge too far from the original plan. No RL/fine-tuning of the base agent.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled, structured natural-language experiences: concise actionable suggestion lists / workflow guidelines (agent_experience, search_agent_experience), reusable abstract plans (agent_planning), and execution-fix hints. Stored as standardized JSON experience units with a task embedding, goal predicates, action-reasoning pairs, and cross-framework metadata. Surface form injected is distilled strategy/guideline text and adapted workflows, not raw trajectories (raw seeds are never retrieved directly) and not executable code/skills.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled strategy / reusable workflow + state-aware corrective guideline. Planning-stage units are abstract, tool-neutral reusable workflows and generalizable behavioral guidelines (e.g. 'Break down multifaceted questions into smaller constraint checks'); feedback-stage units are diagnostic correction rules tied to observed error patterns. Higher abstraction than raw trajectories; not a procedural executable skill/program.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Disagreement gate (the headline mechanism): G(rho, rho') = 1[cos(phi(rho), phi(rho')) >= beta], beta=0.8, applies a refined plan only if it stays semantically coherent with the original plan, explicitly addressing 'knowledge interference' in cross-framework transfer. Plus: hybrid retrieval (lexical precision + semantic coverage) to reduce mismatched retrievals; refine-time adaptation/tool-substitution to avoid invalid transplanted steps; LLM-ranked deduplication and utility-based eviction to keep high-quality entries. No retriever-aware SFT of the base agent.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Structured experience knowledge base / shared cross-framework memory described as hierarchical (workflow-level episodic experiences + execution-pattern semantic knowledge + working memory). Effectively an episodic/workflow experience memory with a semantic experience store and self-evolution; not latent.
- **write back**:
> True. Heterogeneous frameworks write distilled experiences back into the shared KB ('write-back across agents'). Construction normalizes both successful and failed runs into structured experience units; at test time pass@2/pass@3 enrich the KB with failure diagnoses. Self-evolving memory performs addition, LLM-ranked deduplication/conflict resolution, and utility-based eviction.
- **online growth**:
> True. The KB grows during multi-pass deployment and across frameworks (experiences from one framework instantly available to others via shared APIs; failure diagnoses appended across passes). Fig 5c shows performance scaling with KB size (100 -> 500 examples). It is not frozen after offline induction; it self-evolves (add/dedup/evict).
- **write back trigger**:
> On both success and failure, at construction and across passes. Construction: both successful and failed runs are normalized into experiences (failures yield diagnostic/correction templates). Deployment: feedback-stage failure diagnoses are written into the KB to enrich pass@2/pass@3. Human seeds are curated offline but never retrieved directly. Curation/eviction are reflective (LLM-ranked quality comparison; utility-driven). Not purely on-success.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success + failure. Failed runs and failure modes are explicitly abstracted into correction templates / diagnostic experiences and retrieved in the feedback stage to apply targeted fixes; human annotators inspect failed logs to build correction templates that seed automatic experience generation. So failures are used correctively, alongside successful workflows.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Add + dedup-merge (conflict resolution) + forget-prune (eviction). New experiences are added; when a candidate is highly similar to an existing entry (max cosine > tau=0.8) an LLM ranker keeps the superior entry (dedup/conflict resolution); under memory pressure an adaptive eviction policy uses a learned per-entry utility score u_j <- u_j + eta(r_j - u_j) balancing recency, frequency, and cross-framework transferability to prune low-utility entries. Entries are effectively curated/overwritten rather than strictly append-only.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No (mostly). Query-time retrieval is fixed BM25 + embedding hybrid top-k (not an RL/learned retrieval policy). There is a learned/adaptive component only in memory management: a per-entry utility score updated by a TD-style rule from reward (retrieval success/execution gain) governing eviction. Case/experience selection itself is similarity-based, not a trained policy (contrast with Memento's M-MDP soft-Q retrieval).
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Yes - this is the defining contribution. Agent KB is a cross-framework, plug-and-play shared memory infrastructure: a single KB instance is attached to multiple heterogeneous frameworks (smolagents, OWL, SWE-Agent, OpenHands) via standardized APIs, so experiences gathered in one framework are instantly reusable by others, enabling cross-architecture knowledge transfer without retraining ('collective agent intelligence').

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> GAIA validation (165 tasks: 53 L1 / 86 L2 / 26 L3); Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) Bio/Chem cleaned subset (149 tasks, multimodal scientific reasoning); GPQA (198 graduate-level MCQs, physics/chemistry/biology, no external tools); SWE-bench Lite (300 GitHub Python issues, 50- and 100-iteration limits). KB constructed from BrowseComp, MultiHopRAG, HLE, WebWalkerQA, RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval.
- **benchmark family**:
> Tool/long-horizon agentic + web research (GAIA); expert/scientific QA (HLE Bio/Chem, GPQA); code repair (SWE-bench Lite). Construction sources add multi-hop QA (MultiHopRAG/HopRAG), web navigation (BrowseComp, WebWalkerQA), and repo-level code (RepoClassBench, SWE-Gym-Raw, RepoEval).
- **baselines**:
> GAIA: agentic models Search-o1-32B, WebThinker-32B-RL; closed-source frameworks TraseAgent, OpenAI Deep Research, h2oGPTe, Desearch, Alita; open-source frameworks OWL, TapeAgents, AutoAgent, Magnetic-1 (Magentic-One), FRIDAY; and the memory baseline A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025) applied to smolagents. SWE-bench Lite: SWE-Agent and OpenHands base frameworks (vs +Agent KB). HLE: AutoGen, SciMaster, Biomni, OpenHands base. GPQA: Direct Reasoning baselines (o3-mini, Claude-3.7, GPT-4.1) and OpenHands base. Knowledge-type ablation baseline: HANDCRAFTED (student-annotated) vs AGENT KB (auto-distilled). Latency/memory baselines: A-Mem, MemoryBank, ReadAgent.
- **key metrics**:
> Reasoning tasks: pass@1/pass@2/pass@3 accuracy (exact-match for GAIA; accuracy for HLE/GPQA). SWE-bench Lite: success/resolution rate at max-iter 50 and 100, plus pass@1/2/3 with budget caps. Efficiency: retrieval latency, memory footprint, per-task token counts and USD cost. Error-category counts (retrieval/planning/reasoning/format/perception/execution).
- **headline result**:
> On GAIA, smolagents (GPT-4.1) improve from 55.2% to 73.9% pass@3 (+18.7pp); Claude-3.7 smolagents reach 75.2% pass@3. On SWE-bench Lite, OpenHands (GPT-4.1) gains +4.0pp pass@1 (24.3% -> 28.3%) and up to 45.7% at 100 iters pass@3; OpenHands (Claude-3.7) jumps 30.0% -> 51.0% at 50 iters. HLE: OpenHands 9.5% -> 14.1% (pass@3). GPQA: GPT-4.1 62.6% -> 72.7%. Most-cited: +18.7pp on GAIA pass@3 (smolagents).
- **ablations**:
> (1) Module ablation (Table 3, smolagents GPT-4.1 on GAIA, baseline 55.15 -> +Agent KB 61.21): removing Refine causes the largest drop (-6.06, back to 55.15), w/o Retrieve -> 57.58 (-3.63), w/o Reason -> 60.00 (-1.21), w/o Planning Stage and w/o Feedback Stage both cap at 59.39; w/ Raw Workflow 58.18 (must adapt, not replay). (2) Retrieval strategy (Fig 5b): hybrid > lexical (BM25) > semantic alone, robust across top-k, optimal at k=3. (3) Disagreement-gate threshold beta sweep (Fig 5a): best at beta ~ 0.8. (4) KB size (Fig 5c): graceful scaling 100 -> 500 examples; code tasks benefit most, advanced reasoning bottlenecked by abstraction quality not quantity. (5) Auto vs handcrafted (Table 4): AGENT KB 75.15% vs HANDCRAFTED 76.97% on GAIA (auto surpasses on L3: 57.69 vs 53.85; SWE-bench 24.33 -> 51.00). (6) Asymmetric cross-domain transfer (Fig 6): reasoning experience helps SWE (37.0%) but SWE experience transfers poorly to reasoning. (7) Error analysis (Fig 7): net error reduction (GPT-4.1 net -10; Claude-3.7 net +11 corrected).
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome metrics (pass@k accuracy, SWE-bench resolution). Some process-oriented analysis is included: a manual error-category breakdown (retrieval/planning/reasoning/format/perception/execution) with Venn diagrams of corrected vs newly introduced errors, and progressive pass@1->pass@3 improvement curves, but no formal step-wise reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Low marginal overhead. GAIA: the retrieval loop adds only ~$0.27 on top of ~$86 per full evaluation run (<0.4%); planning + feedback modules ~317-417 tokens / ~$0.001 each per task vs the ~206k-token action loop. One-off KB construction: ~5.14M prompt + 0.77M completion tokens (~$10.88), amortized. SWE-bench Lite: hinting averages ~$0.0037/issue (<7k tokens, hint length ~88). Latency/memory footprint competitive with A-Mem/MemoryBank/ReadAgent (Fig 4). Reported tradeoff: 4.0-18.7pp gains for ~$3.0-4.5 per task overhead (deemed acceptable).
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Default retrieval top-k = 3 (SWE-bench retrieve prompt requests 3-5 entries); reranked-then-deduplicated-then-truncated to top-k. Hyperparameters: hybrid fusion alpha=0.5, dedup similarity tau=0.8, disagreement-gate beta=0.8, eviction learning rate eta. Injected hints are short (SWE-bench hint length ~88 tokens, prompts <7k tokens). Base model fixed to GPT-4.1, temperature 1.0 unless stated. Selection is fixed-k (precision-driven, ablated around k=3), not adaptive per query.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A - this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A as a benchmark paper. Uses existing benchmarks (GAIA 165, HLE Bio/Chem 149, GPQA 198, SWE-bench Lite 300). For the constructed experience KB (Table 5): BrowseComp 1266->1266, MultiHopRAG 2556->2556, HLE 3000->~2000 (text subset), WebWalkerQA 680->680, RepoClassBench 100->1000 (10 experiences/case), SWE-Gym-Raw 100->1000, RepoEval 100->1000; total ~7802 tasks -> ~9502 experiences, bootstrapped from 80 human seed trajectories.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Base agent frameworks smolagents (Roucher/Zhu et al. 2025), OWL (Hu et al. 2025), SWE-Agent (Yang et al. 2024), OpenHands (Wang et al. 2024); retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al. 2020); sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings + BM25; classic CBR Retrieve-Reuse-Revise-Retain cycle (Aamodt & Plaza lineage via Hatalis et al. 2025 review); experience/workflow-memory prior work (Agent Workflow Memory, Synapse, Meta-Agent-Workflow); complementary to DSPy declarative pipelines.
- **contrasts with**:
> Single-agent / framework-specific memory systems that cannot transfer across architectures: A-MEM (Xu et al. 2025), MemGPT, MemoryBank, ReadAgent, Learn-by-Interact (single-framework), Agent Workflow Memory, Synapse, and templating pipelines confined to narrow task families. Positioned against these as the first cross-framework plug-and-play shared KB, and against naive experience injection (which causes knowledge interference) via the disagreement gate.
- **lineage**:
> Group F (decision/experience memory; experience-and-memory-augmented agents). Within the CBR-for-LLM-agents / experience-memory lineage (Reflexion -> ExpeL/AutoGuide -> Agent Workflow Memory/Synapse -> A-MEM/MemGPT), Agent KB is distinguished by being a cross-framework, training-free shared experience infrastructure with a two-stage (planning + feedback) Reason-Retrieve-Refine loop, hybrid BM25+embedding retrieval, self-evolving memory (add/dedup/evict with utility scores), and a disagreement gate to prevent cross-framework knowledge interference. Contemporaneous/sibling to Memento, ReasoningBank, AWM, ExpeL.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- evaluation_decoupling
- venue

<a id="item-agentevolver"></a>
### 140. AgentEvolver: Towards Efficient Self-Evolving Agent System

2025  ·  arXiv 2511.10395  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10395)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **authors affiliation**: Yunpeng Zhai, Shuchang Tao, Cheng Chen, Anni Zou, Ziqian Chen, Qingxu Fu, Shinji Mai, Li Yu, Jiaji Deng, Zouying Cao, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou. Affiliation: Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.10395
- **code url**: https://github.com/modelscope/AgentEvolver (Apache-2.0). Experience management implemented via ReMe: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/modelscope/AgentEvolver (actively maintained; homepage https://modelscope.github.io/AgentEvolver/; follow-up releases SeeUPO and CuES tracked in README)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: tool-use / decision-making (long-horizon, tool-augmented LLM agents trained with RL); evaluated on tool/API-calling agent benchmarks
- **problem setting**:
> Interactive, online RL setting for LLM-based agents in tool-augmented multi-turn environments. The agent operates in an 'interaction sandbox' E=(S,A,P) that provides state/action/transition dynamics but no reward function and no predefined task distribution. The agent must autonomously synthesize its own training tasks (proxy task distribution p_train approximating an unknown target distribution p_target) and reward signals, then optimize a goal-conditioned policy via GRPO-style RL. Single-agent (one policy network); supervision (oracle reward/task labels) is NOT assumed at training time — tasks and rewards are self-generated, with an LLM judge providing synthetic rewards. Backbone: Qwen2.5-7B/14B-Instruct.
- **what is retrieved**: experiences — distilled natural-language units of structured knowledge (skills/tactics/precautions and failure notes) derived from past successful and unsuccessful trajectories, each formatted as {When to use, Content}. Used as in-context guidance during rollout.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes: an experience pool P_exp constructed offline from the policy's own rollouts on self-generated tasks (cold-start pool construction) and queried online during rollout. The store is induced from the agent's own trajectories rather than a static external corpus.
- **completeness vs topk objective**: Fixed top-k ranking: experience retrieval selects the TopK (k=5) experiences by cosine similarity, followed by a rerank-and-rewrite refinement. No notion of minimal-set completeness or precision-driven variable-size recommendation is reported.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> Retrieve (yes: cosine top-k retrieval of experiences by query), Reuse (yes: retrieved experience injected into prompt for in-context guidance during rollout), Revise (partial: a re-ranking + re-writing refinement module Omega_refine rewrites retrieved experiences for generality; experiences are distilled/validated rather than per-case adapted to the new problem), Retain (yes: validated experiences indexed into the vector store / experience pool). Flags: [Retrieve=yes, Reuse=yes, Revise=partial, Retain=yes]
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It realizes CBR-like mechanisms (experience acquisition, retrieval, reuse via ICL, retention) under the terminology of 'self-navigating', 'experience reuse', and 'experience pool'.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> experience = a distilled natural-language guideline/insight unit comprising a 'When to use' applicability condition (used as the retrieval key) and a 'Content' body (instructions, precautions, recommended strategies). Conceptually a strategy/guideline distilled from trajectories rather than a raw trajectory; effectively a case-like (condition -> guidance) unit.
- **index source**:
> Hybrid construction: offline-induced cold-start experience pool P_exp built from N_pc=4 rollouts per self-generated task by the initial policy, processed (preprocess -> extract -> validate -> index) into a vector store; queried online at rollout/inference time. Induced from the agent's own experiences (not a static external corpus).
- **index structure topology**: Flat vector index: experiences encoded as embeddings (of the 'When to use' field) in a vector store; retrieval by cosine similarity over flat embeddings (implemented via ReMe). No graph or explicit hierarchy reported.
- **retriever type**: Dense (embedding-based cosine similarity retrieval), followed by an LLM-based re-ranking and re-writing refinement stage.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> None (off-the-shelf) for the retriever itself: retrieval uses fixed embedding cosine similarity (top-k); the retriever is not trained with task-effectiveness, contrastive, or RL signals. (Note: the upstream experience extraction/validation uses an LLM evaluator, but the similarity retriever is off-the-shelf.)
- **query construction**:
> From a task g, an associated query q is extracted and encoded into an embedding h_q; this is matched against experience embeddings h_e (the experiences' 'When to use' fields). Raw task/query embedding; no decomposition or synthetic query expansion reported for the retrieval query.
- **query granularity**: task-level: the query is constructed per task (one-shot at the start of a rollout), and the retrieved experience is injected into the initial prompt of the rollout. Not per-step.
- **when to retrieve**: one-shot: experience is retrieved once per task at the start of an experience-guided rollout and injected into the initial prompt; not iterative or uncertainty-triggered within a trajectory.
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule / proportion-controlled: a fixed fraction eta=0.5 of rollouts within each query group are designated experience-guided (N_e = floor(eta*N)); for those rollouts a relevant experience is retrieved and injected. Retrieval is triggered by the rollout-mixing schedule rather than by token confidence, uncertainty, or an agent-initiated request.
- **reranking**: Yes: a refinement module Omega_refine performs (1) re-ranking of the top-k retrieved experiences to ensure contextual relevance and task alignment, and (2) re-writing to improve generality/adaptability. (LLM-based refinement; not a classical cross-encoder.)
- **retrieved context refinement**: rerank + re-write (rewrite-for-generality). After cosine top-k, Omega_refine re-ranks for contextual relevance/task alignment and re-writes the retrieved experiences to enhance generality and adaptability before injection.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A — retrieved units are experiences (distilled trajectory insights), not tool/skill descriptions; the work does not index tool docstrings for tool retrieval.
- **index content separation**: Partial: the 'When to use' field serves as a lightweight retrieval key/condition (vectorized) while the 'Content' field carries the heavier detailed guidance loaded on use. This is a key-then-content split within each experience rather than a separate index-vs-content store.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A — no tool index or external tool integration protocol (RapidAPI/MCP/RESTful) is the retrieval target. Environments are served via a Gym-compatible Environment Service over HTTP; tool/API calls are part of the environment, not a retrieved/synchronized tool store.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A — retrieval does not model inter-tool dependencies; the retrieved units are experiences, not tools.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> prompt augmentation via in-context learning (explicit experience): a retrieved experience exp_g is injected into the initial prompt following a template {system_prompt}<EXP>{exp_g}</EXP>{query} to steer the experience-guided rollout. Additionally, used as an implicit training signal — RL training (with experience stripping) makes the policy internalize the experience-induced behavior so that retrieval is NOT needed at final inference.
- **planning integration**:
> retrieve-then-act at rollout time (one-shot exemplar/guidance at the start of a trajectory): retrieved experience guides the experience-mixed rollout; combined with an experience-mixed exploration strategy (eta=0.5 vanilla vs experience-guided rollouts) feeding GRPO-style policy optimization. No explicit planner / MCTS / tree search; integration is into the RL rollout-and-update loop.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: per-answer / per-rollout: a single retrieval+injection occurs at the start of each experience-guided rollout (task-level), not interleaved per CoT-step or per tool-call. (Credit assignment, separately, is step-wise.)
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation at the store level: retrieved experiences are re-ranked and re-written (Omega_refine) for generality before use; they are then used as verbatim in-context guidance within the rollout. There is no execution-feedback-driven per-case revision of a single retrieved case; instead RL 'implicit learning' (experience stripping + selective boosting) internalizes the experience.
- **retrieved item representation**: Distilled strategy/guideline in free-text natural language (structured note with 'When to use' + 'Content' fields), injected as plain text in the prompt. Not raw trajectories, not executable programs, not latent tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**: Distilled strategy / state-aware guideline-rule: structured natural-language insights ('When to use' applicability condition + 'Content' advice) extracted from successful, failed, or comparative trajectory pairs — higher abstraction than a raw trajectory.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> Multiple: (1) LLM-based experience validation during pool construction (Omega_process) filters low-quality/unreliable experiences; (2) re-ranking + re-writing refinement (Omega_refine) improves relevance; (3) experience-mixed rollout (eta=0.5) limits over-reliance on retrieved cues; (4) experience stripping removes injected experience tokens before policy-gradient computation so reward is attributed to the model's own reasoning, not to memorized external context; (5) selective boosting handles the off-policy distribution shift from experience-conditioned rollouts.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**: episodic / experience-library (an 'experience pool' of distilled natural-language insights with skill/tactic and failure-note content); stored in a vector store (ReMe).
- **write back**: Yes. Validated experiences distilled from rollout trajectories are extracted, LLM-validated, and indexed into the long-term experience vector store for subsequent retrieval (Omega_process step 4: vector store updating).
- **write back trigger**:
> on-success-and-failure (reflective, validated): experiences are distilled from successful, failed, AND comparative success/failure trajectory pairs, then passed through an LLM-based experience-validation step before being written. Writes are gated by quality/reliability validation rather than success-only.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success + failure: experiences are distilled from successful, unsuccessful, and comparative (success-vs-failure) trajectory pairs. Failed cases yield corrective insights (e.g., the AppWorld example: 'always verify an API's existence/behavior via apis.api_docs.show_api_doc before executing critical actions'). Both positive and negative experiences inform the 'Content' guidance.
- **retrieval as learned policy**: No. Case/experience selection is a fixed cosine-similarity top-k (k=5) with LLM re-ranking, not a learned/RL-optimized retrieval policy. (The agent's action policy is RL-trained, but the retriever is not.)
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**: Single-agent private memory in the reported experiments (one policy's experience pool). The experience pool aggregates the agent's own cross-task experiences but is not shared across heterogeneous agents/frameworks. (Multi-agent co-evolution is listed only as future work.)

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**: AppWorld; BFCL v3 (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard v3, multi-turn split only).
- **benchmark family**: tool / tool-augmented long-horizon agent benchmarks (AppWorld = app/API task completion; BFCL v3 = multi-turn function-calling). Both are tool/API-use benchmarks under sparse terminal rewards.
- **baselines**:
> Vanilla GRPO (standard sparse outcome-only RL, deepseek_math GRPO) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct backbones (zero-shot/Backbone also reported). Internal ablation baselines include: training on Original p_target data vs Synthetic p_train vs Hybrid; Navigating w/o selective boosting; Self-Attributing w/o r_attr and w/o r_out; LLM judge w/o principle / w/o reference solution.
- **key metrics**: Task Goal Completion (TGC) reported as avg@8 (mean TGC over 8 rollouts) and best@8 (best of 8); also avg@4/best@4 in some ablations. Efficiency metrics: Steps@.9 (steps to reach 90% of baseline best), Area Under Curve (AUC) of learning curves.
- **headline result**:
> Integrating all three mechanisms (AgentEvolver overall) on Qwen2.5-14B yields overall avg@8 of 57.6% (vs 29.8% backbone), i.e. +27.8% (AppWorld 48.7%, BFCL v3 66.5%), and best@8 73.1% (+30.3%). On Qwen2.5-7B, overall avg@8 improves +29.4% (15.8% -> 45.2%) and best@8 +36.1% (24.0% -> 60.1%).
- **ablations**:
> Extensive. Main table is itself ablative (Backbone -> +Questioning -> +Questioning&Navigating -> +Questioning&Attributing -> overall), showing self-questioning gives the largest single gain (7B 15.8%->36.1% avg@8). Self-questioning: synthetic p_train approaches human-curated p_target; hybrid p_hybrid surpasses original data; data-volume study (40.3% with 100 samples, diminishing returns at 200/500); cross-domain generalization (14B AppWorld->BFCL drops only 4.3%); LLM-judge ablation shows principle + reference solution are essential. Self-navigating: experience injection at inference +5.4% avg@4 / +6.7% best@4; implicit (RL-internalized) learning beats ICL-only (+34.2% avg@4) and vanilla RL (+7.9% avg@4); removing selective boosting drops below RL baseline (-0.5% avg@4, -2.9% best@4); eta=0.5 best exploration/exploitation balance; eps_hat_high=0.6 best short/long-term balance. Self-attributing: both r_attr and r_out channels needed (w/o r_out worse than w/o r_attr); alpha in [0.10,0.20] optimal; sample efficiency: reaches 90% of baseline best in 40 steps (AppWorld, baseline 90) and 20 steps (BFCL, baseline 60), 55%/67% reductions, higher AUC (46.26 vs 41.03 AppWorld; 61.02 vs 55.78 BFCL).
- **evaluation decoupling**: No. The work does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) separately. Experience retrieval is evaluated only through its downstream effect on task TGC and trajectory reward, not via standalone retrieval-quality metrics.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mixed. Final task TGC (outcome) is the primary metric, but the self-attributing mechanism explicitly introduces step-wise process-quality signals (LLM GOOD/BAD attribution per action) and the analysis discusses process correctness vs outcome effectiveness as two reward channels. Reported scores are outcome-oriented (TGC), while process quality is leveraged as a reward/credit-assignment signal rather than as a separately reported evaluation metric.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A — this is a method/system paper, not a survey.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A as a contributed benchmark, but note the self-questioning module synthesizes its own training tasks (LLM-synthesized via curiosity-guided exploration with environment profiles, e.g. queries with two entities/three attributes/three operations at 'hard' difficulty), filtered (lexical dedup threshold 0.8, real-time + post-generation filtering) and scored by an LLM judge (Qwen3-235B-A22B) with reference-solution-based correctness checks; ~100-500 synthetic samples used in volume studies. Evaluation uses existing benchmarks AppWorld and BFCL v3 (multi-turn).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> GRPO / DeepSeek-Math (deepseek_math) RL objective and simplified advantage estimation (undiscounted cumulative future reward); PPO/GRPO clipping; veRL (HybridFlow, sheng2024hybridflow) distributed RL infrastructure; ReMe (agentscope-ai/ReMe) for experience summarization/management; in-context learning for experience reuse; curiosity-driven / intrinsic-motivation exploration; goal-conditioned RL (universal value functions, schaul2015universal).
- **contrasts with**:
> Vanilla GRPO and PPO/GRPO-style agent RL that rely on massive random trajectory sampling and sparse trajectory-level (uniform) credit assignment; handcrafted Process Reward Models (PRMs) with rigid task-specific scoring (contrasted with the LLM GOOD/BAD attribution); workflow-based / human-engineered agent orchestration; RL methods requiring manually constructed task datasets; intrinsic-reward and UCB-bandit exploration strategies that are ineffective for long-horizon tool agents; explicit ICL-only experience use (shown to have a performance ceiling vs implicit RL internalization).
- **lineage**:
> Decision/Memory + RL lineage (group F_decision_memory_rl): a self-evolving agentic-RL system combining (a) growing experience memory with retrieval-augmented in-context guidance distilled from successful and failed trajectories (skills/tactics/failure notes), and (b) step-level credit assignment via LLM-based attribution, plus self-synthesized tasks. Sits at the intersection of experience-/case-based agent memory and RL-based agent training; positioned as an efficiency-oriented successor to GRPO-style agent RL that internalizes retrieved experience into the policy.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- context_budget_and_selection_count
- cost_efficiency_tradeoff
- memory_evolution_update
- online_growth
- venue

<a id="item-dynamic-cheatsheet"></a>
### 141. Dynamic Cheatsheet (DC): Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory

2025  ·  arXiv 2504.07952  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07952)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: EACL 2026 (main conference, long paper; ACL Anthology 2026.eacl-long.333). First released as arXiv:2504.07952 (cs.LG/cs.CL), Apr 2025.
- **authors affiliation**: Mirac Suzgun, Mert Yuksekgonul, Federico Bianchi, Dan Jurafsky, James Zou. Primary affiliation: Stanford University (James Zou Lab; Suzgun acknowledges an HAI-SAP Fellowship).
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.07952
- **code url**: https://github.com/suzgunmirac/dynamic-cheatsheet
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/suzgunmirac/dynamic-cheatsheet (actively maintained; last push 2026-03-12; 272 stars; MIT license; adds DynamicCheatsheet_CumulativeRetrieval hybrid variant and many new model providers beyond the v1 paper)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Reasoning / math / QA / code-via-tool-use / decision-making at inference time. Tasks span competition math (AIME), graduate-level science QA (GPQA-Diamond, MMLU-Pro), and heuristic-search arithmetic puzzles (Game of 24, Math Equation Balancer).
- **problem setting**:
> Online, test-time / inference-time learning for a black-box LLM over a stream of i.i.d. queries x1..xn ~ D_test, with NO ground-truth labels, NO human feedback, and NO weight updates. Single-agent (one black-box LM plays both Generator and Curator roles via different prompts). The model must self-assess correctness and decide what to store. Sequential processing (one query at a time, carrying an evolving memory M_i forward).
- **what is retrieved**:
> Self-curated reusable problem-solving artifacts: strategies, solution sketches, code snippets (e.g. a Python brute-force solver), heuristics, and general insights stored in an evolving text 'cheatsheet' memory. In the retrieval variant (DC-RS / DR), it retrieves past (input, model-generated output) pairs from previously seen examples.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING / episodic memory that the agent itself writes at test time. There is NO static external corpus, KB, or document index; the store is entirely induced online from the model's own past queries and self-curated solutions. (Explicitly contrasted with classic static-corpus RAG.)
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-k ranking in the retrieval variants (k=3 most similar past input-output pairs by cosine similarity). The cumulative variant (DC-Cu) has no ranking objective at all; the memory itself is the (single) reused artifact. No notion of recovering a complete minimal set or precision-driven variable-size selection.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> Retrieve (DC-RS/DR retrieve similar past cases), Reuse (Generator conditions on memory/retrieved cases), Revise (Curator distills/refines/prunes entries; can correct faulty heuristics), Retain (Curator writes distilled artifacts to memory). All four CBR phases are realized in DC-RS; DC-Cu covers Reuse/Revise/Retain without explicit similarity Retrieve. Flags: [Retrieve: yes (DC-RS/DR), Reuse: yes, Revise: yes, Retain: yes].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The work frames itself as 'test-time learning with adaptive memory' / 'persistent evolving memory' inspired by human cumulative learning and retrieval-practice (Karpicke & Roediger) and online learning; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner or call itself case-based reasoning, though DC-RS/DR realize CBR-like retrieve-reuse-revise-retain mechanics over (problem, solution) cases.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Case = (problem, model-generated solution) pair, i.e. past input-output examples (DC-RS / DR). The cumulative memory itself is a distilled set of strategy/heuristic/code-snippet entries (skill-or-program / guideline). Granularity: single past example (for retrieval) and distilled snippet/strategy (for the curated cheatsheet).
- **index source**: Growing memory, online/test-time-induced. The retrievable store of (x_j, y~_j) pairs and the curated cheatsheet are both built entirely at test time from the model's own stream of queries and self-generated solutions; nothing is induced offline and nothing is a static corpus.
- **index structure topology**: Flat. DC-RS uses a flat vector index over past query embeddings (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). The curated cheatsheet (DC-Cu) is a single flat free-text memory blob. Authors note hierarchical/modular memory and topological clustering only as future work, not implemented.
