### 150. ReMe (Remember Me, Refine Me): A Dynamic Procedural Memory Framework for Experience-Driven Agent Evolution

2025  ·  arXiv 2512.10696  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10696)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2025
- **venue**: ACL 2026 Findings (accepted; 'ACL'26-Findings' noted on arXiv). Preprint arXiv:2512.10696 (cs.AI / cs.CL), v1 submitted 11 Dec 2025, v2 last revised 15 Apr 2026.
- **authors affiliation**:
> Zouying Cao (lead; AGI Institute, School of Computer Science, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; work done during internship at Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group), Jiaji Deng, Li Yu, Weikang Zhou, Zhaoyang Liu (corresponding), Bolin Ding (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group), Hai Zhao (corresponding; Shanghai Jiao Tong University). Primary affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group. Contact: zouyingcao@sjtu.edu.cn, zhaohai@cs.sjtu.edu.cn.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.10696
- **code url**: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe (official; part of the AgentScope ecosystem, ~3.1k stars, 851 commits, actively maintained, last commit 2026-06-05). The paper also releases the reme.library procedural-memory dataset.
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/agentscope-ai/ReMe (continuously-updated open-source memory framework; supports personal / procedural / tool memory types, MCP client, and multiple agent backends such as AgentScope and the Claude Code SDK; broader than the frozen paper).

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**: Tool-use / function-calling and interactive coding agents (decision-making over multi-turn agentic tool execution). Framed as a procedural-memory system for LLM agents that internalizes 'how-to' knowledge to improve task-solving.
- **problem setting**:
> Single-agent, experience-driven self-evolution for LLM tool-use agents. The setting is two-phase: (1) an offline experience-acquisition phase where an execution agent interacts with the environment over a set of TRAINING tasks (50 BFCL-V3 base multi-turn tasks; 90 AppWorld train tasks), sampling N=8 trajectories per task at temperature 0.9 to obtain success/failure pairs, which a summarizer LLM distills into a structured experience pool; (2) a test-time reuse/refinement phase on held-out tasks (150 BFCL-V3 eval, 168 AppWorld test-normal) where relevant experiences are retrieved and injected, and the pool is optionally updated online (ReMe-dynamic vs ReMe-fixed). No gradient training of the agent or retriever; everything is LLM-driven in-context with frozen off-the-shelf embeddings. Backbones are swapped (Qwen3-8B/14B/32B-Instruct as both execution and summarizer LLM; plus GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Qwen3-Max-Preview, Kimi-K2-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7 for generalization). Task success uses environment ground truth (BFCL-V3 AST+execution checks; AppWorld state-based unit tests / Task Goal Completion). Contrasted against the 'passive accumulation' append-only memory paradigm.
- **what is retrieved**:
> Distilled, structured procedural experiences (not raw trajectories). Each experience E = <omega, e, kappa, c, tau> bundles a usage scenario omega (when to use it), the core experience content e, a set of categorization keywords kappa, a confidence score c in [0,1], and the set of tools tau used. Experiences come in three multi-faceted types: success patterns, failure-trigger lessons, and comparative insights distilled jointly from paired success/failure trajectories.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> GROWING / episodic self-written procedural memory (experience pool). ReMe maintains no static external doc/KB/API corpus; the retrievable store is an agent-written experience pool seeded offline from training-task trajectories and (in the dynamic variant) grown/pruned online at test time. Positioned explicitly against static append-only memory.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Fixed top-K ranking objective. Retrieval selects the top-K=5 most relevant experiences by cosine similarity over the usage-scenario embedding (then optional rerank/rewrite). There is no minimal-complete-set or variable-size precision-driven objective; the K-sweep (K=0..10) shows performance rising then saturating/declining with larger K (noise tradeoff), motivating moderate K.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: yes (top-K cosine retrieval over usage-scenario embeddings, plus optional LLM reranking); Reuse: yes (retrieved experiences injected as in-context demonstrations, with an adaptive rewriting module that reorganizes them into task-specific guidance); Revise: yes (context-adaptive rewriting adapts retrieved experiences to the new task; failure-aware reflection revises strategy after a failed attempt); Retain: yes (utility-based refinement: selective addition of validated successful experiences, failure-reflection-derived lessons on success, and utility-based pruning of stale entries)].
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper frames itself as a 'procedural memory' / 'experience-driven agent evolution' framework and positions against memory systems (A-Mem, LangMem, AWM, Agent KB, CER, Synapse, HiAgent). It does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not use the term 'case-based reasoning'; it realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain-like mechanisms under a memory-lifecycle framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> guideline/insight-level procedural experience (a distilled 'keypoint-level' experience), structured as E=<usage-scenario omega, core content e, keywords kappa, confidence c, tools tau>. It is finer-grained than a full trajectory or whole-trajectory workflow: a reusable success pattern, failure-trigger lesson, or comparative insight. The granularity ablation explicitly contrasts this keypoint-level unit against a trajectory-level unit.
- **index source**:
> Hybrid offline-then-online growing memory. The pool is offline-induced from training-task exploration trajectories (experience acquisition), then for ReMe(dynamic) is online/test-time-induced: validated successful experiences are added and low-utility ones pruned during deployment. ReMe(fixed) freezes the pool after offline induction. Stored in a vector database.
- **index structure topology**:
> Flat dense vector index. Each retained experience is indexed by the embedding vector of its usage-scenario field omega and stored in a vector database (experience pool); retrieval is nearest-neighbor by cosine similarity. Keywords kappa support categorization/metadata. No explicit dependency/knowledge graph or hierarchical category tree is used for the procedural pool (the broader open-source framework adds personal/tool memory types, but the paper's procedural pool is a flat scenario-keyed vector index).
- **retriever type**:
> Dense (embedding-based) retriever using cosine similarity over usage-scenario embeddings, plus an OPTIONAL LLM-as-reranker stage (LLM_rerank). Embeddings come from an off-the-shelf text embedding model (text-embedding-v4, dim 1024, in main experiments; Qwen3-Embedding cited as an alternative). No BM25 and no learned/generative retriever; the only learned component used at selection time is the LLM reranker (zero-shot prompted, not trained).
- **retriever learning signal**:
> none (off-the-shelf). The dense retriever uses a frozen pretrained embedding model (text-embedding-v4 / Qwen3-Embedding) with cosine similarity; there is no contrastive fine-tuning, LM-feedback retriever training, or RL/value-based retrieval learning. The closest thing to a downstream-effectiveness signal is the separate utility-based DELETION mechanism (tracks per-experience recall-to-success utility u/f and prunes below threshold beta), but this prunes the store rather than training the retriever.
- **query construction**:
> Raw current-task query embedded with the same embedding model and matched against experience usage-scenario embeddings. The retrieval-key ablation shows the STORED key is an LLM-generated 'usage scenario' field (omega), which outperforms indexing by raw task description, generalized query, or extracted query keywords. So query construction = raw task query on the read side; the value-add is LLM-generated scenario indexing on the write/key side.
- **query granularity**:
> Task-level (one-shot at t=0). Retrieval is performed once at the beginning of each task to fetch the top-K experiences; not per-CoT-step or per-tool-call. The Limitations section explicitly notes the fixed once-per-task retrieval as a constraint, suggesting future context-aware re-retrieval.
- **when to retrieve**:
> One-shot per task. Experiences are retrieved exactly once at the start of each task (matched for all methods for fair comparison). No iterative, uncertainty-triggered, or learned-router re-retrieval within a task. (The dynamic variant updates the POOL after task execution, but does not re-retrieve mid-task.)
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> Fixed schedule. Retrieval is triggered unconditionally once at the beginning of each new task. There is no token-confidence, attention/uncertainty, learned complexity classifier, reflection-token, or agent-initiated mid-step retrieval trigger. (The failure-aware reflection that re-triggers a new trial is a refinement/re-execution trigger, not a re-retrieval trigger.)
- **reranking**:
> Yes (optional). After dense top-K retrieval, an optional context-aware LLM reranker (LLM_rerank) re-evaluates experience relevance against the current task's specific context, constraints, and objectives, bringing the most pertinent experiences to the front. It is a zero-shot LLM-as-reranker (instruction-prompted), not a trained cross-encoder or RRF. Ablation (Table 4, Qwen3-8B, BFCL-V3): +ReMe 27.17 Avg@4/34.66 Pass@4 -> +rerank 28.91/36.67; rerank+rewrite together reach 29.00/40.67.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> Rerank + adaptive rewrite (decompose-then-recompose into task-specific guidance). Beyond optional reranking, a rewriting module reorganizes the multiple retrieved experiences into a single cohesive, task-specific guidance more directly applicable to the new task. This is post-retrieval refinement of the fetched set (not compression/distractor-filtering per se). Write-time refinement (multi-faceted distillation, LLM-as-Judge validation, similarity-based dedup) also reduces noise before items enter the pool.
- **tool document engineering**: N/A. ReMe retrieves distilled procedural experiences, not tool/API descriptions, so there is no tool-docstring indexing pipeline. (Each experience records the tools tau it used, but tools are not the retrievable items.)
- **index content separation**: Partial. Each experience separates a lightweight retrievable key (the usage-scenario embedding omega + keywords kappa) from the heavier core content e injected on use, but there is no explicit progressive-disclosure / index-then-load-content mechanism for the procedural pool.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A. ReMe does not model inter-tool dependencies (it is an experience/procedural-memory method, not a tool-retrieval method). Experiences record which tools tau were used but do not encode tool dependency graphs.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Prompt augmentation (in-context demonstrations). The top-K retrieved (and reranked) experiences are rewritten into task-specific guidance and concatenated into the execution agent's context as in-context-learning demonstrations to guide reasoning and tool calls. No fine-tuning and no latent-token injection; everything is in-context.
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-plan, one-shot at task start. Relevant experiences are retrieved once and injected before the agent begins its multi-turn ReAct-style tool-use rollout, acting as one-shot strategic exemplars/guidance for the whole task. Not interleaved per-step, not inside MCTS/tree search. A failure-aware reflection loop (max 3 self-reflections) can re-execute a failed task with extracted lessons, which is a retry/refinement loop on top of the plan.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**: Per-task / per-answer. Retrieval and experience injection happen once before the agent's rollout and remain fixed for that task; not per-CoT-step, per-token, or per-tool-call.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> LLM-prompted adaptation plus execution-feedback-driven revision: (1) the rewriting module (LLM) reorganizes retrieved experiences into cohesive task-specific guidance (context-adaptive reuse); (2) the failure-aware reflection mechanism (LLM_summ analyzes a failed attempt, extracts improvement lessons, then LLM_execute starts a new trial on those lessons; lessons retained only if the retry succeeds, max 3 reflections). Not verbatim ICL, not RL reuse-finetuning, not latent.
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Distilled structured experience injected as free-text guidance: a structured record (usage scenario, core content, keywords, confidence, tools) that the rewriting module turns into cohesive task-specific natural-language guidance. Not raw trajectories, executable programs, or latent/soft tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled strategy / state-aware guideline (keypoint-level). Above a raw logged trajectory: reusable success patterns, failure-trigger lessons, and comparative insights, each tagged with a usage scenario stating WHEN to apply it. The granularity ablation shows this keypoint-level abstraction substantially outperforms trajectory-level experiences (Table 2).
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> (1) LLM-as-a-Judge validation filters out non-actionable/inaccurate experiences before storage; (2) similarity-based cosine deduplication discards redundant experiences to preserve diversity; (3) multi-faceted distillation (success/failure/comparative) yields fine-grained keypoint experiences rather than noisy raw trajectories; (4) optional LLM reranking selects the most contextually relevant experiences; (5) utility-based deletion prunes frequently-retrieved-but-unhelpful (toxic) experiences (u/f <= beta after >= alpha retrievals); (6) selective addition (success-only at test time) avoids low-quality single-failure experiences; (7) moderate K=5 limits noisy-experience injection. No retriever-aware contrastive training.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Procedural memory (experience pool / skill-like reusable how-to knowledge), realized as a flat scenario-keyed vector store of distilled experiences. Not parametric, not a knowledge graph, not latent. (The broader framework also supports personal and tool memory types, but the paper studies procedural memory.)
- **write back**:
> Yes. New validated experiences are written into the pool. Offline: multi-faceted distillation of training trajectories -> LLM-as-Judge validation -> dedup -> store, indexed by usage-scenario embedding. Online (ReMe-dynamic): selective addition of experiences from newly successful trajectories and from successful failure-reflection retries; plus utility-based deletion of stale entries. Closed loop: distill -> validate -> dedup -> store -> reuse -> track utility -> prune.
- **online growth**:
> Yes for ReMe(dynamic): the pool grows (selective addition) and shrinks (utility-based deletion) during deployment as tasks are executed. ReMe(fixed) freezes the pool after offline induction (the fixed-vs-dynamic comparison is a core contribution; dynamic consistently outperforms fixed across all model sizes and benchmarks).
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success (selective addition) plus reflective on failure with success-gating. The paper compares full addition (add from all trajectories regardless of outcome) vs selective addition (add only from successful trajectories) and finds selective addition superior because a single test-time failed trajectory gives insufficient context for reliable failure analysis. A failure-aware reflection branch lets the agent retry a failed task; the derived lessons are written back ONLY if the retry succeeds, otherwise discarded. Initial offline pool also draws failure/comparative experiences (from collectively analyzed failures). Validation (LLM-as-Judge) and dedup gate every write.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success+failure contrastive, with asymmetric handling. During OFFLINE acquisition, ReMe uses multi-faceted distillation: success-pattern recognition, failure analysis (failure-trigger lessons identifying the earliest key step leading to suboptimal outcomes), and comparative insight generation from paired highest/lowest-reward trajectories. During ONLINE refinement, however, failure experiences are NOT directly added (selective/success-only addition); instead failures trigger a self-reflection retry loop and lessons are kept only upon subsequent success. So failures are used contrastively/correctively but gated to avoid toxic single-failure noise.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Refine-and-prune: selective append of validated successful experiences (with similarity-based dedup-merge to avoid redundancy) plus utility-based forget/prune of low-utility entries. ReMe tracks per-experience total retrievals f and historical utility u (u increments when a recall contributes to a successful task); an experience is removed when, after >= alpha=5 retrievals, u/f <= beta=0.5. Not append-only; combines dedup-merge and forget-prune. (Individual stored experiences are not rewritten in place after storage; evolution is at the pool level via add/dedup/delete plus the test-time rewriting that adapts them on use.)
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No. Experience selection is fixed cosine-similarity top-K over frozen embeddings, with an optional zero-shot LLM reranker; it is not an RL- or value-trained retrieval policy. Utility tracking (u/f) drives pool PRUNING, not a learned retrieval policy. (This is an explicit contrast with M-MDP/soft-Q or RL-retrieval methods such as Memento/ARTIST-style learned case selection.)

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> BFCL-V3 (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard V3; >1,800 test tasks for multi-turn/multi-step function calling; AST matching + executable testing; ReMe uses 50 base multi-turn tasks for the initial pool and 150 for evaluation; full multi-turn category = 750 tasks split Base 150 / Miss Param 200 / Miss Func 200 / Long Context 200) and AppWorld (controllable world of 9 apps, 457 APIs, ~100 simulated users; state-based unit tests; ReMe uses 90 train tasks and 168 test-normal tasks; reports Task Goal Completion). Backbones: Qwen3-8B/14B/32B-Instruct (main), plus GPT-4.1, o4-mini, Qwen3-Max-Preview, Kimi-K2-Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-4.7 (generalization on BFCL-V3).
- **benchmark family**: tool (function-calling / interactive coding agents): BFCL-V3 = tool / function-calling (ToolBench-adjacent agentic tool-use), AppWorld = tool + code (interactive coding agent over app APIs). No QA, web, embodied, memory-conversation, or decision-RL benchmarks.
- **baselines**:
> No Memory (vanilla backbone, no memory mechanism); A-Mem (Xu et al. 2025; agentic memory / memory-centric knowledge graph, reproduced with slight prompt modifications to extract procedural memories); LangMem (LangChain 2025; long-term episodic memory module that extracts info from conversations and refines prompts). Two ReMe variants are reported: ReMe(fixed) (frozen pool) and ReMe(dynamic) (online refinement). For fairness all methods retrieve once per task start and add memory only on successful trajectories.
- **key metrics**:
> Avg@4 (average task success rate over 4 independent trials) and Pass@4 (probability >=1 of 4 trials succeeds); all results averaged over 3 independent runs with standard deviation. For AppWorld the underlying metric is Task Goal Completion (TGC); for BFCL-V3, AST + executable correctness. Efficiency: average inference latency per task. Error analysis: failure-case counts by error category (Reasoning Error, Action Omission, etc.).
- **headline result**:
> ReMe sets new SOTA agent-memory results on BFCL-V3 and AppWorld and shows a memory-scaling effect: Qwen3-8B + ReMe(dynamic) outperforms larger memoryless Qwen3-14B (avg Pass@4 55.03% vs 54.65%; and Qwen3-8B + ReMe(dynamic) average Avg@4 34.94 / Pass@4 55.03 vs No-Memory 27.65 / 46.20). Reported headline gains for Qwen3-8B + ReMe over No Memory: +8.83% Avg@4 and +7.29% Pass@4 on average across BFCL-V3+AppWorld. On Qwen3-14B, ReMe(dynamic) avg Avg@4 44.66 / Pass@4 63.71 exceeds memoryless Qwen3-32B (40.89 / 61.52).
- **ablations**:
> (1) Granularity (Table 2): keypoint-level experiences vs trajectory-level: Qwen3-8B 44.50/65.77 vs 43.00/60.00 Avg@4/Pass@4; Qwen3-14B 51.89/72.44 vs 49.66/69.33; keypoint-level gives substantially larger gains over No Memory. (2) Component (Table 3, Qwen3-8B BFCL-V3): full addition 40.83/62.00 -> selective addition 44.33/64.66 (+3.50/+2.66) -> +failure-aware reflection 45.00/64.66 -> +utility-based deletion 45.17/68.00; quality>quantity, and pruning matters in non-stationary settings. (3) Rerank/Rewrite (Table 4, Qwen3-8B no-thinking): +ReMe 27.17/34.66 -> +rerank 28.91/36.67, +rewrite 28.67/37.33, both 29.00/40.67. (4) Retrieval-key (Fig 4 / Table 8-style): usage-scenario indexing best, beating raw task query / generalized query / query keywords (Qwen3-8B usage scenario 44.50/65.77). (5) Summarizer scaling (Table 5): stronger LLM_summ (8B->32B, fixed 8B executor) lifts Avg@4 +1.83%->+3.33%, Pass@4 +0.23%->+2.23%. (6) Effect of K (Fig 5): performance rises then saturates, K=5 chosen. (7) Error analysis (Fig 6): failures 62->47, corrects 17 baseline errors / introduces 2, Reasoning Errors 22->14.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No. ReMe reports only end-to-end task metrics (Avg@4/Pass@4 success rates) and does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG/completeness) for the experience retriever. Retrieval design is studied via downstream task accuracy in the retrieval-key and K-number ablations rather than via decoupled IR metrics.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Primarily outcome-based (task success Avg@4/Pass@4). A qualitative process analysis is provided via the error-type breakdown (Reasoning Error, Action Omission, etc.) showing where ReMe reduces failures, and case studies/experience examples, but no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality score is reported.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Reported as favorable. On AppWorld, average inference latency per task: No Memory 21.42s vs +ReMe 23.96s (+2.54s), deemed an acceptable overhead. The headline efficiency claim is the memory-scaling effect: a smaller model + ReMe matches/exceeds a larger memoryless model, framed as a computation-efficient pathway to lifelong learning. No token-count or API-cost table is reported. Acquisition cost: N=8 trajectory samples per training task and up to 3 self-reflection retries per failed task.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Fixed top-K=5 retrieved experiences per task (after optional reranking and rewriting into a single cohesive guidance block). K is fixed (not adaptive/precision-driven); the K=0..10 sweep shows saturation, justifying K=5. Agent rollout capped at max 30 iterations; self-reflection capped at 3. No explicit injected-token budget is reported.
- **survey scope and axes**: N/A (ReMe is a method/framework, not a survey).

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Procedural/experience memory for agents: ExpEL (experiential learners), Reflexion (verbal self-reflection retry, cited for the max-3 reflections choice), Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), Agent KB (cross-domain experience, teacher-student dual retrieval), CER (Contextual Experience Replay, fine-grained skills), Synapse and HiAgent (trajectory-as-exemplar memory). Uses LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng et al. 2023) for validation, Qwen3 models, and off-the-shelf embeddings (text-embedding-v4 / Qwen3-Embedding). Builds on the experience-following-behavior study (Xiong et al. 2025) for utility-based deletion thresholds.
- **contrasts with**:
> Static 'passive accumulation' append-only memory systems: A-Mem and LangMem (its main empirical baselines), and trajectory-level / whole-trajectory-workflow memory (Synapse, HiAgent, AWM, Agent KB, CER) which store coarse experiences without adaptation or timely pruning. ReMe contrasts by (a) keypoint-level multi-faceted distillation vs raw/whole-trajectory storage, (b) context-adaptive reuse (rerank+rewrite) vs unadapted injection, and (c) utility-based refinement (add valid, prune stale) vs append-only growth.
- **lineage**:
> Group F (decision/experience/procedural memory for self-evolving agents). A 2025-2026 dynamic-procedural-memory work in the lineage of experience-learning agents (Reflexion -> ExpEL -> AWM / Agent KB / CER) that extends them with a closed-loop, utility-driven, self-pruning memory lifecycle; a non-RL, in-context experience-reuse method (contrast with RL-policy case-selection lines such as Memento).

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- benchmark_construction_and_size
- cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing
- dynamic_index_and_protocol

<a id="item-trace2skill"></a>
### 151. Trace2Skill: Distill Trajectory-Local Lessons into Transferable Agent Skills

2026  ·  arXiv:2603.25158 (2026-03, verified)  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25158)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2026
- **authors affiliation**:
> Jingwei Ni (lead/core contributor; ETH Zurich and University of Zurich), Yihao Liu (core; Peking University), Xinpeng Liu (core; Peking University), Yutao Sun (core; Zhejiang University) [these four marked as core contributors / equal contribution], Mengyu Zhou (corresponding author; zhoumengyu.zmy@alibaba-inc.com), Pengyu Cheng, Dexin Wang, Erchao Zhao, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang. Primary affiliation: Qwen Large Model Application Team, Alibaba; academic collaborators at ETH Zurich / University of Zurich, Peking University, and Zhejiang University.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25158
- **code url**: https://github.com/Qwen-Applications/Trace2Skill (Apache-2.0; official codebase; releases the top spreadsheet skills and the spreadsheet evolution pipeline; ~107 stars at time of access)
- **maintained repo url**: https://github.com/Qwen-Applications/Trace2Skill (releases evolved xlsx skills under released_skills/: trace2skill-xlsx-35B-combined, xlsx-35B, trace2skill-xlsx-122B-combined, xlsx-122B; no leaderboard/paper-list maintained)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> LLM-agent tool-use / file-and-office workflows (spreadsheet/xlsx editing on SpreadsheetBench, plus PDF, DOCX, PPTX document agents), math reasoning (DAPO, AIME), and vision/document QA (DocVQA). Core focus is agentic file-manipulation 'skill' creation and deepening, with table-QA (WikiTableQuestions, HiTab) as OOD transfer.
- **problem setting**:
> Offline, single-agent skill evolution with binary correctness supervision on an evolving set, but no gradient updates. A fixed (frozen-weight) LLM agent pi_theta runs a ReAct-style harness (with bash + Python file tools) using an initial skill S0 over a disjoint evolving set D_evolve to collect labeled success/failure trajectories; an offline pipeline then turns these traces into an improved skill S* = E(S0, D_evolve; pi_theta) such that pass rate on a held-out D_test improves, WITHOUT updating model parameters theta and WITHOUT any test-time retrieval. Two regimes: Skill Deepening (start from a human-written skill, e.g. Anthropic's official xlsx skill) and Skill Creation (start from a weak LLM-generated parametric draft, or No Skill for math/VQA). 100% self-evolution: the same model is trajectory generator, analyst, and merge operator (no external teacher). The setting is single-agent at deployment, but uses many parallel analyst sub-agents during the offline evolution stage (128 sub-agents in parallel in the main spreadsheet runs).
- **what is retrieved**:
> Nothing is retrieved at test time. Trace2Skill is explicitly retrieval-free at inference: the consolidated skill (a SKILL.md directory + references/) is loaded unchanged. During the OFFLINE evolution stage, the system consolidates execution trajectories (successes and failures) into trajectory-level skill patches / distilled lessons that are merged into one skill. So the 'consumed' items are agent execution traces (and the lessons / SoPs distilled from them); the produced/used artifact is a static skill document, not retrieved memory items.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> Offline-induced GROWING-into-STATIC: the source of evidence is a growing pool of the agent's own episodic trajectories (self-written experience), but Trace2Skill compresses them once, offline, into a STATIC skill directory used at inference with no retrieval. There is no static external corpus/KB/API and no live test-time memory store. (Its compared baseline ReasoningBank instead keeps a growing retrievable memory queried at test time; Trace2Skill deliberately avoids that.)
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> Not a top-k ranking objective. The objective is to consolidate the COMPLETE pool of trajectory-level patches into one coherent skill (default '+Combined' / full aggregation applies all consolidated patches), preferring prevalent recurring patterns and discarding idiosyncratic ones. The paper shows patch value is COMBINATORIAL (greedy top-1 selection plateaus below full aggregation; side-effects flip previously-correct tasks), motivating holistic consolidation over greedy/precision-driven subset selection. An optional Bayesian-optimization patch-subset selector is studied but is not the default.
- **cbr cycle coverage**:
> [Retrieve: no (no test-time case retrieval; offline it 'retrieves'/collects trajectories but not for nearest-neighbor reuse), Reuse: yes (the consolidated skill/SoPs are reused at inference, loaded directly), Revise: yes (offline patch proposal + agentic fix-validation + hierarchical merge revise the skill; the error analyst writes and re-evaluates a minimal fix), Retain: yes (consolidated patches are written/retained once into the static skill directory)]. It realizes Reuse/Revise/Retain offline but deliberately omits test-time Retrieve, which is its key contrast with CBR/retrieval-memory systems.
- **explicit cbr grounding**:
> False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames the consolidation as INDUCTIVE reasoning over agent experience (citing inductive-reasoning works) and positions itself within 'agent skills' and 'experience memory for agent self-evolution' literatures. It realizes CBR-like Reuse/Revise/Retain mechanisms under a skill-evolution framing.

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> Offline unit consumed: a full execution trajectory tau_i (query + reasoning/tool-use history + final output + binary correctness). Offline unit produced: a trajectory-level skill patch (a diff-style edit proposing additions to SKILL.md / references), and after merging, a guideline-rule / Standard-Operating-Procedure (SoP) section in a skill directory. At inference the 'unit' loaded is the whole skill document (SKILL.md + auxiliary references), not a retrieved snippet.
- **index source**:
> Offline-induced static store. The skill is built once from evolving-set trajectories (Stage 1 trajectory generation -> Stage 2 parallel patch proposal -> Stage 3 hierarchical consolidation) and then frozen; it does NOT grow at test time. Trajectory corpus is itself growing/episodic during collection but the final retrievable/usable artifact is a fixed skill directory.
- **index structure topology**:
> Hierarchical human-readable skill DIRECTORY: a root SKILL.md holding broadly-applicable procedural SoPs, plus a references/ folder of on-demand auxiliary files/scripts/assets for lower-frequency, niche details (e.g., 13 supplementary reference files in the 122B Deepening run for edge cases like cell-color extraction). General-to-specific organization recovered automatically from trajectory evidence. No vector index, no embedding store (in the default method). The merge itself is a hierarchical (tree) reduction over patches (L = ceil(log_{B_merge}|P|) levels, B_merge=32).
- **retriever type**:
> N/A for the proposed method at inference (no retriever; skill loaded directly). For the offline pipeline, an LLM acts as analyst/merge operator rather than a similarity retriever. The compared ReasoningBank-style baseline uses a dense retriever (Qwen3-Embedding-8B, top-1 memory), and the reproduced XSkill baseline uses lexical overlap top-3 (or Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B), but these are baselines, not Trace2Skill.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> N/A (no learned retriever in Trace2Skill). Patch generation and consolidation are LLM-prompted (off-the-shelf frozen LLM as analyst/merge operator); selection of which patches to keep is by prevalence/coverage heuristics or, optionally, validation-pass-rate-guided Bayesian optimization (downstream-task-effectiveness signal), not a trained retrieval model. No contrastive/RL retriever training.
- **query construction**:
> N/A at inference (no query; the static skill is prepended to the agent context). Offline, the 'query' analog is each individual trajectory fed to an analyst: error trajectories go to an agentic error analyst that inspects artifacts, compares against ground truth, and validates a minimal fix; success trajectories go to a single-pass success analyst that extracts generalizable behavior patterns. Merge operator is given the initial skill S0 plus a batch of patches.
- **query granularity**: Offline analysis is trajectory-level (one patch proposed per trajectory). At inference there is no per-step or per-task query construction; the consolidated skill is loaded once and used throughout the episode.
- **when to retrieve**:
> one-shot / never (test time): no retrieval is performed during inference; the evolved skill is loaded once at the start. Offline consolidation is itself a one-shot parallel batch process (not iterative online editing): all analysts run in a single parallel round, followed by ~2 hierarchical merge rounds (~3 sequential LLM-call rounds total).
- **retrieval trigger signal**: N/A (no test-time retrieval trigger). The skill is always loaded (fixed schedule, prepended to context). Offline patch proposal is triggered per collected trajectory; the write/merge into the skill is triggered by the consolidation stage over the full patch pool.
- **reranking**:
> No retrieval reranking. The closest analog is the merge operator M, which deduplicates patches, resolves conflicts, prefers prevalent/recurring patterns, and discards idiosyncratic edits during hierarchical consolidation (i.e., quality-prioritization of patches), plus deterministic diff-application guardrails (reject edits to missing files, withhold line-range conflicts, validate skill format). Optional Bayesian-optimization subset selection can be seen as a post-hoc patch reranking/selection but is not default.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> The consolidation IS the refinement: many trajectory-local patches are distilled, deduplicated, conflict-resolved, and merged into compact SoPs; idiosyncratic/low-support observations are routed to on-demand references/ files rather than the main SKILL.md (progressive disclosure). Failures that cannot be causally explained are excluded so the patch pool is grounded in verified failure mechanisms (distractor/noise filtering). No test-time context compression because there is no retrieval.
- **tool document engineering**:
> Partially applicable: the learned skill is essentially engineered TOOL/PROCEDURE documentation distilled from execution traces. Skill writing follows Anthropic skill-creator guidance; recurring lessons become concise actionable SoPs with explicit tool-selection guidance (e.g., 'use openpyxl for write-back, not pandas.to_excel(); copy input file first'), deterministic helper scripts (recalc.py), and a general-to-specific layout (SKILL.md for universal rules, references/ for edge cases). Not embedding-based tool-doc augmentation; it is LLM-induced procedural documentation grounded in trajectories.
- **index content separation**:
> Yes (progressive disclosure / on-demand references). The root SKILL.md holds broadly-reusable procedures while low-support/niche details are routed to references/ files loaded on demand (e.g., 13 supplementary reference files in the 122B Deepening run). The agent still procedurally discovers referenced resources/scripts that are not preloaded, mirroring standard skill-loading lightweight-index-then-content practice; Trace2Skill recovers this hierarchy automatically from trajectory evidence.
- **dynamic index and protocol**: N/A (no live tool registry / MCP / RapidAPI / RESTful index). The agent uses a ReAct harness with bash + Python (command-line tools, openpyxl, etc.) over local files; the skill is a static directory, not a synchronized external tool index.
- **tool dependency awareness**:
> N/A (no inter-tool dependency graph). The learned SoPs do encode procedural ordering/safety constraints (e.g., run recalc.py after formula writes then read back; delete rows in descending order to avoid index-shift corruption; copy input workbook before editing), which are workflow prerequisites rather than a modeled tool-dependency retrieval graph.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> Skill reuse via prompt augmentation: the consolidated SKILL.md is prepended/loaded into the agent's context at inference and used unchanged; auxiliary references/scripts are discovered procedurally on demand. No fine-tuning (theta is frozen), no latent-token injection, no test-time retrieval. The skill encodes reusable procedures (SoPs), guardrails, and tool-selection guidance that steer the ReAct agent's behavior.
- **planning integration**:
> Retrieve-then-plan in the loose sense of load-skill-then-act: the static skill is provided up front and the frozen agent runs a ReAct (reason-act-observe) loop with bash/Python tools (up to 100 turns) using that fixed skill context for the whole episode. The skill itself encodes plan-time procedures (e.g., 'explore workbook structure before editing', 'run recalc.py after formula writes, then read back'). No MCTS/tree search and no per-step re-retrieval at inference. The offline pipeline (collect -> analyze -> merge) is a separate hierarchical consolidation, not in-loop planning.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**:
> Per-episode at inference (skill loaded once, fixed across the multi-turn ReAct rollout); no per-step/per-token/per-tool-call retrieval interleaving. Offline, analysis is per-trajectory and merging is hierarchical (multi-level reduction), but these are not interleaved with test-time reasoning.
- **adaptation mechanism**:
> Execution-feedback-driven, agentic revision plus LLM-prompted inductive generalization. The error analyst (A-) runs a ReAct loop that inspects artifacts, compares to ground truth, and validates a minimal fix before proposing a patch (execution-feedback-driven revision); the success analyst (A+) does single-pass pattern abstraction; the merge operator M performs inductive generalization (prefer prevalent patterns, discard idiosyncratic). The adapted artifact (skill) is then reused verbatim at inference (no per-case test-time adaptation, no RL reuse-finetuning).
- **retrieved item representation**:
> Free-text / structured skill document: a human-readable SKILL.md of distilled procedural SoPs and guardrails (e.g., 'CRITICAL WARNING: run recalc.py after formula writes', 'prefer openpyxl over pandas.to_excel()', 'delete rows in descending order'), plus references/ files and deterministic scripts (e.g., recalc.py). Intermediate patches are diff-style JSON edits translated to unified diffs. Not raw trajectories, not latent tokens.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> Distilled, reusable procedural skill / Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs). Many-to-one merging keeps operations that recur across trajectories and turns them into general principles rather than one-off, trajectory-specific tips; the paper frames consolidation as an INDUCTIVE generalization step over agent experience. Concretely, the 122B Deepening +Combined run's 323 patches coalesce into a few dominant SoPs (recalculation+read-back 55.1%, openpyxl-over-pandas 54.8%, explicit read-back verification 42.7%, structural-edit safety 16.4%).
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> (1) Agentic error analysis grounds patches in VERIFIED failure mechanisms: the error analyst inspects artifacts, compares against ground truth, and validates a minimal fix before proposing a patch; failures it cannot causally explain are excluded, reducing log-only false positives (parse-error mis-attribution drops from 57% for log-only LLM to 14% for the agentic analyst). (2) Prevalent-pattern bias in the merge operator: edits recurring across independent trajectories are kept as systematic SoPs while idiosyncratic edits are discarded. (3) Deterministic diff guardrails: reject edits to missing files, withhold line-range conflicts, validate skill format. (4) Niche/low-support observations routed to references/ instead of polluting SKILL.md. (5) A training-set validation step (selecting the best-of-3-seeds evolved skill that does not hurt training-set performance) guards against hallucinated harmful edits.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> procedural / skill-library (a static skill directory of SoPs). It is NOT an episodic test-time memory and NOT a retrieval index; the paper positions itself against experience-memory / retrieval-memory systems (Reflexion, Voyager, ReasoningBank, Memp, AWM, CER) by distilling many local observations into one static skill directory used without nearest-neighbor reuse.
- **write back**: Yes, but OFFLINE one-shot, not online: trajectories are analyzed into patches and the patches are consolidated and written once into the skill directory (replacing S0 with S*). There is no continuous write-back into a memory during deployment; after evolution the skill is frozen.
- **online growth**:
> No. The skill does not grow at test time; it is induced once offline from the evolving set and then frozen. The paper explicitly contrasts this with online/sequential editing and with test-time-growing retrieval memories. (Trajectory collection grows the trace pool, but only during the offline evolution stage.)
- **write back trigger**:
> On-success-and-failure, offline batch (not per-step, not test-time). All evolving-set trajectories are labeled success/failure; +Error consolidates failures only, +Success consolidates successes only, +Combined consolidates both. Writing is a single consolidation event over the whole patch pool, applied via diff edits with deterministic guardrails, then optionally validated/selected on a held-out-from-test validation slice. Not human-validated per item (fully self-evolved) though qualitative SoP audits were done by the authors.
- **failure experience usage**:
> Success + failure, with an asymmetric design and a dedicated failure pathway. Failed trajectories drive an agentic error analyst (A-) that produces verified causal failure-cause items and corrective guardrails/SoPs (e.g., row-deletion safety, formula recalculation); successful trajectories drive a single-pass success analyst (A+) extracting reusable behavior patterns. +Error is often the most stable/transferable signal (e.g., strongest in math; cleanest cross-model transfer), and +Combined usually gives the largest Avg gain on spreadsheets and DocVQA. Failures that cannot be causally explained are dropped (grounded failure use, not log-only guesses).
- **memory evolution update**:
> Refine-overwrite-by-consolidation (offline, one-shot): patches are deduplicated, conflict-resolved, and synthesized into general principles; the consolidated patch p* replaces/edits S0 to produce S*. Default applies ALL consolidated patches (no pruning). It is NOT append-only online editing; the paper shows parallel many-to-one consolidation beats order-dependent sequential editing (Seq-B=1 / Seq-B=4) in both quality (on most 122B metrics) and wall-clock (~3 min vs 15 min / 60 min). After evolution the skill is static (no further mutation).
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> No. The default method has no learned/RL retrieval or selection policy; consolidation is LLM-prompted with prevalence/coverage heuristics. The optional patch-subset selectors (greedy top-1; Bayesian optimization with a TPE acquisition over binary inclusion vectors, validation-pass-rate objective) are search-based selection over patches, not a learned retrieval policy, and are non-default due to validation cost.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Yes - a central claim is cross-MODEL and cross-FAMILY portability of the learned skill artifact (not online memory sharing). Skills evolved from one model's traces transfer to other model scales (e.g., 35B-authored skill improves 122B), across families (Gemma-4-31B-it, GPT-5.5-high author and consume skills; Qwen->Gemma->GPT cross-model trace induction), and to OOD tasks. Because the artifact is a portable skill file, it can be loaded by heterogeneous agents/frameworks without parameter updates or retrieval. Headline: skills evolved from Qwen3.5-35B traces improve a Qwen3.5-122B agent by up to +57.65 pp on WikiTableQuestions.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> Primary: SpreadsheetBench-Verified (400 samples split 200 evolve / 200 held-out test; also full SpreadsheetBench Soft/Hard on 2,529 examples with evolving-set removed). OOD table-QA transfer: WikiTableQuestions (2,810 examples, converted to spreadsheet tasks) and HiTab (1,585 examples). Math: DAPO-Math (400 evolve, 100 held-out test) and AIME 2026 (avg@8 over 30 problems, OOD). Vision/Doc QA: DocVQA (50 examples for evolution, 5,299 held-out test; ANLS and Acc=ANLS>=0.5). Broader document agents: PDF (VRDU Registration Forms -> VAREX Flat), PPTX (TSBench / Talk-to-Your-Slides, deck-disjoint OOD split), DOCX (generated tasks -> OfficeBench DOCX, 64 subtasks). Head-to-head appendix uses SpreadsheetBench-Verified 0:200/200:400 slices.
- **benchmark family**:
> Primarily tool / office-file-agent (SpreadsheetBench, OfficeBench DOCX, PPTX/TSBench, PDF/VRDU/VAREX) plus multi-hop/compositional table-QA (WikiTableQuestions, HiTab) as OOD, math reasoning (DAPO, AIME), and document VQA (DocVQA). Spans tool/code-style file manipulation, table QA, math, and multimodal doc-QA; no embodied or D4RL decision-RL benchmarks.
- **baselines**:
> Skill baselines: No Skill (cli_only); Human-Written (Anthropic's official xlsx / pdf / docx / pptx skills); Parametric (LLM-generated skill from parametric knowledge alone). Trace2Skill variants: +Error, +Success, +Combined; Skill Deepening vs Skill Creation. Design-comparison baselines: sequential skill editing (Seq-B=1 update-after-every-trajectory, Seq-B=4 update-after-4); ReasoningBank-style retrieval memory (top-1 with Qwen3-Embedding-8B, success+failure lessons); single-call +Error LLM (log-only, no artifact inspection/validation); greedy top-1 and Bayesian-optimization patch selection; Anthropic skill-creator (Claude Code, Opus 4.6) external baseline. Head-to-head concurrent systems (Appendix G, shared Qwen3.5-122B): XSkill, EvoSkill (Claude Code and ReAct harnesses), SkillGen.
- **key metrics**:
> SpreadsheetBench: Vrf (verified instance pass rate), Soft (sub-problem pass rate), Hard (all-sub-problems-pass task pass rate); OOD table-QA pass rate (WikiTQ, HiTab). Summary metric Avg = (ID_avg + OOD_avg)/2, equally weighting in-distribution (SpreadsheetBench) and OOD across both user models. Math: DAPO-Test pass rate and AIME avg@8. DocVQA: ANLS and Accuracy (ANLS>=0.5, %). Broader doc agents: task-level pass rate (%). Efficiency: wall-clock skill-generation time (min). All spreadsheet results averaged over 3 seeds (41/42/43).
- **headline result**:
> Skills evolved from Qwen3.5-35B-A3B trajectories (Creation, +Error) improve a Qwen3.5-122B-A10B agent by up to +57.65 percentage points on WikiTableQuestions (OOD table-QA), demonstrating cross-scale, OOD transfer without parameter updates or test-time retrieval. On SpreadsheetBench-Verified Deepening, Human-Written+Combined reaches 69.83 Vrf (122B) vs 48.33 Human-Written and 27.67 No Skill. In the head-to-head (Appendix G, shared Qwen3.5-122B, held-out 200:400), Trace2Skill attains the highest Vrf (65.83 +Error, 69.83 +Combined), above XSkill (23.0), SkillGen (27.5), and EvoSkill (33.5 Claude Code / 59.5 ReAct), and the Human-Written 48.3 floor.
- **ablations**:
> (1) Parallel vs sequential consolidation (same trace pool, +Error): Parallel beats Seq on most 122B SpreadsheetBench metrics (Vrf 65.83 vs 61.83 Seq-B=1 vs 59.00 Seq-B=4) and is far faster (~3 min vs 60 min Seq-B=1, 15 min Seq-B=4); Seq-B=1 is modestly higher only on 35B Soft/Hard. Math and DocVQA show parallel best-or-tied while fastest (math D-Test 95.0 vs 94.0/93.0; DocVQA Acc 92.52 vs 91.05/90.80). (2) Holistic skill vs ReasoningBank retrieval (same trajectory pool): +Combined beats ReasoningBank on Spreadsheet (122B Vrf 69.83 vs 56.00; 35B 29.67 vs 20.50), math (95.0 vs 94.0 D-Test), and DocVQA (Acc 92.52 vs 90.90). (3) Agentic vs single-call +Error LLM: agentic wins Avg in 3 of 4 author-mode blocks and most SpreadsheetBench columns; qualitative audit shows agentic identifies root causes more precisely (parse-error misattribution 14% vs 57%). (4) Analyst type: +Error vs +Success vs +Combined varies by domain (+Combined strongest on spreadsheet/DocVQA Avg; +Error most stable for math). (5) Selective patch aggregation: greedy top-1 plateaus below full aggregation (combinatorial patch value: side-effect flips, semantic overlap); BO selection improves +Error metrics (122B Deepening Vrf 65.83->69.83) but is validation-cost-heavy. (6) skill-creator (Opus 4.6) baseline does not improve over base on average; Trace2Skill +Error consistently stronger (Deepening avg 48.63 vs 23.33 vs 29.00 base).
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> No. Trace2Skill reports only end-to-end task metrics (Vrf/Soft/Hard, table-QA pass rate, DAPO/AIME, ANLS/Acc) plus efficiency (skill-generation wall-clock). It does NOT report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) because it is retrieval-free by design; the ReasoningBank baseline's retrieval is folded into its end-to-end scores. Patch-level analyses (coverage %, fail-to-pass/pass-to-fail flip counts, BO validation pass rate) are diagnostic but not standard intrinsic retrieval metrics.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Mostly outcome-level (final task pass rate / ANLS). Some process-level diagnostics are reported: skill-generation wall-clock time (efficiency), per-SoP coverage shares among patches (e.g., 55.1%/54.8%/42.7%/16.4%), qualitative agentic-vs-LLM root-cause agreement (12.1% strong agreement, 54.5% disagreement on 33 audited cases; parse-error misattribution rates), and fail-to-pass/pass-to-fail flip analyses across greedy iterations. SpreadsheetBench Soft (sub-problem) is a partial-credit process-ish signal. No formal reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Strongly emphasized for skill GENERATION cost: parallel consolidation produces a skill in ~3 min vs ~15 min (Seq-B=4, 5x slower) and ~60 min (Seq-B=1, 20x slower), with the gap scaling linearly in the number of traces N (~70 error lessons, W=128 workers, B_merge=32 => ~3 sequential LLM-call rounds: 1 analyst round + ~2 merge layers). Math: 2.0 min parallel vs 25.9 / 3.8 min sequential; DocVQA: 4.8 min vs 35.9 / 5.2 min. Inference cost is reduced relative to retrieval/online methods because the skill is loaded once with NO test-time retrieval, no parameter updates, and no growing memory. Total compute for all experiments/exploration ~20,000 A100 GPU-hours (8x A100 nodes). BO patch selection is flagged as the main extra-cost component (must materialize and score each candidate skill on a 32-task validation set).
- **context budget and selection count**:
> The consolidated SKILL.md is kept compact and broadly-applicable (e.g., XSkill baseline's merged skill was ~865 words; Trace2Skill keeps the main doc focused while routing niche content to references/, used on demand). Default selection is FULL aggregation of all consolidated patches (no fixed-k cap); greedy/BO selection (BO keeps top m<=15 patches by coverage) are studied as alternatives. Merge batch size B_merge=32; Stage 2 runs 128 parallel sub-agents. Agent rollouts run up to 100 turns (max_turns=100); no separate tool-call budget imposed. Auxiliary files loaded on demand realize progressive disclosure rather than a fixed token budget.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (uses/adapts existing benchmarks rather than constructing a new one). Notable adaptations: SpreadsheetBench-Verified 400 split 200/200; full SpreadsheetBench Soft/Hard on 2,529 examples (evolving-set removed); WikiTableQuestions (2,810) and HiTab (1,585) converted into spreadsheet-format OOD tasks; DAPO-Math 400 evolve/100 test; AIME 2026 (30 problems, avg@8); DocVQA 50 evolve/5,299 test; PDF VRDU Registration Forms->VAREX Flat; PPTX TSBench deck-disjoint OOD; DOCX generated tasks->64 OfficeBench DOCX subtasks (max_turns=100). All scored by each benchmark's official/local verifier.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Agent-skills framing (Anthropic skills; skill-creator guidance; official xlsx/pdf/docx/pptx document skills); ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) harness; experience-memory / self-evolution line (Reflexion, Voyager, ReasoningBank [Ouyang et al. 2026], Memp, AWM/Agent Workflow Memory, Contextual Experience Replay, Investigate-Consolidate-Exploit, skill-set optimization); inductive-reasoning-with-LLMs works; serving via vLLM; uses Qwen3.5-122B-A10B / Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (instruct+thinking hybrid MoE), Gemma-4-31B-it, GPT-5.5-high; Qwen3-Embedding for baseline retrieval. Benchmarks: SpreadsheetBench, WikiTableQuestions, HiTab, DAPO, AIME 2026, DocVQA, VRDU/VAREX, TSBench/Talk-to-Your-Slides, OfficeBench.
- **contrasts with**:
> (1) Online/sequential skill editing (order-dependent updates after each trace) - Trace2Skill does parallel many-to-one consolidation (faster, generally stronger, order-independent). (2) Experience/retrieval memories queried at test time, especially ReasoningBank (also Reflexion, Voyager, Memp, AWM, CER) - Trace2Skill distills into one static skill used without test-time retrieval. (3) Log-only single-call error analysis - Trace2Skill uses agentic artifact-inspecting, fix-validating error analysis. (4) Skill-augmented RL / intrinsic skill evolution / meta-learning that update a policy or maintain test-time memory - Trace2Skill keeps theta frozen and produces a portable artifact. (5) Concurrent skill-evolution systems XSkill, EvoSkill, SkillGen (head-to-head, Trace2Skill higher Vrf) and Anthropic skill-creator (Opus 4.6, no average improvement).
- **lineage**:
> Group F (decision/experience memory & RL-adjacent self-evolving agents) and the agent-skill / experience-memory lineage. A 2026 'trajectory-to-skill' method that advances the Reflexion -> Voyager -> AWM -> ReasoningBank experience-memory line by replacing test-time retrieval/online editing with offline, parallel, inductive consolidation of broad trajectories into one portable, retrieval-free static skill directory. Distinctive contributions: (a) many-to-one parallel consolidation as inductive generalization (vs order-dependent sequential edits), (b) a single distilled skill beating ReasoningBank-style episodic retrieval, (c) agentic (artifact-inspecting, fix-validating) error analysis, and (d) demonstrated cross-scale, cross-family, and OOD portability of the learned skill artifact without parameter updates or retrieval.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- venue
