The survey also cautions that agents over-follow successful trajectories, and that corrected-but-unabstracted trajectories still induce errors under context shift -- motivating abstraction. Thus success+failure contrastive usage is a recognized mechanism.
- **memory evolution update**:
> Survey-level: stored entries are mutated beyond append-only. Reflection performs delta-update/refine-overwrite (error rectification, repair, consistency-based deletion) and dynamic maintenance (incremental schema update via clustering, entity-relation parsing/update, OS-controller persist/evict). Storage uses forget/prune (FIFO eviction, attention/perplexity-based token eviction, temporal decay). Experience performs dedup-merge and compression (cross-trajectory induction satisfying MDL) and link-and-evolve (experience graphs) plus internalization into parameters. So append-only / dedup-merge / delta-update / refine-overwrite / forget-prune / link-and-evolve all appear.
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Survey-level: storage/reflection retrieval is predominantly fixed similarity/weighted top-k (not a learned policy). However, the survey foregrounds a shift toward learned/RL-optimized policies in the Experience stage and in retrieval control: RL on reflections, group-based policy optimization, RL-aligned tool invocation, early-experience/implicit-world-model internalization, and 'Active Memory Perception' autonomous retrieval controllers. It proposes no learned policy itself but documents the trend from fixed top-k to learned policy.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Yes, covered as a recognized and future-emphasized axis: Coordination/Collaborative reflection builds societies of heterogeneous agents using role division and consensus (CSR, CoGent, MIRIX); shared goal memory turns isolated behaviors into coordinated collective execution in multi-agent systems; and 'Distributed Shared Memory' is a headline future direction -- arguing current dialogue-based sharing is bandwidth-limited/noisy and advocating consensus memory systems for socialized experience evolution. So cross-agent/shared memory is both surveyed and flagged as a key open problem.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> No new benchmark is introduced. The survey catalogs 43 representative datasets/benchmarks (Tables 2-3) grouped by stage. Storage stage: LongBench, LongBench v2, RULER, MMNeedle, HotpotQA, MemoryBank, BABILong, DialSim, LongMemEval, BEAM, MPR, LOCCO, MADial-Bench, HELMET. Reflection stage: Minerva, HaluMem, MABench, PRM, PersonMem v2, LoCoMo, WebChoreArena, MT-Mind2Web, StoryBench, PerLTQA, ImplexConv, Share, Mem-PAL, PrefEval, LIDB. Experience stage: StreamBench, MemoryBench, Evo-Memory, LABench. It notes Experience-stage benchmarks are scarce.
- **benchmark family**:
> memory (agent-memory evaluation survey). Sub-families spanned: extreme-context / long-context (RULER, BABILong, HELMET, LongBench/v2, MMNeedle-multimodal), multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MPR), long-term/cross-session dialogue & persona consistency (MemoryBank, DialSim, LongMemEval, BEAM, LOCCO, LoCoMo, MADial-Bench), memory-hallucination/lifecycle (Minerva, HaluMem, MABench), personalization (PRM, PersonMem v2, PerLTQA, ImplexConv, Share, Mem-PAL, PrefEval, LIDB), web/embodied dynamic reasoning (WebChoreArena, MT-Mind2Web, StoryBench), and continual/lifelong/test-time experience learning (StreamBench, MemoryBench, Evo-Memory, LABench).
- **baselines**:
> N/A -- a survey with no experiments. Instead of baselines it organizes and compares representative systems by stage in Figure 4's taxonomy, e.g.: Storage -- PCW, StreamingLLM, SelfExtend, H2O, Quest, LLMLingua (Linear); ARMRAG, MemLong, Larimar, MemoryBank, Stanford Generative Agents (Vector); ChatDB, DB-GPT, MAC-SQL, MemGPT, MemoChat, MemOS, MemLLM, AriGraph, GraphReader (Structured). Reflection -- Reflexion, TiM, LLM-MapRepair, Zep, Mem0, CAMA, MemOrb, LEGOMem, AgentFold, DEAL, ToolMem, CLIN, Memory-R1, MDSF, Self-Goal, MIRIX, CoGent, CSR. Experience -- FLEX, ArcMem, LightMem, CASCADE, IPS, AccelOpt (Explicit); MemGen, LatentEvolve, AgentEvolver, Agent-LV, Verl (Implicit); ReasoningBank, EvolveR, Hybrid-Replay (Hybrid).
- **key metrics**:
> Survey-level: no metrics computed. It discusses, per benchmark, metrics such as QA accuracy / answer correctness, multi-needle retrieval accuracy, multi-hop reasoning accuracy, retrieval precision/recall, persona/relationship consistency, memory fidelity (fabrication/omission rates as in HaluMem), test-time/continual-learning improvement and knowledge-transfer/generalization (StreamBench, Evo-Memory, LABench), and information-decay measures. It also conceptually distinguishes memory capacity vs reasoning precision.
- **headline result**:
> N/A (no empirical headline number; it is a survey). Its headline contribution is the evolutionary three-stage framework -- Storage (trajectory preservation), Reflection (trajectory refinement), Experience (trajectory abstraction) -- formalized as F_ref: T->S (intra-trajectory transformation m'_i = F_ref(tau_i | phi)) vs F_exp: T_batch -> K (inter-trajectory induction with |K| << sum |tau|, an MDL-style compression to a policy prior), plus the two transformative Experience mechanisms (active exploration, cross-trajectory abstraction). 216 references; 6 citations (Semantic Scholar, as of mid-2026).
- **ablations**:
> N/A (no experiments/ablations). The closest analytical artifact is Table 1, a structural comparison between Reflection and Experience along functional signature, output form (refined unit m'_i tied to task context vs universal rules/skills K detached from any scenario), retrieval dependency (similar-task retrieval at inference vs policy prior for unseen scenarios without trajectory matching), and representative works (Reflexion/CLIN/AgentFold vs FLEX/MemSkill/SkillRL).
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Survey-level: advocates measuring more than final outcome. It distinguishes capacity for accurate storage/retrieval, memory fidelity (process-level fabrication/omission, e.g., HaluMem/Minerva over the memory lifecycle), dynamic-reasoning/backtracking quality, and abstraction/generalization/transfer (Experience). The framing pushes toward process- and lifecycle-level memory evaluation, not just end-task success, but the survey itself reports no scores.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> Discussed qualitatively as a primary driver: context-window/storage constraints and the cost of unrestricted memory growth (retrieval latency, inference burden, error propagation). Storage trades capacity vs retrieval speed (tiered architectures); Experience explicitly compresses memory (MDL: |K| << sum_tau |tau|) to cut retrieval/inference overhead and enable zero-shot transfer; implicit/hybrid Experience internalizes experience into parameters to remove retrieval dependence ('Storage Explosion' and 'Retrieval Latency' mitigation). No concrete latency/cost numbers (it is a survey).
- **context budget and selection count**:
> Survey-level: the limited context window vs expanding interaction history is the foundational Storage motivation. Methods manage budget via FIFO eviction, context-window extension (PCW/StreamingLLM/SelfExtend), sparsification/compression (H2O/Quest/LLMLingua), tiered/virtual context (MemGPT), context-folding (AgentFold), and Experience-stage compression into compact rules/skills/parameters. Reads are typically fixed/weighted top-k. No single budget/k value is prescribed.
- **survey scope and axes**:
> Organizing logic is 'Why-How-What' over a dynamic-evolution framework. Axes: (Why / Evolutionary Drivers) Long-Term Consistency {state, goals}, Dynamic Environments {temporal validity of knowledge, causal structure}, Continual Learning {storage constraints, requirement for experience}; (How / Evolutionary Path) Storage {Linear: context-window adaptation, information sparsification; Vector: semantic retrieval, weighted retrieval; Structured: tabular database, tiered architectures, semantic graphs} -> Reflection {Introspection: error rectification, dynamic maintenance, knowledge compression; Environment: environment modeling, decision optimization; Coordination: multi-dimensional calibration} -> Experience {Explicit: heuristic guidelines, procedural primitives; Implicit: latent modulation, parameter internalization; Hybrid: experience transfer}; (What / Transformative Experience) Active Exploration {mechanisms: reward/curriculum/reuse-driven; dimensions: breadth/depth/strategy} and Cross-Trajectory Abstraction {mechanisms: contrastive induction, multi-granularity chunking, code encapsulation, parameter internalization; granularity: shallow NL rules / intermediate executable skeletons / deep parametric}. Future Directions: active memory perception, working-memory organization, Experience benchmarks, distributed shared memory, multimodal memory (Appendix C). 216 references; coverage through 2025 (claimed first evolution-perspective memory survey), with 2026-dated frontier works.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (proposes no benchmark). It tabulates 43 existing datasets with sizes/construction in Tables 2-3, e.g. LongBench (4.7k, up to 32k tokens), LongBench v2 (503, 8k-2M words), RULER (scalable, multi-needle/multi-hop), BABILong (scalable, up to 1M tokens), HELMET (scalable, up to 128k tokens), HotpotQA (113k, multi-hop Wikipedia), MMNeedle (280k, multimodal), MemoryBank (194, 10-day dialogue), LoCoMo (50, 35 sessions), LongMemEval (500), HaluMem (3.5k, fabrication/omission), StreamBench (9.7k, online learning), MemoryBench (20k, continual learning), Evo-Memory (3.7k, test-time learning), LABench (1.4k, lifelong learning). It notes current benchmarks mostly assess static storage/retrieval and that Experience-stage benchmarks are scarce.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Prior LLM-agent memory surveys it extends/critiques -- Zhang et al. 2024 (engineering-module classification of agent memory) and Hu et al. 2025 (dynamic memory processes); cognitive-architecture framing (Sumers et al. CoALA). Foundational memory/agent systems it taxonomizes: ReAct, Reflexion, Generative Agents (Stanford Town), MemGPT, MemoryBank, ChatDB, TiM, MemoChat, MemOS, AriGraph, GraphReader, Mem0, Zep, CLIN; and frontier Experience works ReasoningBank, EvolveR, AgentEvolver, MemGen, LatentEvolve, FLEX. Theoretical grounding: Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle for the Experience-stage compression operator.
- **contrasts with**:
> Positions itself against prior agent-memory surveys (Zhang et al. 2024; Hu et al. 2025; Wu et al. 2025; Du et al. 2025; Wu & Shu 2025; Cao et al. 2025) that organize memory by static functional/engineering categories and lack a unified evolutionary perspective, thereby obscuring the technical drivers of memory development. It also contrasts the two fragmented paradigms it seeks to unify -- OS-engineering memory management vs cognitive-science memory simulation -- and internally contrasts Storage vs Reflection vs Experience (Table 1: intra-trajectory refinement vs inter-trajectory abstraction).
- **lineage**:
> Surveys group -- an evolution-perspective memory survey for LLM-based agents (Storage -> Reflection -> Experience). It sits downstream of foundational agent-memory surveys (e.g., Zhang et al. 2024 'A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of LLM-based Agents') and is a sibling of contemporaneous 2025-2026 memory/experience surveys; it directly anchors the experiential-agent lineage by linking ExpeL/Reflexion/AWM-style works to its taxonomy (Reflexion in Reflection; ReasoningBank/skill-induction/AWM-style procedural primitives and cross-trajectory abstraction in Experience), formalizing the shift from trajectory storage to policy-prior abstraction.

**Uncertain fields** (not researched / unverifiable):

- completeness_vs_topk_objective
- evaluation_decoupling
- reranking

<a id="item-sok-agentic-rag"></a>
### 181. SoK: Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): Taxonomy, Architectures, Evaluation, and Research Directions

2026  ·  arXiv:2603.07379 (2026-03, verified)  ·  [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07379)


**Basic Info**

- **year**: 2026
- **venue**:
> arXiv preprint (arXiv:2603.07379, cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.CR/cs.IR). Submitted 7 Mar 2026 (v1, 3,024 KB). Not a peer-reviewed venue; arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2603.07379. As of indexing, Semantic Scholar (CorpusId 286376927) reports referenceCount 105 and citationCount 4. The HTML bibliography lists ~118 numbered entries.
- **paper url**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.07379
- **code url**:
> N/A (this is a Systematization-of-Knowledge survey; the authors provide no original code/implementation or benchmark artifact. The github.com links appearing in the paper are citations to third-party frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, Smolagents, and AutoGen, not an artifact released by the authors.)
- **maintained repo url**: N/A (no continuously-updated authors' paper list, leaderboard, or living-survey repository is associated with this work; it is a frozen v1 arXiv PDF/HTML.)

**Problem Definition**

- **task domain**:
> Survey / Systematization of Knowledge (SoK). Surveys Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG): RAG pipelines that evolve into autonomous, multi-step, tool-using agentic architectures. Spans knowledge-intensive QA (single-hop, multi-hop, long-form), multi-step reasoning, tool-use/function-calling, web/search-integrated reasoning, decision-making, and memory-augmented long-horizon interaction. It frames the entire class as a sequential decision-making (POMDP) problem rather than a single task domain.
- **problem setting**:
> Analytical SoK paper, not a method or system with original experiments. Its core contribution is a unified theoretical framework: it formalizes agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) with tuple S_ARAG = <S_env, A, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T>, where the external corpus C is a latent partially observable source, the action space A = A_ret U A_reason U A_tool U {STOP}, and working memory M_t approximates the belief state b_t. It then builds a modular architectural decomposition (Planner, Retrieval Engine, Reasoning Engine/Controller, Memory Systems, Tool Orchestration Layer, Verification/Self-Correction) and a multi-axis taxonomy (architectural/topology, retrieval strategy, reasoning, memory/context). Covers both single- and multi-agent, offline and interactive, supervised and unsupervised settings as surveyed sub-areas. It defines NO controlled experimental protocol, training supervision, or benchmark of its own; it formalizes a budget-constrained objective max_pi E_tau[R_task(y,y*) - lambda * sum_t C(a_t)] but reports no empirical numbers.
- **what is retrieved**:
> N/A as an artifact (the SoK itself retrieves nothing). As surveyed content, Agentic RAG systems retrieve: documents/passages/text chunks (vector/semantic retrieval over external knowledge corpora), tool/API outputs (function-calling observations), web-search results, and agent memory entries (episodic trajectories, reflective feedback, persistent long-horizon memory). Retrieval is modeled formally as a discrete action a_t = Retrieve(q'_t) returning an observation o_t in Omega.
- **retrieval grounding**:
> HYBRID at the survey level. It explicitly models retrieval against a STATIC/dynamic external corpus C (latent partially observable knowledge source, plus tools/APIs and web search) AND a GROWING agent memory the agent writes (episodic memory, persistent long-horizon memory in vector DBs, e.g., MemoryBank/MemGPT-style). The POMDP treats both external retrieval (observation function O) and memory write/read/prune (belief-state update on M_t) as first-class.
- **completeness vs topk objective**:
> N/A (survey; defines no retrieval objective of its own beyond a generic top-k retriever in baseline RAG). It instead emphasizes adaptive, state-dependent, iterative retrieval (one-shot vs iterative vs self-refining) controlled by the agent's policy, and surfaces Effective Information Rate (EIR = useful retrieved tokens / total retrieved tokens) and Context Relevance as efficiency-oriented retrieval objectives that penalize context overloading rather than a fixed top-k or completeness target.
- **cbr cycle coverage**: N/A (the SoK is not a case-based reasoning system and implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle).
- **explicit cbr grounding**: False. The paper does not frame Agentic RAG as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It organizes the field around a POMDP formalization, modular architectural components, and taxonomy axes (topology, retrieval strategy, reasoning, memory).

**Retrieval Mechanism**

- **retrieval unit**:
> N/A (survey defines no single retrieval unit). Surveyed/modeled units: text chunks/passages/documents (the typical observation o_t returned by the retriever), tool-API outputs/observations, web snippets, and memory entries (episodic trajectories, reflective notes, persistent long-horizon memory states). Formally any o_t in the observation space Omega.
- **index source**:
> N/A for the SoK (it builds no index). Surveyed Agentic RAG draws on a static/dynamic external corpus C (vector indexes, tools/APIs, live web search) combined with a growing agent memory written online during the control loop (episodic + persistent long-horizon memory persisted into vector databases). The work classifies memory paradigms (dynamic context pruning, episodic memory, persistent long-horizon memory) as the growing/online side.
- **index structure topology**:
> N/A (SoK has no index of its own). It reviews flat vector indexes/databases for documents and for persistent long-horizon memory (MemoryBank, MemGPT), plus graph-structured agentic orchestration substrates (LangGraph graph-structured workloads). Its own organizing structure is a multi-axis taxonomy and a POMDP component map, not an index topology.
- **retriever type**:
> N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). Surveyed retrievers are off-the-shelf dense/semantic retrievers and tool/web-search APIs invoked as actions; the LLM acts as the control policy / query constructor (LLM-as-controller) rather than as the retriever. It also notes learned context filters (FILCO, Provence) and self-retrieval/critique (Self-RAG) as variants.
- **retriever learning signal**:
> N/A (survey; trains no retriever). It reviews systems where retrieval decisions are driven by the LLM control policy via prompting or fine-tuning (pi_theta), by token/log-probability confidence thresholds (Active RAG/FLARE, contrasted with Agentic RAG), by self-critique (Self-RAG), and by learned/RL or hybrid control policies; as a future direction it proposes RL with stability constraints and Bayesian retrieval-confidence calibration. It standardizes no single learning signal.
- **query construction**:
> N/A as a method. Surveyed/modeled: queries are conditionally generated at runtime from the evolving memory state, a_t = Retrieve(q'_t) with q'_t conditioned on M_t (Dynamic Retrieval property). Concrete surveyed constructions include CoT/ReAct thought-conditioned query construction (IRCoT), planner-driven decomposition (Plan-Then-Retrieve, Decomposition-Based Retrieval), and query reformulation/rewriting in self-refining loops. It notes semantic drift as a risk of iterative reformulation.
- **query granularity**:
> N/A (survey). Modeled at multiple levels: task-level (one-shot at t=0), and step/state-level (iterative and self-refining retrieval where later retrievals depend on intermediate state M_t). The taxonomy's retrieval-strategy axis (one-shot / iterative / self-refining) is precisely about query granularity over the trajectory.
- **when to retrieve**:
> N/A (survey). Its retrieval-strategy taxonomy spans one-shot (single retrieval then generate), iterative (multiple state-dependent retrievals during one query), and self-refining (retrieval coupled with critique/revision). It explicitly distinguishes Active RAG (token-confidence-triggered, single-pass) from Agentic RAG (policy-driven, multi-step, explicit deliberation).
- **retrieval trigger signal**:
> N/A (survey defines no single trigger). It catalogs: log-probability thresholds / token heuristics (Active RAG/FLARE, which it explicitly contrasts as NOT agentic), explicit policy-driven reasoning and tool-calling decisions sampled from pi_theta(a_t | M_t) (Agentic RAG), reflection/self-evaluation steps (Reflexion, Self-RAG, RARR), and relevance/critique-driven re-retrieval in self-refining loops. The defining Agentic trait is policy-driven (not confidence-threshold) triggering.
- **reranking**: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). It does not center reranking as a taxonomy axis; instead it foregrounds dynamic context pruning/filtering (FILCO, Provence) and self-refining critique as the post-retrieval selection mechanisms.
- **retrieved context refinement**:
> N/A as a method. Surveyed refinement operations: dynamic context pruning/compression and learned context filtering (FILCO, Provence) to mitigate irrelevant evidence and the lost-in-the-middle effect; self-refining critique/revision of retrieved evidence (Self-RAG, RARR); and memory belief-update operations (selective retrieval augmentation, summarization, pruning of redundant info, learned memory controllers). The SoK frames refinement as belief-state update on M_t.
- **tool document engineering**:
> N/A (the SoK contributes no tool-document-engineering technique). Tool invocation is modeled abstractly as actions in A_tool with outputs returned via the observation function O; it discusses tool reliability evaluation (selection, parameter F1, execution-based sandbox assessment) but not how tool/skill descriptions are indexed.
- **index content separation**: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own). It discusses dynamic context pruning (loading/compressing retrieved content before generation) but not a lightweight-index-then-content progressive-disclosure scheme.
- **dynamic index and protocol**:
> N/A as a contribution. It reviews tool integration via function-calling and agent SDKs/frameworks (OpenAI function calling / Agents SDK, Anthropic tool use, Google ADK, LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Smolagents, AutoGen) and treats tool calling as an explicit multi-step interaction boundary, but it does not center a live-synchronized tool index or a specific protocol such as MCP/RapidAPI as a taxonomy axis.
- **tool dependency awareness**: N/A (survey). It discusses Planner-Executor role separation, multi-agent delegation, and cascading tool-execution errors, but does not center an explicit inter-tool dependency-graph retrieval formalism.

**Utilization Mechanism**

- **how retrieved used**:
> N/A as a method. Modeled formally: retrieved observations o_t are appended to working memory (M_{t+1} = M_t U O(o_t | s_t, a_t)) and the final answer is generated as y = G(M_T) after the policy emits STOP. Surveyed utilization spans prompt/context augmentation, iterative refinement across reflection loops, and feeding validated/refined evidence to a response-synthesis step. Unlike append-only Active RAG, Agentic RAG supports read/write/prune over working memory.
- **planning integration**:
> N/A as a method. Planning is a first-class POMDP/architecture element (Planner module governs tool invocation under a control policy). The SoK catalogs design patterns for retrieval-planning integration: Plan-Then-Retrieve, Retrieve-Reflect-Refine, Decomposition-Based Retrieval, Tool-Augmented Retrieval Loop, Multi-Agent Collaboration, Retrieval-Grounded Self-Verification, and Human-As-A-Tool (HITL). Topology axis covers Single-Agent, Planner-Executor, and Multi-Agent RAG. It reviews these rather than committing to one.
- **reasoning search interleaving granularity**:
> N/A (survey). Its reasoning taxonomy enumerates per-step interleaving styles: Chain-of-Thought, ReAct-style (interleaving reasoning steps with tool actions/observations), reflection-based (per-critique self-evaluation), and tree-based exploration (search over candidate branches with backtracking, e.g., Tree-of-Thoughts). It also contrasts Active RAG per-token interleaving against Agentic RAG per-action/per-tool-call interleaving.
- **adaptation mechanism**: N/A (not a CBR method; no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism of its own).
- **retrieved item representation**:
> N/A (survey). Surveyed injected forms: raw retrieved passages/text chunks, tool/API outputs, web snippets, and memory representations (episodic trajectories, reflective feedback, summarized contextual knowledge). The SoK abstracts these as structured memory representations M_t approximating the belief state, updated via augmentation/summarization/pruning.
- **abstraction level of retrieved unit**:
> N/A (survey). Surveyed units span raw passages/documents and tool outputs (low abstraction) up through summarized/consolidated memory and reflective insights (higher abstraction). The SoK does not fix an abstraction level; it treats the unit generically as observations o_t and memory elements.
- **noise robustness mechanism**:
> N/A as a method (the SoK contributes none). It dedicates major analysis to robustness as a needed evaluation dimension: Noise Robustness (extracting answers from distracting context), Negative Rejection (declining when context is absent), and Adaptive Resilience (recovering when the environment changes mid-task), citing RGB/FaithEval/RAGEval. It also diagnoses noise-driven failure modes (retrieval drift, hallucination despite retrieval, compounded hallucination loops) and proposes future counterfactual-retrieval resilience datasets.

**Memory & Learning**

- **memory type**:
> Survey-level: memory is a central taxonomy axis and architectural module. It distinguishes (1) dynamic context pruning of the active context window (FILCO, Provence), (2) episodic memory (temporally bounded trajectories/feedback, e.g., Reflexion buffer, Generative Agents memory stream), and (3) persistent long-horizon memory across sessions persisted into vector DBs (MemoryBank, MemGPT). Formally, working memory M_t approximates the POMDP belief state b_t. The SoK itself has no memory.
- **write back**:
> N/A as a method. Surveyed Agentic RAG systems DO write back: working memory updates each step (M_{t+1} = M_t U {observations/conclusions}), episodic buffers store reflective feedback, and persistent long-horizon memory stores/recalls/updates interaction memories. The SoK frames write-back as belief-state update; it stores nothing itself.
- **online growth**: N/A as a method. Surveyed memory grows online during the control loop and across sessions (episodic logging per step; persistent memory accumulated across sessions). The SoK itself has no growing store.
- **write back trigger**:
> N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Modeled/surveyed triggers: per-step belief-state updates after each retrieval/reasoning action; reflective writes after self-critique (Reflexion episodic buffer); and persistent-memory refresh strategies (update/consolidate/decay) for long-horizon memory (MemoryBank/MemGPT). It also flags memory-update timing as a security/robustness concern (poisoning persists across writes).
- **failure experience usage**:
> N/A (survey). It reviews reflection/self-correction patterns that act on poor/failed retrieval or outputs (Reflexion stores reflective feedback in an episodic buffer; Retrieve-Reflect-Refine and Retrieval-Grounded Self-Verification patterns), implying use of failure signals, but it also warns that reflection sharing the generator's parametric biases can reinforce errors (Feedback Reinforcement Instability). It contributes no explicit success-vs-failure storage scheme.
- **memory evolution update**:
> N/A (survey). Surveyed post-write dynamics: belief-update operations (selective augmentation, summarization, pruning of redundant info), persistent-memory refresh strategies that update/consolidate/decay entries over time, and learned memory controllers that retain high-utility signals. It proposes no single canonical post-write policy and flags memory robustness/poisoning as an open problem (10.3).
- **retrieval as learned policy**:
> Survey-level YES (as a framing): the SoK's defining thesis is that Agentic RAG is characterized by a stochastic control policy pi_theta(a_t | M_t) over an action space including retrieval, and it formulates policy optimization as a budget-constrained sequential decision problem (max over pi_theta of E[R_task - lambda*sum C(a_t)]). It surveys policies that are heuristic, hybrid, or learned/RL, and proposes RL with stability constraints as a future direction; it implements no learned policy itself.
- **cross agent or cross framework sharing**:
> Surveyed (not a contribution): Multi-Agent RAG distributes planning/retrieval/generation across agents with shared/aggregated memory (AutoGen multi-agent conversation, CrewAI, LangGraph orchestration, Google ADK). It reviews cross-agent coordination and shared memory, and flags multi-agent retrieval drift via delegation and cross-session leakage as risks; it does not implement cross-agent sharing.

**Evaluation**

- **benchmarks**:
> N/A as original experiments (the SoK runs no experiments and reports no results of its own). It catalogs and critiques evaluation frameworks/benchmarks used for (agentic) RAG: RGB (Benchmarking LLMs in RAG), FaithEval, RAGBench (with the TRACe framework: uTilization/Relevance/Adherence/Completeness), RAGEval, CRAG, plus newer rubric-based/contamination-aware frameworks DRACO and CL-Bench. It also references agent-evaluation surveys.
- **benchmark family**:
> Survey-level grouping. Primary families discussed are RAG-evaluation / faithfulness-and-noise frameworks (RGB, FaithEval, RAGBench/TRACe, RAGEval, CRAG) and emerging agentic/trajectory-aware evaluation (DRACO, CL-Bench), plus agent-evaluation surveys. It explicitly argues these are mostly QA/multi-hop static, single-forward-pass benchmarks that fail to capture long-horizon trajectory evaluation, dynamic tool invocation, and multi-step interaction; it does not adopt the embodied/web/tool/decision-RL benchmark families as primary axes.
- **baselines**:
> N/A (survey; no head-to-head method comparison of its own). Its comparative analysis contrasts paradigm classes (static/baseline RAG vs Active RAG vs Agentic RAG) and archetypes (baseline grounded generation, iterative evidence accumulation, reflective refinement, role-separated orchestration, distributed knowledge work, memory-centric long-horizon), anchored by representative systems (RAG, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen, Self-RAG, RARR, Reflexion, HuggingGPT, MRKL, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangGraph, MemoryBank, MemGPT).
- **key metrics**:
> N/A as original measurement (no numbers of its own). It proposes/synthesizes agentic evaluation metrics: Progress Rate (PR = successful reasoning steps / total reasoning steps), Effective Information Rate (EIR = useful retrieved tokens / total retrieved tokens), Context Relevance, Faithfulness (TRACe Adherence / NLI), Tool Reliability (parameter F1, execution-based sandbox verification), and robustness metrics (Noise Robustness, Negative Rejection, Adaptive Resilience). It critiques BLEU/ROUGE, Exact Match, Final-Answer Accuracy, Success Rate, and Pass@k as inadequate for agentic systems (Table VII Metric Failure Analysis).
- **headline result**:
> N/A (survey; no headline number). Its central contributions are conceptual: (1) the FIRST unified framework modeling agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon POMDPs S_ARAG = <S_env, A, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T> with four necessary properties (Iterative Control, Dynamic Retrieval, Tool-Mediated Interaction, State Persistence) plus finite-horizon Termination; (2) a multi-axis taxonomy (topology / retrieval-strategy / reasoning / memory) and modular architectural decomposition; (3) a three-layer evaluation pipeline (component / trajectory / system level); and (4) five doctoral-scale grand research problems (stable adaptive retrieval, formal reasoning evaluation, memory security, cost-aware orchestration, trust calibration). For grounding the diagnosis it cites striking surveyed numbers, e.g., RAG legal tools hallucinating up to 33%, and as few as 5 injected malicious documents causing ~90% attack success.
- **ablations**:
> N/A (survey; conducts no experiments and reports no component ablations). Its closest analogue is the Cross-Dimensional Trade-Off Analysis (Section IV-E): Retrieval Depth vs Cost, Planning Complexity vs Latency, and Cost/Latency/Token Economics (token amplification scaling with iterative steps), plus the consolidated taxonomy Table III mapping archetypes to topology/retrieval/reasoning/memory/policy and Table IV mapping representative systems to taxonomy dimensions.
- **evaluation decoupling**:
> Survey-level YES (as a recommendation, not original measurement). It explicitly argues evaluation must decouple intrinsic/component metrics from end-to-end outcome and proposes a three-layer pipeline: Layer 1 Component-Level (Planner decomposition, Retriever recall/precision, Tool Executor invocation accuracy and parameter F1), Layer 2 Trajectory-Level Coherence (Progress Rate, step-success ratios, memory consistency), Layer 3 System-Level Outcome (final task completion, coordination effectiveness, faithfulness, plus cost/latency/TTFT). It critiques conflating intrinsic retrieval accuracy with final outcome.
- **process vs outcome metrics**:
> Survey-level central thesis: evaluation must assess PROCESS (multi-step reasoning trajectory, tool interaction, decision dependencies), not just final-answer OUTCOME. It introduces trajectory-level metrics (Progress Rate, EIR), an Iterative Reasoning Quality dimension (auditing logical steps, e.g., Reasoning-via-Planning), and warns that final-answer/EM/Success-Rate metrics are 'trajectory blind' and cannot distinguish sound reasoning from lucky guesses. The SoK itself scores nothing.
- **cost efficiency tradeoff**:
> N/A as original measurement (no cost numbers of its own). It treats cost as first-class: the POMDP objective subtracts a step-wise cost term lambda*sum_t C(a_t) modeling latency, token consumption, and API limits; Section IV-E analyzes Retrieval Depth vs Cost, Planning Complexity vs Latency, and token amplification (iterative retrieval scaling cost with number of steps); the evaluation pipeline mandates Cost and Latency Awareness (token amplification, Time-To-First-Token); and Grand Problem 10.4 (Cost-Aware Autonomous Orchestration) targets Pareto efficiency (Compute vs Accuracy) and budget-aware multi-agent routing.
- **context budget and selection count**:
> N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It frames context budget via the lambda regularizer in the POMDP objective and the Memory/Context paradigms axis: long-context models still need structured context selection (lost-in-the-middle), motivating Dynamic Context Pruning (FILCO, Provence) and budget-aware orchestration. It prescribes no fixed-k or token cap; it advocates adaptive, budget-constrained context construction.
- **survey scope and axes**:
> Primary organizing axes: (1) a POMDP system-level formalization (S_env, A=A_ret U A_reason U A_tool U {STOP}, Omega, O, pi_theta, M, T) with a property->POMDP-component mapping table and an Active-RAG-vs-Agentic-RAG distinction table; (2) a multi-dimensional taxonomy -- Architectural/Topology (Single-Agent, Planner-Executor, Multi-Agent), Retrieval Strategy (One-Shot, Iterative, Self-Refining), Reasoning (CoT, ReAct-style, Reflection, Tree-based), Memory/Context (dynamic pruning, episodic, persistent long-horizon), and Control Policy (heuristic/hybrid/learned), with cross-dimensional trade-off analysis; (3) core architectural components (Planner, Retrieval Engine, Reasoning Engine/Controller, Memory Systems, Tool Orchestration, Verification/Self-Correction); (4) seven design patterns; (5) a three-layer evaluation pipeline and a metric-failure analysis; (6) industry frameworks and deployment; (7) failure modes/safety (retrieval drift, hallucination despite retrieval, tool misuse/cascading errors, prompt injection, memory poisoning, systemic risk amplification); and (8) five doctoral-scale grand research problems. Coverage window ~2023-2026 (v1 Mar 2026); ~105 references per Semantic Scholar, ~118 numbered HTML bibliography entries.
- **benchmark construction and size**:
> N/A (this is a survey/SoK, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset). It reports characteristics of frameworks it catalogs (e.g., RAGBench's TRACe framework with uTilization/Relevance/Adherence/Completeness; RGB/FaithEval for noise robustness and counterfactual adherence; RAGEval/CRAG for keypoint-based factual accuracy and multi-hop coverage) but generates none of its own.

**Relations**

- **builds on**:
> Builds on and synthesizes: (1) foundational RAG (Lewis et al. RAG; Gao et al. and the 'RAG meeting LLMs' survey for the static-RAG baseline and survey framing); (2) iterative/active retrieval (IRCoT, Iter-RetGen / iterative retrieval-generation synergy, FLARE/Active RAG); (3) self-refining retrieval and attribution (Self-RAG, RARR); (4) agent reasoning/acting (ReAct, Chain-of-Thought, Plan-and-Solve, Reflexion, Tree-of-Thoughts); (5) modular/neuro-symbolic and controller-executor agents (MRKL, HuggingGPT); (6) context pruning (FILCO, Provence) and lost-in-the-middle analyses; (7) memory systems (Generative Agents, MemoryBank, MemGPT, agentic memory); (8) evaluation frameworks (RGB, FaithEval, RAGBench/TRACe, RAGEval, CRAG, agent-evaluation surveys); and (9) industrial frameworks/SDKs (OpenAI function calling/Agents SDK, Anthropic tool use, Google ADK, LangChain/LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Smolagents, AutoGen). POMDP/sequential-decision framing draws on the RL/control literature.
- **contrasts with**:
> Explicitly positions Agentic RAG against: (1) static/baseline retrieve-then-generate RAG (single forward pass, append-only context, cannot self-correct); and (2) Active RAG (e.g., FLARE) -- it dedicates Table II to distinguishing Active RAG (log-probability/token-heuristic triggers, single-pass forward generation, implicit planning, append-only context, no self-correction) from Agentic RAG (policy-driven reasoning and explicit tool-calling, iterative multi-step planning loops, explicit deliberative phase, read/write/prune working memory, can discard poor retrieval and re-query). As a SoK it also contrasts its formal POMDP-grounded, trajectory-level evaluation stance against prior fragmented, output-only RAG evaluation practice and prior Agentic RAG surveys that lack a sequential-decision formalization.
- **lineage**:
> Surveys group. A 2026 Systematization-of-Knowledge survey that is distinctive for being the first to formalize agentic retrieve-generate loops as finite-horizon POMDPs and to organize the field around a sequential-decision-making frame (control policy, action space, belief-state memory, budget-constrained objective). It serves as an umbrella/foundational reference connecting iterative/active retrieval (FLARE, IRCoT, Iter-RetGen), self-refining/corrective retrieval (Self-RAG, RARR), agent reasoning (ReAct, Reflexion, ToT), memory systems (MemGPT, MemoryBank, agentic memory), tool orchestration, and agentic evaluation -- relevant to multiple sub-topics in this collection rather than being a method within any single one. It complements the 2025 Singh et al. 'Agentic RAG' survey, adding a formal POMDP backbone, a systemic failure-mode/safety analysis, and a doctoral-scale research roadmap.
